v.verdict: The only change is that the contract-item toast is gone, so the keybind legend no longer has a banner pressed against it; the HUD is still a set of mismatched dark boxes with a capital letter and a clipped fill.

findings.where: top-left 'current pillagers' list and top-right 'run info' bar
findings.what: The two panels sit on different components. The list has a 4px radius, no border and tiny text of about 14px. The run info bar is a taller, wider, dark bar with a chevron, and its text is larger and has a different left inset. Both dark fills are semi-transparent and the map shows through, so they read as unrelated boxes. The keybind legend and the ammo card add two more panel styles with different borders and radii.
findings.fix: Build every HUD panel on one component: fill --ui-panel at about 92% opacity, 1px --ui-line-hi border, --rad 4px, 16px padding, header in 16px f-cond 600 +.04em. Give the list, the run info bar, the legend and the ammo card the same border and header height of 32px.

findings.what: The run info bar is collapsed to a header and its text is vertically off-centre. The panel is the same width as the 300px legend, yet the two top-corner elements have different heights and different margins to the screen edge. The run info bar is flush at about 18px from the right edge while the list sits 8px from the left edge, so the HUD has no common margin.
findings.fix: Set one HUD margin of 24px (--sp-3) from every screen edge. Make the 'current pillagers' list and the run info bar the same 32px header height and align both text baselines to it.

findings.what: 'run Info' on the top-right bar shows a capital I, which breaks the all-lower-case rule. The 'current pillagers' header also uses a small 14px size where the scale floor for readable text is 16px.
findings.fix: Change the string to 'run info' (and check that no code uppercases it). Raise the list rows and header to 16px minimum and the money column to 16px f-cond 600.

findings.what: The hp bar is a flat green block that runs off the left edge and touches the screen bottom. The 'hp 100' text is oversized at about 36px and uses a heavier weight than the ammo number, so the corner has two competing heroes. The bar has no panel, no border and no inset, so it does not match the hotbar cells.
findings.fix: Inset it to x=24 and y=1080-24-24. Make it a 24px-tall bar with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius, and put 'hp' in 16px label type with '100' at 20px inside it. Keep 56px --fs-hero for ammo only.

findings.where: bottom-left, two round status icons above hp
findings.what: The orange crossed-eye icon and the teal clover icon are round, use thick coloured outlines and sit 20px from the left edge. Round badges clash with the 4px-radius rectangles everywhere else, and the player cannot tell from the icons what they mean.
findings.fix: Draw them as 32px rectangles with 4px radius, a 1px border and a tinted fill, 8px apart. Put a 16px label under each ('hidden', 'luck') or show the label on focus.

findings.what: The legend is a large 300x300 block with 18 rows and 9 key caps. It is the heaviest object on the left of the screen and competes with the player and the action. The 'lmb' key appears twice, as 'fire' and 'use item'. Section headers 'move', 'gear', 'fight' and 'raid' are muted grey at about 14px and low in contrast.
findings.fix: Fold it to one line by default, as the settled raid-controls rule says (mid-bottom left, F1 opens it). If it stays open, drop it to 85% opacity and raise the section headers to 16px --tx-2 with at least 4.5:1 contrast. Show the second 'lmb' row only while the item wheel is open.

findings.what: The timer is bold and works as the hero, but the 'extract 152m' pill below is a teal-outlined rounded rectangle, a third pill shape. The extract arrow below it overlaps the pill's bottom edge. The 'c 152m' pill at right repeats the same distance with a different style and a bigger size.
findings.fix: Keep one extract indicator. Make it a 4px-radius pill with a 1px --extract border and 16px type, with the arrow inside it. Remove the duplicate 'c 152m' pill or turn it into an edge arrow with no text.

findings.what: The purple-pink location label floats on the map with no plate and no shadow. It does not belong to any palette token (the closest is --r-elite) and its contrast against the orange floor is weak.
findings.fix: Set it in --tx-1 at 20px f-cond 700 on a --ui-panel plate with a 4px radius, centred at the same top margin as the timer, or fade it out after 3 seconds.

v.verdict: The raid HUD is clean and its pieces are legible and in the right places, but it has several small stray elements, mixed type and colour, and hp and ammo sit too far apart from each other.

findings.what: Floating panel with tiny, dim 14-16px text. Grey names on dark have weak contrast. The 'value at risk' column is cramped. Its position at y=143 is unaligned with the 5% margin, and it sits against the left edge at x=8. The 'dead' tags are the same grey as the names, so the danger state is not coloured. The panel also introduces a second panel style, a thin border with a black fill, that differs from the other HUD cards.
findings.fix: Set the text to a 16px minimum in --tx-1 (#efe9dc) for 'you' and --tx-2 (#aaa498) for the others. Colour 'dead' --danger (#e5482f). Use the --ui-panel fill and a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 16px padding. Align the left edge to the 5% margin, which is 48px at 1080.

findings.what: The hp bar is a big flat green bar with 'hp 100' in oversized white type. It is heavy, sits tight against the screen corner at x=24 and y=1035 with no margin, and has no panel or rounded treatment. It does not share a style with the ammo card on the right. The text looks like a different, bolder condensed face. The bar is also the loudest saturated fill on screen, ahead of the weapon and the extraction info.
findings.fix: Put hp in the same card style as the ammo (--ui-panel, 1px border, 4px radius). Use a 16px label and a 32px number, and make the bar 12px high. Inset it 48px from the left and bottom.

findings.where: the long dock cache label, top right
findings.what: This lilac text (about #c9a0ff) floats over the map with no backing. It is a purple that is not in the palette (--r-elite is a different purple and means rarity only). It also reads as a decorative world label next to the HUD, and it sits right against the run info bar.
findings.fix: Draw the location name as --tx-1 text with a 1px scrim backing, or fold it into the run info header. Do not use an off-palette purple.

findings.where: extraction indicators (extract 152m at the top, c 152m at the right)
findings.what: The same information is drawn twice: a teal pill at the top centre and another at the right edge, both reading 152m. This is the duplicate-line defect the quiet-HUD order rules out. The right pill is also tiny, with a teal arrow on the map edge.
findings.fix: Keep the single top-centre 'extract 152m' pill. Delete the right-edge 'c 152m' pill, or show only a bare edge arrow with no text.

findings.what: The black bar with a chevron is fine as a collapse control, but its text is tiny and the bar runs flush into the top and right edges (about 12px margin). Its darker fill and 1px border do not match the scoreboard panel's border or the top-centre timer cluster.
findings.fix: Inset to 48px. Use the shared panel token, a 16px label in --tx-1, and a 4px radius.

findings.where: weapon slots 1-0 and the ammo card
findings.what: The slot row has uneven density. The slots 1, 2 and 4 are drawn as filled tiles, while 3 and 5-0 are ghost silhouettes with faint, near-invisible numbers. Slot 2 shows a white fist icon that looks like a pixel icon. The selected slot has an amber border, which is the P1 colour, not lime, so the 'selected' signal is ambiguous. The ammo card shows '12 / 24' in a hero size, but the slash and the 24 are grey, so the card competes with the weapon bar for the eye.
findings.fix: Draw empty slots at one consistent 40% opacity and size or hide them. Pick one selected style: either lime (--acc) as the guide specifies, or P1 amber plus a lime outer bar. Align the ammo card's baseline with the slot row at y=1035 and align the bottom margin to 48px.

findings.where: f1 controls chip, bottom left of slots
findings.what: A tiny chip with a keycap and 'controls' in 16px, sitting at x=437, y=940. It lies on the water-blue map, has weak contrast, and is unanchored: it floats between the hp bar and the slot row rather than lining up with either.
findings.fix: Anchor it to the left bottom margin at x=48, directly above the hp card. Use --tx-2 and a scrim panel.

findings.where: status icons, bottom left (eye-slashed amber circle and green clover circle)
findings.what: Two unlabeled circular icons with no tooltip and a thick ring each, in amber and teal. The amber ring competes with the P1 amber. They are hard to decode, since the clover and the eye mean nothing at a glance.
findings.fix: Shrink them to a uniform 32px, use --ui-panel fills with 1px rings, and use colour only for state (--warn for a warning). Add a 16px label on first display.

v.verdict: The raid HUD is readable and the ammo card is solid. The scoreboard, hp bar, run info and extraction pills still use different panel styles, margins and type sizes, and the earlier fixes were not applied.

findings.what: The hp bar is a bare, saturated green strip with a large 'hp 100' label that is not the Barlow Condensed scale. It touches the bottom edge, sits about 24px from the left, and has no card. It looks like a different game from the ammo card on the right and is the loudest element on the left. The green also competes with the ok colour.
findings.fix: Put hp in a --ui-panel card (1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 16px padding) inset 48px from the left and bottom. Use a 16px 'hp' label and a 32px number in --tx-1. Make the bar 12px high with a muted fill, turning --danger below 30%. Match the ammo card's height.

findings.where: the long dock cache label, top right (1648,150)
findings.what: The location name is off-palette lilac text with no backing. It floats over the map, collides with the building art, and is hard to read. It also adds a second purple, which the guide doesn't allow.
findings.fix: Draw it in --tx-1 at 20px f-cond 600 with a scrim backing (rgba(6,7,8,.8), 8px 16px padding, 4px radius). Or fold it into the run info header. Align its right edge to 48px from the screen edge.

findings.what: The text is 14 to 16px and the 'dead' rows are --tx-2 on a map. Dead is not flagged in --danger. The first row 'you $1,647' has the same weight as the rest. The panel sits at about 8px from the edge, not 48px, and its border and fill differ from the other cards. The header 'current pillagers 0' is crowded against its chevron. It also repeats the footer 'out · dead' counts, so the same information appears twice.
findings.fix: Inset the panel 48px from the left. Use 16px rows with 8px padding and 16px side padding. Show 'you' in --tx-1 and bold, and the others in --tx-2. Colour 'dead' --danger. Drop either the footer counts or the per-row 'dead' tags.

findings.where: extraction indicators (extract 152m at the top centre, c 152m at the right edge)
findings.what: Extraction distance appears twice, in two pill styles with different type sizes. The right-edge 'c 152m' has an unexplained 'c' and sits on the map next to the run info card. The ring arc at the lower right is a third extraction cue with no label.
findings.fix: Keep one top-centre 'extract 152m' pill. Delete the right-edge text pill. If an off-screen cue is needed, use a bare teal arrow at the screen edge with no text.

findings.where: run info bar, top right (1603,18 to 1902,54)
findings.what: The bar is a thin black strip that touches the building and is only about 18px from the edge. It has a different border and radius from the scoreboard and ammo cards. Its 'run info' label is small, and it overlaps the building wall.
findings.fix: Inset it 48px from the top and right. Use the shared panel token (--ui-panel, 1px --ui-line-hi, 4px radius) with a 16px label in --tx-1 and a 32px height. Keep it the same width as the other top cards.

findings.what: Slot numbers 3, 5 to 0 and the ghost weapon silhouettes are faint and noisy next to the three filled slots. The selected slot has an amber border, but the guide says lime is the 'selected' colour. The amber also matches the P1 ring, which makes it ambiguous.
findings.fix: Hide the empty slot numbers and silhouettes, or lower them to 25% opacity with no numbers. Use a 2px --acc border for the selected slot. Make the slot number labels 16px in --tx-2.

findings.what: The ammo card is the best-built element, with a clear hero number. However it sits about 10px from the right and bottom edges, not 48px. The 'b / i backpack' hint is 14px and near the floor of legibility. The slash and max (24) are the same weight as the current count.
findings.fix: Inset the card 48px from the right and bottom. Set the hint to 16px in --tx-2. Make '/ 24' 32px in --tx-2 so 12 is the hero.

findings.where: status icons (bottom left, 24,940) and 'f1 controls' chip
findings.what: The two round icons use amber and teal rings with no labels, which makes their meaning unclear. They sit tight against the hp bar. The 'f1 controls' chip floats mid-screen over the building art and is smaller than 16px.
findings.fix: Put the icons in the hp card row with 8px gaps and 32px diameter. Make the f1 controls chip 16px in --tx-2 on a --ui-panel backing, aligned to the 48px left margin.

v.verdict: The in-raid HUD is readable and mostly lower case, but the edge-hugging panels, the unpanelled hp bar and the doubled extraction cues are the same problems as last review, and none of them has been fixed.

findings.what: The hp bar is a raw green slab with big text jammed against the bottom edge. It has no panel, no inset and no label hierarchy. It is the loudest colour on screen and sits right next to the quiet ammo card.
findings.fix: Put hp in a --ui-panel card (1px --ui-line-hi, 4px radius, 16px padding) inset 48px from the left and bottom. Use a 16px 'hp' label and a 32px --tx-1 number. Make the bar 12px high with a muted fill, turning --danger below 30%. Match the ammo card's height.

findings.what: The panel sits 8px from the screen edge, which breaks the 48px margin. All rows are the same weight, 'you' is not set apart, and the rows are crowded. Both the per-row 'dead' tags and the footer '0 out · 3 dead' say the same thing.
findings.fix: Inset the panel 48px. Use 16px rows with 8px row padding and 16px side padding. Show 'you' in --tx-1 weight 700 and the others in --tx-2. Colour 'dead' --danger. Delete the footer counts.

findings.where: extraction cues, top centre (960,60) and right edge (1823,487)
findings.what: Extraction is shown twice, as 'extract 152m' and as 'c 152m'. The 'c' prefix is cryptic. The right pill is a different size and style from the top one.
findings.fix: Keep one top-centre 'extract 152m' pill in --extract. Delete the right-edge text pill and keep only a bare teal arrow on the screen edge, with no text.

findings.where: 'the long dock cache' label, top right (1648,150)
findings.what: The label is lavender text floating over the map with no backing. It is hard to read against the busy art and it uses a colour that is not in the palette.
findings.fix: Draw it in --tx-1 at 20px f-cond 600 on a scrim backing (rgba(6,7,8,.8), 8px 16px padding, 4px radius). Right-align it to 48px from the screen edge, or fold it into the run info header.

findings.where: run info bar, top right (1603,18 to 1902,54)
findings.what: The bar is flush to the top and right edges, clipped by the screen, with a chevron and a flat dark fill. It does not match the scoreboard panel's border or its inset.
findings.fix: Inset it 48px from the top and right. Use the shared panel token (--ui-panel, 1px --ui-line-hi, 4px radius) with a 16px --tx-1 label and a 32px height. Make the left and right cards the same width.

findings.where: bandage tip and f1 controls hint (x16,y789 and x435,y940)
findings.what: Two small pills sit at random positions with different styles, and the controls hint floats over the map above the weapon bar. The controls hint is 16px or smaller with low contrast.
findings.fix: Put both on the same 16px label style and the same panel token. Anchor the controls hint to the bottom-left list position with a 48px inset, and stack the bandage tip above the hp card.

findings.where: weapon slot bar, bottom centre (555,957 to 1100,1060)
findings.what: The empty slots 3 and 5 to 0 are faint ghost icons with floating digits and no tile outline. The row looks unfinished, and the bar sits 20px from the bottom edge.
findings.fix: Draw empty slots as 100px tiles with a 1px --ui-line border and a 16px --tx-2 number. Lift the bar to a 48px bottom inset. Only the selected slot keeps --acc.

findings.what: The card is 10px from the right edge, so its inset does not match the other HUD elements. The '12 / 24' hero number is good, but 'b / i backpack' at 14px is below the 16px label floor.
findings.fix: Inset it 48px from the right and bottom. Raise the 'b / i backpack' hint to 16px --tx-2. Keep the 56px hero number.

v.verdict: This is a blank dark screen with only a tiny money, xp and stash readout in the top-right corner. The preraid zones screen (zone picker, title, actions) is missing or failed to render.

findings.what: The screenshot named preraid-zones shows no zones, no title, no cards, no primary action and no back/close control. About 99% of the frame is empty #0b0c0d. The player has nothing to select and no way to continue.
findings.fix: Render the zone picker: a 90% centred card with a 32px title, 3 to 5 zone rows or tiles, a lime-filled primary 'deploy' button, and an x in the card corner. If the screen is meant to be there, fix the capture timing or the render failure.

findings.what: No element is focused or selected, so there is no lime focus bar or highlighted row. A pad player would not know where they are.
findings.fix: Default focus to the first available zone. Give it a 2px --acc outline or a --ui-raised fill with a 4px lime left bar.

findings.what: Three groups sit in a single row with uneven spacing: '$900' at about 28px, '0' beside a tiny 'xp', and the stash and bag line at about 13px. The style guide asks for a vertical 1x1 list of equal-size items in this corner. The stash and bag text is under the 16px minimum for anything read. The '0' and 'xp' have no clear relationship, since xp is a tiny suffix on a large digit. With no screen below it, nothing explains the numbers.
findings.fix: Stack the items vertically, each at 20px f-cond 600 with a 16px label in tx-2. Use equal 8px row gaps, right-aligned to a 5% margin (96px from the right, 54px from the top). Raise the stash and bag text to at least 16px.

findings.what: The eye lands on '$900' in the corner because it is the only thing on screen. It is not the hero number and it is not the primary action, so hierarchy has failed.
findings.fix: Put a 32px screen title and a 56px hero element, such as the selected zone's payout or risk, in the card centre. Shrink the currency readout to 20px.

findings.what: A 1px light border or stroke shows around the whole frame. It is not part of any token (--ui-line is #2e3337), and it looks like a capture artifact.
findings.fix: Remove the stray outline, or use --ui-line at 1px on a panel border and nowhere else.

findings.what: Nothing in the frame says Pillagers or ARC Raiders x Zero Sievert: no map, no atmosphere, no accent, no panel. The lime accent appears nowhere.
findings.fix: Put a darkened map or terrain plate behind the card under the --scrim at 80%. Use lime only on the focused zone and the deploy button.

v.verdict: The hub reads as a busy sandbox with many same-weight tooltip chips, a hard-to-read top-right money readout and off-spec text, so it is not yet a polished, consistent menu.

findings.where: top-right currency row ($900, 0 xp, stash $3,916 bag $0)
findings.what: Three different type sizes and weights sit in one row, and the 'stash $3,916 bag $0' text is tiny, about 14px, and runs against the screen edge with no panel behind it. It sits over a dark void and the arena edge, so its contrast and grouping are inconsistent. It also breaks the guide's 'every item the same size' rule for the top-right list.
findings.fix: Put the money, xp and stash values in one top-right panel with 24px padding. Give them one size (--fs-body 20px, f-cond 600) and stack them 1 by 1. Use tx-1 for values and tx-2 at 16px for labels. Put the panel at x=1920-48 and y=48.

findings.what: The 56px-plus lime label with an exclamation mark is the loudest thing on screen, but it floats on a plain dark chip with no focus ring and no key hint. It is a different size and treatment from every other station label, and it sits under the lime/amber 'selected' semantics. It also has a retail-exclamation tone that clashes with the straight-copy rule.
findings.fix: Set it to --fs-title 32px f-cond 700 in --acc on --ui-panel. Drop the '!' (use 'enter raid'). Add a 3px lime underline bar and an 'e' key chip in 16px below it. Keep the other labels at 20px tx-1.

findings.where: the last pour label and '***experimental feature may glitch***' tag
findings.what: The warning tag is a second chip stuck directly under the station label with a 3-asterisk wrapper, orange text about 14px, and a wide box that nearly touches the label above. It reads as a hack and as an explaining sentence, and it sits on top of the character's head.
findings.fix: Remove the asterisks and shorten to 'experimental'. Render it as a 16px --warn word with a 1px --warn border chip, 8px below the label, aligned to the label's width. Or move it into the interaction prompt shown only when the player is in range.

findings.where: bottom centre stack: toast, controls list, hotbar
findings.what: Three stacked chips (a welcome-pack toast, the key legend and the 9-slot hotbar) are of different widths, each with its own border and fill, and they crowd within about 12px of each other. The toast overlaps the 'the stash' station, and the legend at about 14px is below the 16px floor, with 'wasd walk' and similar text in muted grey.
findings.fix: Use one shared 16px gap between the three. Set the legend text to 16px with tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better, and align it to the hotbar's width (x 455 to 1465). Move the toast above the stash label (or top-centre) so it stops covering the station. Drop the toast to a single short line.

findings.where: station labels (wirt the gambler, the mainframe, shop craft and hire, settings, the stash, fashion)
findings.what: Every station label is the same dark rounded chip at the same weight, with no icon or sign of which station is nearest or focused. Their baselines are inconsistent: the labels sit at different heights above their pads, and 'fashion' overlaps a character and the pad ring. The identical-chip look is the template tell the guide warns about.
findings.fix: Give all labels one 20px f-cond 600 style and a fixed 8px offset above the pad. On proximity, grow the active one to 32px and add a lime 3px bar, and dim the rest to tx-2. Move 'fashion' clear of the characters by 16px.

findings.where: large translucent circles on the floor
findings.what: The grey, teal, purple and brown discs behind each station overlap each other (the mainframe and enter-raid circles, the centre circle) and muddy the floor with washed colour blobs. They compete with the lime accent and with the characters and add no hierarchy.
findings.fix: Limit it to one 2px ring per station at 30% opacity in the station colour, and drop the large fills. Show the filled disc only for the station in range, at 12% opacity.

findings.what: The title (about 28px) and the subline '7 items in stash · 0 runs' (about 14px) are in a small panel at x=81, which is not on the 5% (96px) margin and is not aligned with the currency panel at the top right. The subline is below the 16px floor and is a status sentence the screen does not need.
findings.fix: Move the panel to x=96, y=48, and set the title to 32px and the subline to 16px tx-2. Use the same panel fill, border and 8px padding as the top-right panel. Cut 'runs' if the number is not needed.

findings.where: overall scene: 14 characters in the lobby
findings.what: Many identical-scale characters scatter across the floor with no lead, so the eye has no start point. The black bars at the left and right edges and the grey frame look unfinished, and the pad focus state is not visible for a couch player.
findings.fix: Fill or mask the letterbox bars with --ui-void and a 1px --ui-line border. Add a lime focus ring (3px) and a key chip on the nearest pad, and dim the other stations to 70% opacity.

v.verdict: The screen now renders as a proper 90% card with a title, an x, a map, option columns and a lime ascend button, but three columns share the same visual weight and the small text is too small for a couch.

findings.what: The map, the conditions list, and the kit and pack panel are all dense and similar in weight, so the eye lands on the lime ascend button and then wanders. The 'cold storage' title is only 24px and sits in a sub-header, not as the screen title.
findings.fix: Keep the 32px 'pre-raid' title. Make 'cold storage' the 32px zone name in tx-1 and demote the stats line to 16px tx-2. Add a 2px --ui-line-hi border to the map panel. Give conditions and kit the same 16px label style and 16px column gaps.

findings.where: small text: 'no armour equipped', belt numbers 1-0, '/1', zone labels, map room labels
findings.what: These are about 12-14px, below the 16px minimum for anything read. The warning is orange text at about 13px beside a tiny glyph, and the belt boxes are about 30px with faint digits. Neither is readable from a couch.
findings.fix: Set all of these to 16px f-cond 600. Make the belt slots 40px with 16px digits in tx-2. Make the warning 16px --warn with a 24px glyph, and move it directly above the ascend button with an 8px gap.

findings.what: The prices are red ($2,340, $2,760) in a tiny font next to bold '$660' in white. Red here reads as 'cannot afford', which is accurate, but it is mixed with unlabelled blank cells for smoke canister and burst carbine. The price column therefore has three states with no explanation, and the rows have thin dividers and cramped 0/-/+ steppers.
findings.fix: Use one price style: 16px right-aligned, tx-1 when affordable and --danger when not. Show 'free' or a dash in the blank cells. Make the steppers 40px square with 8px gaps and add 12px more row height.

findings.what: The surface, weather and seed lists are 5 to 8 stacked rows with identical weight, and the '+5% sp' tags are small and low-contrast. Selected rows use a lime check, but the faint outline on the selected row is hard to tell from the idle rows.
findings.fix: Give the selected row a --ui-raised fill with a 4px --acc left bar. Raise the '+5% sp' tags to 16px --warn. Group the rows under 16px tx-2 labels with 24px between groups.

findings.what: The map is a blue-tinted panel with dark-navy room boxes that have no labels. It is the largest area, but its low-contrast blue-on-blue reads as a placeholder next to the neutral grey UI panels. Exit markers in teal are fine, but the purple dashed squares are unexplained.
findings.fix: Dim the room fills to --ui-panel and the map tint to 8% opacity, and draw walls at 1px --ui-line-hi. Keep the teal exits. Add a 16px legend for the purple squares, or remove them.

findings.what: The 'esc close' and 'click pick' key hints at the bottom are small, and a stray 1px outline runs around the whole screen outside the card. The card border is a hard line with no scrim falloff.
findings.fix: Set the key hints to 16px with 32px-tall keycaps. Remove the outer screen outline. Use a --scrim backdrop and a 1px --ui-line-hi card border at 4px radius.

findings.what: The lime button is correct as the single main action, but its label is very large and spaced out, it is bigger than the 32px title, and the 'enter' keycap inside it is tiny. The button fights the title instead of leaving boldness to one place.
findings.fix: Set the label to 32px f-cond 800 with no extra letter-spacing. Set the 'enter' hint to 16px on an --acc-ink chip. Keep the button 64px tall and add --acc-hover and --acc-press states.

v.verdict: The old world-space station-label screen is now a proper centred pre-raid card with an x, one lime primary button and clear columns, but it is crowded, the type sizes are too small and uneven, and the map is an empty-looking block of boxes.

findings.where: pack list rows (medkit to compact smg), prices, belt, no-armour warning
findings.what: Much of the text is below the 16px floor: the price chips (about 13px, red on dark), the '/1' column, the belt digits, 'no armour equipped' (about 13px amber) and the 'pack 0 packed' label. The red prices read as errors instead of costs, and the red is too dim against the panel.
findings.fix: Set every row value to 16px minimum and row names to 20px. Show prices in tx-1 at 16px. Use --danger only on the one row the player cannot afford, and put a 'cannot afford' state on that row instead of colouring the whole column. Set the warning to 16px --warn.

findings.where: right column (kit, pack, belt, warning, ascend)
findings.what: The column is crowded. Kit cards, a 7-row stepper table with its own scrollbar, a belt strip, a warning and the CTA are stacked with uneven gaps (about 8 to 40px). The '+ / - / 0' steppers and price boxes are cramped boxes with different border weights. Scroll is hidden in the pack list.
findings.fix: Use 16px gaps between sections and one row height of 48px. Make the steppers 40x40 with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Make the price column a fixed 96px, right-aligned. Move the belt into its own pane or collapse it. Keep the scrollbar but pad it 8px from the price column.

findings.where: map zone labels (the long dock, packing floor, chill row, scrap line, the sump)
findings.what: Zone names are bold white f-cond over the blue map at mixed sizes (about 18 to 24px), with no backing. 'foreman office' and 'blast freezer' (about 14px) sit tight against their purple dashed boxes, and 'the long dock' overlaps a room outline. The big zone rectangles are empty dark boxes, so the map reads as an unfinished wireframe.
findings.fix: Use one label style: 20px f-cond 600 tx-1 on a --scrim pill with 8px padding, placed 8px clear of any outline. Put the 14px keyed-room labels on the same pill style at 16px. Fill the room boxes with a --ui-raised tint at 40% and add small loot or door glyphs so they are not blank.

findings.where: header and subheader ('pre-raid', 'cold storage', 'ascending here', stat line)
findings.what: There are three competing titles. 'pre-raid' is about 28px, 'cold storage' about 24px, and the 'ascending here' chip carries a tick and a border while the stat line (420 x 340 m ...) is a 16px tx-2 row on the far right at low contrast. The hierarchy is muddled and nothing is the hero.
findings.fix: Make 'pre-raid' the 32px f-cond 700 title. Make 'cold storage' 20px tx-1 as the subtitle. Fold the stat line into a 16px tx-2 line directly under the subtitle on the left, and make 'ascending here' a quiet 16px label with no border.

findings.what: The radio rows use two different selected treatments: a lime tick in a circle plus a raised fill, with no lime bar and a faint border. '+5% sp' is tx-2 at about 16px and low contrast. Section labels (conditions, surface, weather, seed) are about 15px, close to the row text in size and weight, so the groups do not separate.
findings.fix: Give the selected row a 3px --acc left bar plus a --ui-raised fill, and give idle rows a 1px --ui-line border. Set group labels to 16px tx-2 with +.04em tracking and a 24px top gap. Set '+5% sp' to tx-1 at 16px.

findings.what: This is the right primary action, but the 'enter' key chip is about 14px and sits on lime in a dark box that is hard to read. The word 'ascend' uses a heavier, wider face than the rest of the UI, with letter-spacing that looks different from the title type.
findings.fix: Set 'ascend' in f-cond 800 at 32px with the same tracking as the titles. Make the key chip 16px, --acc-ink on a 1px --acc-ink border with no dark fill, aligned 24px from the right edge. Keep the button at 64px high.

findings.where: footer legend (esc close, click pick) and x button
findings.what: The footer legend is about 16px and left-aligned, but it is separated from the card edge by a thin rule and sits very low (y about 990). The x is a 48px box with a heavy white border that is brighter than anything else in the header.
findings.fix: Set the legend in 16px tx-2 with the chips at 24px high, 24px from the bottom edge. Make the x border 1px --ui-line-hi, and show a lime border only on focus.

findings.what: The outer area is a near-black void with only a faint card edge and no scrim difference, so the card does not lift. The card is also about 90% wide, as ordered, but the bottom gutter (about 55px) is larger than the top and side gutters.
findings.fix: Use --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.80) over the dimmed world, give the card a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius, and make the gutters 5% on every side.

v.verdict: The screen is coherent and lower case, and the lime 'ascend' button reads clearly as the primary action. But the map is a flat grid of empty dark boxes that fills the largest area, and the three columns are crowded with small, low-contrast text and uneven type sizes.

findings.where: map panel (left, about 65% of the card)
findings.what: The map is the largest element, so the eye goes there first. It shows only identical empty dark rectangles with thin outlines. It carries no information or art, and the lime button is the only competing focal point.
findings.fix: Put loot, spawn and tier markers or room fills on the map. Otherwise shrink the map to about 50% of the card width and give the freed space to conditions and kit. Cut the rectangle outline opacity by about 40% so the exit markers and zone names carry the map.

findings.where: map zone labels (the long dock, foreman office, blast freezer, chill row, scrap line)
findings.what: The labels are a dark-outlined white condensed face at about 16px, and they overlap or touch rectangle borders. 'foreman office' runs into its box edge and 'blast freezer' butts against the purple marker. They look pasted on and are not set in the same type as the rest of the UI.
findings.fix: Set labels in f-cond 600 at 16px with a 4px padding plate, fill --ui-panel at 80%. Keep at least 8px clear of every box edge and marker, and stop using the outline stroke.

findings.what: The rows are dense, with a 12px gap between the stepper and the price. Prices are small red or white 14px text with no pattern (red where unaffordable, white for $660, blank for the rest). The '/1' cap is faint, and the empty price cells on smoke canister and burst carbine look broken. A scrollbar is jammed against the price column.
findings.fix: Use a fixed 5-column grid: name, cap, stepper, price. Right-align every price at 16px, and show '$0' or a dash when there is no price. Give the stepper buttons 32px hit targets, raise the '/1' to --tx-2 at 16px, and add 8px padding before the scrollbar.

findings.what: Section labels (conditions, surface, weather, seed, kit, pack, belt) are about 14-16px, muted, and hard to tell apart from the row text. 'conditions' and 'surface' stack with no hierarchy. The belt numbers and the keycap hints are about 12px, under the 16px floor. The 'no armour equipped' warning is about 13px.
findings.fix: Give all section labels one style: f-cond 700 at 16px, +.04em, --tx-2. Make 'conditions' a header and drop 'surface' to a plain sub-label. Raise the belt numerals and the warning text to 16px minimum, and the esc/click keycaps to 16px.

findings.what: The title 'pre-raid' is smaller than the 32px spec and sits close to the top edge. The 'cold storage' sub-title is almost the same size, so the two titles compete. The footer legend (esc close, click pick) is small and floats alone with a large empty band beside it.
findings.fix: Make 'pre-raid' 32px f-cond 700 and 'cold storage' 20px with --tx-1. Raise the footer legend to 16px and align it to the 24px inner margin. Reduce the bottom empty band.

findings.what: Lime is used for the check circles, the left bars on selected rows and the button, which is correct. But the kit tile 'my loadout' and the conditions rows use the same raised fill and border as the idle tiles, so selection depends only on a small check. The lime bar on the green-barred pack rows (rarity) is the same hue family and reads as the same signal.
findings.fix: Give a selected row a 2px --acc border and a --ui-raised fill, and leave unselected rows with a --ui-line border. Change the pack-row rarity bars to 3px and keep them out of lime-adjacent greens, or move them to the right of the icon.

findings.what: The lime fill is strong, but the label 'ascend' is in a wide, letter-spaced face that doesn't match the condensed UI type. The 'enter' keycap sits tight to the right edge. The button is jammed 16px under the warning row with no breathing room.
findings.fix: Set 'ascend' in f-cond 800 at 32px, left-aligned with 24px padding. Put an 8px inset on the 'enter' key hint, and add 24px of space above the button.

findings.what: The scrim is almost black with no visible content behind it, and the card has a thin border and nearly square 2px corners. The close x is a heavy outlined square that looks different from the other controls.
findings.fix: Use a 4px radius on the card and controls. Draw the x at 40px with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, matching the other icon buttons.

v.verdict: The pre-raid card has a clear hierarchy, with the lime ascend button as the main action. The map is still a big empty blueprint with clashing labels, and the right column is crowded and uses too many small sizes.

findings.where: map panel (left, about 65% of the card)
findings.what: The map is still mostly empty dark rectangles with no loot, spawn or tier markers. The room outlines are bright and compete with the exit markers. This was flagged last time and not fixed.
findings.fix: Cut the outline opacity by about 40%, or put real content in the rooms (loot tiers, spawns). If not, shrink the map to about 50% of the card width and give the freed 15% to the conditions and kit columns.

findings.where: map zone labels (the long dock, foreman office, blast freezer, packing floor, chill row, the sump, scrap line)
findings.what: The labels are white with a dark outline and no plate. 'the long dock' sits on the top edge. 'foreman office' and 'blast freezer' touch the purple markers and room edges. The labels have different sizes and offsets.
findings.fix: Use f-cond 600 at 16px in --tx-1 on a plate with 4px padding and --ui-panel at 80% fill. Keep 8px clear of every edge and marker, and anchor all labels the same way (centred in the room). Remove the text stroke.

findings.what: Prices are 14px bold in red-outlined boxes, and the red outline reads as 'cannot afford' or danger on most rows. Some rows show '-' and some show a price, so the right edge is ragged. The '/1' is tiny and dim. The stepper buttons are about 28px and tight against the scrollbar.
findings.fix: Use one price style: right-aligned, 16px f-cond 600. Use --tx-1 when affordable and --danger text with no box when not. Show '$0' or a dash in a fixed-width cell. Raise '/1' to 16px in --tx-2. Make the stepper buttons 32px and leave 12px before the scrollbar.

findings.where: type scale across the card (section labels, belt, warning, keycaps)
findings.what: The section labels kit, conditions, surface, weather, seed, pack and belt use mixed sizes and weights. The belt numerals, the warning text 'no armour equipped' and the esc/click keycaps are about 12-14px, below the 16px floor. The belt slots are dim and nearly invisible.
findings.fix: Set all section labels to f-cond 700 at 16px, +.04em, --tx-2. Set the belt numerals, the warning text and the keycaps to 16px minimum. Raise belt slot borders to --ui-line-hi and size the slots to 40px.

findings.where: header row (pre-raid, cold storage, ascending here chip, stats line)
findings.what: 'pre-raid' at about 28px and 'cold storage' at about 24px are nearly the same size, so there is no clear title. The stats line is crammed against the right edge, and the checked 'ascending here' chip looks like a selected option.
findings.fix: Set 'pre-raid' to 32px f-cond 700 and 'cold storage' to 20px. Right-align the stats line at 16px in --tx-2 with a 24px inner margin. Turn the chip into plain text with a check glyph, or drop the check.

findings.what: Row heights are tight, at about 38-40px with 3-4px gaps. The 'daily raid 10-28' seed row sits in its own section with a big empty gap beneath it. Extra '+5% sp' text repeats on 4 rows.
findings.fix: Use a 44px row with an 8px gap. Merge seed into the weather block as a final row, or add 24px spacing under it. Show '+5% sp' once as a column header, or only on the focused row.

findings.what: The warning line sits right above the button in tiny amber text and the button is very tall and heavy. The 'enter' keycap inside it is tiny and low contrast. The button's text is also heavier than the card title.
findings.fix: Make the button 56px high with 32px f-cond 700 text. Make the 'enter' keycap 16px in --acc-ink on a 20% black plate. Raise the warning to 16px with 16px of space above it.

findings.what: The legend is small, about 14px, and sits at the bottom edge with an empty band below it inside the card. Its left edge is not aligned to the card's inner margin.
findings.fix: Set the legend to 16px, align it to the 24px inner margin, and cut the bottom padding to 16px.

v.verdict: A busy raid HUD with several working parts, but the clustered top-centre stack, the clipped objective label, the muddled hp bar and the lack of any clear hierarchy keep it at amateur level.

findings.where: right edge, 'the long dock cache' label under the 'c 151m' chip
findings.what: The objective name is cut through by the 'c 151m' chip and its arrow, so the text is overprinted and unreadable. Its purple text also sits directly on the busy map. The chip's abbreviated 'c' is cryptic.
findings.fix: Stack the chip and the name in one panel (--ui-panel at 80% fill, 8px padding). Put the name at 16px tx-1 on its own line, 8px below the chip. Spell out 'cache 151m' or drop the 'c'. Keep the purple only as a 3px rarity bar.

findings.where: top-centre stack: timer, team score, extract chip
findings.what: Three differently styled boxes are stacked and touch each other. The timer is a pill, the score is a larger dark panel, and the extract chip has a teal outline and its own radius. The score panel is glued under the timer and runs into the extract chip. 'you 0 sp' and 'p2 0 sp' are crammed against the right edge of the panel and misaligned with the big '0 sp'. The teal arrow floats loose.
findings.fix: Use one panel (--ui-panel, 4px radius) with 16px padding, and leave an 8px gap between rows. Make the timer the only hero element (56px). Show the team score at 20px and the per-player scores as 16px tx-2 on one row. Put the extract chip in the same panel as a teal 16px line. Align every row to a common centre line.

findings.what: 'hp 81' is drawn at about 32px over a green bar. The red '-6' damage chunk is a second, saturated fill that clashes with it, and the text sits directly on the bar with no padding. Green is an odd choice against the lime accent and is not in the palette. The bar is flush with the screen edge and the 'f1 controls' hint above it is tiny and low contrast.
findings.fix: Use a 12px tall bar inset 5% from the edge. Fill it with --ok or a tx-1 fill, put the damage chunk in --danger at 60% opacity, and put 'hp 81' at 20px tx-1 above the bar rather than on top of it. Raise the f1 hint to 16px with a 1px --ui-line-hi chip border.

findings.what: Slot numbers 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9 and 0 float with no tiles, so the empty slots read as stray digits over the map. Only the two filled slots have a frame, and the 'f' badge on slot 1 is unexplained. The slot-2 icon is a red glyph in an unframed tile and is hard to read. The selected slot has a gold border, which is too close to the lime accent and to rarity gold.
findings.fix: Draw every slot as a 56px tile with --ui-panel at 70% fill and a 1px --ui-line border, 8px apart. Show empty slots at 40% opacity. Use a 2px --acc border for the selected slot only. Make the number labels 14-16px tx-2, aligned top-left inside the tile.

findings.what: The panel is a rounded dark box in a different style from the top-centre panels. 'riot scattergun' is at about 28px, which competes with the 7/42 numbers, and the greyed weapon silhouette is nearly invisible. The '7' is hero-sized but the '/ 42' is at a similar weight. It is also not aligned to the screen margin used by 'goals' and the hotbar.
findings.fix: Share one panel style with the other HUD boxes (same fill, 4px radius, 16px padding). Set the weapon name at 20px tx-2 and '7' at 56px 800 tx-1 with '/ 42' at 20px tx-2. Align the panel right edge to the same 5% margin as 'goals 0/3'.

findings.what: The bar sits at the screen edge with a tiny teal line and no 'p2' hp number. Cyan and the amber of P1 are meant to be the player colours, but the P2 tag in the world is cyan on blue-grey ground and has very low contrast. The 'player 2' world label overlaps the character.
findings.fix: Add a 1px dark outline or a 60% scrim chip behind the world label, and lift it 8px above the head. Align the left-edge P2 card to the 5% margin and give it the shared panel style.

findings.what: It uses a boxy 4px-radius dropdown with a chevron and its own fill, and it does not match the timer pill. It sits at the edge with only about 20px of margin. The top-right area is meant to be a vertical 1 by 1 list.
findings.fix: Use the shared panel style at 20px text. Move it 5% (96px) in from the right edge, matching the top-right list rule.

findings.what: The toast is a black rectangle with a different fill, a sharp corner and a 16px font, floating in the middle of the lower map with no connection to the feed. The 'keyboard' chip at top-left is a green-on-dark label in a third style.
findings.fix: Send the toast to the left feed at the same panel style, and restyle the 'keyboard' chip as a 14px tx-2 label in a --ui-panel chip. Both should use the 4px radius.

v.verdict: The HUD is a coherent dark-panel set in lower case with a clear ammo hero number, but it is crowded and uneven, with several small labels, too many different sizes, and a score block that contradicts itself.

findings.what: The panel stacks 'team score', a large '0 sp', and 'you 0 sp / p1 0 sp'. The same number is shown three times at three different sizes. The right column is small, so the panel feels crowded. It also has a different width and padding from the timer card above it and the extract chip below it, so three stacked boxes have three different edges.
findings.fix: Drop to a single line per player or show the team total only. Make all three boxes one width (about 270px) with 16px padding, a 4px radius, and 8px gaps. Set the labels to 16px f-cond and the total to the 56px hero or 32px title size.

findings.what: The 'hp 81' label is 32px or more and sits inside a bright green bar. The '-6' damage chunk is red and brighter than the bar itself. The bar is flush against the screen edge, with no 5% margin and no panel, so it matches none of the other HUD cards. The green-on-green label has low contrast.
findings.fix: Put the hp bar in a --ui-panel card inset 48px from the edge. Use 20px f-cond label text in tx-1 on the dark panel, a 12px bar, and 16px for the '-6'. Keep the red only for the damage chunk.

findings.where: weapon slots 1-3 and the empty slots 4-8 (bottom centre)
findings.what: Slots 1 to 3 are tiles, but slots 4 to 8 are bare digits floating over the building wall with ghosted gun icons behind them. The digits and the dim icons are low contrast over the busy terrain, so the row looks unfinished. The tile layout is also off: the 'f' badge on slot 1 collides with the gun icon, and the '180' ammo labels are tiny.
findings.fix: Render the empty slots as real 56px panel tiles at 40% opacity with a 1px --ui-line border, or hide them. Move the 'f' badge to the top-right corner. Set the ammo count to 16px minimum and 600 weight.

findings.where: player 1 tag (top left) and the in-world 'player 1' label
findings.what: There are two different treatments for the same player. The top-left tag is a flat blue bar in 20px with a cyan bar below it. The in-world label is a small blue chip. Blue/cyan is used here, but the style guide says P1 is amber and P2 is cyan, so the P1 colours are wrong. The top-left tag is also flush against the corner with no margin.
findings.fix: Use amber for P1 in both the tag and the world label, and cyan for P2. Place the tag at 48px/48px inside a panel with the same style as the HUD cards, and make the world label a 16px chip.

findings.where: 'in pillager's party' toast (bottom centre) and 'f1 controls' hint
findings.what: The 'in pillager's party' toast is a black rectangle with 14px text sitting on the building wall at an arbitrary place, with a square corner and a different fill from the HUD cards. The 'f1 controls' hint is at a third size and position, with its own key-cap style. Both are small and low contrast against the world art.
findings.fix: Use the standard panel fill (--ui-panel at 90%), a 4px radius, and 16px label text. Align the hint to the same left edge as the hp card, and put the toast above the weapon row with a 16px gap.

findings.what: The teal 'extract 147m' chip is tight, with about 8px of padding and 20px text. The teal arrow below it floats in the world with no link to the chip and sits on top of the terrain. It is correctly teal, but it is small and easy to lose.
findings.fix: Put the arrow inside the chip row, or enlarge it to 24px with a dark outline. Use 16px side padding on the chip.

findings.where: ammo card (bottom right) vs. the other cards
findings.what: The ammo card is the strongest element, with a 56px hero '30', but it has a large 160px by 150px footprint and a thin border that no other card shares. 'compact smg' is right-aligned while '30 / 180' has the slash baseline lower. The card is crowded against the screen's right and bottom edges.
findings.fix: Inset the card 48px from the edges and use the same 1px --ui-line-hi border on every card. Align the baselines of '30' and '/ 180', and set '/ 180' at 32px in tx-2.

findings.what: The red '18' has a ring around it that overlaps the enemy sprite and obscures it. The 'keyboard' badge at the top left is a tiny green chip, with a different style from the other chips, and it reads as debug text.
findings.fix: Offset the damage number 24px above the target, and drop the ring or reduce it to 1px. Restyle the badge as the standard 16px label chip, or hide it outside the debug view.

v.verdict: The HUD is readable in the corners, but the damage numbers overlap the enemy label into an unreadable pile, the ammo readout contradicts itself, and the panels, type sizes and slot states don't follow one system.

findings.where: enemy at centre, 'sen_r-64' tag with '96' damage number and 'weak spot 2.0x'
findings.what: The big cyan '96' damage number is drawn on top of the enemy name tag and cuts it to 'sen96r-64'. The 'weak spot 2.0x' chip sits directly under it and hides the health bar and the enemy sprite. This is the screen's focal point and the text is a pile.
findings.fix: Float damage numbers up 40-60px from the hit point and fade them. Keep the name tag fixed 24px above the enemy head. Move the 'weak spot 2.0x' text into the number as a 16px suffix. Never let the number overlap the tag.

findings.what: The current ammo (60) is larger than the reserve (42), which looks like a bug or a mismatched label. The hero number is 56px+ and competes with the timer. The card is wide and mostly empty, and 'support mg' is small and right-aligned against the number.
findings.fix: Show magazine / reserve in the correct order. Set the hero to 56px f-cond 800 in tx-1 with the reserve at 32px tx-2. Shrink the card to fit the content with 16px padding.

findings.where: hotbar, slots 1-2, 3-5 and 7-0, and the selected slot 6
findings.what: Slots 1 and 2 are filled panels, slots 3-5 and 7-0 are bare numbers floating over the terrain, and the selected slot 6 is an empty box with a thick yellow ring. The selected slot looks like the empty one, and the weapon you are actually holding (support mg) has no highlight. The bare numbers are low contrast on the sand.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots as 56px tiles with --ui-panel fill and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Mark the equipped slot with a 2px --acc border and put the weapon icon in it. Dim empty slots to 40% opacity. Align the numbers inside the tiles at 16px.

findings.what: Three boxes with different widths, corner radii and paddings are stacked and touch each other. The timer is 10:00 in a large font, the weather icon is a separate floating circle, and 'team score' and 'you / p2' are split across two type sizes. It is crowded and the score is less important than the timer, yet it takes more area.
findings.fix: Use one 4px-radius panel column at 8px gaps. Put the timer at 32px and the score at 20px, with you / p2 on one 16px line in amber and cyan. Fold the weather icon into the timer panel. Centre-align all three to the same width.

findings.where: player 2 bars, top-left (16,325) and over the character
findings.what: Player 2 is shown twice: once as a blue/green bar fragment at the top-left that reads as unfinished and is 150px away from everything else, and again as an in-world tag. The cyan name has low contrast on the blue-grey ground, and the bar has no hp number.
findings.fix: Remove one of them. Dock the P2 card under the P1 hp bar at bottom-left with the same 16px label and bar style, in cyan. Give the in-world tag a --scrim backing.

findings.what: The hp bar is a saturated flat green fill with oversized 'hp 100' text clipped to the left edge of the screen with ~20px margin, against the 5% rule. The 'f1 controls' chip is a different style (dark pill with key cap) and sits 100px above, floating on the terrain.
findings.fix: Inset the hp bar to 48px margin, set the label to 20px f-cond 600, and use --ok at a lower fill. Move 'f1 controls' into the mid-bottom-left line as a 16px legend with a 1px border panel.

findings.what: The goals bar is a wide, empty panel with a chevron and a 20px label, and its border and radius do not match the centre panels. The 'keyboard' tag is a tiny green-outlined box that does not match any other chip, and its text is 16px at the very edge.
findings.fix: Shrink the goals panel to content width, 4px radius, --ui-line-hi border, the same fill as the other panels. Restyle 'keyboard' as a --fs-fine legend with a --ui-panel fill and 48px margin.

findings.what: 'scrap line' is wide-tracked grey text laid on the road that nearly vanishes against the ground. The 'player 2 joined' toast is a small 14px-ish black chip, sitting on the building edge with the hotbar numbers right below it, and it is the only 14px text in the centre.
findings.fix: Add a 1px --scrim text shadow, or move the zone name into the top banner at 20px tx-1. Raise the toast to 16px with 16px padding and 24px clearance above the hotbar.

v.verdict: The raid HUD has a clear hero number and a quiet palette, but its overlapping damage text, mismatched panels and tiny, dim labels make it look like a prototype and not a polished game.

findings.where: damage numbers above the enemy, around (530,430)
findings.what: The damage popup overlaps itself. A small 'se' label and a '36' collide with the big orange '324', so the text can't be read. The 'weak spot 3,4x' tag is stuck to it with no gap. This is the screen's subject, and it is the messiest part.
findings.fix: Stack the popup in one column with 8px gaps. Put the hero number at 32px f-cond 800, with a 16px label below it. Drop the 'se' fragment. Draw the hit '36' as a separate popup that floats away at an offset of at least 24px.

findings.where: top-centre cluster: timer, team score, extract
findings.what: The timer, score panel and extract pill are three boxes of different widths (about 145, 270 and 145px) with different fills and corner radii. The score panel is stretched wide and uneven: 'team score' is centred, 'you 0 sp' and 'p1 0 sp' are right-aligned, and the big '0 sp' sits to the left of them. The panel overlaps the sun icon and blends into the map. The timer also fights for the eye with the ammo readout.
findings.fix: Make all three panels the same width (about 270px) and stack them at 8px gaps. Use one --ui-panel fill at 90% opacity, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Left-align the score block with the hero '0 sp' at 56px. Move the per-player rows under it at 16px. Move the sun icon out of the panel's footprint.

findings.where: bottom-right: air strike bar and 'support mg 60 / 42' panel
findings.what: The two panels are different widths and are stacked with almost no gap. The ammo panel is the largest block on screen and has a loose layout: a small title at the top right, then '60' and '/ 42' in different sizes with different greys. The air strike bar has a 4px-high fill that is hard to see, and the orange is too close to the damage text.
findings.fix: Make both panels the same width (about 300px) with a 16px gap between them. Draw the ammo as one hero line at 56px f-cond 800 in tx-1, with '/ 42' at 32px tx-2 on the same baseline. Use a 16px label for the title. Make the air strike bar 8px high, and use --acc for the fill only when it is ready.

findings.what: The slot numbers are only about 14px, dim and unevenly placed: '2', '3' and '5' sit on the empty slots with no frame, and slot 4 has its number on the left but sits on a different grid from slot 1. Empty slots have no border, so the row looks broken. The selected slot 6 has an amber border, but the player colour guide says lime means 'selected'. The weapon icons are small, and the ammo '42' is cramped in the corner.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots at 72×72px with 8px gaps, a 1px --ui-line border on empty ones and a --ui-panel fill. Use a 2px --acc border on the selected slot. Set slot numbers at 16px tx-2 in the same top-left corner everywhere. Move the ammo count to a 16px label at bottom-right.

findings.where: hp bar, bottom left; player 1 tag, left edge
findings.what: The 'hp 100' bar is a flat green block with large text that overflows the bar's edge. It sits flush against the screen edge and has no margin, so it breaks the 5% margin rule. The 'player 1' plate at the left edge is a different thin style with a crowded cyan bar, and it touches the screen edge. Both look unrelated to the other panels.
findings.fix: Put the hp bar inside a --ui-panel frame at 24px from the left and bottom edges, 320×32px. Use a 16px label 'hp' and a 20px value in f-cond. Match the 'player 1' plate to the same frame. Keep P1 amber and P2 cyan as the guide requires.

findings.where: 'in pillager's party' tag and 'f1 controls' hint
findings.what: Both are small and low-contrast, and they are placed at random spots with different panel styles. The 'in pillager's party' tag is about 14px and floats in the middle of the map with no clear reason. The 'f1 controls' hint has a key cap in a different style from the rest of the UI.
findings.fix: Make the minimum text size 16px. Use the same panel style for both. Put the 'f1 controls' line in the mid-bottom left slot the owner chose, as a 16px line with one key cap. Move the party tag to the top-left under the 'keyboard' badge.

findings.where: 'keyboard' badge, top left, and 'c 123m' extract marker, right
findings.what: The 'keyboard' badge uses a green-tinted frame that matches nothing else and sits flush at the corner. The 'c 123m' marker is half clipped by its own arrow and gets close to the right edge. It repeats the 'extract 123m' pill with a different label ('c'), so the same fact is drawn twice.
findings.fix: Put the badge in the standard --ui-panel style at 24px from the corner. Make the edge marker 24px in from the screen edge, and label it 'extract' to match the top pill, or drop the duplicate pill when the marker is on screen.

v.verdict: The in-raid HUD works, but it has too many different panel shapes and type sizes. The team-score block is crowded, the weapon bar looks unfinished, and the hp bar's number is hard to read.

findings.what: Three separate boxes stack with uneven widths and edges: the timer is 10:00 in a rounded box, the team score box has 'team score', '0 sp', 'you 0 sp' and 'p2 0 sp' in four sizes, and extract 125m is a small teal pill. The 'you' and 'p2' lines crowd the big 0 sp, and the box's right padding is almost zero. The same score is shown twice (team 0 plus the 0 and 0 split).
findings.fix: Merge into one 8px-grid column of equal width. Timer is the hero at 56px. Under it, a single 16px line 'extract 125m' in --extract. Drop the 'team score' label and show 0 sp at 32px. Move the per-player split into the P1/P2 corner chips, or use 16px --tx-2 with 16px padding all round.

findings.what: 'hp 100' is dark text on a mid-green fill, with a heavy outline and a size that matches nothing else. The bar is cut off at the bottom edge (y about 1040-1068) and sits against the screen edge with no 5% margin. It is the plainest element on screen and is not the same style as the ammo card.
findings.fix: Put it in a --ui-panel card with 4px radius, 24px from the left and bottom edges. Use a 16px bar with a 20px --tx-1 'hp 100' label, and fill it with --ok. Keep the bar and the card edge on the same 8px grid as the weapon slots.

findings.what: The slots are inconsistent. Slot 3 is selected with an amber border (not the lime --acc) but holds an empty dark silhouette, while slots 1 and 6 hold icons. The numbers 2, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 0 float as faint grey text with ghost icons and no slot frame, so the row reads as broken and unfinished. The selected slot is amber while the P1 convention is amber and 'selected' is lime.
findings.fix: Draw every slot as a 64px frame with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a --ui-panel fill, empty ones dimmed. Number each at 16px in a fixed corner. Use --acc for the selected slot border (3px) and show the weapon icon in it. Remove the ghost silhouettes or put them inside the frames at 30% opacity.

findings.what: The goals chip is a different shape and weight from the other HUD cards: a thin dark bar with a chevron, a 24px label and tight padding. Nothing lines it up with the timer box or the ammo card. The top-right is meant to become the career HUD column, so this one-off chip adds to the inconsistency.
findings.fix: Use the same card as the others (--ui-panel, 1px --ui-line-hi, 4px radius, 16px padding) at 16px label size. Align its top edge to the timer box (y 24) and its right edge to the ammo card (24px margin). Keep the chevron as a 16px glyph.

findings.what: The card is the strongest block, which is right: the 7 / 150 hero is large and readable. The weapon name is right-aligned at about 30px, between title and body size, and the card has a different border from the top-centre boxes. The gap between the name and the 7 is tight, and the large 150 competes with the 7 for the eye.
findings.fix: Set the weapon name to 20px --tx-2. Set the 7 to the 56px hero in --tx-1 and '/ 150' to 20px --tx-2 on the same baseline, so the loaded count is the single hero. Use the same card style as the other HUD panels.

findings.what: The f1 chip sits on the building edge at about 22px and is hard to read: a small key cap on a dark pill over busy tiles, jammed against the bottom of the building and next to slot 1. The 'player 2 joined' toast overlaps the wall with no consistent anchor. The keyboard badge at top-left is also a one-off style in a third font treatment.
findings.fix: Put the 'f1 controls' hint in the left-feed or mid-bottom-left position at 16px in a --scrim chip, 16px clear of the slot bar. Put the toast in the top-centre banner or the left feed only, per the one-place rule. Restyle the 'keyboard' tag as a 16px fine label.

findings.where: player 2 tag (left) and player 2 world label
findings.what: The left 'player 2' bar uses a cyan underline on a plain blue-grey building and is clipped at the left edge with a 17px label. The same player is also labelled over the character in a different style (blue background, cyan outline), so the identity appears twice. The sentry label is orange with a 96 damage number in a third style.
findings.fix: Keep one P2 identity. Use the corner chip as a 16px label with a cyan 3px bar on a --ui-panel card, and keep only a small cyan ring and arrow on the character. Show the sentry name at 16px with a --danger bar, and leave the damage number as the only large figure.

findings.what: The eye hits the 10:00 timer first, then the ammo card. The current weapon and hp, which matter most mid-fight, get the least weight (small hp bar, empty selected slot). The HUD shows five different box styles (dark rounded rectangles, a pill, a bar, an outlined chip, a plain bar) and at least six text sizes, so it reads as assembled, not designed.
findings.fix: Use one HUD card (--ui-panel at 85% opacity, 1px --ui-line-hi, 4px radius). Limit text to the 56, 32, 20, 16 scale. Keep the hero for the ammo count and the timer, and make hp a clear second element in the bottom-left.

v.verdict: The easy-mode prompt is a clear yes/no card with a lime primary button, but it is a flat, empty dark slab dropped over a busy HUD, with a faint countdown, a key-letter prefix on the buttons, and a cramped HUD around it.

findings.what: The countdown is a small grey number in the corner. It is the only time pressure on the card and it reads as a stray digit, with no label or ring. It is about 24px and low contrast, so it is not readable from a couch.
findings.fix: Make it a 56px hero number in --acc, or a thin progress bar along the card's top edge that fills the full width. Right-align it to the 48px padding and baseline-align it with the title.

findings.what: The card is 935x318 with a 32px title in the upper left and a large dead zone between the title and the buttons. The title sits top-left while the buttons span the full width, so there is no clear axis. The lime sliver at the card's top-left (about 70px) looks like a glitch.
findings.fix: Tighten the vertical gaps to 24px, or centre the title over the buttons. Make the lime top bar either the full-width countdown or remove it. Use 32px padding and a 4px radius on the card.

findings.what: The key letter is set in the same weight and size as the label, so it reads as the stray text 'y yes'. The lime fill is about 400x100, so it competes with the HUD and the card title. The 'no' button has a faint border and a text-only look, so it is barely distinguishable from the card.
findings.fix: Put the key hint in a 16px chip (--ui-line-hi border) to the left of the label, and make the labels 20px/600. Cut the button height to 64px. Give 'no' a 2px --ui-line-hi border and a --ui-raised fill. Show a pad-button glyph when a pad is in use.

findings.what: There is no scrim, so the game keeps running at full brightness. The card hides the middle of the map and sits directly over the extract chip and the score panel, which touch its top edge at y≈258. It reads as a placed rectangle, not a modal.
findings.fix: Add --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.80) behind the card, or at least .5 over the playfield. Move the card down by 48px or up by 24px so it clears the extract chip. Keep HUD elements visible only if they matter.

findings.where: top-centre HUD (clock, team score, extract chip)
findings.what: Three stacked boxes of different widths, with 'you 0 sp / p1 0 sp' in a small size crammed next to the big '0 sp'. The extract chip abuts the card. The text sizes (about 14-18px) are below the 16px minimum and sit unevenly.
findings.fix: Align all three to a shared 260px width. Use a 16px minimum for the per-player lines. Add 8px of gap between the extract chip and the card, or hide the chip while the prompt is open.

findings.what: The armour and hp bars use different fills, and the label sizes and weights do not match the 16px/20px scale. 'hp 100' is larger than 'armour 60', so the two read as unrelated. The slot numbers 1-0 float over the wall texture with poor contrast. The 'f1 controls' chip and the 'in pillager's party' tag sit at yet other sizes.
findings.fix: Put both bars at 20px label and 14px height with the same radius. Give the slot numbers a --tx-2 colour at 16px on a dark pill. Align the f1 chip to the bar's left edge at 24px.

findings.where: ammo panel and goals pill, right side
findings.what: The ammo panel has a 56px hero with a 'riot scatter gun' label above it, a good hero. But the panel is cut close to the edge and its corner radius and border differ from the goals pill at top right. The goals pill has a chevron that looks like a native select.
findings.fix: Use one panel style, --ui-panel with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Keep a 24px margin to the screen edge. Replace the chevron with a plain 16px label.

findings.what: A debug-looking green-outlined tag in the corner. Its size, border colour and style match nothing else on screen.
findings.fix: Remove it from the raid screen, or fold it into the f1 controls chip in --tx-2 at 14px with a --ui-line border.

v.verdict: The HUD is still a set of unrelated boxes, each with its own size, fill and edge, and the "c 151m" cache chip from the last review is gone from this shot, so the effort went to the extract chip and little else changed.

findings.where: top-centre stack: clock, team score, extract chip
findings.what: Three separate dark boxes of different widths (about 215, 270 and 145px) are stacked with different gaps. The team score box overlaps the clock's lower edge. The rain icon floats beside the clock with no panel. The 'you 0 sp' and 'p2 0 sp' lines are crammed against the box's right edge.
findings.fix: Merge them into one centred panel (--ui-panel at 80%, 4px radius, 16px padding, 8px row gap). Clock at 56px hero. 'team score 0 sp' at 20px beneath it, with 'you' and 'p2' as two 16px tx-2 items on one row. Extract chip as a 16px teal line at the bottom of the same panel. Move the rain icon inside the panel's right edge.

findings.what: The 'hp 81' text sits on top of the bar and clashes with the green fill. The red '-6' chunk is a loud solid block with small text. The bar is cut at the screen edge with no 5% margin, and it overlaps the world art.
findings.fix: Inset the bar 5% (about 96px) from the left and 24px from the bottom. Bar 12px tall. Put 'hp 81' at 20px tx-1 on its own line above the bar. Draw the damage chunk in --danger at 60% opacity and drop the '-6' text, or make it 16px and put it beside the number.

findings.what: Slots 1 and 4-0 are bare floating digits and the filled slots 2 and 3 are only about 100px wide. The slot number is spaced differently in each slot. The digits are low contrast, with no tile behind them. The row is not centred on the screen and sits against the bottom edge. The orange selection border is the player colour, which clashes with the rule that lime means selected.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots as 56px tiles, 8px apart, --ui-panel at 70% with a 1px --ui-line border, and show empty slots at 40% opacity. Number at 16px tx-2 in the top-left corner of each tile. Selected slot gets a 2px --acc border. Centre the row horizontally and lift it to 24px above the bottom edge.

findings.where: ammo panel bottom-right and goals 0/3 top-right
findings.what: The ammo panel is about 305px wide with a different edge and radius from the other boxes. Its right edge sits at x~1910, while goals 0/3 sits at x~1900. The weapon name is right-aligned and floats in empty space. '25' is bigger than the clock, so there are two competing hero numbers on screen. The 'goals 0/3' bar has a chevron and no clear role.
findings.fix: Use one panel style for all HUD boxes (--ui-panel at 80%, 4px radius, 16px padding). Pull both right edges to the same 5% margin (x=1824). Weapon name at 20px tx-2. '25' at 56px 800, which is the only hero here, and '/ 150' at 20px tx-2. Make the clock 32px so there is one hero. Make 'goals 0/3' 16px with the chevron inside the same panel.

findings.what: The tag is in a green-tinted box with a different border and fill from every other HUD element. It is tight against the corner and shows a status that is rarely needed.
findings.fix: Restyle it as a 14px tx-2 chip with --ui-panel fill, inset 24px from the corner, or remove it after the first 5 seconds of the raid.

findings.where: 'f1 controls' hint, bottom-left, and 'player 2 joined' toast
findings.what: The hint is a dim box at roughly 60% contrast, sitting on the building edge and 16px from the hp bar. The toast is a flat black box with 16px text. Neither shares the HUD panel style, and the toast sits right on top of the hotbar numbers.
findings.fix: Use the same chip style for both (--ui-panel at 80%, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 16px tx-1, 8px padding). Put the 'f1' key in its own 1px-bordered cap. Position the hint 24px above the hp bar's left edge and the toast at screen centre-left, about 120px above the hotbar.

findings.where: player 2 tag, top-left, with the cyan marker and in-world 'player 2' label
findings.what: The top-left tag has a thin cyan bar under a dark box with no panel edge, and sits on the wall art. It overlaps the world at x 16-170 and repeats the in-world label near the character. The 'e search body' prompt has a lime key cap and an off-style body. It reads well but its fill is black while the other panels are charcoal.
findings.fix: Make the player 2 tag the same chip style as the other HUD boxes: 16px tx-1 name over a 4px cyan bar, 8px padding. Place it under the 'keyboard' tag at the 5% margin. Use --ui-panel for the 'e search body' fill and keep the lime key cap.

v.verdict: The HUD reads clearly and the weapon and ammo card is a strong hero, but the earlier advice was mostly not followed: the score panel is still crowded, the hp bar still sits on the floor edge with no panel, and the slot row is still a mess of mismatched numerals and ghost icons.

findings.what: The panel is still crowded. 'team score', a large '0 sp', 'you 0 sp' and 'p1 0 sp' are packed into a box about 270x100. The 'extract 111m' chip is stacked tight under it with a different width and fill. Three adjacent boxes of different widths sit under the clock. The 'you' and 'p1' lines are too small, and 'p1' is ambiguous because the same player is also labelled 'player 1' elsewhere.
findings.fix: Show the team total only, at 32px f-cond, with a 16px label above it. Move per-player splits to the scoreboard. Make the clock, score and extract boxes one width (about 270px), with 8px gaps, 16px padding and a 4px radius.

findings.what: The bar touches the screen edge (about 24px in, 1px from the bottom) and has no panel. The 'hp 81' text is white on mid-green, which has weak contrast, and the '-6' is in pale red on a red fill. The bar sits against the sand terrain with no backing, and it is the vital stat.
findings.fix: Put it in a --ui-panel card inset 48px from the left and bottom. Use a 12px bar, 20px 'hp 81' in tx-1 on the dark panel, and a 16px '-6' in --danger. Keep red for the damage chunk only.

findings.what: Slot numbers 1-8 and 0 float as loose grey digits across 700px with faint ghost silhouettes. Only slots 4 and 6 are filled, and the ghost icons are nearly invisible. The numerals ('4' and '6' inside the tiles, the rest outside) are inconsistent. The 'f' badge sits at the left of the ammo row and collides with the gun icon. The whole row has no shared baseline or backing.
findings.fix: Draw all 9 slots as 56px tiles on --ui-panel at 40% opacity with a 1px --ui-line border. Put the number in the top-left at 16px. Put the ammo count bottom-right at 16px 600. Move the 'f' badge to the top-right. Highlight only the active tile with a lime 2px border.

findings.what: The card is the best element, with a clear hero '7 / 42' at about 56px. But it is sloppy against the rest: the name is right-aligned and the card hugs the right edge about 10px in. The same '42' appears again in slot 6, so the information is duplicated. The slash and the reserve number are the same size as the magazine count.
findings.fix: Inset the card 48px from the right and bottom. Make the reserve '/ 42' 20px tx-2, and keep the magazine count at 56px. Drop the ammo count from the slot tile when the card shows it.

findings.where: player 1 tag (top left) and in-world 'player 1' label
findings.what: The top-left tag is flush against the screen edge, with a thin cyan/green bar and tiny text, and it has no panel or margin. The in-world label has a different look again: a dark chip with blue text. The player colours do not match the settled rule (P1 amber, P2 cyan), and the green ring does not read as either colour.
findings.fix: Place the tag at 48px/48px inside a --ui-panel card. Use amber for P1 in both the tag and the world label, with a 16px chip and 4px padding. Use cyan only for P2.

findings.where: toast 'in pillager's party' and 'f1 controls' hint
findings.what: The toast sits directly on top of the slot 5 area at a different width and fill from every other card. The 'f1 controls' hint floats on the orange rooftop at x=410, not aligned to the hp card or the left edge. Both read as unrelated labels.
findings.fix: Set both to --ui-panel at 90%, a 4px radius and 16px label text. Align 'f1 controls' to the hp card's left edge (48px) and put the toast 16px above the slot row, centred.

findings.where: goals 0/3 dropdown and keyboard tag, top corners
findings.what: The 'goals 0/3' panel is a third style, with a black fill, a chevron and a thick border. The 'keyboard' tag at top-left is tiny, with a lime border and 16px text hugging the edge at about 6px. Neither lines up with the 48px margin the guide calls for.
findings.fix: Inset both at 48px. Use the same --ui-panel fill and --ui-line-hi 1px border, 16px labels and a 4px radius. Keep lime for the focused or selected state only.

findings.where: damage number '18' and the red arc beside the player
findings.what: The red '18' is bold and clear, but the floating red arc to the right of the player has no label or anchor, so it looks like a rendering glitch. The '18' also overlaps the aim reticle.
findings.fix: Remove the arc, or tie it to a visible hit-direction indicator at the screen edge. Offset the damage number 16px above the reticle and fade it in 600ms.

v.verdict: The damage-number and enemy-tag problem is gone, but this is now a different screen: an easy-mode prompt covers the middle of the raid, and the HUD underneath is still crowded and inconsistent.

findings.what: The card is a wide, mostly empty slab with a loose corner countdown ('12'). It sits flush against the team-score and extract panels with no scrim, and a lime sliver is clipped at its top-left edge. The map stays at full brightness, so the card has no hierarchy against the raid behind it. The lime yes button is a huge fill that outweighs the 32px title, which breaks the rule of boldness in one place only.
