findings.fix: Dim the world with the --scrim fill at rgba(6,7,8,.80). Shrink the card to about 640x300 with 32px padding and centre it, leaving at least 48px clear of the top HUD. Delete the stray lime sliver. Make 'yes' a 20px label on a 56px-high button, and make 'no' a 1px --ui-line-hi outline button of the same size. Turn the countdown into a thin 4px lime progress bar along the card's bottom edge.

findings.what: The three panels have three different widths, radii and paddings. 'team score' is centred, but its '0 sp' and the you/p2 lines are crammed side by side at about 16px with no breathing room. The extract pill slightly overlaps the score panel's bottom edge. The timer is the largest element and out-shouts everything else on screen.
findings.fix: Use one 4px-radius column at 8px gaps and one shared width of 240px. Put the timer at 32px, the score at 20px, and the you/p2 split on a single 16px line, with you in amber and p2 in cyan. Stop the extract pill overlapping the score panel by adding an 8px gap.

findings.what: The ammo order is now correct, but the card is oversized and padded unevenly. The weapon name is right-aligned at about 28px, so it reads as a second headline. The reserve '144' is nearly as big as the 24 magazine count.
findings.fix: Fit the card to its content with 16px padding. Set the name at 16px in tx-2, the magazine count at 56px f-cond 800 in tx-1, and the reserve at 32px in tx-2. Use one corner radius and match the hotbar tile border.

findings.what: Only slots 3 and 4 are drawn as tiles. The other slot numbers (1, 2, 5-0) float on the map with faint ghost weapon icons, so the row reads as broken. The selected slot is amber, which clashes with the lime-means-selected rule, and the 'f' badge and ammo count sit tight against the icon. The 'player 2 joined' toast is stacked right above the tiles and crowds them.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots as 56px tiles with --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 8px gaps, and the number at 16px inside the tile. Dim empty slots to 40%. Mark the equipped slot with a 2px --acc border. Move the toast up to the left feed.

findings.what: The bars are different sizes, and the green and blue fills are saturated, which clashes with the palette. The label type is oversized (about 28px) and is drawn directly on the fill with no inset, and the bars sit against the screen edge with a 24px margin. Armour is blue and hp is green, so the pair reads as default-template bars. There is no P2 card.
findings.fix: Use a 320x20 bar for each, both with the same 16px label inset by 8px. Use --ok for hp and --r-rare for armour on a --ui-panel track with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Place both on the 8px grid with a 48px margin and 8px between them. Add a P2 bar below in cyan.

findings.what: The goals dropdown is a bordered bar with a bright white chevron, a different panel style from every other HUD element. The 'keyboard' tag is a tiny green-bordered pill in the top-left corner, which is a third style. Both feel like debug leftovers.
findings.fix: Restyle both with the shared panel: --ui-panel fill, 4px radius, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 16px f-cond text. Make the chevron tx-2. Hide the 'keyboard' tag outside of the settings screen.

findings.where: the 'search body' prompt, right of centre
findings.what: The prompt overlaps a teal 'shie...' label that is cut off underneath it. Its 'e' keycap is a tiny lime chip and the text is about 14px, which is hard to read from a couch.
findings.fix: Show one prompt only. Set the text at 16px with a 24px lime keycap. Back it with a --scrim fill and lift it 16px above the body so it never overlaps the item label.

findings.what: The chip floats loose above the hp bar. Its square panel, key chip and text don't match the other chips, and it sits right next to the slot-1 number.
findings.fix: Use the same --ui-panel chip as the other HUD text, 16px, with an 8px gap from the hotbar and the hp bar. Keep it on one line at the mid-bottom left.

v.verdict: The ammo panel now has a clear hero number and the damage popups no longer overlap, but the top-centre cluster is still three different widths, the weapon slots are inconsistent, and the hp bar has no frame.

findings.where: top-centre cluster: clock, team score, extract chip
findings.what: The three panels are 146, 270 and 144px wide, so the stack looks ragged. The 'you 0 sp' and 'p1 0 sp' rows sit tight against the right edge and read as 16px text next to a 56px hero. The sun icon floats loose beside the clock. The 'extract 122m' chip is teal text on a teal-bordered pill, a different style from its neighbours.
findings.fix: Make all three panels 270px wide, stacked with 8px gaps, on one --ui-panel fill at 90% with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Add 16px padding inside the score panel. Put the per-player rows in a 16px tx-2 column with 8px between them. Move the sun icon inside the clock panel or drop it.

findings.where: weapon slots along the bottom (1, 2, then bare 3–0)
findings.what: Slots 1 and 2 are filled 100px tiles. Slots 3–0 are bare grey digits with ghost icons, drawn on top of the sandy wall and nearly unreadable (about 2:1). The row looks half-built, and the slot numbers do not share a common baseline with the tiles.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots as 72×72px tiles with 8px gaps, using a --ui-panel fill at 85% and a 1px --ui-line border on the empty ones. Keep the 2px --acc border only on the selected slot. Put the numbers at 16px tx-2 in the top-left corner of every tile. Centre the row at 24px from the bottom.

findings.what: The bar is a bare green fill with 'hp 100' in about 32px type sitting on the grass, with no frame. It is nearly invisible against the green terrain and sits 12px from the bottom edge. The 'player 1' plate above it (x15–170, y322) is a different, tiny style with a cyan bar. Its position is also unrelated to the hp bar.
findings.fix: Put the hp bar in a --ui-panel frame, 320×32px, 24px from the left and bottom edges, with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Use a 16px 'hp' label and a 20px value. Use --ok for the fill, which is distinct from the terrain colour. Give the 'player 1' plate the same frame and 4px radius.

findings.where: bottom-right: air strike bar and 'support mg 54 / 240' panel
findings.what: The air strike panel is 390px wide and the ammo panel is 305px, and they are misaligned on the left. The air strike bar is a thin, low-contrast fill with an orange chip, and '8%' is 16px at the far edge, so it is hard to read. The ammo panel is better but has an empty gap above the number. The ammo panel runs to y1018 and the right margin is about 10px, so both panels crowd the screen edge.
findings.fix: Make both panels 300px wide, 24px from the right edge, with a 16px gap between them. Make the air strike bar 8px high, fill it with --warn until it is ready, then --acc, and put '8%' at 16px tx-1 right-aligned. Move the 'support mg' label to the top-left at 16px and put the ammo on one baseline with '/ 240' at 32px tx-2.

findings.where: damage popups and tags above the sentry (x755–890, y370–485)
findings.what: '48 ! 216', 'sentry k-31' and 'weak spot 3.4x' are three lines in three sizes with no gap, all in orange, over a dark building. The '!' sits between the two numbers with no meaning. The orange on orange terrain to the right loses contrast, and the lines are crowded within about 20px of each other.
findings.fix: Stack them in one column with 8px gaps. Draw the damage number at 32px f-cond 800 and the tags at 16px. Remove the stray '!', or move it to a crit tag at 16px. Give each popup a 1px dark outline or a 60% dark pill behind it so it holds contrast over the orange ground.

findings.where: 'f1 controls' hint (x410–535, y922) and 'in pillager's party' tag (x885–1035, y893)
findings.what: The two pieces of floating text use different plates: one a translucent tan, one a black box with white 14px text. The party tag is only 14px and sits on top of the building. They crowd the weapon row.
findings.fix: Use one hint style: a --ui-panel plate with a 4px radius and 16px tx-1 text. Align the 'f1 controls' hint with the left edge of the hp frame at 24px. Move the party tag up to sit above the slot row with a 16px gap.

findings.what: It uses a green mono-bold face on a dark chip, which is a different type role from everything else. It is tiny and sits 8px from the corner, with an unexplained purpose.
findings.fix: Set it in f-cond 600 at 16px tx-2 on the standard --ui-panel plate, 24px from the top-left corner. Or hide it once the input device is obvious.

findings.what: It uses wide-tracked grey type over a dark building with no plate. It collides with the sentry's popup area and is hard to read because the tracking is wide and the contrast low.
findings.fix: Use f-cond 600 at 20px with +.04em tracking in tx-1, on a 60% --scrim pill. Place it 16px below the extract chip, clear of the popups.

v.verdict: The HUD is still a pile of unrelated boxes: the top-centre stack is crowded and the weapon bar is only half done. The ammo card is the one clear improvement, but the 6 is not yet the hero.

findings.where: top-centre stack (timer, team score card, extract pill)
findings.what: This is three differently sized boxes stacked with no shared width. The score card carries a 'team score' label, a 0 sp figure and a you/p2 split, which is clutter. The score card is wider than the timer, and the extract pill is narrower than both. The weather icon floats beside the timer with no frame.
findings.fix: Use one 8px-grid column of equal width, about 240px. The timer is the 56px hero. Below it, one 16px line 'extract 124m' in --extract. Drop the 'team score' label and the you/p2 text. Show 0 sp at 20px --tx-1 in a single row, and move the per-player split to the P1/P2 corner chips. Use 16px padding on every card.

findings.what: The bar has no card. It sits flush at about x 24, y 1035, and the hp 100 text is a squashed label that overlaps the bar and has no padding. It is not aligned to the weapon slots or to the ammo card margin.
findings.fix: Put it in a --ui-panel card with 4px radius, 24px from the left and bottom edges. Make the bar 16px tall in --ok. Put a separate 20px --tx-1 'hp 100' label above or beside it. Align its bottom edge with the slot bar and the ammo card.

findings.what: The two filled slots are framed differently, and the selected one has a 3px amber border (it should be lime --acc). The empty slots 2, 3 and 5 to 0 have no frames, only floating digits and faint ghost silhouettes. The slot numbers sit in inconsistent places. The 'f' key chip on slot 4 and the slot 5 digit collide.
findings.fix: Draw every slot as a 64px frame with a --ui-panel fill and a 1px --ui-line-hi border, with a 16px gap between frames. Dim empty slots to 40% and put the ghost icon inside the frame at 30%. Put the 16px number in the top-left corner of every frame. Use a 3px --acc border on the selected slot. Move the 'f' chip to the bottom-left inside the frame, or remove it.

findings.what: The card is big and heavy, and the faint ghost weapon art behind the numbers adds noise. The '6' (about 70px) is bigger than the 56px hero size, and '/ 240' is almost as large, so the two compete. The weapon name is in white, which is louder than it needs to be.
findings.fix: Set the weapon name to 20px --tx-2. Set the 6 to 56px --tx-1 and '/ 240' to 20px --tx-2 on the same baseline. Remove the ghost art. Fix the card at 24px from the right and bottom edges, with 16px padding, so it matches the hp card.

findings.what: The chip is a wide, mostly empty bar at 28px type, which is bigger than the 16-20px labels elsewhere. Its top edge (y 22) sits slightly off the timer box (y 18), and the chevron is large.
findings.fix: Use the same card style as the other HUD panels (--ui-panel, 1px --ui-line-hi, 4px radius, 16px padding) at 20px type. Shrink the card to fit its content, with a 16px chevron. Put its top edge at y 24 to match the timer, and its right edge at 24px.

findings.where: world labels: sentry t-94, weak spot 2.0x, 64 / 64 numbers
findings.what: The labels stack on top of each other over the enemy: an orange name tag, a blue 'weak spot' tag and two large 64s on either side of a red '!'. The 64s are in a different style from every other number, and the whole cluster hides the enemy sprite.
findings.fix: Show one 16px name tag above the enemy, with the weak-spot callout as a --warn glyph and not a second box. Drop the duplicate 64. Make the damage number a single 20px --tx-1 figure that floats up and fades.

findings.where: player 2 chip (top left) and keyboard tag
findings.what: The 'player 2' bar is a thin outlined strip with a cyan fill at 20px. It has no card padding and does not match the other panels. The 'keyboard' tag in the top-left corner is in a green-bordered box, which is a third border style, and is tiny at about 16px.
findings.fix: Use the same card as the other HUD panels, 24px from the left edge. Remove the green border on the 'keyboard' tag, or restyle it as a --ui-line-hi chip with 16px type.

findings.what: The toast is a small 16px box with a light border that is unrelated to the other cards, and it floats at an arbitrary position above the slot bar. The 'f1 controls' hint sits next to slot 1 and crowds it.
findings.fix: Put the toast in the same --ui-panel card at the top-centre banner position, not above the slots. Move 'f1 controls' to a 16px --tx-2 line, 24px from the left edge and above the hp card.

v.verdict: The card from last time is gone and this is a clean raid HUD, with a strong 6 / 240 ammo hero and a readable clock. The widths, the loud green hp bar and the faint slot row still keep it from looking finished.

findings.what: The saturated, flat green fill is about 410px wide. It is the loudest object on screen, and 'hp 100' sits on it with weak contrast and a rough font edge. It also has no panel, so it doesn't match the dark panels used elsewhere.
findings.fix: Put it in a --ui-panel box with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Make the fill 12px high at about 280px wide, in --ok. Set 'hp 100' as 20px/600 in --tx-1 beside the bar, not on it.

findings.where: top-centre stack (clock, team score, extract chip)
findings.what: The three widths are 148, 270 and 140px, so the stack looks ragged. The clock box overlaps the building wall. 'you 0 sp' and 'p1 0 sp' are about 14px and cramped against the right edge. 'p1' is a second name for player 1, which the screen already calls 'player 1' in two places.
findings.fix: Make all three panels 270px wide, centred, with 8px gaps and a 16px --ui-line border. Set the per-player lines to 16px/600 with 16px of right padding. Use 'you' and 'p2' consistently, or use the same names as the world tags. Drop the 'sp' from the small lines, since the unit is already shown on the big number.

findings.what: Slot numbers 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 0 float over the map at about 12px with low contrast, next to ghosted icons. Only two slots read as buttons, and '240' appears again in the ammo panel. The 'in pillager's party' chip floats in the middle of the row with no relation to it.
findings.fix: Draw every slot as a 72px --ui-panel tile with a 4px radius, a 1px --ui-line border and a 16px number in --tx-2. Mark the selected tile with a 3px --acc bar or border. Drop the per-slot ammo on the idle tile. Move the party chip to the top-left under 'keyboard'.

findings.where: selected weapon tile and p1 colour
findings.what: The selected slot's amber border matches the P1 colour, and the damage numbers and sentry tag are also orange. Lime (--acc) is meant to mean 'selected', so this hurts the focus rule, and the orange text competes with each other.
findings.fix: Use a 3px --acc border on the selected slot. Keep amber for the P1 ring only. Keep damage numbers in --warn but at 20px with a 2px dark outline.

findings.where: damage numbers, 'sentry t-73' and 'weak spot 3.4x' labels
findings.what: The labels stack on the enemy with different box styles and sizes: 72, 162, a '!' glyph, a tag and a wider tag. They crowd the target and cover the sprite.
findings.fix: Combine them into one floating column. Put 'weak spot 3.4x' at 16px/600 above the number. Move the sentry tag 24px above the sprite and use one tag style.

findings.what: The 'player 1' bar is a thin, tight box floating mid-left at y=325, away from any anchor. The 'keyboard' chip is jammed into the corner with 2px of margin and is a different size and style.
findings.fix: Anchor the player plate to the 48px margin at top-left. Use the same panel style as the other cards. Give the 'keyboard' chip 16px type and 24px inset, or remove it once the control scheme has been shown.

findings.where: air strike and ammo panels, right
findings.what: The panels are stacked with different heights and a different radius from the top stack. The air strike bar's orange fill is a 6px sliver, and '7%' is ahead of the label at 14px.
findings.fix: Make both 4px radius and the same left edge. Make the air strike row 56px high with a 16px label and a 6px-high bar. Keep the 56px hero number for ammo only.

findings.where: 'f1 controls' hint and 'packing floor' area name
findings.what: The 'f1 controls' hint is a small chip floating at left of the slot row, away from the left edge, with a faint key cap. 'packing floor' is wide-tracked grey text on the wall, so it is low contrast and it is painted into the world.
findings.fix: Dock 'f1 controls' at the bottom-left at 48px margin, above the hp bar, at 16px in --tx-2 with a --ui-line-hi key chip. Render the area name at 20px in --tx-1 with a dark 2px outline, or fade it after 3 seconds.

v.verdict: This is a small, nearly empty 'tonight's best' card with no scores over a busy blurred lobby. The earlier advice was about a raid HUD, so none of it applies here, and the card has no clear hierarchy beyond its title.

findings.where: empty state: 'no scores yet' and the dead space under the title
findings.what: The card says nothing useful. The body line is a 20px label with no weight difference from the title, so the whole card reads as a placeholder. About 60px of blank space sits between the title and the line.
findings.fix: Show the leaderboard skeleton: 3 to 5 ghost rows with rank, name and sp, at 40% opacity with 1px --ui-line dividers. Make 'no scores yet' 20px --tx-2, centred in that area. Cut the gap between title and body to 24px.

findings.where: card size and position, 558x255 at screen centre
findings.what: The card is tiny against a 1920 canvas. It is only about 29% of the width, and the lobby behind it stays busy and bright. The focus here is weak, and it does not match the 90% centred card used by the other windows.
findings.fix: Raise the scrim to --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.80) with a stronger blur. Enlarge the card to about 720x440, or 90% for the full leaderboard. Keep a 32px inner padding and the 4px radius.

findings.what: This is a party walk-up screen that continues on any key, and the live prompt is already the action. The boxed ×, with its 1px --ui-line-hi border, competes with the prompt as a second dismiss control and is the strongest outlined element on the card.
findings.fix: Drop the border and fill and draw a 16px --tx-2 × at 24px from the corner. Only show it when the input is a mouse or touch. Keep 'press any key' as the single action.

findings.what: The prompt is the primary action but sits at the same 20px as the body text. Its lime radio glyph is the only accent, so it reads as a bullet instead of a key hint. It is also right-aligned, away from the title's left edge.
findings.fix: Set it at 24px 700 --tx-1 with the glyph as a 24px lime key chip. Add a gentle 1.5s opacity pulse from 70% to 100%. Keep the right alignment but use the same 32px inset as the title.

findings.what: The tag is about 12px, dark text on a dark chip at roughly 2:1 contrast. It is clipped against the top edge, and it is below the 14px floor and the 16px minimum for anything read.
findings.fix: Make it a 14px --tx-2 chip with --ui-panel fill, 8px padding and 24px from the top edge. Alternatively, fold it into the prompt as 'press any key (keyboard)'.

findings.what: The wordmark is 28px bold tx-1 floating over the blurred scene with no panel. It competes with the card title in weight, and it sits on a brighter strip where contrast is weaker.
findings.fix: Drop it to 20px --tx-2, or fade it to 60% while a modal is open. Keep it aligned to the 5% margin (x=96, y=48).

findings.where: card chrome: lime tick at the top-left (713-748, y=412) and the divider at y=571
findings.what: The 36px lime tick is the one accent element and has no function. The divider is nearly invisible at --ui-line, so the footer is not separated from the body.
findings.fix: Extend the tick to a 3px bar covering the full title width, or remove it. Draw the divider in --ui-line-hi at 1px, with 16px padding above the footer row.

v.verdict: This is a clean, calm title card with one clear lime action, but the earlier HUD advice no longer applies to this picture. The amber gradient wordmark, undersized secondary text and save-management clutter keep it from reading as polished.

findings.where: player 2 title, 'player 2 window' under the main button
findings.what: This is player 2's walk-up screen, but the only hint of who is playing is a tiny 16px grey label. The big button says 'enter the undercroft' and doesn't name the key or pad button that continues. There's no cyan P2 identity either.
findings.fix: Add a 16px cyan 'player 2' chip with a 4px radius above the title. Make the live prompt the primary action at 20px, for example 'press any key to join', naming the device's key. Delete the loose grey label.

findings.what: The orange-amber vertical gradient with a drop shadow is the one gradient wash left on a screen the guide says has none. Amber is also the P1 colour and sits close to the lime accent, so the title fights the lime button. Bold appears in two places, the title and the button.
findings.fix: Fill the wordmark flat in --tx-1 #efe9dc, f-cond 800, with no gradient or shadow. Use about 96px as the one hero size. Keep the lime fill on the button as the only hot colour.

findings.where: saves block (saves label, save row, name input, change name, create a new save)
findings.what: Walk-up player 2 gets five controls for save management. This is clutter and competes with the single action. The row text at about 15px is below the 16px floor, and the 'saves' label is thin and dim.
findings.fix: Collapse it to one 20px row of 'pillager new · $900' with the stats in tx-2. Move the name input, change name and create a new save into a settings or save window. Set the 'saves' label to 16px f-cond 600 in tx-2 at at least 4.5:1.

findings.what: A green-teal chip floats alone at y≈18, which reads as an extract-teal element. It is the wrong colour use and has no visible relationship to the layout. It is also off the 48px margin.
findings.fix: Move it to the 48px/48px top-left as a 16px chip. Colour it by player: amber for P1 and cyan for P2. Use --extract only for extraction.

findings.what: The two outlined buttons are about 14px bold with tight padding and sit at about 38px from the edge. They are the same weight as the main controls, but they are secondary.
findings.fix: Inset them 48px from the top and right. Use 16px f-cond 600 with 16px side padding and a 1px --ui-line-hi border at 4px radius. Keep the height at 40px.

findings.where: bottom control legend (wasd move, mouse aim, lmb fire, e search, f1 controls)
findings.what: The chip labels are bold white while the words are light grey, and both are small at about 15px. The row is long and tells the player controls they already see in raid. Its baseline is also misaligned with the version stamp on the left.
findings.fix: Show at most 'f1 controls' at 16px. Align it on one baseline with the 14px version stamp at 48px from the bottom. If the full list stays, set the words to 16px tx-2 with 24px between pairs.

findings.what: The tagline is 18px mid-grey, spaced out, and sits 24px under the wordmark. It is explaining copy that contributes little, and its contrast against the near-black is marginal.
findings.fix: Set it to 20px f-cond 600 in tx-2 #aaa498 with +.04em spacing, and drop the periods. Alternatively remove it, since the button already carries the identity.

findings.what: The button is lime, which is correct. But its 20px label looks undersized in a 558x56 bar. There is no focus or bounce affordance, and the 8px gap down to the grey caption is tight.
findings.fix: Use 24px f-cond 700 ink #11150a with 4px radius. Add a 2px --acc-hover outline on focus. Leave 24px before the next element.

v.verdict: The easy-mode modal and stray sliver are gone, and the ammo card now has a clear hero number. The top-centre stack, hotbar and hp bar still don't match each other.

findings.where: top-centre stack (timer, team score, extract pill)
findings.what: The three blocks have three different widths (about 148, 268 and 144px), different radii and different type. The score panel is crowded: 'you 0 sp' and 'p2 0 sp' sit tight against the 0 sp hero and wrap to two lines. The extract pill is flush against the panel's bottom edge, and the storm icon floats off to the side.
findings.fix: Use one 240px column with a 4px radius and 8px gaps. Timer at 32px. Put the score on one line with 'team score' at 16px tx-2 and the number at 32px. Put the you/p2 split on one 16px line, with you in amber and p2 in cyan. Add an 8px gap above the extract pill and move the storm icon inside the timer panel.

findings.what: Slots 1 and 2 are 96px tiles with art, but slots 3 to 0 are bare floating numbers with no tile. The strip reads as unfinished and the row is lopsided. The equipped slot's amber border follows the P1 colour, but it is thick and the lime accent that means selected is absent. The tile's lower line is hard to read. Slot 1's 'f' badge is a stray glyph.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots as 64px tiles with --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 8px gaps. Put the number at 16px in the top-left of each tile. Dim empty slots to 40%. Mark the equipped slot with a 2px --acc border. Drop the 'f' badge or make it a 16px label.

findings.what: The hp bar is a flat green fill with no track or border. 'hp 100' is oversized (about 32px) and cramped inside the bar, so the label outweighs the bar. Its 24px margin matches nothing else, and the bar runs into the clutter at the screen edge. There is no armour bar. The f1 controls chip sits right on top of it and crowds it.
findings.fix: Use a 320x20 bar on a --ui-panel track with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Put a 16px 'hp' label at 8px inset and the number on the right. Set the margin to 48px from the screen edge. Put the f1 controls chip 16px above or beside it, or fold it into the left feed. Add an armour bar in --r-rare 8px above the hp bar.

findings.what: The hero number is good, but the card is oversized (about 305x150). The name is right-aligned at about 28px, the reserve count is nearly as heavy as the magazine count, and there is dead space on the left. The card is flush to the right and bottom edges with a different margin from the left HUD.
findings.fix: Shrink the card to fit its content with 16px padding. Name at 16px tx-2. Magazine count at 56px f-cond 800 in tx-1. Reserve at 32px 600 in tx-2. Set a 48px margin matching the hp bar.

findings.where: world labels near the sentry (damage numbers, 'sentry t-77', 'weak spot 2.0x', 'player 2')
findings.what: There are four label styles within a 100px patch: an orange name tag, a blue-filled weak-spot tag, a cyan name chip and loose damage numbers in three colours with a stray red '!'. They overlap each other and the enemy and make a noisy cluster. The type is soft and low-contrast on the purple floor.
findings.fix: Use one tag style: 16px f-cond 600 on a --scrim pill with a 4px radius. Colour only the hit number: tx-1 for normal, --warn for crit. Stagger the damage numbers 24px apart vertically and remove the '!' or turn it into a 16px glyph.

findings.what: The two corner chips differ in radius, border and type (the goals chip uses a roughly 24px title while the keyboard chip is a 16px green-bordered tag). The chevron is oversized. The goals box is thin against its neighbours and sits off the top margin.
findings.fix: Give both chips a --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Use 16px labels, a 16px chevron and a 24px inset from the top and sides. Align the goals chip's right edge to the same inset as the ammo card.

findings.where: 'player 2 joined' toast and 'chill row cache' label
findings.what: The toast is a small black box floating just above the hotbar with 16px text and no relation to the feed. 'chill row cache' is bare purple text with no panel, and it competes with the world.
findings.fix: Move the toast to the left feed and match its fill and border to the other panels. Render the place name at 20px tx-1 on a --scrim pill, or fade it in at the top-left of the screen.

v.verdict: The HUD is readable and mostly lower case, but its panels still differ in width, padding and fill, and the damage popups, hp bar and empty weapon slots are still loose and unframed.

findings.where: top-centre cluster: clock, team score, extract chip
findings.what: The three panels have three different widths (~145, ~270 and ~145px) and sit crooked. The team-score panel overlaps the clock's lower edge and the sun icon floats outside any frame. 'you 0 sp' and 'p1 0 sp' are crammed against the right edge. The 'packing floor' label below is wide-tracked grey text that is hard to read over the map.
findings.fix: Make all three panels 270px wide, centred, stacked with 8px gaps. Use one --ui-panel fill at 90% with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Add 16px padding in the score panel and give the per-player rows an 8px gap at 16px tx-2. Move the sun icon inside the clock panel. Put a 60% dark pill behind 'packing floor'.

findings.where: weapon slots along the bottom (x670-1480, y955-1055)
findings.what: Only slots 2 and 5 are drawn as tiles. The other numbers (3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 0) float over the terrain with faint grey weapon ghosts, and slot 1 has no tile at all. The row looks unfinished, the numbers sit at different heights and are barely legible, and the 'f' badge on slot 2 is unexplained.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots as 72x72 tiles with 8px gaps. Fill them with --ui-panel at 85% and give the empty ones a 1px --ui-line border. Keep the 2px --acc border only on the selected slot. Put the numbers at 16px tx-2 in the top-left corner of every tile. Centre the row 24px from the bottom.

findings.what: The hp bar is a bare green slab with no frame. It is cropped by the bottom edge and has no hp label panel. Its green reads as terrain. The 'hp 100' text is a different style from the 'player 1' plate above it, and 'f1 controls' sits oddly over the bar.
findings.fix: Put the bar in a 320x32 --ui-panel frame with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius, 24px from the left and bottom edges. Use a 16px 'hp' label and a 20px value, with --ok for the fill. Give the player 1 plate the same frame and anchor it directly above the bar.

findings.where: damage numbers and tags above the sentry (x790-990, y360-480)
findings.what: The row '216 ! 48 16 64' is in four different sizes and colours with no outline or backing. The stray '!' has no meaning. The 'sentry t-15' and 'weak spot 3.4x' tags stack tightly and overlap the sentry sprite. The orange text over an orange and purple ground has weak contrast.
findings.fix: Draw the damage numbers at 32px f-cond 800, one size, and colour only by owner (P1 amber, P2 cyan). Put the tags at 16px on a 60% dark pill with 8px gaps. Drop the '!' or turn it into a 16px 'crit' tag. Keep the tags off the sprite with 8px clearance.

findings.where: bottom-right: air strike bar and 'support mg' ammo panel
findings.what: The two panels have different widths (~360 and ~305px) and different edges. The air strike bar's fill is a tiny orange chip on a grey track, and the '8%' is very close to the bar. The ammo panel's right edge touches the screen edge, and the 'support mg' label is right-aligned with the ammo, so the two compete.
findings.fix: Make both panels 300px wide, 24px from the right edge, with a 16px gap. Make the air strike bar 8px high, with --warn fill until ready, then --acc. Put '8%' at 16px tx-1 with 16px clearance from the bar. Put the 'support mg' label top-left at 16px tx-2 and the ammo on one baseline, 54 at 56px hero and '/ 240' at 32px tx-2.

findings.where: 'in pillager's party' chip and 'keyboard' tag (centre-bottom, top-left)
findings.what: The 'in pillager's party' chip floats at x885-1035, y893 and is unrelated to any panel. The 'keyboard' tag at top-left has a green border style that matches nothing else. Both read as debug leftovers. 'pillager's' also needs a better home than a floating pill.
findings.fix: Put the party chip inside the top-centre cluster, or drop it after 3s with a 200ms fade. Restyle the 'keyboard' tag to the standard 16px tx-2 label on --ui-panel with a --ui-line-hi border, or hide it once input is detected.

findings.what: The hint is a half-transparent grey plate sitting on the terrain, and its key cap style doesn't match the slot number badges or the 'f' badge. It sits 80px from the hp bar rather than aligned with it.
findings.fix: Use one key-cap component (20px square, --ui-raised fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 16px tx-1) for 'f1' and the slot numbers. Left-align the hint at x24, 8px above the hp frame.

findings.what: The 'the forge' label is amber text with no outline on a grey-purple ground. It sits next to the top-centre panel and reads as part of the HUD, and its orange competes with the damage numbers.
findings.fix: Draw world labels at 16px tx-1 on a 60% dark pill, in the same style as the 'sentry t-15' tag, so every world label looks alike.

v.verdict: The HUD is still a set of mismatched boxes. Almost none of the earlier advice was applied: the top-centre stack is still three different widths, the hp bar is still a bare bar, the slots are still uneven, and the goals chip is still a different style from the others.

findings.where: top-centre stack (timer, team score card, extract pill)
findings.what: Three stacked boxes of three widths (about 150, 270 and 140px), each with a different alignment. 'team score' is an explaining label, and the you/p2 split crowds the 0 sp. The weather icon floats beside the timer outside any frame.
findings.fix: Use one 240px column. Show the 10:00 timer at 56px. Below it put one 16px line, 'extract 114m', in --extract. Drop the 'team score' label and the you/p2 text. Show 0 sp at 20px --tx-1. Use 16px padding on every card, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Move the weather icon into the card as a 16px glyph.

findings.what: A 36px bar runs flush into the screen corner with no panel. The 'hp 100' text is drawn on the green fill with only a thin outline, and its size does not match any other label. The bar's bottom edge does not line up with the slot bar or the ammo card.
findings.fix: Put it in a --ui-panel card with a 4px radius, 24px from the left and bottom edges. Make the bar 16px tall in --ok. Put a 20px --tx-1 'hp 100' label above it. Align the bottom edge with the slot bar and the ammo card at y 1056.

findings.what: Only slots 1 and 5 have frames; slots 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 0 are bare numbers at uneven spacing over faint ghost icons. The numbers sit at different heights, and 7, 8 and 0 land on the busy orange building, where they are barely legible. The 'f' chip crowds the 240 count in slot 5. Both framed slots are the same size, but the ammo count in each is too small.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots as 64px frames with a --ui-panel fill and a 1px --ui-line-hi border, spaced 16px apart. Show empty slots at 40% opacity with the ghost icon inside the frame. Put the 16px number in the top-left of every frame. Use a 3px --acc border on the selected slot only. Move the 'f' chip to the bottom-left inside the frame or remove it.

findings.what: The weapon name is right-aligned at about 28px and competes with the title scale. The card runs to about 10px from the right edge with a different inset than the goals chip. The 6 is large and bold, but '/ 240' is nearly as heavy, so the eye has nothing to rest on.
findings.fix: Set 'riot scattergun' to 20px --tx-2. Set the 6 to 56px --tx-1 and '/ 240' to 20px --tx-2 on the same baseline. Use 24px from the right and bottom edges and 16px padding, the same as the hp card.

findings.what: A wide dark bar about 300px across holds only 'goals 0/3' on the left and a chevron on the right. It is the one HUD element with a different corner radius and padding, and its left text is tight against the edge. It sits at y 22, which does not match the timer.
findings.fix: Use the same card style as the other HUD panels: --ui-panel, 1px --ui-line-hi, 4px radius, 16px padding, 20px type. Shrink the card to fit its content, with a 16px chevron. Put the top edge at y 24 and the right edge at 24px.

findings.where: world labels: 'sentry t-64', 'weak spot 2.0x', 96 / 48, player 2 tag
findings.what: The enemy tag, the weak-spot tag and the damage numbers are all stacked at about the same size and overlap the enemy sprite. The orange label and the blue label use two different fills, and the damage numbers have no outline against the grey wall. Together they hide the target.
findings.fix: Show the weak-spot callout at 16px with a 4px radius and 8px padding, 8px above the sentry tag. Add a 2px dark outline to the damage numbers. Pick one fill style for both tags.

findings.what: 'keyboard' is a tiny pill at the screen edge with a 1px outline and no padding to speak of. The 'f1 controls' chip is another style, and it sits 40px above the hp bar at an unrelated left edge. 'player 2 joined' is a third toast style.
findings.fix: Use one chip style (--ui-panel, 1px --ui-line-hi, 4px radius, 16px type, 8px by 16px padding). Align 'f1 controls' to the 24px left margin directly above the hp card. Put the toast in the same style.

findings.what: The cyan label and bar sit on the wall with no panel. The text is 22px, a different size from the other labels, and the bar is thin.
findings.fix: Set the name to 16px --tx-1 with a cyan 3px bar under it, inside a --ui-panel chip at 24px from the left edge.

v.verdict: The in-world tags and damage numbers are merged and tidier, but the hp bar, the stacked top-centre panels and the weapon slot row still follow the same loose, mixed-style pattern as before, so the HUD is only a little closer to the style guide.

findings.what: The bar is a bare 400px green fill with 'hp 100' drawn on top of it. It has no panel, border or margin, and it runs into the screen edge and the '0%' fragment above it. It is also the only element that uses a raw flat green.
findings.fix: Put it in a --ui-panel box with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius, 48px from the left and 32px from the bottom. Make the fill 12px high and about 280px wide, in --ok. Set 'hp 100' as 20px/600 in --tx-1 beside the bar, not on it.

findings.where: top-centre stack (clock, team score, extract chip)
findings.what: The three panels have three different widths and no shared edge, and the 'chill row cache' location name is bright purple beside the team-score panel. The clock panel is narrower than the team panel and the extract chip is narrower again. The per-player lines are tiny, clipped against the right edge, and use mixed names ('you' and 'p1').
findings.fix: Make all three panels 270px wide, centred, with 8px gaps and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Set the per-player lines to 16px/600 with 16px of right padding. Use 'you' and 'p2' consistently. Render the location name at 16px in --tx-2 above the clock, not in purple.

findings.what: Only two slots are real tiles. The other slots (3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 0) are just floating numbers with ghost icons, so the row has no rhythm. The 'in pillager's party' chip sits on top of the row and 'f1 controls' sits to the left, which crowds the bottom edge. The slot numbers are in low-contrast grey.
findings.fix: Draw every slot as a 72px --ui-panel tile with an 8px gap, a 4px radius, a 1px --ui-line border and a 16px number in --tx-2. Mark the selected tile with a 3px --acc border. Drop the per-slot ammo on the idle tile. Move the party chip to the top-left under 'keyboard' and anchor 'f1 controls' to the left edge of the row.

findings.where: right-bottom stack (air strike bar, weapon card)
findings.what: The air strike bar is 16px text on a thin 6% bar with tiny orange fill, and it is narrower than the weapon card below it, so the two right edges look misaligned. The weapon card has a different inner padding. The hero ammo '6 / 240' is correct as the hero number, but the card is a 4th panel size.
findings.fix: Make both panels 300px wide with a shared right margin of 48px and 8px between them. Use 16px/600 labels, a 6px fill in --acc and 16px of inner padding.

findings.where: damage numbers, 'sentry k-13' and 'weak spot 3.4x' tags
findings.what: The merge helped, but the tags still stack tightly over the sprite. The orange 'weak spot' text in a dark chip overlaps the sentry, and the '!' between 108 and 96 reads as a stray glyph. Two chip styles (dark box and bare text) are in use.
findings.fix: Use one floating column. Put 'weak spot 3.4x' at 16px/600 in --warn above the number. Move the sentry tag 24px above the sprite and use the same dark chip style as the other world tags. Keep damage numbers at 20px with a 2px dark outline.

findings.what: The 'player 1' bar at the left is a floating blue bar with no panel. The in-world 'player 1' tag is blue on a blue bar, which clashes with the amber P1 rule. The 'keyboard' chip at the top-left is a third chip style.
findings.fix: Make P1 amber and P2 cyan everywhere, in the same 16px/600 dark chip style. Give the 'keyboard' chip the same 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius.

findings.what: The purple tint over the whole map lowers contrast for the small grey text (slot numbers, '0%' fragment, 'f1 controls'). The '0%' fragment at the left edge is clipped.
findings.fix: Remove the clipped '0%' element or move it inside the 48px safe margin. Raise all slot numbers to --tx-1 at 16px so they reach 4.5:1 on the tint.

v.verdict: The scrim is now darker and blurred, but the card is still a small 558x255 box with an empty leaderboard, a bordered × and a tiny 'keyboard' tag, so little of the earlier advice was applied.

findings.where: empty state, 'no scores yet' and the dead space under the title
findings.what: The body is one small bold line of about 20px, left-aligned, with a divider below it. The card reads as unfinished. There are no ghost rows showing rank, name and sp, so nobody can tell what the screen is for.
findings.fix: Draw 3 to 5 ghost rows with rank, name and sp at 40% opacity and 1px --ui-line dividers. Centre 'no scores yet' in 20px --tx-2. Keep the gap between title and body at 24px.

findings.what: The card is far too small for 1080 couch viewing. It takes up about 17% of the screen width, and the title is only about 32px. The windows rule asks for a centred card at about 90% of the screen.
findings.fix: Enlarge the card to about 720x440, or 90% for the full list. Use 32px inner padding, a 4px radius and a --scrim of rgba(6,7,8,.80).

findings.what: It is a 48px bordered square with a tiny × glyph of about 12px. It competes with the title, and it duplicates the 'press any key' action, since walk-up screens continue on any key.
findings.fix: Drop the border and fill and draw a 16px --tx-2 × at a 24px inset. Show it only for mouse or touch input. Make a 32px hit area for those inputs.

findings.what: It is about 22px with a small lime radio-style dot. It is legible, but the dot looks like a radio button rather than a key glyph, and the prompt is quiet next to the title.
findings.fix: Set it at 24px 700 --tx-1 with a 24px lime key chip showing the device glyph. Pulse opacity from 70% to 100% over 1.5s. Align it to the same 32px inset as the title.

findings.what: It is a tiny, low-contrast tag of about 12px on a dark chip, clipped near the top edge. It is under the 14px floor and almost unreadable.
findings.fix: Set it at 14px --tx-2 on a --ui-panel chip with 8px padding, 24px from the top edge. Or fold it into the prompt as 'press any key (keyboard)'.

findings.where: card top edge, lime accent tick at x≈713 to 748
findings.what: A short 3px lime tick sits on the card border. It is not tied to anything, and it is easy to take for a rendering glitch.
findings.fix: Remove it. Alternatively, make it a full-width 3px lime bar across the card top. Do the same on every card so the look stays consistent.

findings.where: background, 'pillagers' wordmark at top-left and the dim lobby
findings.what: The wordmark stays visible at full brightness above the scrim, and the lobby is only half-dimmed. That makes busy art compete with the card.
findings.fix: Dim the wordmark under the scrim or keep it on every screen at a fixed size and place. Raise the blur to about 12px.

v.verdict: This is a clean, lower-case run-over card with a clear hero number and a visible live prompt, but the card is small and left-heavy, it repeats the score, and its type is undersized for a couch.

findings.what: The score shows twice, as the 56px team score '0 sp' and again as p1's '0 sp' directly below it. With one player the team score and p1's score are the same number, so the second one is clutter.
findings.fix: With one player, drop the p1 'score' column, or hide the team-score block. Show the team total only when there are two or more players (p1 and p2).

findings.what: The card is small for a 1080p couch screen, about 37% of the width. The content hugs the left edge, so the right half of the hero zone is empty, and the dark blurred scene behind it adds nothing.
findings.fix: Widen the card to about 960px (50% of the width) or tighten it to about 560px. Set the padding to 32px. Put the hero number and the stat row on one grid, with the stats spread across the full width.

findings.where: stat labels 'score / kills / extractions / deaths' and 'team score'
findings.what: The labels look about 16px in muted grey #aaa498 on a dark panel. Together with the dim stat grid, the stats read faintly from a couch, and the label-to-value spacing is cramped.
findings.fix: Keep the labels at 16px minimum with +.04em tracking, but use tx-1 at 80% (around #cfc9bc) or confirm 4.5:1 or better. Make the stat values 32px (--fs-title) instead of about 28px. Leave 8px between the number and its label.

findings.what: The prompt is a legitimate live primary action. It is only about 20px, right-aligned and separated from everything else, and the lime ring icon is small. The eye reaches it last, and the lime is the only accent on the card.
findings.fix: Raise it to 24px with the lime ring at 28px. Add a 16px gap before it, and consider centring it or putting it on the same baseline as the title row. Optionally pulse the ring (--m-med) to show it is live.

findings.what: The 32px title is bold and sits tight at the top-left. 'team score' directly under it is another small grey label, so the title, label and hero stack up with no clear spacing rhythm: about 24px between the title and 'team score', then 16px to the hero.
findings.fix: Put 24px below the title and 8px between the label and the hero number, so that 'team score' reads as the hero's caption. Align everything to the 8px grid.

findings.what: The 'p1' tag is amber, tiny (about 16px) and offset from its row. The row's top and bottom dividers are very faint (#2e3337), so the row looks unanchored and the p1 tag floats above the baseline of the values.
findings.fix: Align the tag to the baseline of the stat values. Use 20px f-cond 700 for it, and raise the divider lines to --ui-line-hi (#4a5257). Add 16px of vertical padding to the row.

findings.what: The card has a 1px, low-contrast border and a flat fill. The backdrop is blurred, with the scene still showing faintly, so the card does not lift off it. The look is generic: nothing in it says PILLAGERS.
findings.fix: Use --scrim at .80 for the backdrop, and give the card --ui-panel with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Add a 3px lime or extract-teal top bar on the card as an identity touch.

v.verdict: This is a clean, lower-case run-over card with a clear hero number and a live prompt. It is small and generic, the score appears twice, and the card is mostly empty space.

findings.what: The card is about 37% of the screen width and sits in the middle of a blurred, dimmed backdrop. It reads as a generic dark dialog, with no accent rule, no result state and no ARC Raiders or Destiny 2 hero treatment. The right half of the title and score area is empty.
findings.fix: Add a 4px lime or extract-teal bar on the card's top or left edge. Widen the card to about 960px, or move the hero score to the right in an 80px hero. Put the title and a short status word such as 'extracted' or 'kia' in the header row.

findings.where: hero 'team score 0 sp' vs the p1 row 'score 0 sp'
findings.what: The same figure is shown twice, and the second copy sits at nearly the same weight as the hero. With a single player, the 'p1' row adds no information and the eye splits between the two.
findings.fix: Drop the 'score' column from the player row, since the hero already carries it. Show the p1 row only when there are two or more players. Make the stat values 20px f-cond 600 in tx-1 and the labels 16px tx-2, so the 56px hero clearly dominates.

findings.what: The prompt is the primary action but is only about 20px text with a small ring glyph in the bottom-right corner. It is weak against the card and is far from the title and hero, which is where the eye starts.
findings.fix: Centre the prompt or span it across the bottom of the card. Use 24px lime (--acc) text and a pulse on the ring, with a divider above it and 24px padding. Make the ring 40px and keep it vertically centred on the text.

findings.what: At about 28px the title is smaller than the 32px --fs-title and barely heavier than the 20px stat values. The title and hero compete: the hero is about 50px against the title's 28px, and the title sits cramped at the top-left, 43px from the card top.
findings.fix: Set the title to 32px f-cond 700 and the hero to 56px f-cond 800. Use 24px top padding and put 24px between the title and the 'team score' label.

findings.what: The 'p1' tag is amber and about 18px, which is smaller than the values beside it. It is baseline-misaligned with the values: 'p1' sits at about y=581, which looks 2px high. The columns are spaced evenly but stop at x=1203, leaving a 80px dead gap before the right edge. The row dividers hug the text (the bottom line is 8px under the labels).
findings.fix: Make the p1 chip a 24px amber pill with ink text and centre it vertically against the value. Use four equal columns across the full 652px inner width. Add 16px padding above and below the divider.

findings.what: The labels are about 16px in tx-2 over a dark panel. They are legible, but at couch distance the thin condensed grey is the weakest text on screen, and the contrast looks borderline against the raised panel.
findings.fix: Keep 16px at +.04em tracking and raise the colour to #b8b2a6 or brighter. Check that it stays at or above 4.5:1. Bump the labels to 18px if the card is not widened.

findings.what: The blurred world behind the card is lit unevenly and has a visible outer frame, with lighter vertical bands at x≈155-200 and x≈1760. The scrim looks like a dim blur of a different screen rather than the --scrim .80 flat fill, so the page frame feels unfinished.
findings.fix: Use a flat rgba(6,7,8,.80) scrim over the full viewport with no blur, or one consistent blur. Make sure it covers the letterbox bands.

v.verdict: The modal is tidy and lower case, but it is a small, mostly empty card. 'no scores yet' is dim and tiny, the prompt is a little small, and a half-visible background lobby competes with the card.

findings.what: The empty state is about 16px, tx-2-like grey, and sits alone in a large void with no structure. It looks like a placeholder, not a designed empty state. The title row, body row and prompt row are spaced unevenly (about 80px between title and body, then about 40px to the divider).
findings.fix: Make the empty state 20px tx-1/tx-2 with ≥4.5:1 contrast. Set rows on the 8px grid (title 32, body 24 above and below). Or hide the card and show only the prompt, so no dead copy remains.

findings.what: This is the primary action on a walk-up screen, but at about 22px it is right-aligned at the bottom of the card, away from the eye's entry point. The title is the same weight, so the hierarchy is flat. The lime radio dot looks like a selectable option, not a key prompt.
findings.fix: Raise the prompt to a 32px hero-weight line (f-cond 700), centred or left-aligned under the title, and drop the radio-dot affordance for a key glyph. Add a gentle bounce pulse. Keep lime only on the dot or key glyph.

findings.what: The dimmed, blurred lobby with its glowing circles, characters and 'keyboard' tag still reads at about 30% and competes with the card. The 'pillagers' wordmark at top-left floats with no relation to the card. The tiny 'keyboard' chip at top-centre is almost illegible.
findings.fix: Raise the scrim to .80 per the guide (it looks near .55 now) and blur harder. Remove or enlarge the 'keyboard' chip to at least 16px with contrast ≥4.5:1.

findings.where: close x, top right of the card
findings.what: A boxed x button on a walk-up screen that continues on any key is a redundant control and adds clutter. Its 1px box also clashes with the card border. The title is vertically centred on it, but the x is about 48px tall, which crowds the title row.
findings.fix: Remove it here (any key continues). If kept, use a 40px target with a --ui-line-hi border and no box fill.

findings.what: The short 36px lime bar at the card's top-left is the only accent flourish. It looks like a stray artefact because it is offset about 0px from the title's left edge and has no counterpart.
findings.fix: Extend it to a 3px full-width top bar, or align it to the title's text left edge (x=713) and use it as the title underline.

findings.what: The card is about 556×255px on a 1920×1080 screen: too small and too thin to feel like the shipped 90% centred window. Inner padding is 32px, but the footer row has the least room beneath it (about 36px) and the divider is faint (#2e3337 on #16191b).
findings.fix: Enlarge the card to about 720px wide. Use 32px padding on all sides and a --ui-line-hi divider. Give the empty state a 48px minimum block.

findings.what: The title is 32px in f-cond but uses a curly apostrophe at a different weight, and nothing under it gives it meaning. The empty list gives the title nothing to head.
findings.fix: Add a column header (rank / name / sp) in 16px tx-2 or drop the title until scores exist.

v.verdict: A small, empty modal over a blurred lobby: the title, the empty-state line and the prompt are all about the same size, so nothing leads, and the card is tiny, generic and mostly dead space.

findings.what: The title 'tonight's best' (~32px), 'no scores yet' (~20px) and the prompt (~22px) are nearly the same weight and colour. The player-2 prompt is the primary action but is not the loudest thing. The lime ring bullet is the only accent.
findings.fix: Make the prompt 28-32px tx-1 with a bigger lime focus ring. Drop 'no scores yet' to 16px tx-2. Keep the title at 32px but not bold at the same time as the prompt, so only one thing is bold.

findings.what: The card is about 556x255px, roughly 29% of the screen width. The guide's windows are a centred card filling about 90% of the screen. It looks like a toast, not a window, and the rest of the screen is a busy blurred lobby.
findings.fix: Either use the 90% card or treat it as a small dialog and darken the scrim to .80 so the lobby sprites don't show through. Right now the lobby shows through at roughly .45.

findings.what: 'no scores yet' is a lone 16px line with a divider under it, then a blank band. It reads as unfinished: no empty-state structure, and nothing to show what a score row will look like.
findings.fix: Show 3 ghost rows (rank, name, sp) at 40% opacity, or drop the section and the divider and put the prompt in the body. Keep the padding at 24px on every side.

findings.what: The title left edge (x=713) and the close x (right edge 1207) give 32px padding, but the vertical rhythm is uneven: 18px above the title, 60px between the title and the empty line, and the prompt is right-aligned while everything else is left-aligned.
findings.fix: Use a 56px header and a 72px footer on the 8px grid. Put the prompt on the same left edge or centre it, and don't mix the two.

findings.what: The lime tick on the card's top-left edge (36x3px) is an orphaned decoration. It looks like a tab indicator for a tab that doesn't exist, and it competes with the lime prompt ring.
findings.fix: Remove it, or run it as a full-width 3px top rule. Reserve lime for focus, selected and the one action.

findings.what: The 'pillagers' wordmark top-left and the 'keyboard' chip at top centre (dark green on dark, about 1.5:1 contrast) are unreadable noise behind the modal. The blur still shows busy sprites and rings around the card edges.
findings.fix: Hide the chip, or set it to tx-2 at 16px with a 4.5:1 contrast. Raise the scrim to .80 and increase the blur so the card edge reads cleanly.

findings.what: The x button (48px square, thin grey border, ~12px glyph) is tiny and low-contrast. On a walk-up party screen where any key continues, it is a second, competing affordance.
findings.fix: Remove the x here, since any key continues. If you keep it, use a 20px glyph in tx-1 on --ui-line-hi.

v.verdict: The raid HUD is readable, but its panels sit on top of each other, the feed line is cut off, and the pieces use different sizes, fills and accent colours, so it reads as unfinished.

findings.where: top-centre stack: clock, team score, extract chip
findings.what: The team score card butts straight into the clock card, and its 'you 0 sp / p2 0 sp' column is pushed against the right edge with almost no padding. The lines 'you 0 sp' and 'p2 0 sp' are also cramped together. The clock, sun icon, score card and extract chip have three different widths and no shared left edge or gap rhythm.
findings.fix: Give the stack one 8px grid with 8px gaps between cards. Use 16px inner padding on the score card. Put 'you' and 'p2' on separate rows with an 8px gap, or turn them into a two-column row. Make the extract chip the same width as the score card, or centre both on the clock.

findings.where: left feed line 'select a heal · bandage, medkit or armour p...'
findings.what: The line is cut off with an ellipsis, which makes it look broken. It is a sentence that explains something, and the guide treats explaining sentences as clutter. The white bar on its left edge is jammed against the screen edge, and the pill is wider than the text needs.
findings.fix: Shorten the text to something like 'heal: pick a bandage or medkit' that fits. Better, drop it. Add 24px of left margin (5% safe area) and put the bar inside the pill with 8px padding.

findings.where: bottom HUD: hp bar, 'f1 controls', hotbar, ammo card
findings.what: The bottom row has no common baseline or margin. The hp bar is flush with the left and bottom screen edges. The hp text sits on top of the bar with its glyphs touching the bar's top edge. The 'f1 controls' chip floats alone mid-left, and it is not mid-bottom as the owner ordered. The hotbar slots 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 0 are bare numbers with no tile, so they look like debris on the wall. The ammo card has a different panel size and treatment from the hotbar.
findings.fix: Set a 48px left and bottom margin. Make the hp bar 24px tall with 16px text inside it. Render empty slots as dim 4px-radius tiles at the same 96px size. Dock 'f1 controls' on the hotbar's baseline, left of slot 1, as a 16px label. Align the ammo card's bottom edge with the hotbar's.

findings.what: The eye lands first on the 10:00 clock and the 30/60 ammo card, which are both near-white hero numbers with similar weight, and then on the bright cyan extract chip. The hp bar is a flat green block that looks like a progress bar with no hierarchy. The team score '0 sp' is the same weight as the clock. The accent is not used consistently: the selected slot is amber/orange, the extract chip is teal, and the hp bar is green. Nothing in the HUD uses lime for 'selected'.
findings.fix: Keep one hero per area: the timer at 56px/800 and the ammo count at 56px. Drop the score to 32px/700 and the sub-scores to 16px muted (--tx-2). Follow the guide: P1 amber is allowed for the player ring, but keep the selected-slot outline consistent with the rest of the game's 'selected' treatment.

findings.where: minimap and goals chip, top right
findings.what: The minimap has a thick border and cut-off dashed shapes along its top edge. A tiny icon cluster ('n' and arrows) overlaps the corner, so it looks like an overlap bug. 'goals 0/3' is a separate pill of a different height with a chevron, and it is attached to the minimap with a hairline gap. The minimap's right edge is flush with the screen edge.
findings.fix: Add a 24px right and top margin. Clip the icon cluster inside the map frame, with 8px padding from the edge. Join the goals strip to the minimap as one panel, with a shared border and an 8px radius or less (4px by the guide).

findings.what: The panels do not look like one family. The clock, score card and ammo card are near-black with a large radius, the feed pill is lighter with a left bar, the hotbar tiles are dark with an amber outline, and the hp bar is a flat colour with no frame. Several have soft shadows, and corners are 4, 8 and 12px.
findings.fix: Use one panel recipe: --ui-panel #16191b fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, no drop shadow. Use the same recipe on the clock, score, ammo, feed, goals and hotbar tiles.

findings.what: 'compact smg' is right-aligned at about 28px, but '30 / 60' mixes a huge 30 with a smaller muted '/ 60'. The two numbers' baselines do not match, and the 24px padding on the card is uneven (the left side is much emptier than the right).
findings.fix: Use 20px for the weapon name and the 56px hero for '30', with '/ 60' at 32px in tx-2 sharing its baseline. Pad the card 16px on all sides and shrink it to fit the content, or left-align the text.

findings.what: The feed line and the hotbar number labels (1, 2, 3...) are small and thin against the busy ground, so they are hard to read. The slot numbers 3 to 0 are low contrast, and the controls hint chip text is near the 16px minimum. This does not meet the 1080 couch-readability bar.
findings.fix: Put every number label on a --ui-panel 80% plate. Use 16px/600 text minimum with --tx-1 for the active slot and --tx-2 for the others. Increase the chip's text to 20px.

v.verdict: Only the OLD screenshot was supplied, with no path for the NEW one, so this scores the old frame and cannot compare; the frame is a cluttered mix of boxed HUD pieces with no shared grammar, and its one bold element, the ammo count, sits in the corner.

findings.where: top-centre stack (timer, team score, extract pill)
findings.what: Three differently sized boxes are stacked with no shared width, and the team score box overlaps the timer's sun icon and the building behind it. 'you 0 sp' and 'p2 0 sp' crowd the box's right edge, and the p2 line touches the bottom border. The big '0 sp' competes with the 10:00 timer as the eye's first hit. A pad-only party also gets no separate readout of the second player's score.
findings.fix: Build one 320px-wide panel on the --ui-panel fill with 16px padding and 8px gaps: timer at --fs-hero 56, then a 16px label row. Move the per-player scores into one 16px line in amber (P1) and cyan (P2), and drop the second '0 sp' hero.

findings.what: The teal pill is correct as an extraction-only colour, but it is a third box in the stack with its own radius and a different width. The teal arrow hangs below it and floats over scenery rather than pointing at the extraction.
findings.fix: Fold the pill into the top panel as a 16px teal row, and move the arrow out to the screen-edge compass at 24px. Use --rad 4 on every box.

findings.what: The slot row is inconsistent: slot 1 and the two weapon slots are filled boxes, while slots 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 0 are bare grey digits on the road texture and read as noise. Slot 2's selected state is an amber outline, but lime (--acc) is the 'selected' colour. The slot numbers sit at about 14px and the ammo '60' is tiny and tight against the slot edge.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots at 72x72 with a --ui-panel fill and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Mark the selected slot with a 2px --acc border. Set slot numbers and ammo at 16px --tx-1 with 8px inset, and dim empty slots to 40% opacity instead of showing bare digits.

findings.what: The '30 / 60' is a large number set in a heavy weight and works as the hero. But the panel is much larger than anything else, its right edge is clipped against the screen edge with under 10px of margin, and the weapon name is at about 28px, which competes with it.
findings.fix: Cut the panel to about 240x120 with a 5% (96px) right and bottom margin to match the 8px grid. Set the name at --fs-label 16 in --tx-2 and keep the '30' as the single 56px 800-weight hero.

findings.what: A flat green bar with 'hp 100' laid on top in a large condensed face. The text is bigger than the bar needs, has little contrast against the green, and the bar sits 24px from the left edge while the ammo panel sits about 10px from the right, so the margins are asymmetric. Nothing else in the HUD is green.
findings.fix: Make the bar 320x16 with a --ui-panel track, set 'hp 100' at 16px above it, and use the same 96px margins as the ammo panel. Use --ok green only for the fill.

findings.where: left feed 'select a ... · bandage, medkit or armour plate.'
findings.what: A hint truncated with '...' reads as broken. It sits flush at x=22 with a lime-ish edge tick, its text is mixed in size, and it explains a control in a sentence, which counts as clutter. It also sits in the left margin well away from the controls hint and the hp bar.
findings.fix: Shorten the line to 'select a heal' or remove it. Align its left edge to the 96px margin and set it at 16px with a 4px --acc bar only when it is actionable.

findings.what: The minimap is a large black void with white bars drawn as coloured rails and lime icons, and its tiny markers are about 8px, illegible from a couch. The chevron at top-right sits on the white bar. The goals tab is a second box with a different radius, its text is larger than the bottom feed text, and it hugs the minimap with no gap.
findings.fix: Shrink the minimap to 240x160 with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Draw markers at 12px minimum. Add an 8px gap to goals and set 'goals 0/3' at 16px. When cw-trcol ships, keep this corner out of other screen tasks.

findings.what: The chip floats at screen-centre-left over the wall texture, at about 22px type with a small key-cap, and is not aligned to the hotbar or hp bar. Its grey-on-grey fill gives low contrast against the road, and it is not in the mid-bottom-left position the owner set (folded to one short line).
findings.fix: Pin it at x=96, aligned to the hotbar's baseline, on a --ui-panel fill at 16px --tx-2, with the 'f1' key-cap on --ui-raised.

v.verdict: The HUD is readable and mostly calm, with a clear ammo hero number and a clean lower-case feed line. But the team score panel is cramped and overlaps the timer and extract chips, the feed text is cut off, and the corners are crowded and inconsistent.

findings.what: The card has a cramped 3-line layout. 'you 0 sp' and 'p1 0 sp' sit tight against the right edge and the card's bottom edge, and the card overlaps the timer's lower edge and a building behind it. The hero '0 sp' is off-centre against the 'team score' label. Two scores in different positions (you and p1) look like duplicates, and the score is not obviously the hero.
findings.fix: Make the card 320px wide with 16px padding. Put 'team score' (16px, tx-2) on top and '0 sp' (hero 56px, centred) below. Put the per-player rows (16px) on one line beneath, amber for P1 and cyan for P2. Leave an 8px gap under the timer, with no overlap.

findings.where: left feed line 'select a heal · bandage, medkit or armour p...'
findings.what: The text is truncated with an ellipsis, so the item list is cut mid-word. It also reads as an explaining sentence, which is clutter. A white bar at the left edge sits flush against the screen edge, with no margin. The hint is hidden next to the 'f1 controls' chip.
findings.fix: Shorten it to 'select a heal' and drop the item list, or widen the box so it never truncates. Inset the box 5% from the screen edge (about 48px) and use a 4px radius. Move the 'f1 controls' chip to the same left edge and align it with the feed.

findings.what: The minimap markers are clipped and overlap at the top edge, with an 'n' glyph jammed against the icons. The minimap's lower half is a black void. The collapse chevron sits in the corner over map content. The goals chip is a different size, weight and border from every other panel.
findings.fix: Inset the minimap's markers 8px from its border and move the 'n' compass letter to a fixed corner slot. Crop or fill the empty black area. Give the goals chip the same fill and 4px radius as the timer and score panels, 16px label text, and a 48px margin to the screen edge.

findings.what: Slots 3 and 5-0 are bare floating digits with no slot frame, while slots 1, 2 and 4 are boxes. The row looks unfinished. Digits in dim grey over a light wall have poor contrast. The 'f' badge on slot 4 is a tiny unexplained glyph. The selected slot uses a gold border, which clashes with lime meaning 'selected'.
findings.fix: Draw all 6 slots as 72px frames with a 1px --ui-line-hi border on the --ui-panel fill, and keep empty ones at 40% alpha. Use the lime --acc 2px border for the selected slot only. Use 16px numerals in tx-2. Make the 'f' badge 16px with a panel chip behind it.

findings.what: The 'hp 100' label is drawn over the green bar with weak contrast (white on mid-green). The bar sits flush at the screen edge (x≈24, y≈1035), so the 5% margin is ignored. It is also very plain and has no panel, so it does not match the ammo card on the right.
findings.fix: Put the hp bar in a 4px-radius --ui-panel card with 16px padding, and inset it 48px from the left and bottom edges. Put the label in tx-1 at 20px on the dark panel, and the number on the right side at 32px. Use --ok for the fill.

findings.what: The 'keyboard' tag in the top-left corner is small (about 14px), is clipped against the edge, and is the only element in that corner. It looks like debug text and has a different border from the other panels.
findings.fix: Remove it in the shipped HUD, or move it into the 16px footer legend. If kept, give it the same 4px radius and panel fill and inset it by 24px.

findings.what: The teal 'extract 141m' chip is tight to the score card above it (about 4px gap) and the pointer arrow floats loose below. The chip text is about 22px, a different size from the other chips. The row of stacked panels (timer, score, extract) has inconsistent widths (165px, 305px, 165px).
findings.fix: Use an 8px vertical gap throughout. Align the three centre panels to a common 320px width or centre them on a shared axis. Use 20px f-cond text for the extract chip, in --extract on --ui-panel, and attach the arrow 8px below it.

findings.what: The ammo card is the strongest element (hero '30 / 60'), but it competes with the timer for the first look. It is also too heavy: the weapon name floats in the top-right, '60' reserve is the same weight as the magazine, and the card's right edge is 10px from the screen edge, which breaks the margin.
findings.fix: Inset the card 48px from the right and bottom edges. Set the magazine count at 56px/800 and the reserve at 32px/600 in tx-2, and the weapon name at 20px tx-1. Give the card the standard 16px padding.

v.verdict: Only the OLD screenshot was supplied and no NEW image path was given, so no comparison is possible; this score is for the old HUD, which is cluttered and inconsistent in type and alignment.

findings.what: The NEW screenshot was not provided, only img-23884-1.jpg (the OLD one), so nothing can be compared.
findings.fix: Resend with the NEW image path, such as o09f-p2-feed-after-1080.jpg.

findings.where: top-centre score card (team score / 0 sp / you 0 sp / p1 0 sp)
findings.what: The card has three competing readouts. 'you 0 sp' and 'p1 0 sp' sit tight against the card's right edge and the bottom edge, which crowds them. The 'p1' label is cryptic, and the card overlaps the base of the clock card above it. The result is no clear hierarchy.
findings.fix: Show one 56px hero number only. Move per-player values to a 16px label row with 16px padding. Leave an 8px gap between the clock card and the score card. Use the P1 amber and P2 cyan player colours for the labels.

findings.where: left feed line 'select a ... · bandage, medkit or armour plate.'
findings.what: The text is truncated with '...', which looks broken. It is also an explaining sentence, which the owner counts as clutter. The info icon, the left accent bar and the dim background are weakly contrasted, and the line is flush against the screen edge at x≈20.
findings.fix: Shorten it to 'pick an item' or drop it. Never truncate with an ellipsis. Inset it 48px from the screen edge and use 20px tx-1 text on a --ui-panel fill.

findings.where: HUD type scale (clock, goals, f1 controls, hp, slot numbers, ammo)
findings.what: The sizes are not on the 56/32/20/16/14 scale. The hp bar text, the 'f1 controls' chip, the slot numerals and the goals text all use different sizes and weights, and the key-hint chip styling differs from the 'keyboard' chip in the top-left.
findings.fix: Snap every label to 16px f-cond 600 with +.04em tracking and every value to 20px. Reserve 56px for the ammo count only. Use one shared key-chip style.

findings.where: bottom-left hp bar and 'f1 controls' chip
findings.what: The hp bar is a plain green fill with the text jammed on its left edge and no panel, border or padding. It does not match the rounded, bordered panels used elsewhere. The 'f1 controls' chip floats alone at x≈395, disconnected from the hp bar and the hotbar.
findings.fix: Put the hp bar in a --ui-panel container with a 4px radius, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 8px padding and 20px text. Tie the controls hint to the mid-bottom-left spec with 16px muted text, aligned to the same left margin as the hp bar.

findings.what: The numerals for the empty slots float directly on the terrain with no slot frames. The selected slot's amber border competes with the lime accent rule. The 'f' badge on slot 4 is tiny and unexplained, and the spacing between slots is uneven.
findings.fix: Draw all ten slots as equal 72px frames on an 8px gap. Make the selected slot --acc (lime) with a 2px border. Draw empty slots at 40% opacity inside the frame, and set slot badges at 14px minimum.

findings.what: The minimap is a dark void with no readable labels, and part of it is clipped or empty. The chevrons are tiny and the goals text is large against its thin bar, so the goals bar and the minimap don't read as one panel. The owner has ordered a 1-by-1 vertical HUD column for this corner.
findings.fix: Frame the map and goals bar as one panel with a shared 1px border and 4px radius. Set the goals text to 16px. Put it in the cw-trcol vertical list at 48px from the screen edge.

findings.what: This is the strongest element, but its right edge hugs the screen edge with only about 10px of margin. The '/ 60' reserve count is heavy and nearly as large as the current count. The card also overlaps the terrain without the --scrim treatment used elsewhere.
findings.fix: Inset the card 48px from the right and bottom edges. Set the weapon name at 16px muted, '30' at 56px weight 800, and '/ 60' at 20px tx-2. Use the same 4px radius as the other cards.

v.verdict: A dim, flat racks tab that fills a 90 percent card with about 40 percent content, where every button is greyed, small explanatory paragraphs sit on screen, and the teal headline and the dev-voice copy fight the style guide.

findings.what: The copy reads 'this is some wild idea claude came up with', which is dev or AI chatter shown to players. It is a long explaining paragraph, and the guide treats both as defects. It also breaks the straight-copy rule and the identity of the game.
findings.fix: Delete the paragraph. If one hint is needed, use a single 16px tx-2 line such as 'import a friend's run report', with no more than 60 characters.

findings.what: The eye lands on the teal '0 of 10 racks' at 32px, which is the only coloured element. The main actions are dim grey and have no hero or lime primary. 'build a rack', 'fold 10 racks' and 'core slotted' all look disabled, with grey text on a grey fill at about 3:1, so the player can't tell which action is live. Teal is reserved for extraction only.
findings.fix: Change the counter to tx-1 at 32px, or use --acc only if it is the selected state. Make 'build a rack' the one lime primary button (--acc fill, --acc-ink text, 20px, 600) when it is affordable. Show disabled buttons at 40 percent opacity with a --ui-line border and no fill, so enabled and disabled read differently. Show the cost as a 16px tx-2 line.

findings.where: layout, y≈600-1020 and the left/right margins
findings.what: The card is 90 percent of the screen but the content stops at y=585. The bottom 45 percent is empty, and the content block is offset (x=289 to 1631) instead of aligned to the header margin at x=119. The two columns are unequal and the rack slots overhang to the right. The result looks unfinished.
findings.fix: Left-align the content to the 119px header margin and use a two-column grid with 24px gaps. Put the rack slots in the left column at 64px each. Fill the right column and the bottom with real content, or shrink the card height to fit.

findings.what: The ten empty slots are bare 1px outlines in near-black on near-black, so they read as broken boxes. They have no fill, no index and no empty-state glyph. They are 64px wide but have a 8px gap while the counter text sits 24px away with no alignment to the columns below.
findings.fix: Fill each slot with --ui-panel and a --ui-line-hi border at 4px radius. Add a 16px tx-2 index number to each slot, and fill built slots with --acc. Align the row's left edge with the 'build a rack' column.

findings.what: The cost sentence is in 14-15px grey (about 4:1) and wraps with an orphaned 'board (0 held).'. It is parenthetical noise: '(0 held)' appears four times. It is under the 16px minimum and needs an explaining sentence to be read.
findings.fix: Replace it with four 16px chips, for example 'scrap metal 0/12', 'copper wire 0/9', 'cracked cell 0/6' and 'circuit board 0/6'. Use tx-1 when held and --danger when short. Put them in one row of equal gaps of 8px.

findings.what: '$900', '0', 'xp' and 'stash $0 bag $0' use three sizes and weights in one row, with uneven gaps and a tiny 'xp' baseline-shifted. The cluster crowds the close button at 1760 and competes with the title.
