findings.fix: Use one size, 20px f-cond 600, for every item with 16px tx-2 labels, a 24px gap between items and a 24px gap before the close button. Vertically centre the cluster on the 48px close button.

findings.what: 'core slotted: next raid intel / 1 packed data core used' sits in a flat bordered box. It is a different size and font weight (f-body) from the rest of the screen, and it overlaps the card edge at y=40-56. The text contains a '/' separator and explains itself twice, and the toast duplicates the 'core slotted, burns on ascent' button state.
findings.fix: Use f-cond 20px, a --ui-raised fill, 4px radius and a 3px --ok left bar, placed with at least 16px clearance above the card. Shorten the text to 'core slotted' and keep the button label as the state.

findings.where: tabs row and 'import a friend' input (y≈160, 283-347)
findings.what: The tabs are 16px muted text with only a thin lime underline for the active one. No tab has a visible pad-focus state. The 'friend's name' input and 'import a friend' button are in a dark panel with the strongest weight on screen (bold white), which makes a secondary social feature louder than the core build action.
findings.fix: Make the tabs 20px with the active tab in tx-1 and a 3px --acc underline, and show a --ui-raised pill with a lime border on focus. Move the friend import below the build column in a quieter section, and make the import button an idle outline (--ui-line-hi, 600) rather than bold.

v.verdict: The screen is flat and mostly empty. Every button looks disabled, the one accent is teal instead of lime, and a leaked developer sentence plus duplicated cost copy hurt it badly.

findings.what: The copy reads 'this is some wild idea claude came up with...'. It is a leaked dev or AI note, a long explaining paragraph, and it breaks the straight-copy rule.
findings.fix: Delete it. Replace it with a one-line label of at most 40 characters, such as 'import a run report', at 16px tx-2. Drop the 'claude' reference entirely.

findings.where: toast at top, plus the cost paragraph under 'build a rack'
findings.what: The same cost list ('12 scrap metal (0 held)...') is drawn twice. The toast is a full-width 20px sentence with no clear role, and the paragraph is an explaining sentence that repeats it. Both are clutter.
findings.fix: Show the cost once, as four item chips (icon, count needed, held count) under the button, with held counts in --danger when short. Delete the paragraph. Shorten the toast to 'not enough parts' or remove it.

findings.where: build a rack, fold 10 racks, slot a data core
findings.what: All three actions are identical dim grey bars at around 3:1 contrast. None reads as the primary action and none is clearly disabled rather than idle, so the hierarchy is flat. A pad-focus state is also not visible.
findings.fix: Make 'build a rack' the one --acc primary, or a clear disabled state with a 4.5:1 label and a cost chip. Keep the other two as outlined secondary buttons with a --ui-line-hi border. Show a 3px lime focus bar on the focused one.

findings.where: '0 of 10 racks' and the 10 empty slots
findings.what: The teal heading (--extract, which is reserved for extraction) is the loudest element on the screen and has nothing to do with extraction. The 10 slots are empty black squares with no fill, icon or lit state, so they read as dead boxes. The teal also competes with the lime tab underline.
findings.fix: Set the count in tx-1 at 32px, or use --acc for the filled count only. Fill the slots with --ui-panel and a 1px --ui-line border, and light built slots with an --acc bar. Use 48px slots with a 16px gap.

findings.what: About 40% of the card is empty. The content is a narrow centred block (x 289 to 1631) that matches neither the header's left edge at x=119 nor the right edge, so the layout feels unanchored and unfinished.
findings.fix: Align the content to the 119px header margin. Use a two-column grid, with left 560px for the rack grid and actions and right for the import panel, set inside --ui-panel cards with a --rad of 4px. Move the actions to the bottom footer row or fill the space with a rack detail pane.

findings.what: The 24px bold $900 and the 0 xp use mismatched sizes and weights. The 'stash $0 bag $0' text is tiny at about 14px and reads as muddy grey at couch distance. The three groups have uneven spacing, and the 'xp' unit is smaller and sits on a lower baseline.
findings.fix: Use one 20px f-cond 600 for all three values with 16px tx-2 labels, on a shared baseline, with a 24px gap between groups. Add a thin --ui-line divider before the close button.

findings.where: tabs row and the friend's name input
findings.what: The tab labels are about 16px with weak contrast, and the active state is only a thin underline. The input has a different border and height from the buttons, and its placeholder is as bright as a real value.
findings.fix: Set tabs to 20px, with the active tab in tx-1 and a 3px --acc underline. Dim the placeholder to --tx-2 and match the input's border and height to the buttons (64px, --ui-line-hi).

v.verdict: The HUD tells you what it needs to, but the controls panel is a large always-open block that covers the left of the map, a toast is clipped behind it, and type sizes and panel styles vary from corner to corner.

findings.where: centre-left toast 'bandage, medkit or armour plate'
findings.what: The toast starts underneath the controls panel, so its first letter is cut off and it reads 'andage'. It also floats over the wall with no anchor.
findings.fix: Centre the toast on the screen and give it a z-index above the controls panel. Alternatively, anchor it above the hotbar at about y=900. Give it 16px padding and a 1px --ui-line-hi border.

findings.what: The panel is open at about 300x300px. Per the guide it should be one folded line, bottom-centre-left, that F1 opens. It is the biggest block on screen and covers the map, and its dense three-column key and label grid pulls the eye away from the action.
findings.fix: Fold it to a single line of about 40px height at x≈48, y≈1000, with text like 'f1 controls'. Open it only on F1. If it must stay open, cut it to 6 rows and make the labels 16px --tx-2.

findings.what: Section headers ('move', 'gear', 'fight', 'raid') and the 'f1 full list' line are about 14px dim grey on near-black. They sit under the 16px floor for anything read. The key caps and labels are also tightly packed, with a row pitch of about 24px.
findings.fix: Use 16px minimum, --tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better, row pitch 32px, and 16px gaps between groups.

findings.where: top-left 'current pillagers' panel versus top-right 'run info'
findings.what: The two panels use different widths, different headers and different chrome (a caret at the right of each header). The 14-15px text is very small for couch reading at 1080. The $ values are right-aligned but there is no hierarchy, so 'you' does not stand out and the largest risk figure ($3,950) is not emphasised.
findings.fix: Set rows to 16px with 32px row height and the same panel fill, border and 4px radius as run info. Mark 'you' with a 3px lime or amber bar. Align both panels to the 48px margin.

findings.what: '15:00' is about 28px in the hero slot, and the extract chip below it is small teal text. The bottom-right 'c 152m' chip repeats the same distance, so the line is drawn twice, which the owner's one-place rule forbids. The timer is also not clearly the hero element at 56px.
findings.fix: Remove one of the two distance readouts and keep the teal 'extract 152m' chip at 20px. Raise the timer to the 56px hero size, weight 800.

findings.where: bottom-left status row (hp bar, concealed, in cover)
findings.what: Two oversized pill chips, 'concealed' and 'in cover', sit in yellow-green and teal and look like extra buttons. They compete with the hp bar, and 'hp 40' is large, outlined lettering that mixes styles. The hp bar is amber but hp is not tied to any player colour.
findings.fix: Set the chips at 16px label size, with a 4px radius and a 1px border instead of a fill. Set 'hp 40' at 32px in --f-cond 700 without an outline. Put a 24px gap between the icons and the chips.

findings.what: The '12 / 24' ammo is well placed as the hero element. But 'b / i backpack' is about 13px, below the 14px fine minimum, and the weapon name is right-aligned while the numbers are crowded to the card's right edge with only a 10px inner margin.
findings.fix: Use 16px for the backpack hint, 24px of inner padding, and align the weapon name and numbers to the same right edge.

findings.what: Slot numbers 3-0 float over the map with no frame, and ghost weapon silhouettes are barely visible. The selected slot has a bright amber outline while slot 2 has none, so the row looks unfinished. The slot numbers are about 14px with low contrast.
findings.fix: Give empty slots a 1px --ui-line-hi frame on a --ui-panel fill at 60% opacity. Raise the numbers to 16px --tx-2. Keep the lime or amber outline for the selected slot only.

v.verdict: The raid HUD uses the right tokens, but the open controls list, a clipped tooltip and a crowded set of boxes make it look unfinished.

findings.where: Left side, tooltip 'andage, medkit or armour plate'
findings.what: The tooltip starts under the controls panel, so the first letter is cut off and it reads 'andage'. It also floats in the middle of the map with nothing tying it to an item or key.
findings.fix: Draw it above the controls panel, or move it to the left feed. Keep it at least 16px clear of the panel (x≥340). Anchor it to the hotbar slot or the item it explains. Fix the clipping at the source rather than patching the text.

findings.what: The list is fully open and 300px wide, with 20 key rows and 4 group headings. This contradicts the rule that in a career raid it starts folded to one short line, mid-bottom left, opened with F1. It is the biggest block on screen and competes with the game view. The 'move' and 'gear' columns line up poorly with the 'fight' and 'raid' groups below them.
findings.fix: Start it folded to one line ('f1 controls'), 16px text, at the bottom-left, above the status chips. When opened, use two aligned columns with equal group gaps of 16px, and keep it at or below 240px wide.

findings.what: There are too many separate boxes, each with a different fill, border and corner radius: the pillagers list, the run info dropdown, the extract chip, the 'c 152m' chip, the controls panel, the tooltip, the contract banner, the status chips, the hotbar and the ammo card. Nothing groups them, so the screen looks scattered and template-like. The top-left list is also a table with two columns. The names are tiny and low-contrast against the pale 'value at risk' header.
findings.fix: Standardise on --ui-panel at 85% opacity, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Merge 'extract 152m' and 'c 152m' into one element, since it shows the same number twice. Use 16px type for the pillagers list rows. Keep a 16px gap between panels.

findings.where: Bottom-left, hp 40 bar and chips 'concealed' / 'in cover'
findings.what: The hp bar is 405px wide and hugs the screen edge (x=24, bottom at about 1068). Its yellow fill matches the contract banner and the active hotbar slot, so amber is used for hp, a notice and focus. The 'hp 40' text is in a heavy outline font that doesn't match the other labels. The amber 'concealed' text sits next to the teal 'in cover', so two status colours compete for attention. The circular icons beside them are too small to tell apart.
findings.fix: Keep the margin at 5% of the screen, about 48px from the bottom and left. Make hp a 56px hero number or a plain 20px label, not outlined text. Use --danger below 30 hp and --ok when healthy. Use one chip style for both status chips with a 16px label, and keep the icons at 24px.

findings.where: Contract banner, 'contract item nearby · gold glow marks the box'
findings.what: This is an explaining sentence on screen, and the second half ('gold glow marks the box') is exactly the kind of instruction the owner calls clutter. The banner also overlaps the roofline and sits close to the pool area, so it reads as dropped on top of the map. The yellow icon and bar mimic the focus accent.
findings.fix: Cut it to 'contract item nearby'. Place it in the left feed with the warn glyph rather than --acc. Remove the gold-glow sentence.

findings.what: Slots 3 to 0 are faint numerals with ghosted gun icons that look like leftover placeholders. Their contrast is below 4.5:1, and slot 2 shows a glove icon that reads as unclear. The row also floats off-centre at the bottom of the screen, not aligned to the ammo card or the hp bar.
findings.fix: Show only owned slots, or draw empty slots at a consistent 40% opacity with a 1px --ui-line outline. Raise the slot numbers to 16px --tx-2. Centre the row, or align its baseline to the ammo card (bottom 48px).

findings.where: Top-right 'run info' dropdown and the zone label 'the long dock cache'
findings.what: The 'run info' bar is a 300px dark strip with a chevron, and it overlaps the building edge. 'the long dock cache' is lavender text with no backing, sitting over a busy tile floor at about 20px, with weak contrast. It also introduces a third accent colour (purple) that the palette doesn't assign to place names.
findings.fix: Give the place label a --ui-panel backing, or move it under the clock. Use --tx-1 for it, not lavender. Align the 'run info' panel to the 48px margin and keep it the same width as other panels. Show a shorter value than the chevron alone suggests, or put the info on one line.

findings.what: The card is a good hero-number treatment, with '12 / 24' at about 56px. But the '/ 24' is much dimmer and is set in the same size. The 'b / i backpack' hint is 14px and very low contrast. The card also runs close to the screen edge, 10px from the bottom and right, while the other HUD items are about 24px in.
findings.fix: Keep the 56px current-ammo number and set the reserve at 32px in --tx-2. Raise the hint to 16px, or remove it, since backpack is already in the controls list. Move the card to the 48px margin.

v.verdict: This is a different screen from the rack card I reviewed before, so I can't judge whether that advice was followed. As a hub it has a strong 'enter raid!' label, but the bottom stack is crowded, the top-right HUD is tiny and scattered, and there are overlaps and stray text throughout.

findings.where: bottom centre, y≈850-1065: toast, controls strip and hotbar stacked
findings.what: The toast sentence 'core slotted: next raid intel / 1 packed data core used' sits on top of the controls strip, which sits on top of a 9-slot hotbar. The three have a 3-10px gap, three different box styles and three different type sizes. The toast is an explaining sentence and uses a '/' separator. The hotbar is crowded with 7 greyed-out weapon silhouettes that carry no information.
findings.fix: Delete the controls strip in the hub, or fold it into one 16px tx-2 line. Move the toast above the stack with a 24px gap, with 16px tx-1 text on --ui-panel, and shorten it to 'core slotted'. Show only the owned hotbar slots, and keep the empty ones at 40% opacity with no icon.

findings.where: top-right HUD, y≈20-40: '$900  0 xp  stash $0 bag $0'
findings.what: This is a loose one-line row on the dark void. '$900' is about 22px bold, '0' is about 22px, 'xp' is about 12px, and 'stash/bag' is about 14px dim. It has three sizes, no panel, and 'xp' falls below the 14px floor. It conflicts with the settled vertical 1 by 1 list for the career HUD. The 'stash $0 bag $0' line is also redundant with the 'the undercroft' card, which already says '0 items in stash'.
findings.fix: Build it as the cw-trcol vertical list: each row 20px f-cond 600, tx-1 value with a 16px tx-2 label, rows 32px apart, right-aligned to the 5% margin (96px). Remove 'stash $0 bag $0' or merge it into the title card.

findings.what: This is an explaining or warning sentence in a stray 14px amber box, wrapped in asterisks. It sits directly under 'the last pour' and covers the character and the station. The asterisks look like a template wink, and the box has a different fill and border from the other labels.
findings.fix: Delete it. If a flag is needed, use a 16px --warn word 'beta' inside the 'the last pour' label, with no asterisks and no second box.

findings.where: station labels versus characters: 'the last pour', 'the stash', 'fashion' and 'shop, craft, and hire'
findings.what: Labels overlap player sprites. The purple character sits on the 'the last pour' label, one character stands under 'the stash', and a figure is cut by the 'fashion' label. The mainframe zone has a second overlapping circle at about (1440, 275) that produces a doubled ring. The result looks messy rather than designed.
findings.fix: Place every label at a fixed 12px above the pad ring and draw it above the sprites with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Remove the stray second zone circle. Give each station a single 2px ring.

findings.what: It is the correct first read, with 56px lime on a dark chip. But the '!' is the shouty arcade tone the guide rules out. The chip is a different size and border from the other station labels, and it floats over the pillar tops. It has no key prompt, so the player does not know what triggers it.
findings.fix: Use 'enter raid' with no '!'. Put it in a --ui-panel chip with a 1px --acc border and 8px padding. Add a 16px tx-2 'e' key hint beneath it, 8px away.

findings.what: Slot 1 has an amber outline and slot 2 holds a duplicate fist. The slot numbers are about 12px and dim. Slot 1 has a warm fill while the other slots are flat dark, and the slots are not 8px-grid aligned (about 112 by 104 with an uneven pitch).
findings.fix: Use equal 96px square slots with 8px gaps. Put 16px tx-2 index numbers in the top-left at 8px inset. Show the selected state as a 2px --acc border only. Collapse the duplicate fist slot.

findings.what: The card is good but small. Its second line, '0 items in stash · 0 runs', is about 13px and dim, which is under the 16px floor. The '·' separator and the 0-count phrasing add clutter.
findings.fix: Set the sub-line to 16px tx-2. Show it as two short stat pairs, 'stash 0' and 'runs 0'. Align the card's left edge to the 96px margin.

findings.where: the black bars left and right of the map (x<157 and x>1763), and the grey wall frame
findings.what: The playfield does not fill the 16:9 frame. The pillarboxed black areas, plus the washed-out lavender wall border, make the screen feel unfinished. The HUD text on the right sits on the void at an arbitrary position.
findings.fix: Extend the floor and background art to the screen edges, or darken the wall frame to --ui-bg and align the HUD to the 96px margin inside the frame.

v.verdict: The in-raid HUD is clean and the one-place-per-line rule holds, with a good hero ammo number. But several elements are tiny, the pickup card is a crowded two-colour sentence, and the player-list panel and the 'run info' dropdown don't match each other or the rest of the HUD.

findings.where: bottom-centre toast 'select a heal · bandage, medkit or armour plate'
findings.what: An explaining sentence sits mid-screen, close to the player. It uses a white-on-black pill with a different weight and radius from the other callouts, and a 'select' line should sit beside the heal slot rather than float. It competes with the character for attention, and the owner called explaining sentences a defect.
findings.fix: Cut to 'heal: 1 bandage · 2 medkit · 3 plate' as 16px f-cond chips anchored 16px above the hotbar. Use one callout style: 4px radius, --ui-panel at 90%, 1px --ui-line-hi border.

findings.where: left callout 'contract item nearby · gold glow marks the box'
findings.what: The callout is explaining text with an amber icon and a 3px left bar. Its yellow-orange text is close to the lime accent and to the 'the forge' label, and its pill style differs from the heal toast. The sentence is long, and the second half gives away the obvious.
findings.fix: Shorten to 'contract item nearby'. Put the 'gold glow' half in the tutorial only. Match the callout shell to the heal toast (--ui-panel, 4px radius, 16px label). Use --warn only for the icon and tx-1 for the text.

findings.what: The panel is dense, and its type is small and pixel-crunchy, at about 14px for the names and 'value at risk'. Names and dollar amounts sit tight, with no row dividers and no padding on the right. The header is a different style from 'run info' top-right. Row height is about 18px, so it is hard to read from a couch.
findings.fix: Set rows to 16px f-cond 600 with 28px row height and 16px padding, and tx-2 for the header. Tint the 'you' row with the P1 amber 3px bar. Give the panel the same --ui-panel fill and 4px radius as the other HUD panels.

findings.what: The bar is a flat, saturated green slab that looks unfinished. 'hp 100' is oversized and hard-edged against the fill, and the bar bleeds off the left edge to the screen edge with no safe margin. It sits very close to the bottom edge, and the hotbar starts only 120px away. The bar is also much louder than the hero ammo number.
findings.fix: Inset it 48px from the left and bottom, make it 20px tall with a 4px radius and a 1px --ui-line-hi track, and put 'hp' at 16px label and 100 at 20px in tx-1 inside the bar. Use --ok at about 85% brightness.

findings.what: It is a lone dropdown chrome with a chevron, wider than its content, and it looks like a web select. It does not share the style of the player list panel. The 'chi...' text clipped at the far right edge (y≈663) is a clipping bug.
findings.fix: Restyle it as a --ui-panel pill at 4px radius, 16px type, the same chevron as the pillagers panel and 16px padding. Fix the clipped label at x=1893 by keeping a 48px safe margin or fading the label.

findings.what: Empty slots show only faint numbers and ghost weapon silhouettes, which have low contrast and add noise. The numbers are tiny (~14px), and the 'f' key chip on slot 2 is tiny. The selected slot has a good amber-yellow border, but slots 1 and 2 are far larger than the empty ones, so the rhythm breaks.
findings.fix: Draw empty slots as 56px --ui-panel boxes with 1px --ui-line borders and 16px tx-2 numbers, and drop the silhouettes. Keep the selected slot bigger, with an --acc 2px border.

findings.where: 'f1 controls' hint and 'b / i backpack' at the bottom
findings.what: The hint is small (~14px) and low contrast. 'f1 controls' sits in the bottom-left at an awkward spot, close to the hotbar, and the chip is crowded. 'b / i backpack' inside the ammo panel is tiny and tx-2.
findings.fix: Make both 16px with tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better. Put 'f1 controls' 24px left of the hotbar on the same baseline as the slot numbers, and keep 'b / i backpack' as a footer line in the ammo panel with 8px spacing.

findings.what: They use three styles: letter-spaced grey text, small cyan text and orange text with no backing. 'packing floor' is spaced out and runs behind the crate and barrel icons, so it is hard to read, and 'the seal 0%' is too small.
findings.fix: Use one world-label style: 16px f-cond 600 with a 1px dark outline or a 60% --ui-void chip. Drop the extra letter-spacing, and move 'packing floor' off the props.

v.verdict: The raid HUD has the right pieces, but it uses too many type sizes, panel styles and accents. Several elements are too small to read from a couch, and the ammo readout is the only part that reads as intentional.

findings.what: The text is about 14px and tightly packed, and the money values are right-aligned far from the names. The panel is a small, dense table with a sharp edge, and it competes with the HUD for attention. It lists other players' values at risk, which is clutter, and the 'value at risk' header is dim and tiny. Its black fill with a white border matches no other panel.
findings.fix: Use 16px minimum text on a --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Set the row height to 24px and the padding to 8px. Collapse it by default to the single line 'you $162'. Make the header --tx-2 at 16px.

findings.where: bottom-left controls tag and top-right 'run info'
findings.what: Both are tiny. The 'f1 controls' tag is about 14px and sits dim against the busy map, so it is nearly invisible. The 'run info' dropdown is a different black bar with a chevron and does not match the panel style. The raid-controls rule asks for a mid-bottom left folded line, and this one looks like a footnote.
findings.fix: Make the 'f1 controls' tag 16px with a 24px key chip on a --ui-panel fill, placed 16px above the hotbar's left edge. Restyle 'run info' to the same 4px-radius panel with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 16px --tx-1 text.

findings.where: center toast 'self-revive spent · one per raid'
findings.what: The toast is the largest, brightest text in the middle of the screen and sits on a wall. It is an explaining sentence, and it covers the play area directly below the player. The dot separator and the near-black pill do not match the banner style used for 'extract 104m'. Nothing says it is the alert banner, and the style guide wants alerts only in the top-centre banner.
findings.fix: Move it to the top-centre banner slot under the clock, or the left feed. Shorten it to 'self-revive spent'. Use the same 4px-radius panel and 20px type as the extract banner, and fade it after 3s.

findings.what: Slot numbers 3 to 8 and 0 float as dim 16px digits over ghosted weapon silhouettes with no slot frames, so the row has no clear edges. The two filled slots have different borders: gold on slot 1 and dark on slot 2. Slot 1's lime/gold selection ring is close to the rarity gold and loot highlights. The ghost silhouettes add noise.
findings.fix: Draw all 8 slots as 72px --ui-panel tiles with a 1px --ui-line border and a 16px --tx-2 number. Make the selected slot's 3px border --acc only. Remove the ghost silhouettes or drop them to 15% opacity.

findings.what: Four label styles are in use: wide letter-spaced grey, orange, cyan, and a magenta label clipped at the right edge. The letter-spaced 'packing floor' collides with the barrels and crates under it. The mix of colours reads as unsystematic.
findings.fix: Use one label style: 16px f-cond 600, --tx-1, with a 2px dark outline and no letter spacing. Use colour only for state (--acc for the interactable the player is near). Clamp labels to 24px inside the screen edge.

findings.what: The 'hp 100' text is bold, about 36px, and sits on a flat green bar clipped by the screen bottom and left edges. It has no frame or margin, so it does not line up with the hotbar or the controls tag. The green fill is not the --ok token. It is a second hero-size number competing with the ammo.
findings.fix: Inset the bar 24px from the left and bottom edges and use a 4px radius with a --ui-panel track. Use --ok for the fill and 20px type for the hp number. Align its baseline with the hotbar bottom.

findings.what: The callout shows an orange left bar with an icon, gold text and a grey tail, and it explains the gold glow with a sentence ('gold glow marks the box'). It sits at an arbitrary position (y 790) with no relation to the other HUD edges. Gold text breaks the rule that gold is a bar only.
findings.fix: Shorten it to 'contract item nearby' with --tx-1 text and a 3px gold bar. Put it in the left feed stack above the controls tag, aligned to the 24px left margin.

findings.what: This is the strongest element: the 56px hero number is clear. But the panel is a heavy black box with a tiny 14px 'b / i backpack' hint. It is the only panel with a visible border and radius, and its corner meets the screen edge with no margin. The '/ 24' secondary number is not aligned to the hero's baseline.
findings.fix: Inset the panel 24px from the right and bottom edges. Set the hint to 16px --tx-2. Baseline-align '/ 24' at 32px with the hero. Use the same --ui-panel and border tokens as the other HUD panels.

v.verdict: The in-raid HUD has a strong ammo hero number, but it is a stack of mismatched, tiny, low-contrast widgets, with several callouts and small labels competing at different sizes and no consistent panel language.

findings.what: The 12-14px text is cramped, with 18px row pitch and no padding. Money values are right-aligned in a different weight and colour from the names. The panel is a black box with a hard border, unlike every other panel. It violates the 16px floor and competes with the clock for attention.
findings.fix: Raise rows to 16px label type on a 32px pitch. Use --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius and 16px padding. Colour the P1 row amber and the others --tx-2, and keep values in tabular f-cond 600.

findings.where: mid-screen callout 'select a heal · bandage, medkit or armour plate'
findings.what: This is an explaining sentence sitting in the middle of the play area. It is the brightest text in the frame, so it pulls the eye away from the player. It also has a different style from the contract callout lower left, and it covers the wall behind it.
findings.fix: Cut it to a short label such as 'heal: 1 bandage 2 medkit', or move it into the left feed. Make it a single shared callout component at 16px with a 4px radius, --ui-panel fill and a 3px left accent bar. Place it 48px above the hotbar.

findings.where: callouts: 'contract item nearby · gold glow marks the box' and 'select a heal'
findings.what: Two different callout designs appear on one screen: an amber-bar tag at the left edge versus a centred black pill. The contract one has an orange left bar and a doc icon, but the heal one has no bar. The contract one is also cut flush against the screen's left edge, with no 5% margin. The text is gold on dark, which is not the accent and not a warning glyph. Both also carry explaining copy.
findings.fix: Use one callout component. Put it on the 5% (96px) left margin, with --tx-1 text and a 3px --warn bar only for warnings. Shorten the copy to 'contract item nearby'.

findings.what: The 'hp 100' text sits on a flat green bar that is clipped at the bottom screen edge, with 0 margin. The numerals sit tight against the left edge of the fill. The bar is not aligned with the hotbar or the other panels, and the dark text on a mid-green fill has weak contrast. The bar is also visually heavier than the hotbar.
findings.fix: Inset it to 48px from the bottom and 96px from the left. Use a 24px-tall bar, a --ui-line track, an --ok fill, and the number in --tx-1 at 20px f-cond 700 with 8px padding. Align the baseline with the hotbar slot bottoms.

findings.what: The slot numbers 3 to 0 float with no slot boxes, at about 12px in --tx-2 grey over a busy map, and are almost unreadable. The weapon silhouettes are ghosted behind them, which is clutter. The 'f1 controls' chip is tiny, at 14px, and floats off the grid with a different panel style.
findings.fix: Draw empty slots as 72px boxes with a 1px --ui-line border at 40% opacity and 16px numbers. Delete the ghost silhouettes. Align the controls chip's left edge with the hp bar and use the same 16px chip style.

findings.where: top-centre clock, 'extract 104m' chip and the sunrise icon
findings.what: The 14:59 timer is about 30px, below the 56px hero size. The teal extract pill is stacked tight under it with a 4px gap, and the sunrise icon is an unexplained extra element. 'the seal 0%' in light blue sits just below, with a third colour and a small size, and no panel behind it, so it is weak against the map.
findings.fix: Set the timer to 40px f-cond 800 and group it with the extract chip in one 8px-gap stack. Add a scrim behind it. Render world labels such as 'the seal' at 16px in --tx-1 with a 1px dark outline, not in an ad-hoc cyan.

findings.what: This is a generic web-style select with a chevron. It looks like a form control, not part of the game's UI, and its border and radius do not match the panels at top left. It is also under-explained: a player does not know what it opens.
findings.fix: Replace it with a panel in the same style as the pillagers list, with a 16px label and a small key hint. Align its top edge with the list at y=144 or match both to y=48, and use the same 96px margin.

findings.what: The hero number '12 / 24' is good, but the panel is a dark box with a different border and radius from the others. 'b / i backpack' at about 13px in grey is below the 16px floor. The slash and the 24 are grey, so the hierarchy is fine, but the panel is flush against the screen corner at roughly 20px margin, not 5%.
findings.fix: Move it inward to a 48px bottom and 96px right margin, and use the shared panel style. Raise 'b / i backpack' to 16px in --tx-2 with 16px padding. Keep '12' at 56px f-cond 800.

v.verdict: A busy raid HUD whose callout works as a banner, but it sits mid-screen over the walls where the eye never looks. The hud is scattered across mixed type sizes, the panels are unrelated, and there are stray capitals and clutter.

findings.where: top-right 'run info' dropdown, and the right edge text 'chi'
findings.what: 'run info' is a bright white-bordered select that looks like a debug control. It has no relation to the other panels and sits where the career HUD column should be. A clipped 'chi' (pink) at the right edge at y~663 is cut off at the screen edge.
findings.fix: Restyle 'run info' as a --ui-panel card with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, a 4px radius and 16px label type, in the cw-trcol corner list. Remove the 'chi' fragment or keep it inside the 5% margin (96px).

findings.where: 'self-revive spent · one per raid' callout, center ~y653
findings.what: The alert sits mid-screen over a wall and the player. It is a thin white-on-black pill that blends into the wall, and its 'one per raid' text explains. The order of 10-27 says alerts are the top-centre banner only, and top centre already has the extract banner.
findings.fix: Move the alert to the top-centre banner slot below the clock. Cut it to 'self-revive spent'. Use a --ui-panel fill with a 3px --warn left bar and 20px f-cond 600 text.

findings.what: The panel is crowded: dense 16px rows with tight leading, value-at-risk right-aligned dollar figures in a different weight, and a caret that is unexplained. It has no hierarchy, since 'you' looks the same as the others, and no P1 amber or P2 cyan player tint. $ figures are fine, but capitals appear in the $ amounts only.
findings.fix: Use 24px row height and 16px --tx-2 labels. Make the 'you' row --tx-1 with an amber 3px left bar. Make the header 16px, 600, +.04em. Inset the panel 48px from the edges.

findings.what: Three label styles at three sizes: 'packing floor' is wide-tracked grey serif-like text that collides with the barrel props and is almost unreadable, 'the forge' is orange, and 'the seal' is thin cyan. They have no outline or backing, so they fail contrast against the purple floor.
findings.fix: One label style: 16px f-cond 600, +.04em, --tx-1, on a --scrim chip with a 2px outline. Colour only a 3px tick by meaning. Remove the letter-spacing on 'packing floor'.

findings.what: The hp bar is a flat, saturated green slab with oversized 'hp 100' text in a different type style (a heavy rounded font that reads as another game). The slot numbers 3 to 0 float as faint, unlabelled grey digits, and ghost weapon silhouettes below them are noise. Slots 1 and 2 have different borders.
findings.fix: Set the hp bar to 12px tall in --ok on a --ui-panel track, with a 20px f-cond 700 number right-aligned. Use one 4px radius for slots and a --acc 2px border for the selected slot. Hide empty slots or show them at 40% with 14px numbers. Remove the ghost icons.

findings.what: This is the strongest element: 12 / 24 is the hero number. But 'scav pistol' is right-aligned with unrelated type weight and 'b / i backpack' is 14px grey, below the 16px reading minimum.
findings.fix: Use 16px --tx-2 for 'b / i backpack' with key chips. Set the 12 at 56px / 800 and the '/ 24' at 32px / 600 in --tx-2. Align the panel to the 5% margin (96px from the right, 54px from the bottom).

findings.what: The chip is tiny (16px or less) with a pale chip on a dark box, and it floats at the left of the hotbar without aligning to either the hotbar or the hp bar. The 'fl' glyph reads as 'f-l' rather than 'f1'.
findings.fix: Centre it on the hotbar baseline 16px above the slots, at 16px f-cond 600 with a 4px key chip. Use the same chip style as the 'b / i' hints.

findings.what: The clock at ~28px sits over a wall with only a shadow, so it is hard to read, and the sun icon is unexplained. The teal pill is correct for extraction but its text is 16px with tight padding.
findings.fix: Put the clock on a --scrim chip, 32px / 700. Use 20px text with 8px/16px padding in the extract pill, and give the clock and pill one shared 4px radius.

v.verdict: This picture is the undercroft hub with a 'not enough parts' toast. The rack-build screen the earlier review covered isn't visible, so nothing from that advice can be judged as fixed, and the hub has its own hierarchy and clutter problems.

findings.what: The '***experimental feature may glitch***' tag is an explaining sentence in warn amber at about 14px. It breaks the quiet-label rule. It is wrapped in asterisks, and it sits on top of a character sprite and the station circle.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence. If a flag is needed, use a 16px 'beta' chip in --warn on --ui-panel, with no asterisks, anchored 8px under the station label.

findings.where: the screen the review was meant to show (rack build / import a friend)
findings.what: The shot shows the hub, not the rack-parts panel, so the earlier advice can't be checked. The import-a-friend text, the cost paragraph, the single primary button and the 0 of 10 slots are all missing from this frame.
findings.fix: Recapture with the rack window open at 1080p. Show a centred 90% card with a 56px header, an x in the corner, and the three action buttons.

findings.where: enter raid! at the top centre (850-1070, 90-145)
findings.what: The lime 56px label is the hero, but it has an exclamation mark and a heavy outline. That reads as arcade copy, against the straight-copy rule. It also sits over a pillar and a station circle, and it competes with the 4 lime-framed slot at the bottom.
findings.fix: Change it to 'enter raid' at --fs-title 32px in --acc, with no '!'. Put it on a --ui-panel plate with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 3px --acc bottom bar.

findings.where: not enough parts toast at (960,870), and the controls hint at (960,918)
findings.what: The toast is dark on dark, about 16px. It is jammed 12px above the controls strip and sits over the stash station label area. The two stacked boxes crowd the hotbar and the stash tag.
findings.fix: Move the toast to the top-centre banner slot. Give it a --danger left bar and a 4.5:1 label. Keep at least 24px between the toast, the controls strip and the hotbar.

findings.what: '$900' and '0 xp' are big, but 'stash $0 bag $0' is about 14px in grey on the busy dark map, mixed with 'xp'. The three items differ in size and weight. The owner wants a vertical list with every item the same size.
findings.fix: Use one 20px f-cond tx-1 line per item in a vertical list, with a --ui-panel plate behind it and 16px padding. Keep the labels at 16px tx-2. Remove the mixed sizes.

findings.where: station labels (the gambler, shop craft and hire, settings, the stash)
findings.what: Every label is an identical dark pill, so the hierarchy is flat. The stash tag is overlapped by a character, and 'fashion' is half covered by a circle. The glow circles at 15-30% opacity muddy the floor and lower the label contrast.
findings.fix: Use --ui-panel pills with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 16px text. Put the focused station's pill in --acc with --acc-ink text. Cut the circle fills to 8% opacity and keep only the ring.

findings.what: Nine slots are shown, and eight of them are dim, low-contrast weapon silhouettes that are close to invisible. Only the lime-ish selected slot reads, and it is amber rather than --acc. The number labels are about 12px.
findings.fix: Set unowned slots to 40% opacity on --ui-panel with a 16px tx-2 number. Make the selected frame a 3px --acc border. Use one 8px gap everywhere.

findings.what: The title is fine, but the card is at 5% of screen, not on the 48px margin. The 14px subline 'items in stash · runs' repeats the stash $0 strip at the top right. The screen shows both.
findings.fix: Move the card to the 48px margin. Drop the subline, or keep one place for stash and runs. Use a 4px radius to match the other panels.

v.verdict: The raid HUD reads cleanly in the lower-left controls list and the ammo block. It scatters about six chrome styles across the screen, and its small text sits below the 16px floor. The hero numbers are weak, and a capital letter and a $/score mix-up break the owner's rules.

findings.what: The title is 'run Info' with a capital I, which breaks the all-lower-case order. The bar is a flat black strip with a chevron, and it floats against the building wall. Its width, border and type size match none of the other widgets.
findings.fix: Change the text to 'run info'. Give the bar the same panel fill (#16191b), 1px #4a5257 border and 4px radius as the other panels. Use a 20px f-cond 600 title and inset the bar 24px from the screen edge.

findings.what: Rows are about 12px, and the dim 'dead' rows (crouchspammer, lootlordlucas, griefthegriefers) sit well below the 4.5:1 contrast floor. The header, the 'value at risk' label and the 0 / 3 dead footer all use the same weight, so nothing leads. The figures are tabular, but the dollar signs and '$2,187' are not aligned in a clean column.
findings.fix: Raise rows to 16px (--fs-label) with --tx-2 (#aaa498) for dead rows. Make the 'you' row --tx-1 at 20px with a lime 3px left bar. Use a 24px row pitch and right-align the values in one column.

findings.where: controls list, mid-left (move / fight / gear / raid)
findings.what: This is a dense wall of about 24 rows in 12-13px text, which is clutter even though it is the intended folded-line replacement. It is not the one short line the owner ordered, because it is fully open. Its section labels (move, gear, fight, raid) are as dim as the body text, and the 8px grid is not followed. It also covers a lot of the map.
findings.fix: Fold it to a single 16px line at mid-bottom left, as the owner ordered ('f1 controls'), and open it only on F1. When open, use 16px minimum text, 24px column gaps, and --tx-2 section labels with a 1px --ui-line divider.

findings.what: The bar is a bright flat green with a large 'hp 100' in a different, bigger type than every other label. The text sits flush against the bar's left edge with no padding. The bar is also squeezed against the screen edge, only about 8px from the bottom and left. It is the loudest element on screen but the least important state at full health.
findings.fix: Make the bar 12px high on a --ui-panel track with 1px border, and use --ok only for the fill. Put 'hp 100' in --fs-body at 8px padding. Place it at 24px from the edge, aligned to the status chips.

findings.where: status chips (concealed, in cover) and contract banner
findings.what: The chips use three treatments: a round amber icon, a round teal icon, and rectangular pills with a warn-amber border and a teal border. The banner uses an amber left bar and gold text with a '·' separator. The chip text is large (about 22px) against 12px elsewhere, and chip heights do not match the weapon slots beside them. The gold glow explanation ('gold glow marks the box') is an explaining sentence, which the rules list as a defect.
findings.fix: Use one chip style: 32px high, 4px radius, --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, a 16px label, and a colour only on the 16px glyph. Shorten the banner to 'contract item nearby' and cut the second half.

findings.where: weapon bar and ammo block, bottom
findings.what: Slots 4 to 0 are faint ghost icons, so they read as a rendering bug. They are also unlabeled in the 4-0 row. The numbers 1, 2 and 3 in the selected slot are tiny at about 12px. The ammo block (scav pistol 12 / 24) is the strongest element, with a good hero number. But the 'b / i backpack' hint at 14px is too dim, and the block has a different border and radius than the slots next to it.
findings.fix: Hide empty slots, or draw them as 48px 1px --ui-line outlines with no icon. Use 16px slot numbers. Make the ammo block a --ui-panel with the 4px radius and 1px --ui-line-hi border to match the slots. Raise the hint to 16px --tx-2.

findings.where: top centre: timer, extract banner, objective marker
findings.what: The '15:00' timer is about 28px, not the 56px hero size. The sun icon in a ring is unlabeled. The teal 'extract 707m' pill is the right colour, but it is cramped under the timer. The 'a 15m' marker is a loose, 4th pill style, a teal-bordered box that is not clearly linked to the arrow above it. The marker's single letter 'a' is cryptic.
findings.fix: Make the timer 56px f-cond 800 only when it matters, such as the last minute, and otherwise 32px with a 8px gap to the extract pill. Give all pills the one chip style. Use 'a' only with a lime or teal diamond glyph, with the distance in 16px.

findings.what: Panels are inconsistent. The controls, pillagers and ammo panels have sharp, semi-transparent black fills, while the chips are rounded and the top-right bar is flat. Margins to the screen edge vary between 8px and 24px, and each corner is a different density. Nothing in it says Pillagers beyond the pixel-art map, and the HUD reads as generic. Lime is not used at all, even though the selected slot is amber.
findings.fix: Use a single HUD panel token (rgba(22,25,27,.85), 1px #4a5257 border, 4px radius), and use a 24px margin on all corners. Use lime #e6ff3d for the selected slot ring instead of amber, since P1 amber is already used for the player. Give the ammo number a lime hero tint, one per screen.

v.verdict: The raid HUD works as a readable set of panels, but it is crowded, the type sizes are inconsistent, a capital letter shows on screen, and the controls list is open and large instead of folded to one line.

findings.what: The list is fully open, about 300x300px, with two columns and about 22 rows. The guide says a career raid shows it folded to one short line at mid-bottom left, and F1 opens it. It is the biggest panel on screen and takes attention from the play area. Its keycap boxes are also small and low in contrast.
findings.fix: Fold it to one 16px line at the bottom left ('f1 controls') and open it only on F1. If it stays open, cut it to 8 or fewer rows and drop the repeated headers.

findings.what: The text is 'run Info' with a capital I, which breaks the all-lower-case rule. The dropdown is a wide dark bar on top of the building art and is clipped by the wall. It has no clear relation to the left value-at-risk panel, which has the same job.
findings.fix: Fix the string to 'run info'. Match this panel's padding, border and chevron to the left panel. Size both at 16px label text.

findings.what: Type is about 14 to 16px, and the muted rows (crouchspammer, lootlordlucas, griefthegrifers) are dim grey on a translucent dark fill. At couch distance they are hard to read. The header, column label and rows all share the same weight. The '$' values and 'dead' text crowd the right edge, with about 8px of padding.
findings.fix: Set rows to 16px f-cond 600 in tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better. Make 'you' tx-1 with a 3px amber (P1) bar. Use 16px padding and a solid --ui-panel fill.

findings.what: The 'hp 100' text sits on a flat green bar, in a heavy outlined font that does not match the Barlow Condensed of the other panels. The bar is clipped by the screen edge. The status chips ('concealed', 'in cover') and the hp bar line up with neither each other nor the weapon slots.
findings.fix: Use f-cond 800 at 32px with no outline. Inset the bar 24px from the edges and give it a 4px radius, a --ui-panel track and a 1px border. Put the chips and bar on one baseline.

findings.what: Slot 1 has a lime-yellow frame, but it is amber and thick, so it reads as P1 colour rather than the lime 'selected' colour. The empty slots 4 to 0 are very faint, with ghost gun icons at about 20 percent opacity, and the numbers float with no frame. Slots 2 and 3 have no frame at all. The row looks unfinished.
findings.fix: Give every slot a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius on a --ui-panel fill. Use --acc for the selected slot only, 2px. Keep empty slots at 40 percent opacity inside the same frame.

findings.what: '12 / 24' is a strong hero number and it works. 'scav pistol' is right-aligned at about 24px and competes with it. 'b / i backpack' is about 14px and low contrast. The panel corners and padding do not match the other panels.
findings.fix: Set the weapon name to 16px tx-2 and the footer hint to 14px in at least 4.5:1 contrast. Make all corners 4px and use 16px padding in line with the other HUD panels.

findings.what: '15:00' is drawn bare on the map with no panel, so it loses contrast over the building art. The teal 'extract 707m' chip below it has a different style from the 'a 15m' chip, and the two teal chips and the cyan marker add to the clutter around the top centre.
findings.fix: Put '15:00' in a --ui-panel pill with a 56px hero style. Use one shared chip style (16px f-cond, --extract border) for both extract and objective markers.

findings.what: The four corner panels differ in fill opacity, border, padding and type size, and no shared token is applied. The look is generic 'dark box' and has no clear accent hierarchy, so the eye goes first to the controls list and to the bright red barrels instead of the HUD.
findings.fix: Apply one panel style everywhere: --ui-panel at 80 percent, a 1px --ui-line-hi border, a 4px radius and 16px padding. Reserve --acc for selected and focus states, and keep amber for P1 only.

v.verdict: The raid HUD is still a pile of mismatched panels: the 'run info' bar has a capital I, the controls list is open instead of folded, and the status chips, banner, hp bar and tags all use different styles.

findings.what: It reads 'run info' with a capital I, which breaks the all-lower-case order. It is still an unstyled dark bar with a chevron, flush to the edge, and it does not match the other panels.
findings.fix: Change the text to 'run info'. Use fill #16191b, a 1px #4a5257 border, a 4px radius, a 20px f-cond 600 label and a 24px inset from the top and right edges. Make the chevron --tx-2.

findings.where: controls list, mid-left (move / fight / gear / raid)
findings.what: It sits open as a large 300x300 panel over the playfield. This contradicts the owner's order that it start folded to one line at mid-bottom left, with F1 opening it. The section labels are dim and 16px or smaller, and the key caps are crowded.
findings.fix: Fold it to one 16px line, 'f1 controls', at x=24 and bottom=96. Open it on F1 only, with 16px text, --tx-2 section labels, a 24px column gap and a 1px --ui-line divider.

findings.where: the long dock cache label, right edge
findings.what: The lavender, unboxed text is flush against the screen edge and clipped in feel. The colour is not in the palette. It has no panel and the contrast on the busy purple ground is poor. It also sits apart from the 'a 15m' chip and its arrow.
findings.fix: Put both in one 32px chip with the --ui-panel fill and a 1px --ui-line-hi border, inset 24px from the edge. Use --tx-1 text at 16px and keep the teal only on the arrow glyph.

findings.what: The rows are about 14px, and the dead rows in dim grey on a translucent fill are hard to read. The 'you' row is not distinguished by weight or a bar. The '0 out · 3 dead' footer is more noise. The header has a chevron and the 'value at risk' label is in a different style from the title.
findings.fix: Use 16px rows on a 24px pitch with --tx-2 for dead rows. Make the 'you' row --tx-1 at 20px with a 3px --acc left bar. Right-align the values in one column. Drop the footer line or merge it into the header, and use an opaque --ui-panel fill.

findings.where: status chips (concealed, in cover) and the contract banner
findings.what: The chips use bordered amber and teal text, and the banner has a hard orange left bar. These are three different chip styles. The banner is a long sentence that explains the game, 'gold glow marks the box'. The coloured text is also too saturated.
findings.fix: Use one chip style: 32px high, 4px radius, --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, a 16px --tx-1 label, and colour only on the glyph. Change the banner to 'contract item nearby' and remove the explaining half.

findings.what: It is a saturated green slab, 400x34, with 'hp 100' in a larger, heavier type set directly over the fill. It is the loudest element at the bottom and competes with the ammo hero number. It also does not align with the chips above it, and there is no track or border.
findings.fix: Make the bar 12px high on a --ui-panel track with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, and use --ok for the fill only. Put 'hp 100' at 20px f-cond 600 --tx-1 above or beside the bar, at 24px from the edge and aligned with the chips.

findings.what: The 'scav pistol' name, '12 / 24' and the 'b / i backpack' hint are all different sizes. The hint is about 13px, below the 16px floor. The hero number is good, but the panel has no border and its edge is fuzzy.
findings.fix: Set the hint to 16px --tx-2. Set the weapon name to 20px --tx-1 and the hero 56px 800. Give the panel a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius, and align its right edge 24px from the screen edge.

findings.where: enemy name tags (sentry r-60, crawler c-75/74/73)
findings.what: The tags are 14px with a thin orange underline. They stack at uneven angles and overlap the enemies. The tag fill is translucent, so contrast drops over the purple ground.
findings.fix: Use a 16px label on an opaque --ui-panel fill with a 4px radius and a 2px --danger bar. Offset each tag 8px above its entity and avoid overlapping tags.

v.verdict: The name tags now sit tidily over the enemies, but the HUD is still a stack of mismatched boxes. The controls list is open and large, 'run info' still has a capital I, and the hp bar is raw.

findings.what: It still shows a capital 'I' ('run info'), which breaks the all-lower-case rule. It is also a full-width dark bar with a chevron and no content, and its padding and chevron don't match the 'current pillagers' panel.
findings.fix: Change the string to 'run info'. Set both panels to 16px label text, 16px padding, a --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Make the run info box 280px wide, not 330px.

findings.what: It is still fully open, about 300x300px, with 22 key/action rows and three sub-headers in very dim text. It covers the map and is the biggest block in the HUD, so it pulls the eye away from the action.
findings.fix: Fold it to one 16px 'f1 controls' line at the bottom left, 24px from the edge, and open it only on F1. If it stays open, cut it to 8 or fewer rows. Make the headers 16px tx-2 and use one --ui-panel fill.

findings.what: The text is small and low contrast, about 14px grey. It has two columns, a '0' next to the title, and a '0 out · 3 dead' footer, so it is cluttered. 'you' is not tx-1 and has no amber P1 mark. It sits tight against the screen edge, with 8px of padding and a panel that is nearly transparent.
findings.fix: Set rows to 16px f-cond 600, with tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better. Make 'you' tx-1 with a 3px amber bar. Use 16px padding, a solid --ui-panel fill and a 24px margin from the edge. Drop the '0' and the footer, and move the 'dead' tags to a danger-red glyph.

findings.where: bottom left hp bar and status chips
findings.what: The 'hp 100' text is rough: it is outlined and in a different weight from the other text, and it sits directly on the bar with no padding. The bar runs to the screen edge with no inset, border or radius. The chips ('concealed', 'in cover') use a different size and a lime fill that competes with the selected weapon slot.
findings.fix: Put hp at f-cond 800, 32px, with no outline. Inset the bar 24px from the edges and give it a 4px radius, a --ui-panel track and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Put the chips and bar on one baseline, and make the chips 16px with a --ui-panel fill and a 1px border. Keep lime for selected only.

findings.what: Slots 1 to 3 are framed, but 4 to 8 and 0 are just floating numbers over faint ghost icons that clash with the buildings. The frames are inconsistent, and the slot labels are tiny (about 12px).
findings.fix: Draw all nine slots with the same 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius and --ui-panel fill, 72px wide. Make empty slots 40 percent opacity inside the same frame. Use 2px --acc for the selected slot only and 16px numerals.

findings.what: The hero number is good, at about 56px, but the panel is a different size and has a different corner radius from the other panels. 'b / i backpack' is about 12px. The panel is cramped at the bottom right and the 24px margin isn't consistent with the others.
findings.fix: Use the same 4px radius, 1px border and --ui-panel fill as every other panel. Make the hint 16px tx-2. Set all outer margins to 24px.

findings.where: right edge, 'a 15m' chip and 'the long dock cache' label
findings.what: The location label is lilac, a colour not in the palette, at about 20px with no panel, so it floats over a busy map and loses contrast. The teal chip's 'a 15m' arrow is not tied to the label.
findings.fix: Put the label in tx-1 on a --ui-panel plate, 16px, and group it with the chip in one 8px-gap row. Reserve teal for extraction only.

findings.where: enemy name tags (sentry r-60, crawler c-75/74/73)
findings.what: The tags are legible and now spaced, but they are tiny (about 13px) with a thin amber underline. They stagger diagonally, so the stack reads as a staircase. The amber underline reads as the P1 colour and not as hostile.
findings.fix: Set the tag text to 16px f-cond 600 in tx-1 on a --ui-panel plate with a 4px radius. Use --danger for the hostile underline, not amber. Put the tags on a fixed 24px vertical stack.

v.verdict: The controls list is now folded to one line and the run info dropdown is clean, but the HUD still uses mixed chip styles and type sizes, the pillagers panel is cramped, and the banner still explains.

findings.what: Rows are about 12px on an 18px pitch and the panel is cramped. The 'you' row is not set apart (no 20px size, no accent bar). Dead rows are not dimmed, and the footer '0 out · 3 dead' is redundant. The panel sits at x=8, off the 24px margin.
findings.fix: Set rows to 16px on a 24px pitch and the 'you' row to 20px --tx-1 with a 3px --acc left bar. Dim dead rows to --tx-2 and drop the footer. Make the fill opaque --ui-panel with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 16px padding, and move it to x=24, y=24.

findings.what: The explaining half 'gold glow marks the box' is still on screen, and the banner uses a different style from the chips below it: 3px yellow bar, document glyph, mixed text colours. Its text is about 18px.
findings.fix: Change the text to 'contract item nearby'. Use the same 32px chip as the status chips: --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 16px --tx-1 label, and the glyph the only colour.

findings.where: status chips (concealed, in cover) and hp bar, bottom left
findings.what: The chips have yellow-green text on dark with a different border from the other chips. The text is about 22px, which is not on the type scale. The hp bar is a large flat green slab with 'hp 100' at about 32px, and it is the loudest element in the corner. The icons, chips, banner and hp bar do not share an x-edge or a spacing rule.
findings.fix: Use one 32px chip style with --tx-1 16px labels and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Reduce the hp bar to 12px high with 20px 'hp 100' text above it. Put everything on a 24px left edge with an 8px gap between rows.

findings.where: right-edge markers: 'a 15m' chip and 'the long dock cache' label
findings.what: The two use different styles: teal text on a teal-outlined chip versus white text on a plain dark box. The cache label at about 20px bold is louder than the objective marker. The label overlaps the building art, and it is not clear which marker is the objective.
findings.fix: Use one 32px chip with --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border and 16px --tx-1 text, inset 24px from the edge. Put the teal only on the arrow glyph. Stack the two chips with an 8px gap.

findings.where: score panel and clock, top centre
findings.what: Two stacked boxes with different widths (about 108 and 200px) and the 'score' label at about 16px. The 'extract 707m' chip hangs underneath as a third box. The group looks pasted together.
findings.fix: Make one 200px-wide column with the same --ui-panel fill and 4px radius: clock 32px, then score at 20px with a 16px --tx-2 label, then the extract chip at 16px. Use an 8px gap and the same width for all three.

findings.where: weapon slots and ammo panel, bottom centre and bottom right
findings.what: The ammo panel is a 4th panel style. 'b / i backpack' is about 14px, and the empty slots 4 to 8 show faint weapon silhouettes with low-contrast numbers, which adds clutter. The '12 / 24' hero number is good.
findings.fix: Use 4px radius and a 1px --ui-line-hi border on all slot and ammo panels. Make 'b / i backpack' 16px --tx-2. Hide empty slots 4 to 8 or drop their silhouettes and keep only a 1px outline at 40% opacity.

findings.what: This is now mostly right, but the 'run info' label is about 16px against the 20px that was asked for. The panel is also at y≈18, which is not on the 24px inset.
findings.fix: Set the label to 20px f-cond 600 and the inset to 24px from the top and right edges. Colour the chevron --tx-2.

findings.where: f1 controls hint, bottom left (x≈440, y≈940)
findings.what: The hint is folded as asked, but it floats at x=440, not at x=24, so it does not line up with the chips and hp bar. The text is about 16px at low contrast on a busy background.
findings.fix: Move it to x=24, bottom=96 and give it a --ui-panel fill with a 16px --tx-1 'f1' keycap and a --tx-2 'controls' label.

v.verdict: The controls list is now a single 'f1 controls' line, 'run info' is a collapsed bar and the weapon slots are more consistent. The HUD is still scattered across the screen: panel styles, corner margins and type sizes don't match, and the top-left panel and weapon slots still look unfinished.

findings.what: The rows are still tiny, about 14px, with dim tx-2 names and values. The '0' after the title is still there, and so is the '0 out · 3 dead' footer. 'dead' is plain text on every row. The panel sits 8px from the edge with a near-black fill and a different border from every other box.
findings.fix: Set rows to 16px f-cond 600 with names in tx-1 and 16px padding. Drop the '0' and the footer. Replace each 'dead' with a 16px --danger glyph. Move the panel 24px from the edge. Give it the shared --ui-panel fill and a 1px --ui-line-hi border at 4px radius.

findings.what: The bar is a 350px dropdown with a chevron and only a 14px label. It is wider and heavier than anything it controls, and it hugs the top edge with a different border from the other panels.
findings.fix: Make it 280px wide, 40px tall and 24px from the top and right edges. Use a 16px f-cond 600 label, a --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Shrink the chevron to 16px and tx-2.

findings.where: bottom-left status chips and hp bar
findings.what: The chip icons are round and the chip fills are mixed: lime-text 'concealed' and a green-tinted 'in cover'. The hp bar is a flat green block with a 'hp 100' label whose size doesn't match the chips. The bar sits 24px from the edge and the chips float above it on a different baseline. Neither lines up with the weapon slots.
findings.fix: Set the chips to 16px text on a --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius, in tx-1 with no lime. Make the 'hp 100' text f-cond 800 at 32px. Give the bar a --ui-panel track, a 1px border and a 4px radius. Put the chips and bar in one column at x=24 with 8px between them.

findings.what: Slots 1-3 are 100px filled cards, but 4-8 and 0 are bare floating numerals with ghost icons. The selected slot has a 3px amber border where the guide says lime, and the lock glyph has no frame. The row looks unfinished.
findings.fix: Draw all nine slots at 72px wide and 72px tall with an 8px gap. Use the same --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Dim empty slots to 40 percent inside the same frame. Use a 2px --acc border on the selected slot only. Make the numerals 16px tx-2.

findings.where: top-centre timer, score and extract stack
findings.what: The timer, score and extract pill are three differently sized boxes stacked edge to edge, with different widths and near-black fills. The 'score' label is 16px but 'extract 707m' is 14px and has a teal border. The score card hangs off the timer's left edge and overlaps the building. The stack is the strongest thing on screen but it looks uneven.
findings.fix: Make one 240px-wide column centred on x=960 with 8px gaps. Give each box the --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Keep 15:00 as the one f-cond 800 hero at 56px. Make the score 32px. Set 'extract 707m' to 16px with a teal glyph only, not a teal border.

findings.what: The panel is 240px wide and anchored to the screen edge with a different margin from the other corners. The 'scav pistol' name is 20px, the '12 / 24' is 56px and 'b / i backpack' is 14px, which is below the 16px minimum. The fill and border don't match the other panels.
findings.fix: Move it to 24px from the right and bottom edges. Set the weapon name to 16px tx-2 and 'b / i backpack' to 16px. Keep 12 as the 56px f-cond 800 hero and show '/ 24' at 32px tx-2. Use the shared panel fill and a 1px border.

findings.where: right-edge objective tags 'a 15m' and 'the long dock cache'
findings.what: The 'a 15m' pill is cyan-bordered and 'the long dock cache' is a white-text box on a different fill. They sit 8px from the right edge, partly under the arrow, and don't match the extract pill's styling.
findings.fix: Pull both 24px in from the right edge. Use one 16px f-cond 600 style in tx-1 on --ui-panel with a 1px border and a 4px radius. Keep teal for the arrow glyph only.

findings.where: 'f1 controls' hint and floating name tags
findings.what: The 'f1 controls' hint is a 14px low-contrast chip that sits to the right of the chips at x=450, away from the 24px left margin. The enemy name tags ('sentry r-60', 'crawler c-75' and so on) are about 14px with thin orange underlines. They stack close together and cover the sentry and crawlers.
findings.fix: Set the hint to 16px tx-2 and move it to the left margin, 24px from the edge, 16px above the chips. Set the name tags to 16px with 4px padding and a 2px --ui-line-hi underline instead of orange. Stagger them 4px apart so they don't touch.

v.verdict: The HUD is readable and mostly lower case, but the earlier panel, chip and column fixes were only partly applied, so it still reads as several unrelated widgets with tiny text, mixed fills and uneven edges.

findings.what: The text is still about 14px on a tight pitch. The panel is translucent black with a thin border, sits at x=8 instead of 24, and the footer line '0 out · 3 dead' is still there. The 'you' row is the same weight as the dead rows, so the eye has no entry point. The dead rows are not dimmed.
findings.fix: Set rows to 16px on a 24px pitch. Make the 'you' row 20px --tx-1 with a 3px --acc left bar. Dim dead rows to --tx-2 and delete the footer. Use an opaque --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 16px padding, and position it at x=24, y=24.

findings.what: The banner is a sentence with an explanation, 'gold glow marks the box'. It has an amber bar and glyph and lime-yellow text, so it competes with the accent and it is not the same chip as the status chips. It also sits at x=16, which is off the left edge used by the status chips and hp bar.
findings.fix: Cut the text to 'contract item nearby'. Use a 32px chip with --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 16px --tx-1 text, with the glyph as the only colour. Place it at x=24.

findings.where: bottom-left stack: status chips, 'f1 controls', hp bar
findings.what: The status chips (concealed, in cover) use 20px lime-tinted text in outlined pills, and 'f1 controls' floats at a different x and baseline on a dim fill. The hp bar is a saturated green slab about 32px tall with an oversized 'hp 100' on it, and it is the loudest element at the bottom edge. The left edges are 24, 16 and 24px, and the vertical gaps are uneven.
findings.fix: Use one 32px chip style with 16px --tx-1 labels and a 1px --ui-line-hi border for the status chips and the f1 hint. Reduce the hp bar to 12px high with 'hp 100' at 20px above it. Put everything on a 24px left edge with an 8px gap between rows.

findings.where: right-edge markers: 'a 15m' chip and 'the long dock cache' label
findings.what: The chips are different widths, sit at different insets and are ragged against the right edge. The teal arrow floats beside the chip instead of belonging to it. The label 'a 15m' is cryptic, and the 14px text is hard to read over the busy map.
findings.fix: Use one 32px chip per item with --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 16px --tx-1 text. Put the arrow inside the chip as its only colour. Inset the chips 24px from the right edge and stack them with an 8px gap. Rename 'a 15m' to '15m'.

findings.where: top centre: clock, score, extract chip
findings.what: The three pieces have three different widths, 200, 200 and 114px, and the extract chip is teal-filled text on a different panel. The score label is tiny and the 'sp' unit is the same size as the number. The sun icon floats on its own.
findings.fix: Make one 200px column with the same --ui-panel fill and 4px radius: clock 32px, then score at 20px with a 16px --tx-2 label, then the extract chip at 16px with the same width. Use an 8px gap. Put the sun icon inside the clock panel.

findings.what: The dropdown is a wide 300px bar with 16px text and a chevron, and it is half empty. Its fill and border differ from the other panels, and it sits at y=18 where the top-left panel sits at y=142.
findings.fix: Shrink it to a 160px chip with the same panel style as the others. Align its top edge and right inset to 24px.

findings.what: The 'b / i backpack' hint is about 14px on a translucent panel. The 12/24 ammo is a good hero number, but the panel's left edge doesn't line up with anything. The empty slots 4 to 8 are faint ghosts.
findings.fix: Use a 16px --tx-2 hint. Give the panel an opaque --ui-panel fill, 24px right and bottom inset, and a 4px radius. Hide the slots that are empty.

v.verdict: The HUD is readable and the ammo card and weapon slots are fairly clean, but the top-right bar has a text collision, the top-centre stack is ragged, and the panels still don't share one frame and edge margin.

findings.what: The 'run' label is overprinted by '$900', so the text collides. The bar is crammed against the top and right edges. It also mixes sizes, with a large $900, a tiny 'xp' and 'stash $0 bag $2,187', and the stash text runs into the border.
findings.fix: Make the bar 280px wide and 40px tall, at 24px from the top and right edges. Use 16px f-cond 600 text with 16px padding and a 16px gap between items. Drop the 'run' label or give it its own 8px slot. Keep '$900' at 20px and put stash and bag in tx-2. Set the border to 1px --ui-line-hi, the radius to 4px and the fill to --ui-panel.

findings.what: The panel is flush to the left edge (x=8) and the rows are cramped at about 14px. The '0' after the title is stray. 'dead' repeats on three rows, and the footer '0 out · 3 dead' repeats it again. The chevron is hard to see.
findings.fix: Move the panel to x=24, y=24. Use 16px rows with 16px padding and a 24px row pitch. Delete the '0' and the footer. Replace 'dead' with a 16px --danger glyph. Use a --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius.

findings.where: top-centre timer, score and extract stack
findings.what: The three boxes have different widths (138, 198 and 116px). The timer is offset left of the sun icon. The extract pill uses a teal border and teal text and sits tight under the score box with no gap. The result reads as a ragged stack.
findings.fix: Use one 240px column centred on x=960 with 8px gaps. Give every box the same --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Keep 15:00 as the one 56px hero and set the score to 32px. Set 'extract 707m' to 16px tx-1 with a teal glyph only. Move the sun icon outside the column.

findings.where: bottom-left status chips and hp bar
findings.what: The chips are 20px text in lime-yellow on dark and mixed in size with the round icons. The hp bar is flat green and flush to the screen edge at y=1080. 'hp 100' is drawn over the bar in a different weight and size. Nothing is aligned to the weapon row.
findings.fix: Put the chips and bar in one column at x=24, 8px apart, with a 24px bottom margin. Make the chips 16px tx-1 on --ui-panel with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Make 'hp 100' f-cond 800 at 32px, using --ui-panel for the track and 4px for the radius. Use --ok for the fill.

findings.what: Three filled slots are 100px wide and two are 100px tall. Slots 4 to 0 are bare numerals with ghost icons and no frames, so the row reads as ragged and half missing. The 'f1 controls' hint also floats above the row at a different size.
findings.fix: Draw all nine slots at 72px wide and 72px tall with an 8px gap. Use the same --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Dim empty slots to 40 percent inside the same frame. Use a 2px --acc border on the selected slot only. Make the numerals 16px tx-2. Align the row's baseline with the ammo card at y=1056.

findings.what: The card is the best HUD element, but it is flush to the edge. 'b / i backpack' is under 16px and low contrast. The '/ 24' is dim next to the 12, and the 12 is fine as the hero.
findings.fix: Move it to 24px from the right and bottom edges. Set 'b / i backpack' to 16px tx-2. Set the '12' to 56px f-cond 800 and the '/ 24' to 32px tx-2. Use the same 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius as the other panels.

findings.where: left contract hint and right 'the long dock cache' tags
findings.what: The contract hint is an explaining sentence ('gold glow marks the box') and has a different frame from every other panel. The right-edge tags are tiny, at 14px, and pressed against the edge. The 'a 15m' tag is cryptic.
findings.fix: Cut the hint to 'contract item nearby' at 16px. Give it a --ui-panel fill, a 1px border and a 4px radius, at x=24. Keep the right tags at 16px, with a 24px margin from the right. Rename 'a 15m' to something readable, such as '15m'.

findings.what: Every panel has its own fill, border and edge margin, from 0 to 24px. The player's eye gets four heroes: 15:00, 12 / 24, hp 100 and $900. There is no single hierarchy.
findings.fix: Use a single panel token (--ui-panel, a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius) and a 24px safe margin on all four corners. Keep the 56px hero only for 15:00 and the ammo count. Demote $900 and hp to 32px at most.

v.verdict: The title screen is clean and has a clear hierarchy, with the lime '1 player' button as the single hot action. The orange gradient wordmark, the cramped saves block, the small dim text and the capital 'ET' in the version stamp keep it from looking polished.

findings.what: The wordmark is an orange-amber gradient with a drop shadow. This is the gradient wash the guide bans. It also sits next to the lime button as a second hot colour, and amber is reserved for P1 or warnings. It is the one non-flat, non-token element on the screen and reads like a default web title.
findings.fix: Make it flat --tx-1 (#efe9dc) at 800 weight, or flat --acc. Remove the gradient and shadow. Raise it from about 72px to the 56px hero token with a taller tracking, or keep the size and place a 3px lime bar under it.

findings.what: The stamp contains the capitals 'ET', which breaks the all-lower-case rule. It is also about 13px and dim grey. Its left edge sits at x=97 while the menu column sits at x=681, so it follows no margin. It reads as a debug string.
findings.fix: Write 'et' in lower case. Use 14px --fs-fine in --tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better. Put it on the 5% margin (x=96) and align its baseline to the key-hint row at y=1042.

findings.where: saves block (label, row, name field and buttons)
findings.what: The 'saves' label is small, dim 16px text. The save row is a thin lime-outlined strip with lime text, which competes with the main CTA as a second 'selected' item. The row is 42px tall against 48px menu buttons. The name field, 'change name' and 'create a new save' form a third control row with a different height (40px) and different widths. Three styles of box sit within 90px.
findings.fix: Give the save row the same 56px height and 4px radius as the menu buttons. Fill it with --ui-raised and use a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Mark selection with a 3px lime bar on the left edge instead of a full lime outline. Put 24px between the main block and 'saves', and 16px between 'saves' and the row. Make the name field and the two buttons 48px tall to match.

findings.what: The four mode buttons have uneven heights (56px for the lime one, 48px for the others) and spacing (8px between them). The label '2 player co-op (same machine)' puts an explaining parenthetical on screen. The arcade demos are not separated from the real modes. All four read as equal siblings except for the fill.
findings.fix: Make every button 56px tall with an 8px gap, and keep the lime fill as the only difference. Change the label to '2 player co-op'. Put the two demos under a 24px gap, or in a quieter second group with --tx-2 text, so the career modes read first.

findings.what: This is the key-hint row (wasd move, mouse aim, lmb fire, e search, f1 controls), and it is about 15px in muted grey. Under the 1080 couch-readability bar it is too small. Its key caps are heavier than the words, so it competes with the version stamp. It is also keyboard-only and shows no pad glyphs.
findings.fix: Set the labels at 16px --tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better, with the key caps at 16px, 600 weight and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Show the glyphs of the device in use. Hide 'e search' here, since it is a raid control.

findings.what: The two buttons are 48px tall with a 1px light border, about 16px text, and a gap of 16px. They sit at x=1611-1823, which is not on the 5% margin (x=1824 is close, but the top margin is 33px against 5% of 1080 = 54px). They are small, and 'settings' does not read as the main utility.
findings.fix: Move them to 54px from the top and 96px from the right edge. Make 'settings' the first of the two and use an icon. Make 'go fullscreen' a --tx-2 text button without a border. Raise the text to 18px.

findings.what: The tagline is about 18px in dim grey with wide tracking and sits 36px under the title and 24px above the buttons. It sits in a vertical gap that is neither tight nor generous, and its contrast is marginal at about 4:1 on the dark background.
findings.fix: Use 20px --tx-2 (#aaa498) with +.04em tracking. Set 16px above it and 32px below, so it reads as part of the title lockup.

findings.what: The background is a flat near-black vignette with no art, grain, or silhouette. The column occupies the centre with about 300px of dead space above the title and 250px below the save row.
