findings.what: Slot 1 has a lime border and slot 2 has a grey fist with no border. Slots 3-0 are ghost silhouettes, so the row is an uneven mix of box sizes and loose icons. The slot numbers sit at two different baselines (1, 2 inside the boxes, 3-0 outside). The 'f' key chip on slot 2 is tiny, about 12px, which is under the 16px minimum.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots as 104x100 boxes on a --ui-line border with an 8px gap. Put the slot numbers at 16px in the same top-left corner of every box. Raise the key chip to 16px.

findings.what: 'scav pistol' is right-aligned with a long gap to 'b / i backpack', which is left-aligned at 14px. The panel is 2px from the right screen edge, tighter than the other panels, and its rounded corners differ from those of the controls list.
findings.fix: Set a 24px right and bottom margin, a single 16px label baseline, and left-align the backpack hint to the panel padding of 16px. Use a 4px radius on every panel.

findings.where: mixed small text and the map readout
findings.what: The 'c 152m' pill with an arrow floats at the right edge over the building, duplicating the top 'extract 152m' pill. The 'the long dock cache' tooltip floats in the map with no anchor. Both repeat information, and the guide says a line drawn twice is a defect.
findings.fix: Remove the 'c 152m' pill and keep the top banner only. Show the cache name only when the player focuses on it, and anchor it with a 4px pointer.

v.verdict: This is the title menu, not the extracted HUD card the file name promises, so there is nothing to compare with the earlier HUD review. As a title screen it has a clear lime primary button but an off-palette orange gradient logo, a second lime focus in the saves list, and tiny, dim secondary text.

findings.what: The picture is the main title screen (version v0.1263), not the extracted card. The earlier controls-list, banner and chip advice cannot be judged from it.
findings.fix: Re-shoot the extracted state of goal-career-host and re-submit it. Treat this title screen as a separate review.

findings.what: It uses an orange-gold vertical gradient with a drop shadow. The guide bans gradient washes. The orange is near rarity gold and warn amber, and it sits right above the lime button, so the two accents fight. The 'ascend. pillage. extract.' tagline underneath is dim grey at about 18px.
findings.fix: Draw the logo flat in --tx-1 #efe9dc with no shadow, or as flat --acc. Keep it at 72-96px f-cond 800. Raise the tagline to 20px --tx-2 with +.04em tracking, 16px under the logo.

findings.what: There are four buttons in one equal-weight block. 'arcade demo' items have the same size and border as 'co-op', so the secondary choices compete with each other. The lime 'player 1' button is a flat 56px bar with dark text. It is the right primary action, but the gap to the next row is 8px against 8px between the others, so nothing separates the groups.
findings.fix: Keep the lime button at 56px. Make the other three 48px with 1px #4a5257 borders. Put the two demos in a half-width row, or 24px below as a quieter 16px text group. Use a 16px gap after the primary.

findings.what: The 'pillager new' row has a lime border and lime text, which reads as a second selected item next to the lime primary button. Lime should mean selected only. The 'saves' label is about 14px and low contrast. The row below mixes a text box with two buttons of different widths, and 'change name' and 'create a new save' sit at 14-15px.
findings.fix: Make the idle row --ui-panel with a #4a5257 border and tx-1 text. Show lime only when it has focus. Set the 'saves' label to 16px --tx-2. Make the name field and buttons 48px high with the same 16px type. Align the 'new' tag to a 16px right inset.

findings.what: The key hints are about 14-15px, low-contrast grey on near black, and the keycap boxes use a bright white outline. The version stamp is about 12px, below the 14px floor. Hints for 'wasd, mouse, lmb, e' are clutter on a menu.
findings.fix: Show a single 16px --tx-2 line such as 'f1 controls' with a 1px #4a5257 keycap. Move the version to 14px --tx-2 at the 5% margin. Delete the movement hints from the title.

findings.what: A tiny teal chip with a teal border is stuck to the top edge. Teal is reserved for extraction. It is about 15px text and reads as a stray debug tag. It is not aligned to anything.
findings.fix: Use a --tx-2 16px label with the device icon, at the same 24px margin and baseline as the top-right buttons. Or put it inside the bottom legend.

findings.what: They are about 14-15px text in boxes whose borders are brighter than the menu buttons'. The right margin is about 97px and the top is 33px, so the margins don't follow the 5% rule, and they are unaligned with the version stamp at left (96px).
findings.fix: Make them 48px high with 16px f-cond 600 text and 1px #4a5257 borders. Use the same 96px side margin and 48px top margin as the version stamp.

findings.what: A soft radial vignette fills the screen with no art, no key visual, and no hint of the game's world. The 640px of empty space left and right makes the screen feel like a web form, not an ARC Raiders-style title.
findings.fix: Add a dim top-down raid art layer at about 25% opacity behind the card, with a --scrim .80 overlay. Or offset the menu column to the left third and leave the art on the right.

v.verdict: The image is the title screen, not the raid HUD this file name promises. The title is clean and the lime CTA reads first, but the amber gradient logo competes with it, and the small text and teal chip are weak.

findings.what: goal-career-peer-extracted should show the raid HUD (extracted card, peer list, controls line). This image is the title menu, so none of the earlier HUD advice can be checked: folding the controls to one line, the right-edge chip, the peer panel colours and the contract alert.
findings.fix: Re-capture the real extracted state and re-run the review. Until then the earlier five findings stay open.

findings.what: The amber gradient logo with a drop shadow is the heaviest element and fights the lime CTA, which breaks the one-accent rule. The gradient and shadow are also template tells. Amber is reserved for P1 and warnings.
findings.fix: Set the wordmark flat in --tx-1 at about 96px f-cond 800 with no gradient or shadow. Keep lime only on the CTA, or use a flat 3px lime underline.

findings.what: It is about 14px in muted grey, directly under the CTA, and has no button affordance. It looks like a caption, so a second player cannot tell it is an action or find its focus state.
findings.fix: Make it a 40px outlined secondary button at 20px f-cond 600 in tx-1 with a --ui-line-hi 1px border. Put it 16px below the CTA, full width or paired beside it. It needs a lime focus border.

findings.what: The 'saves' label is dim at about 16px, and the focused save row has only a thin lime outline. The name field and the two buttons below look the same weight as the row. The field text 'pillager' also repeats the save name 'pillager new', which is confusing.
findings.fix: Raise the label to tx-2 at 16px with +.04em tracking. On the focused row use --ui-raised plus a 4px lime left bar, and bring the name to 20px. Use a 16px gap between the row and the controls row. Show the field as a placeholder, not a filled value.

findings.what: The teal-outlined chip uses the extraction-only colour for a device label, and it sits tight to the top edge at about 7px.
findings.fix: Set it in tx-2 with a --ui-line-hi border, 16px type, and 24px from the top. Alternatively merge it into the bottom hint row.

findings.what: The row has 8 to 10px key caps with 16px muted text. It runs 3px from the version stamp's baseline and is not aligned with it. On the title screen it is clutter and sits in the same band as the legal text.
findings.fix: Keep one 16px line, aligned to a 24px bottom margin, with the keys in tx-1. Put the version stamp on the same baseline. Drop the cap fills.

findings.what: The buttons have a wide right margin of about 98px, which doesn't match the 5% margin grid. They are the same weight as the secondary buttons, and the 2px outer frame on the page adds noise.
findings.fix: Set the margin to 48px right and top. Use 20px f-cond 600 with a 40px height. Remove the page-edge border.

findings.what: It is about 18px in grey with wide tracking and sits between the logo and the CTA. It is not on the type scale, and the gap above the CTA is tight at about 24px.
findings.fix: Use 20px f-cond 600 in tx-2. Leave 32px below the logo and 32px above the CTA.

v.verdict: The capture now shows the real title screen, but the gradient amber logo with drop shadow, the bright lime 'retry' that competes with the focused row, and the stack of near-identical outlined bars make it read like a template; none of the earlier fixes have landed.

findings.what: The logo is an orange-to-amber gradient with a hard drop shadow. It is the only warm, glossy element on a flat dark screen. It clashes with the lime accent and the flat ARC Raiders style, and it breaks the no-gradient rule. The 'ascend. pillage. extract.' tagline is small, bold and dim, and has too little space under the logo.
findings.fix: Draw the logo flat in --tx-1 #efe9dc with no shadow and no gradient, 80px f-cond 800. Set the tagline to 20px --tx-2 with +.04em tracking, 16px under the logo, in weight 600 or less. Keep the amber for P1 colour only.

findings.what: The 'retry' button is a large solid lime fill, the loudest thing on the screen. It pulls the eye away from the focused menu row and from the logo. A raid warning should not be the primary action. The two-line sentence is explaining copy, in a body size around 15px that is below the 16px minimum. The red panel is also wedged between the menu and the saves block with no spacing separation.
findings.fix: Make 'retry' a 40px outlined button with a 1px --danger border and tx-1 text, with lime only when focused. Shorten the copy to one 16px line, such as 'player 2 is in a raid in the other window'. Put 24px of space above and below the banner, or move it above the stack as a slim 48px strip.

findings.what: Four same-width, same-height, same-weight bars give no hierarchy. '1 player' should be the main action but looks like the others. The focused row (2 player co-op) has only a thin lime outline and a 3px left bar, which is easy to miss from a couch. The two arcade demos are given the same weight as the real modes. '2 player co-op (same machine)' puts a parenthetical in a button label.
findings.fix: Make '1 player' 56px high with the --acc fill and --acc-ink text, or give the focused row an --acc fill. Make the other rows 48px, left-aligned, with a --ui-line-hi border. Drop '(same machine)' to a 16px --tx-2 sublabel. Move the two arcade demos 24px lower as a quieter 16px text group.

findings.what: The saves block is cramped and inconsistent. The label 'saves' is tiny and dim, about 14px. The save row 'pillager new' is lime text on a lime-outlined box, so it competes with the focused menu row. The row below mixes a text field and two buttons at different widths, and 'change name' and 'create a new save' are 15px type. The field's left edge differs from the button text. 'new' is dim at the right with little inset.
findings.fix: Set the 'saves' label to 16px --tx-2 with 8px below it. Make the idle save row --ui-panel with a --ui-line-hi border and tx-1 text, lime only on focus. Make the field and both buttons 48px high with 16px/600 type. Use a 16px inner inset and align the 'new' tag to the same 16px right inset. Put 24px above the block.

findings.what: The legend lists movement controls (wasd move, mouse aim, lmb fire, e search) on the title screen, which is clutter. The keycaps are tiny and bold, and the text is about 15px dim grey on near black. The version stamp is about 12px and sits off the 5% margin, so it fails the 14px 'fine' size.
findings.fix: Show a single 16px --tx-2 line, 'f1 controls', with a 1px --ui-line-hi keycap. Remove the movement hints from the title. Set the version to 14px --tx-2 at the 96px (5%) margin.

findings.what: 'go fullscreen' and 'settings' are two small outlined 48px buttons in 15px bold type that look unrelated to the menu stack below. They sit about 1000px from the focus area, and the first is a utility with no reason to be this prominent. Their border and type weight don't match the main menu.
findings.fix: Make both 40px, 16px/600, with a --ui-line-hi border. Right-align them to the 5% margin (x=1824, y=96). Fold 'go fullscreen' into settings, or show it as a text link.

findings.what: The 558px column holds the logo, menu, banner and saves, but the spacing is uneven: 8px between menu rows, about 10px before the banner, 22px before 'saves', and 8px under it. About 200px of empty space sits at the bottom while the cluster sits above centre, and the flat void with a faint vignette has no art or identity beyond the logo.
findings.fix: Put every gap on the 8px grid: 16px between menu rows, 24px between groups. Centre the cluster vertically at about y=540. Add one low-contrast piece of key art, such as a faint extraction-site silhouette, behind the column.

findings.what: Menu labels, buttons, saves and the legend all use similar bold condensed type at 15-20px, with no size jump except the logo. The 'saves' label and the banner copy are in body font at small sizes with low contrast.
findings.fix: Limit it to the guide scale: 32px title for the logo group if needed, 20px/600 for menu rows, 16px/600 for labels and buttons, 14px for the version. Keep --tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better for anything read.

v.verdict: This is the in-raid hud, not the title screen. The ammo block is a good hero, but the rest is small mixed-style panels with explaining text, a duplicated extract readout and a hp bar that does not hold its number.

findings.where: top-right run info panel (1603-1900, 20-158) and left 'current pillagers' panel (8-367, 143-242)
findings.what: Body text is about 14-16px on a translucent map. The rows are all the same weight and size, so objectives and players read as a wall of text. The run info panel has two different indents and a chevron, and the two panels use different paddings and header styles.
findings.fix: Set row text to 20px f-cond 600 --tx-1 and labels (dawn, clear, value at risk) to 16px --tx-2. Use 8px row gaps, 16px panel padding, a --ui-panel fill at .9 opacity and a 1px #4a5257 border. Use one header style (16px --tx-2) for both panels and put the chevrons at the same 16px right inset.

findings.what: The 'hp 100' number is about 34px bold and taller than the 30px bar, so it spills out of the bar top and bottom. It is a saturated green block with no frame, so it reads as a template bar. It sits right against the screen edge.
findings.fix: Make the bar 24px high with a 1px #2e3337 track and an --ok fill. Put the number at 32px f-cond 700 left of the bar or inside it with 8px padding. Inset everything 5% (96px left, 54px bottom) to line up with the ammo block.

findings.where: extract info, top centre (904-1016, 47-73) and bottom-right marker 'c 152m' (1800-1890, 470-500)
findings.what: The extract distance appears twice, 'extract 152m' under the clock and 'c 152m' on the right. The owner's one-place rule makes a line drawn twice a defect. The teal pill has a different shape from the panels, and the 'c' prefix is cryptic.
findings.fix: Keep the top-centre pill only, as 20px f-cond 600 --extract on a --ui-panel fill, 4px radius. Delete the right-edge pill, or reduce it to an arrow with no text if an off-screen pointer is needed.

findings.what: 'contract item nearby · gold glow marks the box' is an explaining sentence with a middle dot and a second clause, and it sits in amber over the map. It is clutter, and the amber bar and icon look like the old accent.
findings.fix: Cut it to 'contract item nearby', 20px --tx-1 on a --ui-panel fill, with a 3px --warn bar. Drop the 'gold glow' explanation (teach it once in how to play). Align the left edge to the 5% margin, 96px.

findings.where: 'player 2 not linked' toast (881-1039, 893-930) and 'f1 controls' chip (435-538, 930-952)
findings.what: A black toast floats in mid-screen over the hotbar area. It is a third panel style, with a hard black fill, no border and no radius. The 'f1 controls' chip is about 14px and overlaps the map next to the hotbar, so it is hard to find and low contrast.
findings.fix: Move the toast to the top-centre alert banner slot or drop it. Show the controls hint as one 16px --tx-2 line, 'f1 controls', mid-bottom left, in a 1px #4a5257 keycap, 16px above the hotbar and aligned to the 96px margin.

findings.what: Two round icons and two text chips use amber and teal, with a different border colour on each, 28px text and tight padding. They look like the loudest items on the left, louder than the hp bar. The teal competes with the extract teal, which is reserved for extraction.
findings.fix: Use one chip style: 48px high, 16px --tx-1 label, 1px #4a5257 border, a --ui-panel fill. Show status with a glyph tint only (--warn for concealed, --ok for in cover). Reserve teal for extraction.

findings.what: The slot number labels (3-0) are about 14px and very dim, around 2:1 on the map. The slot 1 selected frame is amber-orange, but the selected colour is lime. Slots 1 and 2 are 100px wide while the ghosted weapon silhouettes are inconsistent in size and scale.
findings.fix: Make the selected frame 2px --acc #e6ff3d. Set the slot numbers to 16px --tx-2 on a --ui-panel plate. Make all slots 96px squares on an 8px gap with the same silhouette box.

findings.what: A purple-grey overlay washes the map, so the panels' translucent black fills don't match it and the white text fringes against the busy tiles. 'value at risk' lists 'you  -' with no $ and the text 'in' in objectives looks capitalised ('In chill row').
findings.fix: Give every HUD panel a solid --ui-panel fill at .9 opacity instead of .6 translucent black. Check that the 'in' glyph is lower case (the 'i' in Barlow Condensed has a dot) and show '$0' for you.

v.verdict: A busy raid HUD with six separate corner panels at mixed sizes, no clear hero element, and tiny low-contrast text; this is a different screen from the title screen reviewed earlier, so there is no earlier advice to judge.

findings.where: top-left 'current pillagers' list (8-367, 143-242) and top-right 'run info' (1603-1900, 20-160)
findings.what: Text is 14-16px, below the 16px minimum, and tightly packed with 4px row gaps. The panels differ in width, padding and border. Both have a caret in the corner, which conflicts with the order that windows close with an x. The 'value at risk' label is dim grey. Two large text blocks compete with the centre action.
findings.fix: Make the rows 20px f-cond 600 with 8px gaps and 16px padding. Use one --ui-panel fill with a 1px #4a5257 border and 4px radius, and the same width for both. Make the labels 16px --tx-2 #aaa498. Collapse 'run info' to one line by default, as the quiet-hud order requires.

findings.what: The bar is a flat bright green rectangle with 'hp 100' at about 32px in a thin dark outline. It is the loudest thing on screen and sits on the busy map with no panel. The bar is flush at the bottom-left, clipped by the screen edge, and 8px from the status chips above it. 'hp 100' fights the 56px ammo number for hero status.
findings.fix: Put the bar on a --ui-panel plate at the 5% margin (54px left, 48px up from the bottom). Make it 20px high with a 1px #4a5257 border. Use --ok #76b97c only for the fill. Set the 'hp 100' text to 20px f-cond 700 inside the bar. Leave a 16px gap above for the chips.

findings.what: The amber 'concealed' text is warn-coloured and the 'in cover' text is teal. This is two bright colours on a dark pill, sitting right against the hotbar. Teal is reserved for extraction. The icons are circled in different colours, so they read as two unrelated styles. The pill padding differs from the top-left panel.
findings.fix: Draw both chips in --tx-1 on --ui-panel with a 1px #4a5257 border and the 4px radius. Use a small 16px glyph in --tx-2. Only a hostile or hurt state gets --danger or --warn. Remove the teal and amber rings, and keep amber for P1 identity only.

findings.what: The hotbar is cut off by the bottom edge, with no bottom margin, while the ammo card sits 28px up. The two are not aligned. The slot numbers 3-0 are small, dim ghost icons and nearly invisible on the map. The selected slot has an amber border, but lime is meant to mean 'selected'. The weapon name 'scav pistol' is 20px and 'b / i backpack' is about 14px at the card edge.
findings.fix: Align the hotbar and ammo card bottoms to the same 48px bottom margin and 5% right margin. Make the selected slot border 2px --acc #e6ff3d. Fade the empty slot icons to 40% and make the numbers 16px --tx-2. Raise 'b / i backpack' to 16px.

findings.what: A tiny 14-16px chip floats mid-map with a keycap, not at a margin and not aligned with the hotbar. It also looks different from the other chips. The raid-controls order says it should be one short line mid-bottom left.
findings.fix: Anchor it to the same left margin, directly above the status chips, at 16px --tx-2, with a 1px #4a5257 keycap. Drop the extra panel fill.

findings.what: The '15:00' clock is 30px, light grey, on the map with no plate. The teal 'extract 152m' pill below it is a second, differently styled label. The same distance appears again as 'c 152m' at (1812-1890, 485). A line drawn twice is a defect.
findings.fix: Show the clock at 32px f-cond 700 on a --ui-panel plate. Keep one extraction readout: the pill in --extract with 16px text. Remove 'c 152m' or move the arrow to the screen edge without a repeated number.

findings.what: A 16px label sits in a small green-bordered tag at the very top-left, 10px from the edge. This is off the 5% margin and clashes with the 'current pillagers' panel just below it. The letter colour is neither tx-1 nor lime.
findings.fix: Move it to the 5% margin, or remove it once the prompt device is known. If it stays, make it 14px --tx-2 with a 1px #4a5257 border and the 4px radius.

findings.what: Panel treatments are inconsistent: black translucent boxes with a white outline (top-left, top-right), a heavier black ammo card, bare text for hp and the clock, and pills for chips. Some corners are 4px and some about 8px. The panel opacity varies, so contrast on the orange rooms differs from panel to panel.
findings.fix: Use one HUD panel recipe: --ui-panel at 85% opacity, a 1px #4a5257 border and a 4px radius. Make every HUD element use it or none of them.

v.verdict: The raid HUD is readable and the ammo block is a good Destiny-style hero number, but the panels disagree with each other. Left-edge stacking, a capital letter, mixed type sizes and the dense controls list keep it from polished. The earlier findings were about a title screen, which is a different screen from this one.

findings.where: run info header (top right, x1604-1900, y20-55)
findings.what: The header shows a capital 'I' in 'run Info', which breaks the all-lower-case order. It is also a heavy dark bar with a chevron that reads as a dropdown control. Its frame, type size and fill differ from the pillagers list and the ammo panel.
findings.fix: Change the string to 'run info'. Give it the same 4px radius, --ui-panel fill and 1px --ui-line-hi border as the other panels. Use 16px f-cond 600 in tx-2 with a 16px chevron.

findings.what: This is a large 300x300 panel of about 22 rows. It covers the left side of the screen, sits mid-left instead of mid-bottom, and is open by default. It holds three group labels at tx-2 and about 14px, and 12 key chips at mixed widths. That is clutter, and the style guide says it should start folded to one line.
findings.fix: Fold it to one 16px line, 'f1 controls', at bottom-left, x24 / y1000. When it opens, set every label and row at 16px tx-1 with group labels in tx-2 at 16px. Use equal 40px-wide key chips and a 24px panel padding.

findings.where: banner 'contract item nearby · gold glow marks the box' (x330-725, y777-802)
findings.what: It is an explaining sentence wedged against the controls panel and the pool wall, with a 3px amber bar. It is a second explanatory line next to the controls list. Its yellow text is close to the lime accent, and its left edge is under 20px from the controls panel.
findings.fix: Shorten it to 'contract item nearby', with the explanation removed. Put it in the left feed or at top-centre as the only alert, in --warn at 20px f-cond 600 on a --ui-panel fill, and leave 16px of clearance from other panels.

findings.what: The 'concealed' and 'in cover' pills use 24px amber and teal text, which makes them louder than the weapon slot. The hp bar is a filled mid-green block with 'hp 100' in about 32px white type placed on top of the fill. That type is oversized and low in contrast. The cluster also has no 24px margin: the hp bar nearly touches the bottom and left screen edges.
findings.fix: Make the pills 20px f-cond 600, with the text in tx-1 and a 1px border in --warn or --extract. Make the hp bar 12px tall, with the 'hp 100' label at 20px above it. Move the cluster in by 24px from the left and the bottom.

findings.where: pillagers list (x8-368, y143-242) and top-centre timer (x900-1035, y10-75)
findings.what: The list sits 8px from the screen edge, against a 24px or larger margin elsewhere. It carries three type sizes, with 'value at risk' in tx-2 at 14px. Its table of five rows is as small as the controls list. The 'extract 152m' teal chip and the 15:00 timer are close together and different in scale: 15:00 is 28px in white and the chip is 16px.
findings.fix: Move the list to x24/y24 and set the rows to 16px with a 24px-wide right-aligned money column. Use 'value at risk' in 16px tx-2 and a 4px radius. Keep 15:00 at 32px and centre the 'extract 152m' chip 8px below it in the --extract style at 16px.

findings.what: Both are small fragments of UI. The 'keyboard' chip is green on dark, with a border colour matching no other panel. It sits at 8px from the top-left corner and is the third distinct frame style on this screen. The extraction marker 'c 152m' is the only text starting with a letter that makes no sense without context.
findings.fix: Put the 'keyboard' chip in the controls row of the folded list as a 16px tx-2 label with a --ui-line-hi border, or drop it. Change 'c 152m' to 'extract 152m', or draw only the arrow and the distance.

findings.what: The panel is good: the hero number '12 / 24' is the right size. But it reaches 10px from the right screen edge, and the weapon name 'scav pistol' at about 22px is nearly as large as the 56px ammo count. The 'b / i backpack' hint at 14px is below the 16px minimum.
findings.fix: Move the panel in by 24px from the right and the bottom. Set 'scav pistol' to 20px tx-2 and the hint to 16px tx-2. Keep the 56px ammo count as the one hero number and make '/ 24' tx-2 at 32px.

findings.what: Slot 2 holds a fist icon with a tiny 'f' badge. The unselected slots 3-0 are faint ghost silhouettes with digits at about 14px. The slot digits sit around 16px at low contrast against the busy pool and wall art. The two filled slots have a 3px amber border, which competes with the other warning amber on this screen.
findings.fix: Put all slots on a --ui-panel fill at 80% with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Make the selected slot border lime (--acc), 3px, not amber. Set digits to 16px tx-2 and drop the ghost silhouettes for empty slots to 30% opacity.

v.verdict: This is a clean, lower-case run-over card with a clear lime 0 sp hero and a single lime leaderboard button. It is held back by an empty score panel, text that is too small, and a weak lower half, so a player would call it decent but not polished. It is not the same screen as the earlier title-screen review, so I can't compare the two.

findings.what: The panel is stretched to match the money panel but holds only two rows. The bottom 150px is empty, and the 56px hero 0 sp sits mid-panel and floats. The two panels look unbalanced.
findings.fix: Anchor the hero to the same baseline as the $5,065 total at y~485 and separate it with the same 1px divider. Or move the sp total to a full-width hero strip above both panels. Fill the gap with the 3 medal/bonus rows instead of leaving it blank.

findings.what: The labels (raid score, money, items secured, haul value) are about 14px in --tx-2 grey on a dark panel. That is below the 16px minimum and hard to read from a couch. The values are bold and bright by comparison, so the label/value contrast is extreme.
findings.fix: Set all labels to 16px f-cond 600 in --tx-2 #aaa498 (4.5:1 or better), and set value rows to 20px. Use a 36px row pitch and keep the 'raid score' and 'money' headers at 16px with +.04em tracking.

findings.what: 'run goals: support mg (field)' is a long label squeezed against the $2,565 value with about 10px between them. It reads as crowded and is nearly clipped. The parentheses and the colon also look like debug text.
findings.fix: Split it into two rows, 'run goals' and a sub-line of 'support mg' in 16px --tx-2 with a 24px indent. Or shorten it to 'support mg' and give the label column at least 16px of gap before the value.

findings.what: The three octagon medals are 40px with a 14px star. They are dim, with hairline outlines and a thin amber underline, and are not centred in the card. The amber underlines look like a link or a rarity bar. All three show an identical star, so they give no information, and the row is the weakest part of the card.
findings.fix: Enlarge each medal to 56px with a 2px --ui-line-hi border. Give each its own distinct glyph, or fill it with --acc-ink on --acc when earned. Replace the amber underline with a 16px tx-1 label. Make the gap between medals 24px.

findings.where: +130 xp and 'how did that run feel +' (889-1030, 740-808)
findings.what: Both lines are small, grey, floating text between the medals and the button. The 16px or smaller type is hard to read. The xp reward is a progression number and has no emphasis. The '+' affordance on the survey is cryptic, and the 60px of empty space around both lines makes the lower half sparse.
findings.fix: Show '+130 xp' at 20px f-cond 700 in --tx-1, 24px below the medals. Make the survey a 16px --tx-2 text button with a 1px --ui-line border, 40px high, or remove it from the card. Pull the leaderboard button up so the gaps are 24px, 24px and 32px.

findings.what: The button is correct as the primary action in lime with dark text, but the 'leaderboard' label is only about 20px and the button is a plain slab with no focus ring or hover cue. It looks like the only interactive element. The x at top-right is a heavy white-bordered square that competes with it.
findings.fix: Add a 2px --acc-hover outer ring or glow as the pad focus state, and set the label to 24px f-cond 700. Draw the x with a 1px --ui-line-hi border in --tx-2, 40x40, and show lime only on focus.

findings.what: The teal --extract title is correct, but at about 32px it is small for the screen's headline. It is overshadowed by the 56px lime 0 sp, and the large x box is offset from the title baseline.
findings.fix: Keep it teal, with the x vertically centred on the title baseline (y~177). Add 24px more space below the title before the panels. Set the stat tile numbers at 24px and the labels at 16px, so the 0%, 0, 0:00 and 100 tiles read as one tier.

findings.what: The four tiles have uneven widths (about 132, 133, 134 and 132px) and use faint borders on a near-identical fill, so they barely read as separate objects. The labels are 14px grey. All values are zero, so the row gives no information.
findings.fix: Make the four tiles exactly equal, 8px apart and 72px high, with a 1px --ui-line-hi border on --ui-raised. Set the labels to 16px --tx-2 and the numbers to 24px --tx-1. Hide tiles that are all zero, or dim them.

v.verdict: The clock, ammo and hotbar read well, but the top-right goals panel is still a dense wall of mixed small text, the left panel is tiny, and the duplicate extract markers, the explanatory feed line and the off-grid hp bar were not fixed.

findings.what: It is a 10-row wall of ~16px text with no header hierarchy. Sub-headers (dawn clear, contracts, run goals) look the same as the rows. The last row reads 'down a warden item', with a garbled 'item' tag. The panel's text is almost flush with its edges and there is no row spacing, so the whole thing looks like debug output.
findings.fix: Use a 16px --tx-2 header row ('goals 0/3'). Use 20px --tx-1 rows with 8px gaps. Put a 1px --ui-line divider between 'contracts' and 'run goals'. Use 16px inner padding. Show progress right-aligned as 16px --acc only on the active row, and fix the 'item' tag to a 16px --warn glyph.

findings.what: The text is ~14px, so names, 'dead' and the footer are hard to read at couch distance. The 'value at risk' header and the '-' dashes are cramped. The panel sits at x=8 with no 5% margin, and its right edge touches the building art. Its style does not match the top-right panel.
findings.fix: Set the rows to 20px f-cond 600 with the header at 16px --tx-2. Use 8px row gaps, 16px padding, --ui-panel at .9 fill and a 1px #4a5257 border. Move it to x=96 and share one chevron inset with the goals panel.

findings.what: The same distance is drawn twice. The top pill is jammed under the score card at 10px spacing and looks like part of it. The right-edge pill has a tiny 14px label with a teal arrow.
findings.fix: Keep only the pill, in 20px --extract. Put it 16px under the score card or move it next to the clock. Delete the right-edge text and keep only a teal arrow at the screen edge.

findings.what: The line is still the explanation 'gold glow marks the box'. It is two voices in one line, and the amber bar sits at x=15, outside the margin.
findings.fix: Cut it to 'contract item nearby' at 20px --tx-1 on --ui-panel with a 3px --warn bar, x=96. Teach the glow once in how to play.

findings.what: The bar is 8px from the bottom edge. It is flush with the left edge, off-grid against the 5% margin, and it crowds the status chips above it. 'hp 100' is dark text on mid-green with low contrast and is clipped by the bar's height.
findings.fix: Move it to x=96, bottom 54px. Make the bar 24px high with a #2e3337 track and an --ok fill. Put '100' at 32px f-cond 700 --tx-1 left of the bar, with 16px gaps to the chips.

findings.what: The two chips use different colours (amber and green) and different borders. The icon circles are a third style. All three clash with the lime accent and the hotbar.
findings.fix: Use one chip style: --ui-panel fill, 1px #4a5257 border, 4px radius, 20px --tx-1 text. Use colour only on the 16px icon. Align the chips to x=96.

findings.what: It floats mid-left at ~14px, partly hidden by a prop. It is not aligned to the hotbar or the margin and is hard to read.
findings.fix: Make it a 16px --tx-2 line with a 1px #4a5257 keycap, sitting 16px above the hotbar and aligned to x=96 or the hotbar's left edge (555).

findings.what: 'score' is a tiny 16px label over a 36px number, and the card is wider than the clock above it. The two cards have different fills and widths, so the top-centre stack looks unplanned.
findings.fix: Match the width of the clock card (~140px). Put '0 sp' at 56px --fs-hero f-cond 800 and the 'score' label at 16px --tx-2. Use 8px between the cards.

v.verdict: This is now the real extracted card and it reads cleanly, with a clear lime CTA, a clear total and a teal title, but the two stat panels are uneven, the text is too small and dim, and the lower half drifts.

findings.what: The raid score panel is mostly empty: two rows and about 150px of dead space beside the 8-row money panel. The raid score (0 sp, lime 56px) pulls the eye harder than the $5,065 money total, which is the number the player cares about. Labels such as 'raid score' and 'money' look like 16px tx-2 at low contrast and carry no weight.
findings.fix: Make the two panels equal height with the content top-aligned, or merge the score into one row above the money panel. Make the one hero number the money total (56px, tx-1) and set the sp total to 32px. Use 16px tx-2 headers with +.04em tracking and a 1px --ui-line underline.

findings.where: money rows 'run goals' and 'run goals: support mg (field)' (y389-427)
findings.what: The two rows have near-identical labels, and the second one looks like an explaining sentence. The label is crowded against the value ($2,565 sits right after '(field)'). The rows are also unclear: a +$2,500 line followed by a $2,565 line without a + sign.
findings.fix: Rename the rows so each says what it is ('goal bonus', 'field goal'), make the signs consistent, and keep at least 16px between label and value. If the second row is a sub-line, indent it 16px in tx-2.

findings.where: lower half (y630-830): medals, '+130 xp', 'how did that run feel +'
findings.what: Three disconnected centred items sit loosely with irregular gaps (about 50px, 52px, then 68px before the CTA). The medal underlines are amber, close to the lime and gold family. '+130 xp' at about 16px in the body font is weak, and 'how did that run feel +' is tiny, dim and not recognisable as a control. There is no pad focus state.
findings.fix: Use a 24px rhythm: medals, then '+130 xp' at 20px f-cond 600 in tx-1, then the survey as a 40px outlined secondary button at 20px with a --ui-line-hi border. Make the medal underlines --ui-line or the rarity colour as a 3px bar. Move the survey to the left of the CTA row.

findings.what: The four tiles use values at about 24px and labels at about 16px in a dim grey. Zero values ('0%', '0', '0:00') make the row look empty, and the tile borders are barely visible against the panel.
findings.fix: Set the labels to tx-2 at 16px with +.04em tracking, values at 32px f-cond 700, and borders in --ui-line-hi. Align the tile row edges with the panel edges at x681 and x1239 (they already match, keep them).

findings.what: The x is a heavy white-bordered 48px box. It is brighter than the title and competes with it, and it sits asymmetrically at 24px from the card edge while the title is centred.
findings.fix: Make it a 40px square with a --ui-line-hi border and a tx-2 glyph, 16px from the card edge, with a lime border only on focus. Keep the title at 32px.

findings.what: The CTA is correctly the one lime fill, but its label is about 20px, so the button is wide and tall for a small word. It is 24px from the card bottom but about 68px from the survey line above.
findings.fix: Set the label to 24px f-cond 700 and the button to 56px tall, with 32px above it and 32px below. Add a lime focus ring or an outer glow so pad focus is visible.

findings.what: The 718px card sits on a very dark, faintly noisy background, and the card fill (#161a1c) is nearly the same as the scrim. Separation depends only on the 1px border, and there is no identity beyond the lime and teal colours.
findings.fix: Add a 3px teal top bar under the title (extract colour, flat) and make the card border --ui-line-hi. Dim the scene to the .80 scrim so the card sits clearly above it.

v.verdict: The top-left list is gone, run info folds to a compact goals card and the hud reads cleaner, but the bottom-left stack and the top-centre cluster still ignore the shared panel, type and margin tokens.

findings.where: top-centre cluster (845-1075, 18-340): clock, team score, extract chip, goal-done banner
findings.what: Four stacked boxes with different widths, borders and fills, jammed together (score card touches the clock, extract chip overlaps the score card edge). The banner shows teal and bright 32px text, so it out-shouts the 56px-class clock and the eye has no single first target.
findings.fix: Use one 16px gap between boxes and one --ui-panel fill with a 1px #4a5257 border and 4px radius. Make the clock the only hero at 56px f-cond 800. Set the goal-done banner title to 20px f-cond 700 and animate it away after 2s. Centre all boxes on x=960 with the same 280px width.

findings.what: The hp bar is a flat full-green slab with 'hp 100' at roughly 32px, which is too loud. The armour bar is a different, thinner blue with 20px text. The two bars use different heights and fonts, and sit on the world with no plate.
findings.fix: Put both bars at 20px high on a --ui-panel plate with a 1px #4a5257 border and 4px radius. Set the text to 16px f-cond 700 --tx-1, and fill hp with --ok #76b97c. Keep the armour fill as one muted blue. Use an 8px gap between the bars. Leave the left margin at 54px and the bottom margin at 48px.

findings.what: 'concealed' is amber text on an amber-bordered chip, and 'in cover' is teal. The two chips read as different systems, and the round icons add a third border style. Amber is reserved for P1 identity and warnings, so using it for a neutral state is a colour-meaning clash.
findings.fix: Make both chips --tx-1 on --ui-panel with a 1px #4a5257 border, 16px f-cond 600, and a 4px radius. Keep the two icons at a 24px square with no ring. Use --acc, --warn or --danger only when a state is actually good, risky or bad.

findings.what: Empty slots draw only faint ghost icons with 16px numbers sitting on the map, so the row has no frame, and the two filled slots use mismatched borders (amber on the selected one, none on the other). The selected slot uses amber where the guide says lime --acc means 'selected'. The numbers are low-contrast over the water.
findings.fix: Draw every slot as a 72px tile with a --ui-panel fill, a 1px #4a5257 border and a 4px radius. Give the selected slot a 2px --acc #e6ff3d border. Set the numbers to 16px --tx-2 inside the tile at top-left. Drop empty icons to 30% opacity. Align the row bottom to the same 48px margin as hp.

findings.what: The text is about 16px, tight, and packed: 'goals 1/3' and 'run goals' repeat each other, and 'done power-up' repeats on each row. The green 'done' row, the white 'power-up' and the caret sit with no column alignment. The 4px-radius panel has no visible border, unlike its neighbours.
findings.fix: Remove the 'run goals' line. Show each row as 'name' left and a --ok check or 'power-up' at the right, in a right-aligned 16px column. Use 16px padding, an 8px row gap and a 1px #4a5257 border. Match the 280px width of the centre cluster.

findings.what: The same buff is shown twice, once as a red label over the player and once as a timer chip, in --danger red, which is meant for hostile or KIA and so reads as a threat. A line drawn twice is already ruled a defect.
findings.fix: Keep only the timer chip, in --acc ink on a --ui-panel plate, 16px. Delete the red over-head label. Keep 'shield' as a small 14px tag, or remove it too.

findings.what: It uses a 56px hero number, which is correct, but the card sits flush to the right edge (10px) and 30px above the hp baseline, so it does not align with the hp bar bottom (1068). 'auto rifle' at 20px is fine, but the '/ 150' is nearly as large as the hero number.
findings.fix: Set the right margin to 96px (5%) and the bottom to 48px. Make '/ 150' 20px --tx-2. Use a 1px #4a5257 border like the other panels.

findings.what: A small, low-contrast keycap with 16px text floats over the map between the chips and the hotbar, not attached to anything.
findings.fix: Dock it to the left margin directly above the chips, with a 16px --tx-2 label and a keycap drawn with a 1px #4a5257 border. Remove the extra panel fill.

v.verdict: The HUD is much quieter than before: the controls list is folded to one line, the banner explainer is gone, and the old pillagers list and the 'run info' header are gone. It still looks like a stack of unrelated boxes, with a crowded top-centre, mixed type sizes and mixed corner radii.

findings.what: The timer, team score, extract chip and goal-done toast are four separate boxes piled into one column, about 320px tall. They have different widths, fills and radii, and the toast sits right under the extract arrow, so it looks like a fifth item. The eye lands on the timer, the team score and the toast at once. Nothing has a clear first place.
findings.fix: Keep the 10:00 timer at 32px with the extract chip 8px below it. Move the team score to the top-left feed at x24/y24 at 16px. Show the goal-done toast only at y120 as the single alert, with a 16px gap below the chip. Give every box a 4px radius, a --ui-panel fill and a 1px --ui-line-hi border.

findings.what: The panel has a 'goals 1/3' title and a 'run goals' subtitle that say the same thing. The 'power-up' tag is repeated on every row. Row text is a mix of sizes and colours, with the green done row and white rows mixed together. The chevron is tiny. It is flush against the 20px margin, so it looks cramped.
findings.fix: Delete the 'run goals' line and the repeated 'power-up' words. Use a 16px tx-2 header ('goals 1/3'), 16px rows in tx-1 and the done row in --ok with a check glyph. Use 16px padding, a 4px radius, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and x1872/y24 from the right and top edges (24px margin).

findings.what: The concealed and in-cover pills use 20px amber and teal text with no clear rule. The armour bar and the hp bar are both 30px tall with a 24px label. The hp number looks like a second hero number next to the ammo. The armour label on the blue bar has weak contrast, and the labels are cramped against the left edge. The 'f1 controls' chip is parked in the middle of the water at x435, with no link to this cluster.
findings.fix: Make both bars 12px tall with a 16px label above each in tx-1. Keep the hp number at 20px, not 32px. Use equal-height pills with a 1px --warn or --extract border and tx-1 text. Put the 'f1 controls' chip at x24/y1000, directly above the hp bar, so it joins the cluster. Keep the 24px margin from the left and the bottom.

findings.what: The 24 / 144 ammo block is the strongest thing on screen, which is right, but at 56px it is bigger than it needs to be. It sits flush against the right edge, only 10px from it, and is out of line with the goals panel above (x1900). 'burst carbine' is in a plain, unconstrained weight.
findings.fix: Right-align the panel to x1896 (24px margin) and align the bottom with the hp bar at y1056. Set 'burst carbine' at 16px tx-2. Keep the 56px f-cond 800 number, with '/ 144' at 20px in tx-2.

findings.where: weapon slots (x890-1105, y955-1060) and slot numbers (x560-1460, y960-975)
findings.what: Slots 4 and 5 are lit, while 1-3 and 6-0 are bare grey numbers floating over the map. They are low in contrast, and their spacing is uneven and unrelated to the filled slots. The 'double damage 15s' buff chip above them has a red left border and uses a 14px font.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots on one row of equal 48px tiles with an 8px gap and a --ui-panel fill, with empty ones at 40% opacity. Put the buff chip on a 16px f-cond 600 line, 8px above the row, with a --danger left bar of 3px. Use 'double damage' only at 16px.

findings.where: world tags 'double damage', 'shield' (x327-435, y530-610) and 'c 152m' (x1810-1880, y470-500)
findings.what: The 'double damage' tag is red on a dark fill, with a repeat of the buff that is already shown in the bottom chip. 'shield' is a 12px label in teal that is hard to read. 'c 152m' is another extract distance, shown a second time next to the one at top-centre. Lines are drawn twice, which the guide forbids.
findings.fix: Delete the world 'double damage' tag, since the bottom chip already shows it. Raise 'shield' to 16px tx-1 or remove it. Delete the 'c 152m' chip. Keep one extract chip, at the top-centre.

findings.what: The round sunrise icon sits as a loose circle to the right of the timer, with no label. Its meaning is unclear. It sits outside the timer box and breaks its edge, so the box looks off-centre.
findings.fix: Put the icon inside the timer box at 24px, 8px from the right edge, or remove it. Centre the 10:00 text at x960 with 16px padding.

findings.what: Panels use at least three fills (near-black, teal-edged and translucent), different border styles and corners from 2px to 6px. They look like different systems. Type runs from about 12px to 56px in a dozen sizes.
findings.fix: Use one panel: --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 16px padding. Allow only the 56, 32, 20 and 16px type steps listed in the guide.

v.verdict: The hub does feel like this game, with a clear lime 'enter raid!' beacon. But the screen is crowded: overlapping translucent aura discs, two stacked prompts at the bottom, and a loud amber 'experimental' tag all compete for attention, and the capital letter in the [e] hint isn't the only break from the rules.

findings.where: bottom centre, around the stash station and the 'enter raid!' prompt
findings.what: The stash label, the sentence 'the welcome pack is in your stash.', the '[e] enter raid!' prompt and a blue aura disc all stack on top of each other over a half-hidden station. It reads as a collision. The explaining sentence is clutter. The prompt is the live primary action but is small and low-contrast on blue.
findings.fix: Delete the welcome-pack sentence, or move it to the left feed. Show one prompt only, at 20px f-cond 600 on a --ui-panel pill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Place it 16px under the station label and clear the aura disc behind it. Use lime (--acc) text only when the prompt is the focused action.

findings.where: the whole floor: 8 aura discs of different tints, plus a large central disc
findings.what: The translucent circles overlap each other and the characters (mainframe/settings, stash/last pour, the empty centre). The tints (purple, teal, tan, pink) have no meaning and look muddy over the navy floor. The centre disc has no label and no purpose. They compete with the enter-raid beacon.
findings.fix: Remove the centre disc and keep one 1px ring per station at 12% opacity. Use one neutral tint, and lime only on the nearest station. Never overlap neighbours.

findings.what: At around 56px it is the hero element, which is right for the hierarchy. But it is a lime-outlined black box on dark art. The exclamation mark is an arcade-style wink, and its bold 800 weight is as loud as the title. It sits on top of the pillars and the characters at the station, and the lime border is thin, inconsistent with the panel borders elsewhere.
findings.fix: Use a --ui-panel plate with a 4px radius and a 2px --acc border. Set the text at 32px f-cond 700 in --acc and drop the '!' so it matches the straight-copy rule. Align it centred 16px above the station, clear of the pillars.

findings.where: '***experimental feature may glitch***' tag under 'the last pour'
findings.what: This is a sentence-style warning on screen, set in amber (--warn) at about 14px, with asterisks as decoration. It looks like a debug leftover, it is cramped against the station label, and it adds clutter in a corner that already has the aura disc.
findings.fix: Replace it with a 16px '--warn' glyph and one word ('beta') inside the station label chip, or drop it. Remove the asterisks.

findings.where: top-right currency strip: '$900 0 xp stash $5,064 bag $0'
findings.what: The strip runs together with no panel and is spread over several type sizes (large $900, small 'xp', tiny 'stash/bag'), so they read as scattered text. It sits against the border of the arena, and the 'stash' figures are about 14px, below the 16px minimum for anything read. Per the guide, the career HUD should be a vertical list of identical items.
findings.fix: Use a vertical list on the right with a 16px label in --tx-2 and a 20px value in --tx-1, all items the same size. Put it in a --ui-panel box with 16px padding, 24px from the screen edge. Leave the build to cw-trcol if that job owns it.

findings.where: station name labels (wirt the gambler, the mainframe, shop, craft and hire, settings, the stash, fashion, the last pour)
findings.what: The chips are a consistent dark style, but the placement varies: some sit above the station, some overlap the furniture (shop, settings), and 'the stash' and 'fashion' sit at different offsets. Labels cross the aura discs and furniture edges.
findings.fix: Anchor every label centred 16px above its station, 20px f-cond 600 on --ui-panel with a 4px radius, and 8px/16px padding. Move the shop and settings chips above the furniture tops.

findings.what: The hotbar slots 3 to 0 are dimmed weapon silhouettes, nearly indistinguishable from the background. Slot 1 has a gold/amber border. The key numbers (about 12px) are far below 16px. The bar overlaps the arena floor edge and the wall.
findings.fix: Set slot numbers at 16px in --tx-2. Use lime (--acc) for the selected slot border, not amber, since lime means 'selected'. Raise locked-slot icons to 40% opacity with a 1px --ui-line border. Leave a 16px margin from the screen bottom.

findings.what: This is the cleanest element on screen. But the sub-line '12 items in stash · 0 runs' is about 14px, which is below the 16px floor, and the panel is flush-ish to the arena edge with an inconsistent margin against the right-hand strip.
findings.fix: Raise the sub-line to 16px in --tx-2. Put the panel at 24px from the top-left corner and match the right strip's margin. Keep the 32px title.

v.verdict: The hub reads as a prototype: the 'enter raid!' sign is the only strong accent but it clashes with the soft-rounded name tags, the bottom of the screen is a pile-up of tooltip, prompt, stash tag and hotbar, and nothing has a consistent type scale or panel style.

findings.where: bottom centre: the stash tag, the 'welcome pack' tooltip, the '[a] enter raid!' prompt and the lift pad
findings.what: Four stacked elements sit on top of each other over the lift pad, and the prompt is low contrast white-on-blue. The tooltip is an explaining sentence, and 'enter raid!' is shown twice (top sign and prompt).
findings.fix: Keep one prompt pill at 20px f-cond, --acc fill with --acc-ink text, 8px above the pad. Delete the welcome-pack sentence (or move it to a 16px label on the stash tag only). Drop the duplicate prompt, since the top sign already names the action.

findings.what: A stray second translucent circle overlaps the mainframe radius and reads as a rendering bug. Zone halos of different tints (purple, teal, tan, pink) also muddy the floor.
findings.fix: Remove the stray circle or snap it to the zone centre. Use one halo style: 2px --ui-line-hi ring at 12% fill, with only the active zone in --acc or its own colour.

findings.what: A 56px-class lime-on-black sign with an exclamation mark, in a hard-edged box, competes with the title card. It sits against the pillars and its bounding box is not centred on the avatars below. It is also louder than the real hero (the lime hotbar focus is the only other accent).
findings.fix: Make it a 32px f-cond 700 label in a --ui-panel box with a 1px --acc border, 4px radius, and remove the '!'. Reserve a filled lime fill for the live prompt only.

findings.where: name tags (gambler, mainframe, shop, settings, the last pour, fashion, the stash)
findings.what: Tags use different sizes and padding, and float at inconsistent distances from their stations. Some are cut by characters (fashion beside the avatar). Tag fill is lighter than the panel tokens.
findings.fix: One tag spec: 16px f-cond 600, 8px 12px padding, --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, centred 12px above the station. Offset 'the stash' and 'fashion' to avoid avatars.

findings.where: '***experimental feature may glitch***' under 'the last pour'
findings.what: Amber text with asterisks, an explaining sentence in a different tag style, and it butts against the 'the last pour' tag. It is a warning shown as clutter.
findings.fix: Replace with a small 14px --warn glyph plus the word 'beta' inside the station tag, or drop it. Remove the asterisks.

findings.where: top-left title card and top-right money readout
findings.what: The title card is a different style (dark outline, 32px) from the tags. The top-right '$900  0 xp  stash $5,064 bag $0' is a ragged row of mixed sizes, and 'xp' and the stash text sit at about 14px, too small for couch reading. The right strip also sits over the black letterbox with no margin alignment to the title card.
findings.fix: Use the same panel spec for both. Make the top-right a vertical list at 20px/16px with equal row heights (per the cw-trcol order). Move both to the 5% margin (96px) and align their baselines. Raise the 14px text to 16px, --tx-2 minimum.

findings.what: Slots 3 to 9 are dim, nearly invisible weapon silhouettes. The slot numbers are tiny (about 12px). Only slot 1 shows focus, in amber and not lime. Two identical fists in slots 1 and 2 look like a bug.
findings.fix: Slot number 16px --tx-2. Focus border 2px --acc (lime, not amber). Empty slots at 40% opacity with a dashed --ui-line border. Show the fist once.

findings.what: The black bars left and right, plus a grey wall frame, leave the hub looking like a cropped window, and the HUD text floats half on black and half on the map.
findings.fix: Fill the letterbox with --ui-void and keep all HUD inside the 5% safe area, or extend the scene to full width.

v.verdict: The hub is readable and the lime 'enter raid!' call-out is the right first read, but it is let down by a crowded middle, overlapping glow circles, mixed label styles and an untidy top-right readout.

findings.where: station labels (gambler, mainframe, shop craft and hire, settings, last pour, stash, fashion)
findings.what: Every station label has the same weight and the same small dark box. Nothing marks which station the player is at or near, and no focus or selected state is visible. The labels float away from their pads, e.g. 'the last pour' sits above the pad and its warning tag hangs below it. The 'enter raid!' label carries all the emphasis.
findings.fix: Light only the nearest station: 2px --acc border and --tx-1 text, with the others dimmed to --tx-2 at 70% opacity. Anchor every label 8px above its pad. Use the same 20px f-cond 600 for all labels, with 8px/16px padding and a 4px radius.

findings.what: Three different styles sit on one line: a large bold $900, a '0' with a tiny 'xp', and a small stash/bag string. The gaps are uneven and the 'xp' and stash text are below 16px. They sit on a bare background with no panel and are crowded against the frame edge. This is not the 1 by 1 same-size list the guide asks for.
findings.fix: Make every item 20px f-cond 600 in one panel (--ui-panel, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 16px padding). Stack them vertically with 8px gaps. Use --tx-1 for values and --tx-2 for labels, and keep the right margin at least 32px.

findings.where: '***experimental feature may glitch***' under 'the last pour'
findings.what: The tag is amber on a dark pill at about 14px, which is below the 16px floor. The asterisks look like debug text. It adds clutter and an explaining sentence, and it crowds the label above it.
findings.fix: Drop the asterisks and shorten it to 'experimental'. Set it at 16px --warn inside the label pill as a small tag. Alternatively, drop the text and use a 16px warn glyph beside the title.

findings.where: hub floor: translucent glow circles and rings
findings.what: The large pale circles overlap each other and the characters: the extra circle near the mainframe, the one at bottom-left near fashion, and the centre one. They muddy the floor, hide the pads and read as a template effect. The ring colours (purple, teal, gold, grey, violet) have no stated meaning.
findings.fix: Remove stray and overlapping circles. Keep one 1px --ui-line-hi ring per station, with the nearest station's ring in --acc at 40% fill. Keep each pad's colour only if it is a tied-down meaning, and cap the circle fill at 8% opacity.

findings.where: bottom toast 'the welcome pack is in your stash.' and the hotbar
findings.what: The toast is a full sentence at about 16px. It overlaps the stash station's blue panel and sits only 8px above the hotbar, which looks like a layout collision. The hotbar slots 3-0 are very dim, so the number labels and weapon icons are hard to read. The amber selected slot border is an amber/lime mismatch, since lime means selected.
findings.fix: Move the toast to the top-centre banner slot, or the left feed, and trim it to 'welcome pack in stash'. Raise the empty-slot icons to 50% opacity. Change the selected slot border to --acc 2px. Keep the hotbar at least 24px from the toast.

findings.where: top-left card 'the undercroft / 12 items in stash · 0 runs'
findings.what: The title is fine, but the sub line is about 14px, below the 16px floor. The card has different padding and a different border from the label pills and the top-right readout. The 12 items count duplicates information shown elsewhere.
findings.fix: Set the sub line to 16px --tx-2. Use the same panel style as the other cards (--ui-panel, 1px --ui-line-hi, 4px radius, 16px padding). Align the card left edge to the 32px margin.

findings.what: It is clearly the hero, but the exclamation mark reads as hype and conflicts with the straight-copy rule. The glow and text size (about 48px) sit on a plain dark pill with no pad or key prompt. It also overlaps the pillars behind it.
findings.fix: Change the copy to 'enter raid' and put it in a panel with a key hint chip, 16px, reading 'e'. Use f-cond 800 at 56px (the hero size) or drop to 32px. Do not overlap the pillars.

findings.what: The play area has uneven black and grey bands. The right side has a wide dark gutter while the left is narrower, and the HUD elements hug the edges at different distances. This makes the margins look unplanned.
findings.fix: Put all HUD elements on a common 32px safe-area margin. Centre the playfield, or make the letterbox bands symmetrical.

v.verdict: the hub reads as a busy template: a huge lime 'enter raid!' sign is the only strong hierarchy, while a noisy room of overlapping glow circles and a clipped, mixed-style HUD make it look unfinished.

findings.where: top-right currency strip ($900, 0 xp, stash $5,064 bag $0)
findings.what: The strip runs into the right screen edge, and the 'stash/bag' line sits in a different size and weight from '$900' and '0 xp'. The 'xp' label is tiny and dim, and 'stash $5,064 bag $0' is about 14px muted text on the void strip. It is also not a 1x1 vertical list. Everything is ragged and sits against the right edge with no 5% margin.
findings.fix: Make it one vertical list in the top-right with a 48px margin: $900, xp and stash each as a 20px f-cond 600 row, tx-1 for the value and tx-2 for the 16px label. Remove the 'xp' sub-label size jump and put 'bag' on its own row.

findings.what: At about 56px it is a lime fill-less text sign with an exclamation mark, in the f-cond hero size, and nothing else on the screen is that large, so the eye lands there before the player, the HUD or anything else. The '!' is arcade-style copy the guide forbids. The sign is also a one-off style: every other station label is a small white tag with a dark fill. It reads as a different UI.
findings.fix: Make it the same 20px tag as the other stations, lime text only when focused or in range, no '!' ('enter raid'). If it must be the hero, give it the 32px title size and keep the same dark tag fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius.

findings.where: proximity glow circles around each station and the player
findings.what: Large translucent circles (blue, teal, purple, tan, pink, brown) overlap each other and the characters. Their colours are not tied to player colours or rarity and carry no meaning, and the one near the mainframe tag overlaps two circles into a muddy blob. They add clutter and make the floor look like a template effect.
findings.fix: Remove the fills and show one 2px ring in --acc at 60% only on the station the player is currently in range of; the other stations show a 1px --ui-line ring or none.

findings.where: '***experimental feature may glitch***' under 'the last pour'
findings.what: A warning in amber with asterisks, 14px, jammed against the station label with 4px gap and a different pill size. Asterisk decoration and a sentence on screen are clutter, and the amber text is small on a mixed brown/purple floor.
findings.fix: Replace with a small --warn glyph or the single word 'beta' at 16px inside the same tag as the station label; delete the asterisks.

findings.where: toast 'the welcome pack is in your stash.' and 'the stash' tag
findings.what: The toast is a full sentence in a box that overlaps the stash table and sits 16px under its label, with a different border and fill from the station tags. It crowds the stash station and reads as a second, unrelated component. Explaining sentences are a defect here.
findings.fix: Show it in the left feed only (one place for a line), 16px, or drop it. If it stays, place it in the bottom-left above the hotbar, never on a station.

findings.what: Ten slots with nine greyed-out gun icons that are not owned, and two identical fist icons for 1 and 2. They give the player no information, the number labels are tiny (about 12px) and low contrast, and the hotbar clips the bottom edge of the map with a 12px margin. The selected slot uses a thin amber/gold border, not the lime focus, which breaks the rule that lime means selected.
findings.fix: Show only owned slots or dim empties to a 1px --ui-line outline with no icon; number labels 16px --tx-2; selected slot 2px --acc border with --ui-raised fill; keep 24px from the bottom edge.

findings.where: top-left plate 'the undercroft / 12 items in stash · 0 runs'
findings.what: A heavy bordered box with a 32px-ish title and a 14px subline that is dim and sits on a tight 8px padding. The stash count duplicates the 'stash $5,064' in the top-right, so the same information is shown twice. The box border and radius differ from the station tags.
findings.fix: Drop the second line (the counts live in the top-right list), keep only the zone title at 32px with the shared tag style, and align the left edge to the 48px margin.

findings.where: station labels (gambler, mainframe, shop craft and hire, settings, the last pour, the stash, fashion)
findings.what: All use the same dark pill at about 20px, which is right, but they sit at inconsistent distances from their station (some overlap the table or character, 'settings' sits on top of the wall panel, 'shop, craft, and hire' overlaps the counter). The pad focus ring is not distinguishable from the proximity circles, so which station is selected is not obvious from a couch.
findings.fix: Anchor every tag 16px above its station's top edge, centred; give the in-range tag a 2px --acc border and the others --ui-line-hi.

v.verdict: This is a clean, calm column menu with one clear lime primary button and lower case throughout. The amber gradient wordmark, the small type and the weak links between the saves and mode groups keep it below polished.

findings.what: The wordmark is an orange-amber gradient with a drop shadow. This breaks the 'no gradient washes' rule and conflicts with the lime-only accent. Amber is reserved for P1 and warnings, so the title looks like a different game's logo. It is also the only boldly styled element above the lime button, which splits the eye between the title and the main action.
findings.fix: Fill the wordmark flat in --tx-1 (#efe9dc), 800 weight, with no gradient or shadow. Alternatively, treat it as art with a proper logo lockup. Make the title and the 1 player button the only two strong elements.

findings.where: mode buttons and the saves block
findings.what: There are four mode buttons at about the same weight, and two of them are 'arcade demo'. The party-only modes get as much visual weight as the career modes. The saves section sits under them as a separate cluster with no clear relationship to '1 player'. Which save is loaded is easy to miss.
findings.fix: Move the two demo buttons into a quieter row. Make them 16px --tx-2 text buttons, or move them under settings. Keep 1 player and 2 player co-op as the two main rows. Put the active save row above the buttons as a 56px-tall card (name 20px, stats 16px tx-2), then add a 32px gap before the mode buttons.

findings.where: saves row and the save controls row
findings.what: The selected save is drawn as a thin lime-outlined row with lime text, and the lime outline is nearly the same weight as the idle buttons' border. The name field, 'change name' and 'create a new save' are three equal-weight buttons, which is clutter at the end of the column. The input has no label, and the 'pillager' text reads as a button.
findings.fix: Draw the selected save with a --ui-raised fill and a 3px lime left bar, with the text in tx-1 rather than lime. Collapse the name field, 'change name' and 'create a new save' into one 'manage saves' text link, or make 'create a new save' a quiet text button and show the name field only when it is in use. Give the input a 16px label.

findings.what: Button text is about 18px bold condensed at 1080, and the saves label, subtitle and key hints are about 15-16px with dim --tx-2. The footer legend and 'saves' label look under 16px and low contrast, which is hard to read from a couch. The tagline 'ascend. pillage. extract.' is small and grey beside the large title.
findings.fix: Set the button text to 20px f-cond 600. Set the saves label and the key hints to 16px with tx-2 at #aaa498 or brighter. Set the tagline to 20px tx-2 with +.04em tracking.

findings.what: These are two same-size outlined buttons that look as important as the mode buttons. They are far from the column, with no clear focus order and no visible pad focus state. The two use different widths.
findings.fix: Make 'go fullscreen' a 16px text-only toggle. Keep 'settings' as the only boxed button, at a fixed 120×48. Align the group to the 5% margin (96px) and align its baseline with the version stamp's margin. Add a lime focus bar.

findings.what: The footer legend lists wasd, mouse, lmb, e and f1 as keycap pills. It is a list of explaining text on a main menu, which counts as clutter. It also sits off the column's centre and has no relationship to the grid.
findings.fix: Remove it from the title menu, since F1 already opens controls in a raid. Or reduce it to one 'f1 controls' hint at 14px in the bottom-right corner, matching the version stamp's baseline.

findings.what: The background is a near-black vignette with no texture, so the screen reads as a generic template. The column is placed slightly below centre, with the large empty top band around 280px, and the version stamp is dim and tiny at the left margin. Nothing ties the screen to the game.
findings.fix: Add a low-opacity raid-map or silhouette art layer behind the column at about 15% opacity. Centre the title-and-column group vertically on the 540px line. Raise the version stamp to --tx-2 at 14px.

findings.where: mixed content in button labels and save stats
findings.what: '2 player co-op (same machine)' is a parenthetical explaining sentence on a button, and 'arcade demo' repeats on two rows. The save row mixes '$900' (money, correct) with '0 xp' and '0 raids' at the same weight, so the key figure doesn't stand out.
findings.fix: Rename it '2 player co-op'. Show the 'same machine' detail only in the 16px tx-2 sub-line, or drop it. In the save row, render '$900' in tx-1 at 20px and '0 raids · 0 xp' in 16px tx-2.

v.verdict: A clean, calm title screen with a clear lime primary action and no capitals, but the big orange gradient wordmark ignores the lime accent, the content is a small cluster in a huge empty field, and many small texts sit under the 16px floor.

findings.what: The hero is an orange-to-amber gradient with a drop shadow. It breaks the guide's ban on gradient washes, it sits close to the 'warn' amber, and it fights the lime button as a second hot colour. It looks like a generic template logo, with no mark or art that says this game.
findings.fix: Fill the wordmark flat --tx-1 (#efe9dc) or use real logo art. Remove the gradient and shadow. Keep lime only for the enter button. Wordmark cap height about 56px (--fs-hero), weight 800.

findings.what: The menu is a 560px column of small items in the middle of 1920x1080, with a large dead void above it (about 330px) and below it (about 340px). The background is a flat vignette with no scene, no key art and no atmosphere. It has none of the ARC Raiders or Halo Reach identity.
findings.fix: Put key art, a raid scene or a slow parallax layer behind the column. Shift the column to the left third, or enlarge the title block to about 25% of screen height. Cut the dead space so the group is centred at y of about 45%.

findings.where: Secondary text: 'player 2 window', 'saves', save row stats, bottom key legend, version stamp
findings.what: These render at about 13-15px in mid-grey. 'player 2 window' is the tiniest and dimmest, and it reads as a stray caption rather than an action. 'saves' and the stats are weak from a couch. The version stamp is lonely at bottom-left and not aligned to the 5% margin.
findings.fix: Set labels and stats to 16px with +.04em tracking, in --tx-2 #aaa498 (4.5:1 minimum). Make 'player 2 window' a real ghost button, 40px high, border --ui-line-hi, or move it to the top-right group. Align the version stamp to x=96 and keep it at 14px.

findings.where: Top-right 'go fullscreen' and 'settings' buttons vs the 'keyboard' pill at top-centre
findings.what: Two different button styles sit in the top area. The 'keyboard' device pill is green-bordered and tiny, wedged against the top edge at about y=19. The two utility buttons have white borders, which differ from the save-row buttons' grey --ui-line-hi. The right margin is 97px and the top is 33px, which is inconsistent.
findings.fix: Use one idle border (--ui-line-hi #4a5257, 4px radius, 40px high) for every secondary button. Move the 'keyboard' pill into the same top row with a 32px top margin, or into the footer next to the legend. Match the top and right margins to 48px.

findings.where: Save row 'pillager new' and the name input row
findings.what: The selected save has a thin lime outline and lime text. It is the only focus cue, and its fill is the same as the background, so the focus state looks weak next to the filled lime button. The name field, 'change name' and 'create a new save' sit on a row with three unequal widths and tight 8px gaps, so the row feels like form clutter on a menu.
findings.fix: Give the focused save row a --ui-raised #1e2225 fill, a 3px lime left bar and a 56px row height. Set the input and buttons to the same 48px height. Move the name controls into a quieter 'new save' sub-row, or show them only on focus.

findings.what: This is correctly the dominant element, but the text is only about 20px and bold on a 56px bar. The width of 558px is wider than the title above it, so the button outweighs the logo. It also has no focus ring, hover glyph or bounce cue.
findings.fix: Make the label 24px weight 800 with +.04em tracking. Set the button 64px high and 480px wide, centred under the wordmark. Add a 4px outer ring --acc-hover for pad focus.

findings.what: It is 18px grey with the same visual weight as the labels below. It floats between the wordmark and the button with uneven spacing (about 36px above and 24px below).
findings.fix: Use 20px --tx-2 with 16px between the wordmark and the tagline, and 32px to the button. Align all three on the 8px grid.

findings.where: Bottom key legend (wasd move, mouse aim, lmb fire, e search, f1 controls)
findings.what: The key caps are bordered white boxes at about 13px with 14px labels. They compete with the save row and the legend is a long row of small items, which is clutter on a title screen. The row also has uneven gaps between pairs.
findings.fix: Trim to the keys needed on this screen, or fold them into the F1 controls list. Set the caps to 16px with a --ui-line-hi border. Use 32px between pairs and 8px inside a pair.

v.verdict: The raid HUD has a readable hero ammo number and a clear hotbar, but two overlapping tooltips, a clipped prompt, stray capitals and uneven type sizes in the corner widgets make it look unfinished.

findings.what: The 'in pillager's party' tooltip is drawn on top of the bandage card and cuts off the lime key chip, which now reads 'lmb'. The chip is unreadable and the same line is drawn twice, which the one-place-per-line rule forbids.
findings.fix: Move the party tag out of the card, for example into the left feed, or put it inside the card at x≥200px from the card's left edge. Stop drawing a second tooltip over the first. Keep the key chip fully visible at 16px, with 8px padding on each side.

findings.what: Money is the loudest thing on the panel. $3,950 and $1,418 are as large as the names, and the 'you' row ($162) has no emphasis. The panel is a text block that duplicates the top-right 'run info' collapse and fights the HUD for attention. The title, count and caret are unaligned.
findings.fix: Make the title 16px tx-2, names 16px tx-1, values 16px tabular tx-2, and give the 'you' row a 3px lime bar and tx-1. Use one --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Align the caret to the right padding of 16px.

findings.where: top-right 'run info' and 'the long dock cache' tags, bottom-left 'f1 controls'
findings.what: Capital letters appear on screen ('run Info' shows a capital I, 'f1 controls' sits in a differently styled chip). Three different chip styles, sizes and fills sit within a few hundred pixels of each other. The 'c 146m' marker is tiny, about 12px.
findings.fix: Render 'run info' fully lower case. Use one chip style: --ui-panel at 90%, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 16px f-cond 600, 8px/16px padding. Raise the 'c 146m' text to at least 16px.

findings.what: The 'hp 100' label is about 32px bold, white on a flat saturated green fill with no panel or border. It is the loudest element in the corner, yet it is not the hero. It sits against the screen edge with a ragged 24px inset and clashes with the dark panel language of the rest of the HUD.
findings.fix: Put the bar in a --ui-panel plate with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius and a 32px inset from the edges (matching the other corners). Make the label 20px f-cond 700, with the green as the fill only. Save the 56px hero size for ammo.

findings.what: '1 / 0' is a good hero number, but the 0 reserve in red-orange and the lime 1 compete. The 'b / i backpack' hint is small and low contrast, about 14px grey on black. The card is not aligned with the hotbar baseline, and its left edge is not on the 8px grid with the slots.
findings.fix: Colour the reserve tx-2 and keep 'danger' for empty. Raise the hint to 16px tx-2 (4.5:1 or better). Line the card's bottom edge up with the hotbar slots' bottom edge at 32px from the screen edge.

findings.what: The empty slots 2 to 8 show floating numerals with no slot outline, so the hotbar reads as scattered digits. The focused slot (9) has an amber frame, not lime. Under the rules lime means selected, and amber is P1's colour. The ammo bars under slots 1 and 0 are tiny.
findings.fix: Draw all ten slots as 56px squares with a 1px --ui-line border, 4px radius and a --ui-panel fill. The selected slot gets a 2px --acc border. Keep the numerals at 16px inside each slot's top-left corner at 8px.

findings.what: A second cyan-on-dark nameplate sits in the left margin, separate from the player list, with a bar that is almost the same colour as the hp bar. Its text size and fill differ from every other chip. It duplicates the in-world 'pillager' tag at (380,471).
findings.fix: Keep one nameplate: the in-world tag above the character. Remove the left-margin plate or merge it into the party list. Keep the in-world tag at 16px with the P2 cyan fill.
