findings.what: The 15:00 timer is about 28px, which is not on the type scale, and the sun icon next to it is 24px and crowds the digits. The teal 'extract 146m' chip sits 4px under the timer with no grid gap and repeats the 'c 146m' marker on the right, so the distance is shown twice.
findings.fix: Set the timer at 32px (title) with an 8px gap to the icon and 16px to the chip. Drop the duplicate 'c 146m' edge marker, or drop the distance from the chip and keep one.

v.verdict: This is the in-world hub, not the title menu I reviewed before. The lime 'enter raid!' sign is a strong hero, but the amber 'pillager' tag, the asterisk warning, the toast and the tiny top-right readouts all compete with it and collide with other labels.

findings.where: 'pillager' name tag over the fashion station (bottom left)
findings.what: It is roughly 34px bold amber, bigger than every station label and about as loud as the hero sign. It sits on top of the 'fashion' chip and the player's head, so the label is clipped and unreadable. It also breaks the rule that boldness goes in one place per screen.
findings.fix: Set the tag to 16px f-cond 600 tx-1 on a 4px-radius --ui-panel chip. Float it 8px above the head and shift it away from station labels. Amber is for the P1 ring only.

findings.what: Two uneven clusters of about 14-16px text sit on near-black, with mixed weights and no panel. The 'xp' unit is a faint 12px. The corner is cramped against the edge, only about 20px in, not the 5% margin. The cluster is unreadable at couch distance and does not match the left 'the undercroft' card.
findings.fix: Build one 1 by 1 list on a --ui-panel card at 96px from the right edge. Use 20px tx-1 values with 16px tx-2 labels, all the same size. Show $900 as the single 20px value, keep stash and bag on a 16px tx-2 line, and use the 'xp' unit only if it is a real stat.

findings.where: '***experimental feature may glitch***' under 'the last pour'
findings.what: This is an amber warning string with asterisks and tiny text. It is a second explaining sentence jammed under the station label, and it overlaps the station circle. It reads as clutter and debug text, and the asterisks look amateur.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence and the asterisks. Put a 16px '--warn' 'beta' tag inside the 'the last pour' chip, or show the warning only when the player approaches.

findings.what: All 10 slots are always drawn, with ghosted dim weapon icons and 12px number labels. Only slots 4 and 0 are lit, and slot 1 has an amber border, so three different highlight styles compete. The bar crowds the fashion station and the player at the bottom.
findings.fix: Use one focus style: a --ui-raised fill with a 3px lime bottom bar for the selected slot only. Drop empty and unavailable slots to 40% opacity with no border. Make the number labels 16px tx-2. Move the bar to 24px from the bottom edge.

findings.what: The toast is a plain 16px black chip floating on the stash desk, with no relation to the other chips. The 'keyboard' chip at top centre is 14px green text with a green border in a different style, and it collides with the wall. Both are on-screen noise with no place in the layout.
findings.fix: Give every notice one chip style: --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 16px tx-1. Put the toast in the left feed. Show the 'keyboard' chip as a 16px tx-2 hint, not a green box, or remove it.

findings.what: Eight labels with the same chip style sit on dim translucent circles, and the circle tints vary (purple, teal, brown, grey). A stray grey circle overlaps the mainframe ring, and the 'the stash' chip overlaps the desk. The ring colours look random and sit close to the lime and amber meanings.
findings.fix: Use one neutral ring colour for stations at 24% opacity and raise it only for the nearest station. Remove the overlapping circle at the mainframe. Move the stash chip 16px above the desk. Keep P1 amber and P2 cyan for players only.

findings.what: The sign is the right hero, but the lime fill on 56-64px type with an exclamation mark reads like a template shout. It sits in a black box with a thick border, unlike the thin chips elsewhere. The undercroft card has a different border and tight padding, and its '2 items in stash · 0 runs' is cramped at 16px.
findings.fix: Keep the sign as the only lime item, at 56px f-cond 800. Drop the exclamation mark and use the same 4px --ui-panel chip. Give the undercroft card 16px padding and set its title at 32px, its stats at 16px tx-2.

findings.where: screen frame, left and right edges
findings.what: The black bars and the grey wall frame the map unevenly, with a wide dark strip on the right that holds the HUD and a narrower one on the left. The playfield looks off-centre, and the HUD text floats in dead space.
findings.fix: Centre the map at 1920 width, or fill both bars with --ui-void. Anchor the HUD to the 96px safe margin inside the playfield rather than the screen edge.

v.verdict: This is a different screen from the earlier title column (it's the in-world hub with a hotbar). It reads as a crowded prototype: the lime 'enter raid!' sign shouts over everything, there are three unrelated label styles, a debug-looking warning, and the rim/HUD margins are unaligned.

findings.where: '***experimental feature may glitch***' under 'the last pour'
findings.what: This is a debug-style disclaimer with asterisks, drawn in amber at about 13px on top of a station tag. It is an explaining sentence, and it reads like a dev note.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence. If a flag is needed, show a 16px '--warn' #f5b73b word 'beta' with no asterisks, set inside the tag as a small chip. The tag keeps the same 4px radius and fill as its neighbours.

findings.what: It is a 56px+ heavy lime italic with a hard shadow and an exclamation mark, set on a dark box that overlaps the pillar. It is the only place lime is used as a fill, which is correct, but it overpowers the title card and everything else. It is also not built like a button or a panel. The text is cramped inside the box (about 8px padding), and the box is clipped by the scene geometry.
findings.fix: Use a 'enter raid' label (no '!') in f-cond 800 at 40px, --acc-ink on a flat --acc fill, 56px high, 4px radius, 24px side padding. Keep the lime fill and drop the glow and shadow. Show the pad/key prompt next to it at 16px. Move it clear of the pillar, centred on the portal.

findings.where: All station tags: 'wirt the gambler', 'the mainframe', 'shop, craft, and hire', 'settings', 'the stash', 'fashion', 'the last pour', 'in pillager's party'
findings.what: Tags use about three different paddings and fills. 'in pillager's party' is a different black box with a smaller font, and 'fashion' is offset from its station. Text is about 18px with no consistent border. The big translucent circles in blue, purple, teal and brown look like muddy blobs that overlap one another (see the mainframe overlap).
findings.fix: One tag spec: --ui-panel #16191b fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 20px f-cond 600 in --tx-1, 8px/16px padding. Centre each tag 24px above its pad. Drop the circle fills to 8% opacity, or use only the 2px ring. Fix the double circle on the mainframe.

findings.what: The three items use different sizes and weights. '$900' is bold at about 22px, '0' is the same size but 'xp' is 12px, and the stash text is about 14px and is pushed against the right screen edge (about 20px) with no panel. The black bar at the right edge does not match the other screens. It also breaks the order for a vertical 1×1 list.
findings.fix: Put these in one 1×1 list as the cw-trcol job does: every row 20px f-cond 600, labels at 16px in --tx-2, values in --tx-1, 48px from the right and top. Use '$' for money only. Remove the 'xp' size change.

findings.what: Slot 1 has a gold border, slot 4 a blue fill, and slot 0 a gold fill. Three selection styles collide, and none uses lime, which should mean selected. The weapon icons on empty slots are barely visible (about 2:1), the number labels are about 12px and the stack count '1' is cramped.
findings.fix: One state only: selected gets a 2px --acc border and a --ui-raised fill. All the rest get a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Draw the numerals at 16px in --tx-2 and the empty icons at 40% opacity or more. Keep a 8px gap and the same slot size of 90px.

findings.what: The card is a good panel, but its title is 28px and the sub-line is about 14px with a middle dot, which is under the 16px floor. It sits 80px from the edge while the HUD sits 20px, so margins disagree.
findings.fix: Title 32px f-cond 700, sub-line 16px in --tx-2, both at a 48px margin to the screen edge. Drop the 'runs' count, or show it as a label/number pair.

findings.where: 'keyboard' chip, top-centre, and the 'pillager' player name
findings.what: 'keyboard' is a green-teal pill with mono text that is the only teal element and is not a defined state. The 'pillager' name label is 28px bold amber with no plate and it fights with the sprite. Amber for P1 is fine, but this is too large.
findings.fix: Show 'keyboard' as a 16px --tx-2 label in the footer legend with no pill. Set the player name at 16px f-cond 600 in P1 amber with a 1px dark outline, 8px above the head.

findings.where: Scene frame, left and right edges
findings.what: The room is not centred. The black bar on the right is wider (about 160px) than on the left (about 155px), with a lighter grey wall rim and a dark void that look unfinished. It crowds the right-hand HUD text.
findings.fix: Centre the arena and fill the side bars with --ui-void #0b0c0d, then put the HUD list inside the playfield at a 48px margin.

v.verdict: The raid HUD is clean and readable, with a good hero ammo number. But it repeats the extract distance, stacks small chips unevenly along the bottom, and doesn't follow the one-place-per-line rule or the single-accent rule.

findings.what: The extract distance is drawn twice. The right-edge marker is an unexplained 'c 152m' with a teal arrow, which breaks the rule that a line is drawn in only one place.
findings.fix: Keep the top-centre banner and drop the edge text, or keep only the arrow with no text. If an edge marker stays, spell it 'extract' and set it at 16px with the teal --extract colour.

findings.where: Bottom-left status row (concealed, in cover, f1 controls) and the hp bar
findings.what: Four unrelated elements sit in a ragged cluster. The amber 'concealed' chip, the teal 'in cover' chip and the grey 'f1 controls' chip each have a different border, fill and height. The 'f1 controls' chip floats at x≈440 above the hotbar, half-hidden against the map. The 'hp 100' text is oversized and overlaps the green bar, so it looks cramped.
findings.fix: Put both status chips on one 40px-high row aligned to the 96px margin, with the same --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Make 'concealed' warn amber and 'in cover' extract teal, both as small glyph-plus-word at 16px. Place 'f1 controls' on the same baseline as a 16px --tx-2 key hint. Set the hp number at 20px f-cond 700 inside a 32px bar with 8px padding.

findings.what: The selected slot is outlined in amber while lime is supposed to mean 'selected'. Slots 2-8 are ghosted icons with faint numerals (about 12px at low contrast), and there is a large unexplained gap between slot 8 and slots 9/0. The slots have no panel or border, so they float on the map and the numerals are hard to read.
findings.fix: Draw every slot as a 64×64 --ui-panel tile with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Mark the selected slot with a 3px --acc bar and a --ui-raised fill. Put the slot numbers at 16px in --tx-2 (#aaa498). Close the gap by grouping 1-8 and 9-0 with an even 8px spacing and a single 24px divider.

findings.what: The label shows a capital 'I' ('run Info'), which breaks the all-lower-case rule. The 300px black bar with a chevron is also heavier than anything near it and has a different border from the top-left panel.
findings.fix: Render it as 'run info' in lower case. Use a 40px-high --ui-panel bar with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 16px label, and keep it collapsed to roughly 160px wide.

findings.where: Top-left 'current pillagers 3' panel and the 'pillager' bar below it
findings.what: The panel packs 16px bold white text on a near-black fill, with the 'value at risk' header muted and the rows undivided. It is dense next to a thin, unlabelled 'pillager' bar a few pixels below, and the lime-green hp bar there matches nothing else.
findings.fix: Add 8px of row padding and 1px --ui-line dividers. Make the header 16px --tx-2 and the rows 16px --tx-1, with the values right-aligned in tabular numerals. Leave a 24px gap before the 'pillager' bar, and use the same bar style and green as the bottom hp bar.

findings.what: The green mono-looking badge is flush against the screen corner. It uses a different font and colour treatment from every other chip, and it sits outside the 5% margin.
findings.fix: Restyle it as a --ui-panel chip with a 16px f-cond --tx-2 label, and inset it 48px from the edge, or move it into the top-left panel.

findings.what: A solid black box with 20px body text sits over the map in the middle of the screen. The rule is that alert lines go to the top-centre banner and all other lines go to the left feed, so a toast here splits the lines across places.
findings.fix: Move the line into the left feed stack, or into the top-centre banner if it counts as an alert. Use a 16px --ui-panel row with a 3px left accent bar.

findings.what: The block is good: the hero '12 / 24' is the right size and in the right place. The 'b / i backpack' hint is 14px and dim, and the panel's edge and fill differ slightly from the top-left panel.
findings.fix: Raise the hint to 16px --tx-2. Match the panel to the shared token (--ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius). Show the weapon name at 20px and keep '12' at 56px f-cond 800.

v.verdict: The overlapping bandage card is gone, but the HUD is still a pile of mismatched chips and panels, with a capital I in 'run info', a full-bleed hp bar, and tiny text.

findings.what: It shows a capital 'I' ('run Info'). It is also a 300px-wide bar with a heavy chevron, and it is much wider than the tags beneath it. Its rounded-bar style matches nothing else on screen. The earlier advice to render it fully lower case was not followed.
findings.fix: Render it as 'run info' with no capitals. Make it one chip: --ui-panel at 90%, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 16px f-cond 600, 8px/16px padding. Hug the text and push the chevron to the right padding. Sit it 32px from the top and right screen edges.

findings.what: It is a raw green bar 410px wide, flush against the bottom and left edges, and clipped by the screen. 'hp 100' is oversized at about 36px. The green fill dominates the whole corner and competes with ammo. It has no plate or border and does not match the other corners.
findings.fix: Put it in a --ui-panel plate with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius and a 32px inset from the bottom and left edges. Make the label 20px f-cond 700, and the fill 16px tall in --ok. Keep the 56px hero size for ammo.

findings.what: The 12-14px text is under the 16px minimum. The three rows have tight 18px spacing and no 'you' emphasis. The caret hugs the panel edge. The 'pillager' health plate floats below it with a different fill and no relation to the panel. The 'value at risk' header is dim.
findings.fix: Set all text to 16px, with 32px rows. Give the 'you' row a 3px --acc bar and tx-1. Set values in tabular f-cond tx-2 and the header in tx-2 at 16px. Use one --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius and 16px padding. Move the caret to 16px from the right. Dock the 'pillager' hp plate to the panel, or move it to the hp corner.

findings.where: bottom centre 'in pillager's party' tag and 'f1 controls' chip
findings.what: Two tags sit in different spots with different styles. The party tag is a floating black box in the middle of the arena and reads as a stray tooltip. 'f1 controls' is small, about 14px, and sits against the hotbar. It has an unlike key chip.
findings.fix: Use one chip style for every tag. Put the party tag in the left feed, or at top-centre under the extract chip. Set 'f1 controls' at 16px with a 1px --ui-line-hi key chip, mid-bottom-left at 32px from the edge, 24px clear of slot 1.

findings.what: Slots 2-8 are bare numerals with no frame, in dim 14px grey. Slots 9 and 0 are boxed and jump 120px to the right. The row reads as broken, with an unexplained gap and a lost weapon silhouette. Slot 1's amber ring is the one strong element, but it is the same hue family as the warn colour.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots at 72px square with 8px gaps, each in --ui-panel with a 1px --ui-line. Numerals 16px tx-2. Keep slot 1 selected with a 3px --acc border. Centre the whole row on the screen and align its bottom with the ammo card at 32px from the edge.

findings.what: This is the right hero use of 56px, but the card is a hard black box 240px wide with a 14px 'b / i backpack' hint in dim grey. Its bottom edge sits about 28px from the screen edge while the hotbar sits lower. The card's corner radius and border differ from the others.
findings.fix: Use the --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi, 4px radius. Set the weapon name at 20px f-cond 600 tx-1. Put the reserve in 24px tx-2. Make the hint 16px tx-2. Align the card bottom with the hotbar bottom at 32px from the screen edge.

findings.where: top-right tags 'the long dock cache' and 'c 146m'
findings.what: Both are tiny, about 14px, with a hard white border and square corners. They float with no alignment to each other. The 'c 146m' tag is cryptic and the teal arrow beside it floats.
findings.fix: Use the same chip style as 'run info', with 16px type. Right-align both chips at 32px from the right edge. Change 'c 146m' to 'extract 146m' to match the top banner, or drop it, since the top banner already shows the distance. That also avoids drawing the line twice.

findings.what: The clock is 28px. The extract chip is a green-bordered pill at 16px. The sunset icon beside the clock is a different style, and the arrow under the chip is an orphan. The clock is the right hero and is well placed, but the extract chip uses --extract teal text inside a green border, so it is neither teal nor ok.
findings.fix: Set the clock to f-cond 800 at 32px. Use a chip with a 1px --extract border and text in --extract. Drop the stray arrow or anchor it 8px under the chip. Keep both centred on the same axis.

v.verdict: This is a competent dark stash window with a clear lime 'take' action, but it is crowded: the tab row carries too many controls, the keys pane is a dense grid of small tiles, and about two thirds of the stash pane is empty. The previous review was of a different screen (the title screen), so this is a fresh read.

findings.where: Left stash pane, below the 4 items
findings.what: The 4 item tiles fill the top-left corner and the rest of the pane (about 700px tall) is empty, so the window looks unfinished. Nothing shows the grid, capacity or slots.
findings.fix: Draw the full grid of empty slots (for example 6 columns by 5 rows of 152px tiles with a 1px --ui-line border at 40% opacity) so capacity reads like the Diablo IV inventory. Or add a 20px tx-2 'nothing else stashed' line, centred in the pane.

findings.where: Tab row (all, guns, consumables, parts, salvage, keycards, valuables, locked, search, sort, armory, trophies)
findings.what: There are 12 items of one weight on one line. Category filters, search, sort and two navigation links (armory, trophies) look the same, and the zero-count tabs are as bright as the live ones. The eye has no entry point.
findings.fix: Dim the zero-count tabs to tx-2 at 60% opacity, or hide them. Move 'armory 3/16' and 'trophies 0/8' to the header row, or draw them as outlined 40px-tall buttons. Shrink the search field to a 240px icon field, and keep 'sort' as a quiet 16px dropdown.

findings.where: Keys pane: gun keys and item wheel tiles
findings.what: The 22 tiles are about 120×70, with tiny 20px icons and 16px labels. The small lime key numbers (1 to 0) are cramped against the tile edge, and the dashed 'wheel' and 'empty' tiles look the same as filled ones. The bind grid needs a squint at couch distance.
findings.fix: Make the tiles 128×88 with 32px icons. Place the key number in a 20×20 chip at the top-left with 8px padding. Drop empty tiles to 40% opacity with a dashed border. Give the item wheel a 24px gap from the gun keys and make the wheel tile a circle or a centre marker.

findings.where: Header row, right side ($900, 0 xp, stash $365 bag $0)
findings.what: The $900 hero number sits beside 'xp' and the stash/bag figures, all at near-equal sizes. 'stash $365 bag $0' is a run-on of small text, and it duplicates '$365 going up' in the keys pane.
findings.fix: Keep $900 at 32px tx-1 as the only large number. Set '0 xp' and the stash/bag value at 16px tx-2, with 24px between them. Remove the duplicate '$365 going up' or the header copy. Align the group's baseline to the 'stash' title.

findings.where: Footer key legend (drag, right click, shift, ctrl, alt, 1-9,0)
findings.what: The legend is 14-16px grey with wide tracking, and it sits above a second bar. The two stacked bars (legend plus 'freebie kit / take') crowd the bottom of the card.
findings.fix: Set the legend text to 16px at #aaa498 or brighter with +.04em tracking, not +.15em. Add 16px of padding between the legend and the 'freebie kit' row. Put a 1px --ui-line divider between them.

findings.what: The row is the primary action and it works, but the 'take' button is small (about 120×48) and flush against the right edge. The lime left bar on the row, the lime button and the lime 'keyboard' pill all compete. The row has no detail about what the kit holds.
findings.fix: Make the 'take' button 160×56 with 24px right padding. Use the lime left bar only on the row, and keep 'keyboard' in tx-2 with a --ui-line border. Add a 16px tx-2 contents line under 'freebie kit', such as 'medkit, bandage'.

findings.where: Title 'stash / pillager' and the close X
findings.what: The title is 32px but the 'pillager' breadcrumb is small and low-contrast. The X is a thin outlined box with no hover or focus treatment visible. The top-centre 'keyboard' pill floats over the scrim and the card edge.
findings.fix: Set 'pillager' to 20px tx-2. Give the X a 48×48 target with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a lime focus outline. Move the 'keyboard' device pill into the footer legend row, or place it 16px clear of the card edge.

findings.what: The card has a faint warm vignette gradient in the header and a 1px border, while the HUD hotbar shows through below it. The gradient breaks the flat-panel rule and the see-through hotbar adds noise.
findings.fix: Fill the card with flat --ui-panel (#16191b). Raise the scrim to .80 so the hotbar and the scene behind it fall away.

v.verdict: This is a raid HUD, not the run-over card I reviewed before, so the earlier advice can't be checked here. It reads as a clear but heavy HUD: the controls panel and the squad list are too large and compete with the play field.

findings.what: It is a big opaque card of 28 entries in 16px text, and it sits permanently over the playfield at the lower left. It outweighs the hotbar and the ammo, which are the things that matter. The key chips, section labels and descriptions are all the same weight, so there is no hierarchy.
findings.fix: Fold it to one 16px line ('f1 controls') at x24 y~1040, the spec'd mid-bottom-left spot, as the settled raid-controls order requires. If it stays open, drop the fill to scrim .6, set the section labels (move, gear, fight, raid) in tx-2 and put the keys in tx-1 on --ui-raised chips.

findings.what: The panel is dense, with three bright rows of '$' values in a different style from every other panel. The header ('value at risk') is small and has a chevron, and the names are crammed with 2px row gaps. Its left edge (x8) does not match the controls card (x15) or the bar (x24).
findings.fix: Use 24px row pitch with a 16px tx-2 header. Show the money in tx-1 and keep 'you' as the only lime row. Set every left edge to x24 (the 5% margin) and use the same --ui-panel fill and 4px radius on all HUD cards.

findings.what: The saturated green block with a 32px 'hp 100' is the loudest element on screen. It competes with the 56px ammo hero. The text is also unevenly placed, with 'hp' small and the number large, and the number sits on the bar fill with weak contrast.
findings.fix: Make the bar 12px tall and 260px wide with a --ui-line track. Put 'hp' at 16px tx-2 and '100' at 24px f-cond 700 tx-1 above or beside the bar. Leave 56px as the only hero (ammo).

findings.what: There appears to be a capital I in 'run Info'. The all-lower-case rule is broken. The wide dropdown box also looks like a web form control, not a game HUD element.
findings.fix: Render it as 'run info' in lower case. Shrink the box to about 160px wide and align the chevron to a 16px grid.

findings.what: The slots are small (90px) and the selected one has an orange-amber outline. Amber means P1 and lime means 'selected'. The number labels along the rail (1, 4-0) float at 14px in low contrast, and there is no visible ammo-type distinction.
findings.fix: Make the selected-slot outline 2px --acc. Set the idle slot border to --ui-line-hi. Set the slot numbers to 16px tx-2 and put them inside the slot's top-left corner.

findings.what: The 'contract item nearby · gold glow marks the box' toast is an explaining sentence with a long dot-separated string. It touches the controls card, with a 19px gap and a different left edge. Gold and amber are both used on it, which clutters it.
findings.fix: Shorten it to 'contract item nearby' and cut the explanation. Use a 3px --r-gold bar and tx-1 text, 16px, with an 8px radius-4 panel. Move it to the left feed column at x24.

findings.what: It is the correct hero (56px), but the card is flush to the screen edge at x1910 and y1052, without the 5% margin used by other panels. 'b / i backpack' at 14px is below the 16px floor.
findings.fix: Inset the card 24px from the right and bottom edges. Set the hint to 16px tx-2. Keep '25' in tx-1 and '/ 50' in tx-2.

findings.what: The black chip sits directly on the player sprite and the 'pillager' nameplate (overlap around y868-930). It hides the character. The p2 tag has a cyan outline whose contrast is weak in this lighting.
findings.fix: Move the toast to the left feed or the top-centre alert slot (x24, y~260). Give the nameplate a 1px --ui-void backing.

v.verdict: This is a clean, calm title screen with a clear lime primary action, but the amber gradient logo fights the lime accent, the page is mostly empty, and the secondary text and edge furniture are weak and misaligned.

findings.what: The orange gradient logo is the loudest thing on screen, and the lime button below it is a second hot colour. The style guide bans gradient washes. Amber is also the P1 player colour and warn colour, so it reads as 'player 1' on a menu. The logo and the button split the boldness the guide wants in one place.
findings.fix: Make the logo flat --tx-1 (#efe9dc), 56px hero at weight 800, or flat --acc. Remove the vertical gradient and drop shadow. Leave the lime button as the only saturated fill.

findings.what: It sits directly under the primary button as 14px grey bold text with no affordance. It is unclear whether it is a link, a label or a hint. It is hard to see, and a pad player cannot tell it is focusable.
findings.fix: Make it a real secondary button at the same 558px width as the save row and 48px high. Use a 1px --ui-line-hi border, --fs-body 20px text in --tx-1, and 16px spacing from the primary button. If it is only a hint, delete it.

findings.what: The 'saves' label is thin f-body grey of about 15px, below the 16px floor and lower contrast than the row text. The three controls in the bottom row (name field, 'change name', 'create a new save') all have the same weight and border. The name field looks like another button. The saves list has no clear title or hierarchy beyond one lime outline.
findings.fix: Set the 'saves' label in f-cond 600 at 16px with +.04em tracking, in --tx-2, with a 8px gap above the row. Give the name field a --ui-raised fill so it reads as an input. Make 'create a new save' the only bolder button there. Keep 24px between the list and the row of controls.

findings.where: top edge: 'keyboard' chip (about 960,19) and top-right 'go fullscreen' / 'settings' (1611-1823 x 33-81)
findings.what: The teal 'keyboard' chip is jammed against the top edge, about 8px down. It is the only teal element on the menu, and teal is reserved for extraction. The right-hand buttons sit 33px from the top and 97px from the right, and the chip and the buttons share no baseline or margin.
findings.fix: Move the device chip into the top-right group as a neutral --ui-line-hi chip in --tx-2. Place the group with a 48px margin from the top and right. Make all three the same 48px height. Never use teal here.

findings.where: bottom key legend (about 726-1195 x 1030-1056) and version stamp (97,1047)
findings.what: The legend has 14-16px grey labels with white key caps. The caps are the brightest thing at the bottom and they pull the eye away from the screen's main block. Five hints on a title screen is clutter. The version stamp starts at x=97 and aligns with nothing else on the screen, and it is smaller than 14px and blurry.
findings.fix: Cut the legend to 'f1 controls' only at 16px in --tx-2, and give the key caps no fill and a 1px --ui-line border. Align the version stamp to the 48px left margin, at 14px in --tx-2, on the same baseline as the legend.

findings.what: It is mid-grey, about 18px, with a thin letter-spaced look, and it ends with a stop that adds noise. It is also close to the logo's descender zone, so the logo block feels crowded above and loose below.
findings.fix: Set it to 20px f-cond 600 in --tx-2, with 16px between logo and tagline and 32px between tagline and the primary button. Remove the trailing full stop.

findings.what: The content column is 558px wide in a 1920px frame, vertically centred with a lot of dead dark space and only a faint vignette. There is no art, no world and nothing ARC Raiders-like behind the menu, so it reads as a generic template and the identity score suffers.
findings.fix: Put a darkened, slow-moving key-art or raid scene behind the menu at about 30% brightness under the --scrim (rgba(6,7,8,.80)). Or at least use a --ui-panel card with a 4px radius and a 1px --ui-line-hi border, with 48px of inner padding, to anchor the column.

findings.what: The lime fill is correct and has good contrast. The label is only 20px, so the button's size is carried by the fill and the text looks small inside it. The lime save-row outline and lime 'pillager new' text repeat the accent as 'selected', which is right, but it competes with the button for the first look.
findings.fix: Raise the label to 24px at weight 700 with +.04em tracking. Keep the button at 64px high. Make the save row's selected state a 3px lime left bar with --ui-raised fill instead of a full lime outline.

v.verdict: A clean, consistent dark stash card with readable rarity bars, a lime 'take' button, and an X in the corner. The left half is mostly empty, the eye has nowhere to land first, and the small text is dim and cramped.

findings.what: Nine items fill the top of a pane that is about 60% empty. The right pane has the same problem (backpack empty, nothing under the hotbar). There is no focus or selected item and no detail pane, so the eye has no anchor and the screen feels unfinished.
findings.fix: Put a 360px detail pane in the empty space, showing the focused item's name, rarity bar and stats, with the focused tile outlined in --acc 2px. Alternatively, enlarge the tiles to 176px so the grid fills the pane.

findings.what: Four money and xp figures sit side by side in mixed sizes: '$48,250' in bold, '0 xp' at about 16px, and 'stash $17,654 bag $0' at about 14px. They read as clutter and there is no single hero number. 'xp' is also a different weight from the '0'.
findings.fix: Keep one hero, '$48,250', at 32px f-cond 700. Put 'stash $17,654 · bag $0' as one --tx-2 16px line beneath it. Drop or move 'xp'. Align it all to the 24px right edge, left of the X.

findings.where: tab row, sort, armory and trophies (y 125-170)
findings.what: Eleven items share one row with the same weight and size: category tabs, a search box, sort, armory 7/10 and trophies 0/8. Filter and navigation are mixed together. The tabs are about 16px and --tx-2 grey, so they are weak at couch distance. The active underline on 'all 10' is thin and dim.
findings.fix: Move sort, armory and trophies into the footer or a separate right-aligned group, at least 24px from the search box. Make tabs 20px --fs-body. Make the active tab --tx-1 with a 3px --acc underline.

findings.what: The 'backpack' tab, the 'backpack' sub-header and '0 packed' say the same thing twice. 'keys' is a tab with no weight difference. '$0 going up', '0 on keys' and '10 held' are 14px bold counters that are hard to read.
findings.fix: Delete the second 'backpack' label and fold '0 packed' into the tab as 'backpack 0/12'. Set all counters to 16px --tx-2. Remove '$0 going up' when it is zero.

findings.what: The dashed outlines at about #2a2e31 on #16191b are nearly invisible, and the hotbar slots are only 62px with 16px numerals in dim grey. Slots 2 and 3 show icons so small they cannot be identified.
findings.fix: Use a solid 1px --ui-line border instead of dashed. Raise the slot numerals to --tx-2 and make the hotbar slots 72px. Draw the icons at 80% of the slot.

findings.what: The legend is six key-cap and action pairs in 14-15px letter-spaced grey. It is explaining text on screen, and it is too small for a couch at 1080. On a pad the keyboard prompts are wrong.
findings.fix: Show only the 2 or 3 actions that apply to the focused item, at 16px. Switch to pad glyphs when the pad is in use. Cut the rest.

findings.what: The row is a bare 16px-tall strip with a lime left edge. The lime 'take' button is the only primary action but it is flush to the right with no description, and the tooltip-like row has no icon or contents. The bold lime fill competes with the title as the single loud element, and its right inset is only 16px.
findings.fix: Add one --tx-2 16px line saying what the kit contains, for example '3 guns + ammo', and put the 'take' button on a 24px inset. Give the row a --ui-raised fill with a 1px --ui-line border so it reads as a distinct card.

findings.where: item tiles (rarity borders and stack badges)
findings.what: Full 1px rarity borders on every tile, plus a gold-rimmed star tile and lime number badges ('1', '2') on the same tiles, mean lime and rarity gold sit side by side. The guide says rarity is a 3px bar, never an outline. The lime badges look like 'selected' markers but mean something else.
findings.fix: Use a 3px bottom rarity bar only, with a neutral --ui-line-hi border. Make the number badges --ui-raised with --tx-1 text, and keep lime for the focus ring alone.

v.verdict: The HUD is functional, but it still reads as stock dropdown boxes plus a thin bar. The controls list is now folded, which is correct. Capitals remain in 'run Info', and the left cards and hp bar have not been reworked.

findings.what: This was flagged last time and is unchanged. It has a capital 'I', which breaks the all-lower-case rule. It is a 300px full-width black bar with a chevron. It is the largest chrome element on screen and it carries no information.
findings.fix: Render it as 'run info'. Shrink it to about 160px wide at x1736-1896. Use --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Use 16px f-cond 600 text and a 12px chevron.

findings.what: Unchanged. 'hp 100' is a big 30px+ condensed number jammed into the bar's left end. It is bolder than anything else except the ammo, so it competes with the one hero number. The bar is a flat green slab with no track, so the missing health cannot be read.
findings.fix: Make the bar 260x12px with a --ui-line track at x24 y1048. Put 'hp' at 16px tx-2 and '100' at 24px f-cond 700 tx-1 on a line above it. Keep 56px for the ammo only.

findings.where: 'current pillagers 3' x8-367 y143-242 and 'pillager' tag x15-170 y325-358
findings.what: The party card is a black dropdown bar. It starts at x8 instead of the x24 margin, and its text is 16px, cramped and tight to the left edge. The 'pillager' ally card at y325 has a different style: a tint fill with a green bar and a different left edge. Two HUD card styles sit in one column.
findings.fix: Put both on the same --ui-panel fill with a 4px radius at x24. Use a 16px tx-2 header on the party card and a 24px row pitch. Make the ally name 16px tx-1 with a 6px hp bar on --ui-line.

findings.what: The slots are small (about 90px), and the slot numbers 4 to 0 are faint 16px glyphs on the wall strip at y979. They are low in contrast and they align with nothing. The selected slot has an amber/orange border, which collides with the P1 amber and weakens the rule that lime means selected.
findings.fix: Draw the selected outline at 2px --acc. Make idle borders --ui-line-hi. Put the slot numbers inside each slot's top-left at 16px tx-2. Draw empty slots 4-0 as 90px --ui-panel squares at 60% opacity.

findings.what: It is folded correctly, but it sits at x440 on the wall strip with a translucent grey fill. It is not on the left margin and it is nearly lost against the strip. It also floats right above the hotbar numbers.
findings.fix: Move it to x24 y1000, above the hp bar. Use --ui-panel fill, 16px tx-2 text and an 'f1' key chip in tx-1 on --ui-raised.

findings.where: toast 'contract item nearby · gold glow marks the box' x15-410 y776-802
findings.what: It is an explaining sentence, which the brief lists as a defect. It also uses amber for the whole line, and the 4px bar at x15 sits flush to the edge of the screen.
findings.fix: Shorten it to 'contract item nearby'. Show it in tx-1 with a 16px --warn icon, and start it at x24. Drop the 'gold glow marks the box' clause.

findings.what: It is a black box that overlaps the player sprite and the 'pillager' name tag at y868. It has no border or accent, so it reads as a debug label.
findings.fix: Move it to the left feed at x24, with no overlap on the sprites. Use --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius, with 16px tx-1 text.

findings.what: The card is good, and 25/50 is a clear hero number. The right margin is only 10px, not the 5% margin. 'b / i backpack' at 14px is under the 16px minimum for anything read.
findings.fix: Set the right edge to x1896 (24px margin). Set the 'b / i backpack' hint to 16px tx-2. Put 'auto rifle' at 16px tx-2 in place of its current larger size.

v.verdict: The shot is now a raid HUD instead of the title, and it is a set of mismatched widgets: two native-looking dropdowns, a green chip, a green hp slab and a black tooltip, with a capital letter on screen.

findings.what: It reads 'run Info' with a capital I, which breaks the all-lower-case order. It is also a native-style select with a chevron at the screen edge, and it sits at a different height and width from the left dropdown.
findings.fix: Change the label to 'run info'. Replace both selects with one 48px-high pill style: --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 16px --f-cond 600 text. Put both on a 48px margin and the same top baseline.

findings.what: It floats mid-left, flush against the screen edge with a 0 margin, at a different y from the right dropdown. It is a wide, empty bar that covers the map and has no clear role.
findings.fix: Dock it to the top-left at x=48, y=48, about 240px wide. Align it with the right dropdown, or collapse it to a '3' chip.

findings.what: The 'hp 100' text is oversized, about 36px, and sits in a saturated green slab with no panel or border. It is the loudest element on screen and competes with the ammo hero number. It is flush with the left and bottom edges, and the green is a different green from --ok.
findings.fix: Set it in a --ui-panel container 320x32 at x=48, y=1080-48-32, with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a --ok fill. Put 'hp' at 16px --tx-2 and '100' at 20px --tx-1, with no 36px text.

findings.where: 'keyboard' chip (5-105 x 6-32) and the 'pillager' bar (16-170 x 325-358)
findings.what: The device chip is a green-outlined chip jammed into the corner with 5px margins and a mono-looking label, in a style that matches nothing else here. The 'pillager' name bar is a second plate that repeats the nameplate over the character.
findings.fix: Make the chip a neutral --ui-line-hi chip in --tx-2 at 16px, with a 48px margin. Drop the 'pillager' bar or fold it into the hp block. Show the name once.

findings.what: The selected slot has an amber/orange ring, but lime (--acc) is the 'selected' colour. The slot has no panel fill, the dim digit rail 1-0 runs through the stone wall behind it, and the wall texture makes the numbers hard to read.
findings.fix: Use a 2px --acc border on the selected slot. Give every slot a --ui-panel fill at 85% opacity and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Draw the digit labels at 16px --tx-2 inside the slot corners, not on the wall.

findings.what: It is a pure black box with thin 14px white text, on a different fill and radius from the other panels. It also explains something the nameplate already says.
findings.fix: Delete it. If it stays, use a --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border, a 4px radius and 16px --tx-1 text.

findings.what: It is a small chip with a grey fill sitting on the pale wall tile. Contrast is low, and it floats with no relation to the hotbar or hp bar.
findings.fix: Give it a --ui-panel fill, 16px --tx-2 text and a 1px --ui-line border. Align its bottom edge with the hotbar slots at y=1032.

findings.what: The ammo panel is the best-built element, but 'b / i backpack' is a 14px grey line that is hard to read, and the panel has a 10px right margin instead of 48px. The 14:58 timer is about 30px, below the 56px hero size, and the extract chip stacked under it is teal on teal.
findings.fix: Move the ammo panel in to a 48px right and bottom margin. Raise the backpack hint to 16px --tx-2. Make the timer 32px --tx-1 and keep the extract chip as a flat --extract outline.

v.verdict: The gamble window is tidy and uses the style tokens correctly, but the lower third of the card is empty, the gamble panel has a hole in it, and the small type is under the guide's 16px floor.

findings.what: The two panels stop at about 65% of the card height. A dead band of about 320px sits below them, so the card looks unfinished and the content floats at the top.
findings.fix: Stretch both panels to the card's bottom padding (bottom edge near y 1000). Or shrink the card to fit its content. Or center the panels vertically in the body. Give the body 24px padding on every side.

findings.what: About 150px of empty space sits between the odds rows and the gamble button. The mystery box is small (190px) and the odds table is cramped beside it, so the left panel feels hollow next to the filled offer panel.
findings.fix: Enlarge the question-mark tile to about 280px, centered like the offer art, with the odds list below it at 20px row height. This mirrors the right panel's layout. Alternatively, pin the button to the bottom and spread the content evenly.

findings.where: odds labels and percentages, header stats
findings.what: The labels (common to gold), the percentages and the stash/bag/xp stats are about 12-14px, below the 16px minimum. They will be hard to read from a couch. The rarity bars are thin (4px) and their labels are tiny.
findings.fix: Raise the labels, percentages and stats to 16px with +.04em tracking, in tx-1 or tx-2. Make the bars 8px tall. Use a row pitch of 36px.

findings.what: $48,250, 0 xp and stash $6,415 bag $0 are three different sizes and weights, spaced unevenly. The close X (48px box) is crowded right next to them. The hero money number is competing with the title.
findings.fix: Use one style for all three stats: 20px label, with only the money value in tx-1 600. Space them 32px apart. Leave a 24px gap before the X. Do not use a bold white number for xp.

findings.what: The offer's name is 32px bold. The 'worth' and 'new offer arrives in 3 minutes' lines are muted grey and read as explaining sentences. The art tile floats without a framing border.
findings.fix: Cut the 'new limited time offer arrives...' line to a short timer such as '3:00' (label size, beside the panel title). Keep one line, 'worth $14,904', in tx-2 at 16px. Give the art tile a 1px line-hi border.

findings.what: Only the lime gamble button is filled. The buy button is an outline with no focus indicator, and no pad focus is visible on either. The two buttons are the same width as their panels, so they read as bars rather than actions.
findings.fix: Show a visible focus state on the selected button (2px lime outline, +2px offset) and keep the other idle at line-hi. Set the button height to 56px with 20px text.

findings.what: 'the welcome pack is in your stash.' is a sentence in a small box. It sits tight against the top edge and overlaps the card's top-border zone, and it is a different style from the panels.
findings.fix: Put the toast 24px below the top edge, use the panel fill with a 1px line-hi border and a 4px radius. Make it a short phrase such as 'welcome pack in stash'.

findings.what: The card border is a hairline at 97px inset against the near-black scrim, and the title 'wirt the gambler' is 32px but its header band is thin. The card does not stand out from the background, and the screen has little identity beyond the generic dark panel.
findings.fix: Set the card fill to --ui-bg with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Use a 56px header row with a bottom divider. Add a 3px lime or gold bar to the left of the title. Add a subtle gambler motif in the question-mark tile, such as a card back or dice art.

v.verdict: The window is clean, dark and consistent. The earlier P1 problems are still there: the stash grid leaves a large dead area, the header money is split into three small pieces, and the controls row is crowded.

findings.where: stash grid and lower left pane (x 110-1085, y 530-890)
findings.what: Eight 152px tiles fill about a third of the pane. The bottom 360px is empty, and the focused item has no detail pane. The hover tooltip covers four neighbouring tiles, so the grid can't be read while it is shown.
findings.fix: Dock a 320px detail pane in the empty area below the grid, with name, rarity bar and stats for the focused tile. Remove the floating tooltip for pad and keyboard focus. Keep the 2px --acc outline on the focused tile.

findings.where: right pane below the hotbar (x 1087-1810, y 590-890)
findings.what: The right pane is empty from y 590 to 890, and the 12 dashed backpack slots are empty and low-contrast. Nothing tells the player what the pane does.
findings.fix: Enlarge the backpack slots to fill the pane height, or add a loadout summary below the hotbar. Use solid 1px --ui-line borders in place of dashes.

findings.what: '$48,250' (24px), '0 xp' and 'stash $17,654 bag $0' sit side by side at three sizes with uneven gaps. There is no clear hero and the 14px text is hard to read from a couch.
findings.fix: Show '$48,250' alone at 32px f-cond 700 --tx-1. Put 'stash $17,654 · bag $0' on one 16px --tx-2 line beneath it, and move 'xp' into that line. Right-align it with a 24px gap left of the X.

findings.what: There are 8 tabs plus a search box plus 3 more items (sort, armory, trophies), all in one row at about 17px. The active-tab underline is thin and the row is crowded.
findings.fix: Set tabs to 20px --fs-body and add a 3px --acc underline on the active tab. Move sort, armory and trophies into a separate right-aligned group at least 24px from the search box, or into the footer. Shorten the search box to 280px.

findings.what: 'backpack' appears twice, once as a tab and once as a sub-label. 'stash' and 'backpack' have different type styles. Counters such as '10 held', '0 packed' and '$0 going up' are small and bold with no clear order.
findings.fix: Remove the second 'backpack' label and fold the count into the tab as 'backpack 0/12'. Use one style for all counters: 16px --tx-2. Hide '$0 going up' when it is zero.

findings.what: The hotbar slots are 62px with dashed borders, and the numerals and icons are tiny and low-contrast. Two items have small slot numbers in odd corners.
findings.fix: Make the slots 72px with solid 1px --ui-line borders. Set the numerals to --tx-2 16px. Draw the icons at 80% of the slot, and put every slot number in the same corner.

findings.where: footer key legend (y 898-922) and freebie kit bar (y 935-1005)
findings.what: The legend is 16px with wide tracking, and its 6 key caps are in white outline boxes, so it competes with the grid. The 'take' button is the loudest element on the screen and sits far from the content. The freebie kit bar has a lime left edge but no description.
findings.fix: Set the legend to 14px --tx-2 with ghost key caps. Keep 'take' as the one lime action, but give it a 160px width, 40px height and 4px radius. Add a one-word reward tag next to 'freebie kit'.

findings.where: focused tile and its star (x 120-278, y 214-372)
findings.what: The focused tile has a lime outline, a lime star and a 2 badge in the corner, so lime is used three times in one place. The first row of tiles, behind the tooltip, shows a lime border on one tile (y 376-528) in addition to the focus tile.
findings.fix: Use lime only for the focus outline. Show the star and the count badges in --tx-1 on --ui-raised, and use rarity colours for the bottom bars only. Make sure only one tile at a time has an --acc border.

v.verdict: The HUD is readable and mostly follows the lower-case, one-accent rules, but the missed-extraction alert is a small amber banner with no urgency. The top-centre status cluster has no clear order, and the leaderboard and run-info panels compete with it.

findings.what: This is the one event the player must notice. It is a ~280x48 banner at roughly 28px type with a thin amber left bar and no fill, icon colour or motion cue. It sits mid-upper screen over the map and is smaller than the 56px hero or 32px title tiers. It also reads as the same grade as the teal 'extraction a available' tag, and 'extraction missed' has no next step.
findings.fix: Make it a 56px f-cond 800 banner (hero tier) on --ui-panel with a 4px --danger left bar and a --danger icon. Use the bounce-in motion (--m-in 240ms) and hold it for 3s. Add a short second line in 20px tx-2, such as 'next extraction in 2:10', so the player has something to do.

findings.what: The timer, the teal pill and the alert are three stacked items with different treatments: the timer is a bare number over the map, the pill is teal-filled and the alert is amber-barred. Their left edges don't align, and the timer sits on a busy wall texture with weak contrast. The alert also sits about 100px below the cluster, so it looks like a separate element.
findings.fix: Put the timer and the pill in one --ui-panel plate, 8px padding, 4px radius, centred on x=960. Put the alert directly under it with a 16px gap, on the same centre axis. Give the timer a solid plate so it is no longer bare text over the walls.

findings.what: The 360x190 panel is dense and sits in the top-left over the map. It has ten rows at ~15px, which is under the 16px minimum, and 'value at risk' headers in tx-2 that look dim. The magenta 'fbi_surveillance_van' name introduces an off-palette colour with no key. Every row says '$x dead' in the same weight, so nothing stands out. The 'you' row ($1,920) is the only one the player cares about and it is barely distinguished.
findings.fix: Raise the rows to 16px and make the 'you' row 20px tx-1 with a 3px --acc left bar. Drop the dead rows to a single '7 dead' summary line, or fold them with a chevron. Remove the magenta unless it is the P2 cyan or an agreed player colour. Make the dead rows tx-2 and the dollar amounts tabular and right-aligned.

findings.where: 'extraction a available' and 'elite cache' world tags
findings.what: One tag is teal-filled and the other is a black pill with white text, so two unrelated tag styles share the same scene. The teal tag clashes with the teal ring and sits at 16px with tight padding over a busy olive background. 'extraction a available' also contradicts the 'extraction missed' alert above it, so the player gets mixed messages.
findings.fix: Use one tag style: --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 16px f-cond 600, 8px/4px padding. Keep teal only for the extraction tag's glyph or border. Hide 'extraction a available' while the missed alert is showing, or change it to 'extraction a: closed'.

findings.what: The minimap has no border or title, and it is dark enough to look like a hole in the screen. 'run info' is a full-width dropdown bar that reads like a form control. Its chevron is tiny, and the 16px label sits against a map that is close to it with only a ~12px gap. The key-hint and the career top-right list (cw-trcol) are still unbuilt.
findings.fix: Frame the minimap with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Set the 'run info' bar to the same 4px radius, an 8px gap and a 20px label. Align the right edge to the 5% margin (96px) used elsewhere, as the leaderboard does on the left.

findings.where: bottom-left 'f1 controls', '4 minutes left' and hp bar
findings.what: Three unrelated bottom-left elements use three different treatments: the 'f1 controls' keycap is a floating chip, '4 minutes left' is an amber-barred chip jammed against the screen edge (x=0, flush left), and hp is a flat green bar with a large number. The '4 minutes left' chip also repeats information from the 3:20 timer, so the same line is drawn twice. The hp bar has no frame or border and is about 400px wide, with the 100 sitting loose on its left.
findings.fix: Move '4 minutes left' inside the 5% safe margin (x=96px) and remove it, since the clock already shows the time. Pad the hp bar and frame it in --ui-panel with a 4px radius. Align 'f1 controls' on the same left axis, stacked 8px above the hp bar.

findings.what: The ammo block is a strong hero: '30 / 60' is ~56px with a good size contrast. 'b / i backpack' is a ~14px hint in a dim tone that is under the 16px minimum. The hotbar slot numbers 3, 5-0 float with no cell, so the empty slots are invisible. Slot 2 has an amber focus ring while the weapon card above it is white, so selected is not lime.
findings.fix: Raise the hint to 16px tx-2. Draw empty hotbar cells as 1px --ui-line outlined slots with 4px radius. Change the selected-slot ring from amber to --acc, since lime only means selected.

findings.what: The map's olive, teal and brown zones leave the white thin-stroked text with little protection, notably the timer and the tags. There is no scrim under the top-centre cluster, and only the leaderboard has a panel. Panel treatment is inconsistent: the leaderboard, run-info and weapon card are panels, while the timer and tags are bare.
findings.fix: Apply --ui-panel at about 85% opacity to every HUD element with text. Add a 2px text shadow at rgba(0,0,0,.6) only where no plate is possible.

v.verdict: The raid HUD has the right pieces, but the 'extraction missed' state is weak: the event is a small left-edge toast far from the action, while the large leaderboard and the stray 'extraction available' tag compete with it.

findings.what: The key event on this screen is a tiny 16-20px teal chip hard against the screen edge, below the leaderboard and away from the top-centre alert zone. The style guide says alerts belong in the top-centre banner only, and the player's eye never lands on it. It also sits only a few px from the left bezel, outside the 5% safe margin.
findings.fix: Put 'extraction missed' in the top-centre alert banner at --fs-title 32px with a --danger or --warn accent bar. Remove the left-edge copy. If a feed line remains, set the left inset to at least 48px.

findings.where: 'extraction a available' tag over the extraction ring (x≈570-725, y≈460-480)
findings.what: The string is misspelled ('a available'). It also contradicts the 'extraction missed' state, because it still says extraction is available. The tag is small, sits on foliage, and shows teal text on a teal chip with weak contrast.
findings.fix: Fix the text, for example 'extraction open'. Hide or switch the tag to a 'closed' state once the extraction is missed. Use 20px --f-cond on --ui-panel with --tx-1 text and a 3px --extract bar.

findings.what: This is the largest text block on screen: 9 rows at about 15px, with a dim 'value at risk' header and a collapse chevron. It outweighs the alert, and the dead/alive status is carried only by tiny grey 'dead' text. Rows have no divider and the money column is hard to track. Row text is under the 16px minimum, and muted grey on the translucent fill is below 4.5:1. 'fbi_surveillance_van' in purple is an unexplained one-off colour. The 'current pillagers 0' and '0 out · 7 dead' lines are redundant.
findings.fix: Collapse to the top 3 rows plus 'you' by default. Set rows to 16px --f-cond with 24px line height and --tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better. Mark dead rows with a --danger dot instead of text. Drop the purple, or tie it to rarity or party colour and explain it. Use an opaque --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border.

findings.where: Top-right minimap and 'run info' dropdown (x≈1603-1900, y≈18-362)
findings.what: The minimap is a bare, unframed pixel texture with no border or rounding. The 'run info' dropdown bar below it is a different panel style (dark fill, chevron) and has no spacing rhythm with the map. The tiny 'n' and the corner icons at the top are clipped and unreadable. The map is also much busier than the HUD around it.
findings.fix: Give the minimap a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius on a --ui-panel plate. Sit 'run info' flush under it with the same width, a 16px gap and the same 4px radius. Enlarge or remove the compass 'n'. Keep a 48px margin from the screen edge.

findings.what: The timer reads 3:20 at about 30px and the 'extract 30m' chip is about 16px, both over a busy wall texture. The chip is semantically unclear: '30m' conflicts with a 3:20 clock, and the small teal arrow underneath is unexplained. This should be the hero element, but it is as weak as the other chips.
findings.fix: Show the timer at --fs-hero 56px f-cond 800 on a --ui-panel plate. Replace 'extract 30m' with one clear line, for example 'extract in 30:00'. Move the direction arrow onto the screen edge or the minimap.

findings.where: Bottom-left hp bar and hotbar (x≈25-950, y≈965-1060)
findings.what: 'hp 100' is large bold text sitting on the green bar with only a thin gap above the screen edge, and the bar's right end at x≈430 does not line up with the hotbar. The hotbar slots 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 0 show bare numerals floating on the terrain with no slot boxes. Slots 2 and 4 are framed in different colours (amber and purple) with no legend. The 'f' key badge is tiny and the bar is flush to the bottom edge with under 20px margin.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 hotbar slots with the same --ui-panel box, a 1px --ui-line border and a 4px radius. Frame only the selected slot in --acc. Mark the rarity of slots 2 and 4 with a 3px bar at the bottom edge, not a full frame. Make the hp bar 24px tall, text inside it at 20px, bottom margin 32px and left margin 48px. Align the hp bar width to the hotbar.

findings.what: The 30/60 numeral is a good hero, but the card is edge-hugging with about 10px margin. 'b / i backpack' at 14px is too small and low contrast. 'compact smg' is right-aligned while the numbers use a different baseline, so the card reads loosely aligned.
findings.fix: Inset the card 48px from the right and 32px from the bottom. Raise the hint to 16px --tx-2. Align name, number and hint on one right edge with 8px gaps.

findings.where: 'f1 controls' and 'elite cache' tooltips (x≈440-540, y≈940-965 and x≈748-825, y≈602-627)
findings.what: Two small floating chips use a different style from the other panels: they have no border, the key cap is a different shape, and the text is under 16px. 'f1 controls' sits in the middle of the lower area, not mid-bottom-left as the style guide specifies, and it overlaps the building texture.
findings.fix: Use one chip style across the HUD: 16px f-cond, --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius. Put the f1 hint on the left-hand side, centred on the hotbar's baseline at about 48px from the left edge.

v.verdict: The missed-extraction banner is clear and sits in the right place, but the HUD around it is crowded, uses mixed type sizes and has a few text errors.

findings.where: extraction missed banner (top centre) and the 'extract 30m' pill plus clock above it
findings.what: Two extraction messages compete for the same area. 'extraction missed' is amber and 'extract 30m' is a teal pill, and they sit about 100px apart with the clock between them. The teal pill reads as a live prompt although the extraction was missed. The banner also has a thin amber underline that looks half-finished. The amber is --warn, which is correct for a warning, but the left bar and underline add a second accent shape.
findings.fix: Remove or grey the 'extract 30m' pill while the missed state is showing. Make the banner 56px tall with a 4px left bar and no underline. Use tx-1 for the text with the amber only on the glyph. Keep the banner at least 160px from the clock.

findings.what: The text has a typo ('a available'). A teal extraction ring and label are still shown even though the banner says extraction was missed. The player gets mixed signals about whether extraction is still possible.
findings.fix: Fix the string, or hide the label and ring when the extraction is missed. If extraction really is still available, change the banner wording so the two do not contradict each other.

findings.where: scoreboard panel at top left ('current pillagers 0', 'value at risk')
findings.what: The panel is dense. Eight rows of 14–16px text, with about six sizes of grey and purple, sit on a panel with weak edges. The header 'current pillagers 0' and the footer '0 out · 7 dead' repeat each other. The purple row (fbi_surveillance_van) adds an unexplained colour. The names and values are dimmer than the 4.5:1 floor, and the whole panel competes with the banner.
findings.fix: Show only the top 3–4 rows plus 'you'. Drop the footer line. Set every row to 16px in tx-2, with 'you' in tx-1. Put the purple row in the P2 cyan or in tx-1. Use the --ui-panel fill at 85% opacity with a 1px --ui-line-hi border.

findings.where: bottom-left 'hp 100' bar and the '4 minutes left' tag
findings.what: The hp bar is a flat green block with a large 'hp 100' label clipped to its left end. The label is about 32px and has the same weight as the ammo hero number, so two heroes compete. The '4 minutes left' tag floats at mid-left with an amber left bar and no panel. It has no clear relationship to the HUD corners, and the banner already tells the same story.
findings.fix: Make the hp label 20px inside the bar and let the bar be 24px tall with a 4px radius. Move the timer into the top-centre cluster next to the clock, or drop it. Keep one hero number per screen: the ammo.

findings.what: The slot spacing is uneven: slots 1, 2 and 4 are filled while 3 and 5–0 are bare numbers. This leaves a gap and loose digits with no tile. The selected slot 2 uses an amber border, but lime --acc means selected. The slot icons are small inside 90px tiles.
findings.fix: Draw empty slots as 1px --ui-line tiles of the same size, or hide them. Change the selected border to --acc at 3px. Use a 96px grid with 8px gaps.

findings.where: ammo panel (bottom right) and 'f1 controls' hint
findings.what: The ammo panel is good, with a 56px hero number, but the weapon name 'compact smg' is right-aligned at a size nobody scales to, and 'b / i backpack' is about 14px. The 'f1 controls' hint sits in the middle of the map, 1px above the hotbar, in a dark pill that nearly touches slot 1's top edge. It is not placed mid-bottom left as specified.
findings.fix: Set 'compact smg' to 20px and the backpack hint to 16px. Move 'f1 controls' to the mid-bottom-left spot, at least 24px away from the hotbar, folded to a single line.

findings.what: The minimap has no border radius and no outline, and its header 'run info' is a dropdown with a chevron. The map bleeds into the world without a clear edge. The two-tone panel (black map, grey header) does not match the other panels.
findings.fix: Add a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Give the header the same --ui-panel fill as the other HUD cards. Align its left edge with the right margin used by the banner and scoreboard (48px).

findings.what: A small green pill reading 'keyboard' sits at the edge with a different border colour and radius from every other element. It touches the screen edge, with no margin. It is debug-looking.
findings.fix: Remove it from the HUD, or move it inside the 48px margin as a 14px tx-2 label with no fill.

v.verdict: The HUD is readable and mostly lower case, but it shows contradictory extraction messages, scatters small low-contrast text around the screen, and shows a tiny, easy-to-miss missed-extraction notice.

findings.where: extraction state: world label 'extraction a available' (648,470), left feed 'extraction missed' (105,789), top banner 'extract 30m'
findings.what: The screen says three conflicting things at once. The ring is still labelled available, the feed says extraction was missed, and the banner counts down to extraction. The label also has a typo ('a available'). The feed line is the only signal for a major event, and it is small and sits low on the left edge. The top-centre banner is meant to carry alerts, and it says nothing about the miss.
findings.fix: Remove the 'extraction a available' label once extraction is missed, or change it to 'closed'. Fix the typo. Send the miss to the top-centre alert banner at --fs-title 32px in --danger, and keep the left feed to one short line. Make the banner and the ring state agree.

findings.what: The line is about 18px high, set in teal with a thin teal edge bar. Teal is reserved for extraction success, so a miss reads as good news. It also sits on busy green terrain with a small icon and no panel weight, and it is not the same size as the other feed or label text.
findings.fix: Use --danger for the miss, set the text at 20px, and put it on a --ui-panel fill (80% opacity) with a 3px bar. Use the same 24px padding as the other feed rows and give it a 160ms bounce-in.

findings.what: The panel is the biggest block on the screen. It has 9 rows of roughly 14px text, with the value column and the 'dead' tags all set at the same weight and in muted grey. It crowds the corner and covers the map. There is no hierarchy, 'you' barely stands out, and the purple 'fbi_surveillance_van' row has no explained meaning. The header ('current pillagers 0') and 'value at risk' are only slightly larger than the rows.
findings.fix: Show only the top 3 plus 'you', or fold the list into 'run info'. Use 16px minimum text, make the 'you' row --acc or --ui-raised with a 3px bar, and show 'dead' as --danger glyphs, not words. Set the header at 16px in --tx-2 and the 'you' value at 20px in --tx-1. Give every row a 32px height.

findings.where: HUD type sizes overall: 'f1 controls' (440-540, 942), 'run info', 'b / i backpack' (1684, 1027), slot numbers 3,5-0 (~14px)
findings.what: Several labels are 12-14px and dim, which is below the 16px floor and unreadable from a couch. The unused slot numbers float on terrain with no plate, so they clash with the world art.
findings.fix: Set all labels to at least 16px in --tx-2 on a --ui-panel plate. Remove or dim the empty slot numbers, or fold them into slot frames. Move 'f1 controls' to sit left-aligned with the hp bar, in one short line on a plate.

findings.what: The hotbar is cropped by the hp bar and the ground. Slots 1, 2 and 4 are different widths from the empty slots 3 and 5-0, which have no frame at all. The selected slot has an amber outline, which is the player colour, not the lime 'selected' colour. The numbers sit at different offsets and the 'f' badge crowds slot 4.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots at 72px with a 4px radius and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Mark the selected slot with a --acc 3px border. Use a consistent 8px gap and put the numbers at one fixed offset.

findings.where: bottom-left hp bar (22-430, 1034-1068) and bottom-right ammo card (1668-1910, 902-1052)
findings.what: The hp bar is a flat, saturated green slab with a big 'hp 100' that sits on the bar and is not aligned to the ammo card. It touches the screen edge (about 22px margin against 5% elsewhere). The ammo block follows the hero 56px style and is the right call, but it has the weakest margin, and its 'b / i backpack' hint is tiny.
findings.fix: Use 5% margins (96px horizontal, 54px vertical) for both corner blocks, and make their bottom edges line up. Set the hp number to 32px in --tx-1 and use a thinner 12px --ok bar. Set the hint at 16px.

findings.what: The 'run info' dropdown is a small bar with a chevron whose text is about 16px, and the minimap sits tight to the screen edge and has no label. The two read as separate blocks with differing border weight and radius compared with the left panel (square corners versus the others).
findings.fix: Give the minimap and 'run info' the same 4px radius, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 16px gap. Align the top-right edge to the 5% margin and use the same panel header style as the left list.

findings.what: The timer has a small sun icon in a dark circle and a text chip below. It is about 30px high, so it is smaller than the hero size, and it competes with the 'the sump' map label (900-1015, 170), which is a wide-letterspaced, faint, serif-like label that looks like another font and sits on the wall art.
findings.fix: Set the timer at 56px f-cond 800 only when the extract is within 60s, and 32px otherwise. Remove the 'the sump' label or move it into the 'run info' panel, and keep the font to Barlow Condensed.

v.verdict: The HUD is readable and mostly lower case, but it is still a set of mismatched boxes. The big controls panel, the tiny party list, the full-width 'run info' bar and the stray HP bar each use their own size, fill and type, and the controls panel steals attention from the play area.

findings.what: The panel is a 311x346 black block of about 28 rows of 16px text, open mid-left in a live raid. It is the most visually dominant HUD element and it covers the playfield. The brief says a career raid shows it folded to one short line, mid-bottom left, until F1 opens it. It is also a wall of explaining text, which is clutter.
findings.fix: Fold it by default to one 32px-high chip at x24 y1000 reading 'f1 controls'. Use --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Expand it only on F1. If it stays open, shrink it to 3 columns at 60% opacity.

findings.what: The bar sits flush against the bottom-left edge with no margin. The 'hp 100' label is about 32px and larger than the title scale, so it competes with the ammo hero number. The fill is a flat green with no track and no frame. The bar also runs into the hotbar's left edge.
findings.fix: Make the bar 260x12px with a --ui-line track at x24 y1040. Put 'hp' at 16px tx-2 and '100' at 24px f-cond 700 tx-1 on a line above it. Keep 56px for the ammo only. Leave a 24px gap to the hotbar.

findings.what: The card has a 8px left margin that does not match the 24px margin used elsewhere. The type is 16px, cramped, with 18px row pitch and no divider. 'value at risk' and the chevron are tiny. The pure black fill with the thin border differs from the ammo card and the controls panel. Names and values are the same weight, so the 'you' row does not stand out.
findings.fix: Move the card to x24. Use --ui-panel fill and a 4px radius. Use a 24px row pitch and a 1px --ui-line divider under the header. Give the 'you' row an amber P1 mark and a --ui-raised row fill. Set names to 16px tx-1 and values to 16px f-cond 700 right-aligned.

findings.what: It is a 297px full-width bar with a hard black fill and a lone chevron. It is far wider than its 'run info' content needs. It overlaps the building art, and its edge is not aligned with the 'c 152m' chip below it at x1812-1890.
findings.fix: Shrink it to about 160px wide at x1736-1896. Use --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border, a 4px radius, 16px f-cond 600 text and a 12px chevron. Align its right edge with the 'c 152m' chip at x1896.

findings.what: The card is the right hero element, but the 'scav pistol' name, the 56px '12 / 24' and the 'b / i backpack' hint are crowded. The card's right padding is about 14px, which is not on the 8px grid. The card also overlaps the wall art behind it, and the dark fill is at about 85% opacity. That makes the name look too light on the busy background.
findings.fix: Use --ui-panel fill at 92% opacity and 24px padding. Set the name to 20px f-cond 600 tx-1. Keep the 56px 800 weight for '12'. Make '/ 24' 24px tx-2. Set the hint to 16px tx-2. Align the card's right edge at x1896.

findings.what: The selected slot has a thin amber outline, but lime --acc means 'selected', so this breaks the colour rule. Slots 3 and 5-0 are ghost icons with floating numbers that look unfinished. Numbers sit outside the slots at inconsistent positions. The slot sizes are 90px with 20px gaps and do not match.
findings.fix: Draw the selected outline at 2px --acc. Make idle borders --ui-line-hi. Put the slot numbers inside each slot's top-left at 16px tx-2. Draw empty slots as 90px --ui-panel squares at 60% opacity with an 8px gap.

findings.where: Top-centre timer and extract chip x905-1035 y10-72
findings.what: The '14:37' timer is mid-weight grey text on a busy map with a faint outline, so contrast is low. The teal 'extract 152m' chip is fine on colour, but its 14px type is below the 16px minimum and there is a duplicate 'c 152m' chip at right.
findings.fix: Make the timer 32px f-cond 700 tx-1 with a 2px dark shadow on a --scrim pill. Raise the extract chip to 16px. Remove the duplicate 'c 152m' chip, or keep only the arrow.

findings.where: Bottom-left status icons x24-110 y940-980 and 'keyboard' tag x10-105 y8-30
findings.what: The two round icons, an amber eye and a green clover, have no labels and are crammed 8px above the hp bar. The 'keyboard' tag at the top-left is the only element with a green fill and a different radius, and it sits at a 10px margin.
findings.fix: Put the icons in 32px --ui-panel circles on a 24px left margin with a 16px gap from the hp bar. Restyle the 'keyboard' tag as a --ui-panel chip at x24 y24 with 16px tx-2 text and a 4px radius.

v.verdict: The ammo block and the hotbar selection are decent, but the HUD still has no consistent margin, size or panel system: the hp bar is oversized and clipped at the edge, the corners are cluttered, and a stray 'run info' dropdown, a keyboard chip, a banner with a capital letter and a '$' prefix on 'value at risk' dominate.

findings.what: It is the biggest and loudest element on the screen, a red 32px headline plus a sub-line sitting over the play area and crowding the extract banner just above it. The two banners are stacked within 30px of each other and use different styles (amber outline pill vs red filled card). The alert should be a single quiet top-centre banner that fits the HUD system.
findings.fix: Restyle it as the same 48px-high --ui-panel banner as the extract pill, with a 1px --danger border and 20px --f-cond text, and a 16px --tx-2 sub-line. Keep 16px of gap below the clock row and fade it out after 4s.

findings.what: The 'hp 100' text is about 36px, which is off the type scale and larger than the ammo label. The bar is a flat unframed green strip that touches the screen's bottom edge, with a 24px margin instead of 48px, and it sits against the hotbar and the 'f1 controls' chip with no alignment.
findings.fix: Put it in a --ui-panel container 320x32 at x=48, y=1000, with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a --ok fill. Draw 'hp' at 16px --tx-2 and '100' at 20px --tx-1. Align its bottom edge with the hotbar slots.

findings.where: top-right 'run info' dropdown (1603-1901 x 19-54) and top-left 'current pillagers' table (8-367 x 142-170)
findings.what: Both are different widths and on different offsets (the table is at x=8, the dropdown 19px from the top), and neither is on the 48px safe margin. The dropdown looks like an HTML select with a chevron, and the table's header text is cramped at roughly 14px. The table also floats at y=142 for no reason. 'the long dock cache' is an unrelated tooltip chip hanging under the dropdown.
findings.fix: Dock both at a 48px margin (x=48 and right edge 1872, y=48). Use the same --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius and 16px --f-cond text for both. Make the row height 32px and right-align the money column. Move the 'the long dock cache' label to the map object.

findings.what: A green-tinted debug-looking chip stuck in the corner at a 5px margin. Its green reads as 'ok' or 'selected' and competes with the lime accent. It tells the player nothing useful in this view.
findings.fix: Remove it from the raid HUD, or make it a neutral --ui-line-hi chip in 16px --tx-2 at x=48, y=48. Never use a green fill for a device label.

findings.what: The slots are two 90px tiles, but the digit labels 3-9 and 0 are loose text floating on the map with no slot, and they are low contrast against the wall art. The row looks broken, with only two slots out of ten visible. The selected slot has a good amber border, but amber is meant for P1 and lime for 'selected'.
findings.fix: Either draw all ten slots as 64px --ui-panel tiles at 85% opacity with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, or hide the empty digits entirely. Make the selected border 2px --acc and move the digit to the slot's top-left corner at 16px --tx-2.

findings.where: extract pill (873-1047 x 47-75) and clock (933-1030 x 10-42)
findings.what: The pill uses amber text on an amber outline with a 14px label, which is below the 16px minimum. The clock with the sunrise icon is a different weight, so the three bits of text at top centre have no shared system, and the pill hangs 5px under the clock.
findings.fix: Set the pill text to 16px --f-cond 600 in --tx-1 with a --warn 1px border and a --ui-panel fill. Put 8px between it and the clock and centre both on x=960.

findings.what: This is the best-crafted element: the hero number is clear and the panel is solid. But it sits 10px from the right edge and 28px from the bottom, so it is off the 48px margin. The '24' total is dimmer than needed, and 'b / i backpack' is about 14px.
findings.fix: Move it to a right margin of 48px (right edge x=1872, bottom y=1032). Make 'b / i backpack' 16px --tx-2 and the reserve '24' --tx-2 at 32px.

findings.where: 'f1 controls' chip (440-540 x 941-964) and 'value at risk' header (250-340 x 147-162)
findings.what: Tiny labels at about 14px. The chip floats on the map above the hp bar with its own darker fill, and a dim 'value at risk' header sits next to the chevron with poor contrast.
findings.fix: Set both to 16px --tx-2 on --ui-panel. Place the controls chip at the mid-bottom left, 8px above the hotbar, and bring the header to --tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better.
