Numbers 1 and 2 are inside the tiles while the empty ones sit outside. The selected slot in amber is the same hue family as the P1 tag, and that is not the lime 'selected' colour the guide calls for. The nearby '4' slot with its purple gun uses a different state style from the rest.
findings.fix: Hide empty slots, or draw them as 1px --ui-line outlines at a fixed 64px size. Make the selected border --acc, 2px. Align all number labels top left at 16px inside the tile.

findings.where: 'extract 62m' pill and the clock, top centre
findings.what: The teal 'extract' pill is stuck right under the clock with about 4px between them, and its little arrow marker points straight at the clock. The sun icon next to '14:59' is a different art style from the rest of the HUD. The clock is large but gets no panel, so it floats over a busy tile background.
findings.fix: Put 12px between the clock and the pill. Put the clock on a --scrim chip. Reduce the sun icon to match the 16px label scale. Keep the teal for extraction only.

findings.where: 'pillager joined' toast and 'view backpack' hint, bottom
findings.what: The toast sits at about 45px above the slot row on a black box with no border, and it duplicates the left feed that is meant to carry every non-alert line. 'view backpack' is 14px grey text jammed against the card's lower edge at x≈1700, y≈1027, and no key is shown with it.
findings.fix: Move the toast text into the left feed and remove the centre box. Set the hint at 16px in --tx-2 with a key chip, and give it 16px of padding from the card edge.

findings.where: world labels ('packing floor', 'the seal 0%', 'the forge', 'sentry r-57', 'p1' tag)
findings.what: Five label styles are in use: wide-tracked grey, cyan boxed, yellow plain, tiny grey on a dark chip, and an amber-outlined box. The 'sentry r-57' label is about 12px, below the 14px floor. Several have weak contrast against the lilac floor.
findings.fix: Use one world-label style, 16px f-cond 600 in --tx-1 on a --scrim chip with a 4px radius. Colour only a 3px left bar by type (teal for extract, red for hostile, grey for neutral). Raise the sentry label to 16px.

v.verdict: This is a clean, consistent modal. The lime button is the clear primary action and the rarity bars work. It's still a plain list in an oversized card, with an unfocused title, a stray lime fragment and small row text.

findings.what: The title is about 28px and sits low and left with no hero or reward feel. It is the same weight as the row names, so the eye goes to the lime button first. The card is a spec list with no moment of reward, and the 'welcome' framing is weak.
findings.fix: Set the title to 32px, f-cond 700, with 24px of space above it. Add a one-line quiet subtitle in tx-2 at 16px, or a hero count such as '7 items' at 56px, so the card has one clear focal point.

findings.what: Row names are about 19px at 600 weight, and the quantity labels 'x2' and 'x3' are in muted grey at the far right edge. Between the name and the quantity sits a 600px empty gap, so the eye cannot track across the row. The rarity bars carry the only colour, and nothing says which rarity each one is.
findings.fix: Set row height to 72px and name size to 20px. Raise the quantity to tx-1 at 20px, and put it next to the name or in a fixed 64px column with tabular numbers. Give the rarity bar a 3px width and a rarity-coloured tag in the 16px label style on the right.

findings.where: top-left corner of the card (x≈504, y≈157)
findings.what: A short lime fragment sits on the card's top edge and is unexplained. It reads as a rendering bug or a clipped accent. Lime means 'selected', and here it marks nothing.
findings.fix: Either extend it into a full 3px accent bar across the card's top edge, or delete it. Do not leave a 36px stub.

findings.what: The card is 960px wide for a seven-row list with little content. The bottom padding under the button is about 56px, but the top padding above the title is about 64px. The title baseline floats, and the header divider and footer divider are both thin and low in contrast.
findings.fix: Use equal 32px padding on all sides. Put the header divider on --ui-line-hi. Narrow the card to about 720px, or add a right-hand detail pane that shows the selected item.

findings.what: The button is about 56px high, flat and sharp-cornered, with 20px black text and no visible focus ring or bounce. It is right-aligned and far from the title, while the X sits at the top right. The two actions are 600px apart, so the layout feels uneven.
findings.fix: Add a 2px outer focus ring in tx-1 with a 4px offset. Make the button 64px high with 20px bold text. Centre it, or span it across the footer, to match the shop and codex cards.

findings.what: The X is a boxed 48px control with a thick white outline, heavier than the button next to it. It competes with the title and does not match the quiet line tokens. For a welcome pack the player should take the reward, so a close X that skips it is ambiguous.
findings.fix: Use a 40px X with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, and show a lime outline only on focus. Confirm that the X does the same as 'take the pack', or remove it.

findings.where: 'keyboard' chip at top centre and the dim background
findings.what: The 'keyboard' chip floats in a teal-green outline unrelated to the card and sits 150px above it. The background behind the scrim is a dark blur with a faint dark-green blob that looks like a leftover. The result is a muddy frame around the card.
findings.fix: Move the device chip into the footer legend at 14px in tx-2. Use a single flat --scrim at .80 over the screen, with no tinted blobs.

v.verdict: A busy, cluttered raid HUD with inconsistent type, redundant labels and a bright diamond mark that competes with the player, so it reads as a debug layer rather than polished AAA UI.

findings.where: Run Info header, under the minimap (top right)
findings.what: A capital 'I' in 'run Info' breaks the all-lower-case rule on screen. The header also looks like a dropdown, with a chevron, and the minimap collapse chevron above it looks the same.
findings.fix: Change the string to 'run info'. Use one collapse pattern with the same chevron size and weight on both, and make the header 16px label type in tx-2.

findings.where: Party/mark readout: 'pillager · 15m' tag, the 'in pillager's party' box, the 'pillager' bar at left, the 'current pillagers 3' dropdown, and the name over the player
findings.what: The same name appears 4-5 times in four different chip styles (black tag, black box, blue-text bar, dropdown). The mark tag and the party box float over the map with no anchor. The 'in pillager's party' sentence is explaining clutter. The player colours are also unclear, since the map mark is amber but the P2 name is blue.
findings.fix: Show the name once per entity. Delete 'in pillager's party' and the standalone party box. Use one chip spec: 16px f-cond 600, --ui-panel fill at 90%, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 8px padding. Anchor the mark tag 8px above the diamond, with a leader line if it sits off-screen.

findings.where: Map mark diamond at (840,492), and the minimap diamond
findings.what: The ping/mark is a thin amber outline diamond with no fill, and it is nearly invisible against the tan floor patches. The minimap diamond is filled and heavy, so the two do not read as the same mark. The mark should be a recipe shared by both.
findings.fix: Draw the world mark as a 24px diamond with a 3px stroke in the P2 cyan or P1 amber, a dark 1px outer stroke for contrast, and a filled centre. Add a 1.5s bounce on placement. Use the same glyph and colour on the minimap, scaled down.

findings.where: Hud typography overall: hp 100 (≈32px), 12 / 24 (≈56px), clock 14:59, 'f1 controls', 'packing floor', weapon slots
findings.what: There are too many sizes and fonts: a wide-spaced zone name, a condensed digit style for the clock, and many small 13-14px labels (slot numbers 3-0, 'b / i backpack', 'f1 controls'). Several fall below the 16px floor. The hp bar's label looks oversized for its bar and is the heaviest thing at the bottom left, ahead of the ammo, which should be the hero.
findings.fix: Keep hero 56px for ammo only. Set hp to 32px or move it into a 40px-high bar with a 20px label. Raise the small labels (slot numbers, 'f1 controls', 'b / i backpack') to 16px at tx-2 or hide them. Set the zone name in f-cond 600 at 20px with normal tracking.

findings.where: Left edge stack: 'current pillagers 3' dropdown, the 'pillager' bar and the controls label
findings.what: These are three differently styled elements on the left, and they float over map art. The pillager bar is a thin blue-text box with a green bar, which is not the style used elsewhere. The dropdown has a chevron but no clear function in a quiet HUD. The 'f1 controls' chip is mid-bottom but tiny and low-contrast.
findings.fix: Merge them into one party panel at left: 8px margin, --ui-panel fill, 4px radius, and one row per player with a 4px coloured player bar, a 16px name and a 24px-high hp bar. Remove the dropdown chrome. Make 'f1 controls' a 16px chip with a 1px border.

findings.where: Top-centre cluster: clock 14:59, the sun icon, the 'extract 62m' chip and the cyan arrow
findings.what: The chip is teal-on-black with a small arrow underneath it that is easy to miss. The clock text is grey and thin on a busy brown wall, and the sun icon is an unexplained orange blob. The clock is not the focus, yet it competes with the extract chip.
findings.fix: Put the clock and extract on one line inside a single 40px panel (--ui-panel at 85%). Clock in tx-1 at 32px, extract in --extract at 20px. Remove the sun or make it a 20px time-of-day glyph in tx-2. Put the direction arrow inside the chip.

findings.where: Weapon slots bar (bottom centre) and ammo panel (bottom right)
findings.what: The slot row mixes the lit slot 1 (amber border, which clashes with the lime focus rule), the unlit slot 2, and ghosted 3-0 slots with faint gun silhouettes. The ghosted slots add noise, and the number labels sit at slightly different offsets. The ammo panel's 'scav pistol' text is right-aligned while the stack is left-aligned.
findings.fix: Show only occupied slots, 72x72px, with a 2px --acc border on the selected one (not amber). Put the slot numbers at a fixed 8px inset, top-left, at 16px. Align the ammo panel's name and numbers to one edge with 24px padding, and let the panel sit on the same bottom margin (24px) as the hp bar.

findings.where: World labels: 'the seal 0%', 'the forge', 'sentry r-57', 'packing floor'
findings.what: Each label uses a different style: blue outlined text, yellow text with no panel, a grey chip, and wide-tracked grey text with no contrast on the floor. The colours do not follow a scheme, and 'packing floor' is close to illegible.
findings.fix: Use one world-label spec: 16px f-cond 600, tx-1 with a 2px dark outline or a --ui-panel chip at 80%. Reserve colour for state only: --warn for interactable, --danger for hostile, --ok for done. Give 'packing floor' a chip or raise its contrast to at least 4.5:1.

v.verdict: The window frame is clean and consistent (title, x close, footer legend, lime key chip), but the map is a crowded sea of overlapping small labels with no single focal point, and the contract rows have dim text and weak separation.

findings.what: There are about 30 labels at 14-16px in four colours (white, grey, red, teal). Several collide or crowd: the 'cache' cluster at top right, 'extract b' over 'stays open' beside the 'hot ground' text, 'foreman office · locked' beside 'cache', and 'seal 0%' touching the circle. Many grey labels ('packing floor', 'strongbox', 'chill row', 'the sump') are lower contrast than 4.5:1 against the dark floor plan.
findings.fix: Show one label tier by default: extracts, the mark and the player only. Reveal room and cache names on hover or zoom. Give all labels a 1px --ui-void text halo. Use at least 16px and --tx-1 or --tx-2. Add collision nudging with a 8px minimum gap.

findings.what: This screen is about the new map mark, but it is the weakest element. The lime-less amber arrow sits on an amber disc with a tiny 'mark' label that overlaps the arrow tip. It is smaller than the teal extract rings and gets lost. The mark colour is also not tied to the P1 amber or the lime selected rule in any visible way.
findings.fix: Make the mark a 24px pin with a 2px ring and a 40px pulse. Put the 'mark' label 8px clear of the glyph on a --ui-panel chip. Use the P1 amber consistently. Do not let the label overlap the glyph.

findings.what: Row names are about 20px tx-2 grey, and the prices and progress are 16px right-aligned. Every row has the same weight, so there is no hierarchy beyond the title. The divider bars are thick, grey and low contrast, and read like progress bars that are all empty. 'holding' in green is the only state cue. The $ values compete with the names.
findings.fix: Names in --tx-1 at 20px 600. Prices in --tx-2 at 16px. Make the dividers 1px --ui-line. Draw a real 4px progress bar in --acc only on rows with progress. Highlight a done or holding row with a 3px --ok bar on the left edge.

findings.what: 'cold storage' is a 32px bold title with 'sector map' in a dim 20px next to it. '6pm · clear' sits far right beside the x with unequal spacing. The x button is a boxed 56px square, bigger than the other header items, and it competes with the title.
findings.fix: Set the subtitle to 16px --tx-2 with a 16px gap after the title. Group '6pm · clear' 24px from the x. Reduce the x to 40px with a --ui-line-hi border so it matches other windows.

findings.what: 'click set mark · right-click clear' and 'surveyed 3%' are 16px grey at the left, with uneven gaps. The only lime element is a tiny 'm' chip beside 'close' in the far corner, so the primary action is barely visible. The key chip is too small for a couch.
findings.fix: Make the chip 28px with 16px text. Use a 24px gap between footer items. Align 'surveyed 3%' to the map's right edge, or move it into the map frame as a 16px corner stat.

findings.what: The map frame is inset 56px from the card's left edge, while the contracts panel ends 56px short of the right edge. The map has a 4px light border and the contracts panel has none, so the two panes look like different components. There is a dead dark band between the map and the contracts panel, and below the last row.
findings.fix: Give both panes the same 1px --ui-line-hi border and --ui-panel fill. Set the gap between them to 24px and the outer padding to 32px, and align the pane bottoms to the footer rule.

findings.what: The red encampment diamonds, the red danger circle, the blue water patch and the hatched areas all use low-saturation fills. The legend is missing, and the several icon styles (ring, circle with dot, square with glyph) are indistinguishable at 1080. Caches and strongboxes are plain dots.
findings.fix: Limit the map to three icon shapes at 20px and give each a distinct colour: extract teal, loot --warn, hostile --danger. Drop the blue patch to 8% opacity or remove it. Make the hatch 1px at 20% opacity.

v.verdict: The in-raid HUD is readable and the 30/60 ammo hero number is strong, but its corners are inconsistent (green hp bar, bare '1-0' slot row, mixed dropdown headers), and the world callouts are inconsistent too: the 'run Info' header has a capital letter, the mark and 'you' pills are loose, and the sentry label sits on top of the sentry.

findings.what: A capital 'I' appears in 'run Info'. The owner ordered all lower case, and this is the only capital on screen outside art. The header also looks like a dropdown with a chevron but has no visible pad focus state.
findings.fix: Change the string to 'run info'. Give the header a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a lime 2px focus bar when selected, and match the 'current pillagers 7' header's height, 32px.

findings.what: The hp bar is a flat, saturated mid-green slab. It runs to the screen edge and is clipped at the bottom. It is the loudest colour block in the HUD and outweighs the ammo hero number. 'hp 100' is 30px type with a blurry glow against the green fill.
findings.fix: Inset the bar 48px from the left and bottom. Make it a 12px-tall track on --ui-panel with a --ok fill. Put 'hp 100' at 20px in --tx-1 on the panel above the bar, not on the fill.

findings.what: Only three slots are filled. The empty slots show bare numerals 3 and 5-0 in muted grey, with faint ghost gun silhouettes. At 14px or less, those numerals are below the 16px minimum and low contrast. The row reads as unfinished clutter. Slot 4 carries a purple rarity bar next to an amber bar on slot 2, and the lime selected frame competes with both.
findings.fix: Show only owned slots plus at most 2 empty placeholders drawn as 1px --ui-line outlines. Set numerals to 16px --tx-2. Keep lime only on the selected slot. Make every tile 80x80 with a 4px radius.

findings.where: top-centre mark pill, 'you · 15m' tag, 'search crate' prompt
findings.what: There are three different label styles. The 'mark 15m' pill is a black chip with an amber arrow. The 'you · 15m' chip is a black pill with no pointer. The 'e search crate' prompt has a lime key chip. The 'you' chip floats about 60px away from the player and points at nothing. The timer sits right above 'mark 15m' and crowds the 9:00 hero number.
findings.fix: Use one world-tag recipe: 16px f-cond 600, --tx-1 on --scrim, 4px radius, 8px padding, plus a 6px pointer toward the target. Put 'you' tags within 16px of the player. Leave 16px between the clock and the mark pill.

findings.where: sentry label (1120-1190, 470-490) and the enemy cluster
findings.what: The orange 'sentry r-46' label has a white-ish outline and sits directly over the sentry sprite, with an exclamation mark above it. It overlaps the target and the red threat cone. The label is tiny, about 13px, and orange on red-tinted ground, which is low contrast.
findings.fix: Offset the label 24px above the sprite on a --scrim chip. Use 16px --warn or --tx-1 text. Draw the threat cone at 15% alpha so the label stays readable.

findings.what: The minimap is a stark black panel with thick white wall bars and no border. The unlabelled icons, including a yellow triangle, a red triangle and several cyan marks, are tiny. The panel clashes with the grey-brown world and with the 'run info' header under it, so the top-right corner reads as three separate widgets.
findings.fix: Give the minimap a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius, and set the wall bars to --ui-line-hi instead of pure white. Attach 'run info' flush under the map as one 297px-wide panel with an 8px gap. Make the map icons at least 10px.

findings.what: The 'compact smg' name, the 56px '30 / 60' number and the 'b / i backpack' hint are well structured. But the card sits 10px from the right edge and 28px from the bottom, not 48px. It also sits on the same baseline band as the hp bar but with different margins. The hint is only about 14px.
findings.fix: Set the card to 48px margins from the right and bottom edges, matching the hp bar inset. Raise the hint to 16px --tx-2. Keep a 4px radius and a 1px --ui-line-hi border.

findings.where: 'the seal 0%' and 'the forge' world labels, 'f1 controls' chip
findings.what: The seal label is blue text on a dark-blue chip, the forge label is bare yellow text with no chip, and 'f1 controls' is a grey chip tucked at the left of the slots. All are about 14px, off the 16px floor. The three colour treatments have no clear meaning.
findings.fix: Put all three on the shared world-tag chip at 16px. Colour only a 3px left bar to signal type. Leave the text --tx-1. Align 'f1 controls' to the slot row's left edge.

v.verdict: The card is now clean and consistent, with the close x in the corner, a clear lime main action and rarity bars, but the quantity column is still weak, the item names are small, and the card is still wider than its content needs.

findings.what: The quantities are small, dim and far from the names, about 600px away across empty row space, so the eye has to cross the whole row. Single-item rows show nothing, so the column is inconsistent.
findings.fix: Show 'x1' on single rows. Set quantities to 20px f-cond 700 in tx-1 in a fixed 64px right-aligned column. Or move them straight after the name.

findings.where: card width and row content (x480-1440, rows 72px)
findings.what: A 960px card holds rows that are nearly empty: icon, name, and a number far away. The rows read as sparse, with no second layer of information, and the card looks like a generic list.
findings.fix: Narrow the card to about 640px centred. Add a 16px tx-2 type tag ('smg', 'heal', 'grenade') after each name. Or keep the width and put the rarity word in the tag.

findings.what: The title is about 28px and competes with the 20px item names and the lime button, so the hierarchy is flat. The button is the loudest element and the title sits quiet in the top-left with a lot of empty space above it.
findings.fix: Set the title to 32px f-cond 700 in tx-1. Put its baseline 32px from the card top, and cut the top padding from about 64px to 32px.

findings.where: orphan lime tick at the card top-left (x504-540, y157)
findings.what: A short lime fragment sits on the top border and looks like a rendering glitch rather than a deliberate marker.
findings.fix: Extend it into a full-width 3px lime top rule, or remove it.

findings.what: The names are small and tx-1 only at medium weight, and the 3px rarity bar is thin and floats with a 12px gap from the icon, so the rarity cue is weak.
findings.fix: Make the rarity bar 4px by the full 64px row height, flush with the icon edge, and set names to 20px f-cond 700.

findings.what: The button is right-aligned with a 57px gap below it, while the title has only about 40px of top padding in comparison. The bottom padding looks uneven. There is no pad-focus ring on the main button other than its fill.
findings.fix: Use 32px bottom padding. Add a 2px tx-1 outline offset 3px as the focus ring on the button.

findings.what: The chip has a green outline and green text, a colour that does not match the lime accent, and it is the only element on the dimmed background.
findings.fix: Use a tx-2 outline and text at 16px, or recolour it in --acc.

v.verdict: The capture shows the welcome-pack modal over the dimmed lobby, not the partner raid HUD, so the map-mark change and the earlier HUD advice can't be judged; the modal itself is tidy but undersized and its hierarchy is flat.

findings.what: The shot does not show a raid. The welcome-pack modal covers the lobby, and no HUD, minimap, mark diamond or 'pillager · 15m' tag is visible. The earlier P1 items (run info header, mark glyph, HUD corners, hp bar, weapon slots) are unverified.
findings.fix: Dismiss or suppress the welcome pack for this capture, or trigger it before the shot is taken. Re-shoot at raid time with the P1 and P2 HUD visible and the mark on screen. Until then the o-00v-239 change cannot be accepted.

findings.what: The card is about 50% of the screen width. His Q43 order was a centred card at about 90%. The rows stop at 1398 while the lobby behind stays readable, so the modal looks small and unfinished.
findings.fix: Size the card to 90% (about 1728x972) or, if it is meant as a small confirm, drop the fake-window chrome. Use --scrim at .80 so the lobby behind is not legible.

findings.what: All seven rows have the same weight, and the name sits far from its x2 or x3 quantity across an empty 700px gap. Rarity is only a thin 2px bar, and the 20px rows carry no category or stat. It reads like a plain list, not a Diablo-style grid, and the two guns don't stand out from bandages.
findings.fix: Make the guns larger (96px tile, rarity name in a 16px --tx-2 label) and keep consumables compact. Put quantity as a 16px chip directly after the name, or use a 2-column tile grid. Make the rarity bar 3px and as tall as the tile.

findings.what: The x is a heavy white-outlined square that is the brightest element on the card. It competes with the lime CTA and with the title. The title is also small and weak at about 28px; the hero needs the title or the main action, not the close box.
findings.fix: Draw the x as a 1px --ui-line-hi 40px box with a --tx-2 glyph, which brightens to --tx-1 on focus. Set the title to 32px f-cond 700 with the 24px margin the rest of the card uses.

findings.where: primary button 'take the pack', bottom right
findings.what: The lime fill is the correct single accent, but the label is letterspaced wider than the other 20px text and the button sits tight to the divider above it. Nothing shows which element has pad focus.
findings.fix: Set it to 20px f-cond 700 with +.04em tracking, 56px tall, with 24px above it. Add a visible 2px --acc-hover outer ring as the focus state, and give the close x its own focus ring.

findings.what: A short lime stub sits on the card's top border with no meaning. It reads as a rendering glitch.
findings.fix: Remove it, or make it a full-width 3px --acc top bar on the card if an accent edge is intended.

findings.what: A green bordered chip floats on the page edge. Its colour, 16px bold and border don't match any panel or label style. It is also a different green from --ok.
findings.fix: Restyle it as a 16px --tx-2 label with a --ui-panel 4px-radius chip and 1px --ui-line-hi border, and place it on the 24px margin.

findings.what: There is 57px of dead space under the button against 40px at the sides. The title gap above the first rule is also bigger than the row padding, so the vertical rhythm is uneven.
findings.fix: Use 24px padding on every side and an 8px grid. Move the footer rule and button as one row, 24px from the card edge.

v.verdict: The card is clean and consistent with the lime-button and x-corner system, but the earlier advice on title size, row scale, quantity weight, the corner stub and the button's focus ring was not applied, so it is still a flat list with weak hierarchy.

findings.what: The title is about 28px. It sits tight against the divider and has no subtitle or hero count, so the eye lands on the lime button first and the screen has no clear focal point.
findings.fix: Set the title to 32px f-cond 700 with 24px of space above it. Add a 16px tx-2 subtitle such as '7 items', or a 56px hero count. Put 24px between the title and the divider.

findings.where: row names and quantities (x≈625 and x≈1387)
findings.what: Names are about 19px and quantities are muted grey, with a 900px gap between them. Rows with no quantity (smg, carbine, smoke) leave dead space on the right, so the eye cannot connect name to count. The rarity bars are thin and there are no rarity tags.
findings.fix: Use 72px rows and 20px names. Set the quantity to tx-1 at 20px tabular, in a fixed 64px right-aligned column, and show 'x1' on single items. Make the rarity bars 3px wide and 32px tall. Add a 16px rarity-coloured tag before the quantity.

findings.what: The button is right-aligned at about 56px high. Its text is small, with wide tracking, and it has no visible focus ring. This is the one main action, but its pad focus state is not readable.
findings.fix: Make the button 64px high and at least 240px wide, with 20px f-cond 800 text and normal tracking. Add a 2px tx-1 ring with a 4px offset to show focus. Centre it, or span the footer, to match the shop and codex cards.

findings.where: top-left corner of the card (x≈504–540, y≈157)
findings.what: A 36px lime stub on the card's top edge looks like a rendering glitch. It is not a full accent bar.
findings.fix: Draw a full-width 3px --acc bar across the top edge of the card, or delete the stub.

findings.what: The card is 960px wide, with 40px side padding and about 56px of empty space under the button. The rows are stretched wide, which spreads the content thin.
findings.fix: Use 32px padding on all sides and cut the bottom gap to 32px. Narrow the card to about 720px, or add a right-hand detail pane.

findings.what: The x box is 47px with a thin outline, and it sits closer to the card's top edge than to its right edge. That is inconsistent with the 32px padding used elsewhere.
findings.fix: Make the x box 48px and inset it 24px from both the top and right edges. Use a --ui-line-hi border and give it a lime focus ring when focused.

findings.what: The device chip floats over the scrim with a teal border and green text. That colour is reserved for extraction, and the chip is detached from any panel.
findings.fix: Restyle the chip in tx-2 on --ui-panel with a --ui-line-hi border at 16px, or move it into the card footer legend at 14px.

v.verdict: This is a clean, readable welcome-pack modal, but it is not the partner-raid screen with the ping and map mark that the label and my earlier review describe. The card is also only about half the screen and the type hierarchy is flat.

findings.what: The shot shows the welcome pack modal over a blurred menu. There is no raid HUD, map mark diamond or ping, so the earlier P0/P1 advice on the mark, minimap and party panel cannot be judged and has not been verified.
findings.fix: Re-capture mark-p2-partner-raid-1080 in a live raid with the P2 mark placed and the minimap visible. Capture the welcome pack as its own screen.

findings.what: The card is 960 wide, 50% of the screen, and the rows leave a lot of dead space between the name and the quantity. This conflicts with the owner's rule that windows are a centred card of about 90% of the screen (Q43).
findings.fix: Either widen it to a 1728x972 card, or keep a deliberate narrow dialog of 640px with the rows tightened. Do not leave a half-size card with 700px rows.

findings.what: The title is about 28px, bold and cream, and sits left-aligned with 80px of empty padding above it. The X, the title and the lime button all compete, and nothing says this is a gift. The 1px rule under the title is the only separator.
findings.fix: Set the title to 32px f-cond 700 and align its baseline with the centre of the X. Cut the top padding to 32px. Put a 16px tx-2 count such as '7 items' on the right of the title row.

findings.what: The X box has a bright cream 1px border and a heavy glyph. That is louder than any idle border in the guide (--ui-line-hi) and it pulls the eye away from the title. A small lime sliver at the card's top-left (504 to 540, y157) also looks like a stray artifact.
findings.fix: Use a 40px box, a --ui-line-hi border and a tx-2 glyph that goes tx-1 on focus. Remove the sliver, or extend it into a full 3px lime top bar if it is meant as an accent.

findings.what: Rarity is shown only by a 2px bar, which is faint for the grey, green and blue tiers. The quantity text 'x2' sits far right and is hard to tie to its row. Row names are the same size and weight as the button, so the list reads as flat.
findings.fix: Make the rarity bar 3px and 32px tall. Put the quantity in tx-1 at 20px f-cond 700, or place it beside the name. Add a 16px tx-2 type tag such as 'smg' or 'consumable' under each name.

findings.what: The button is correct as the one lime action, but the wide letter-spacing makes it look like a different type style. It is right-aligned with no left counterpart, and there is no visible focus or pressed state. The bottom padding of 57px is uneven against the 24px above the footer rule.
findings.fix: Use 20px f-cond 700 with normal tracking, make the button 240x56, and add a 2px --acc-hover outline offset 3px for pad focus. Set the footer padding to 32px top and bottom.

findings.what: The teal-outlined chip is small, roughly 14px type, and the teal is reserved for extraction. It reads as debug text sitting on the card's scrim.
findings.fix: Make it 16px tx-2 with a --ui-line-hi border, or hide it in release captures.

v.verdict: The window shell is clean and consistent, but the map is still crowded with about 30 labels at mixed sizes and colours, and the contracts panel is flat, so the screen stays at a competent 3.

findings.what: The earlier advice to show one label tier was not followed. About 30 labels (cache x9, room names, locked, encampment, extract, seal, hot ground, peddler) all compete. They run 12-15px, mix white, grey, red and teal, and sit on top of each other. Clusters at the top right and the right-centre ('cache cache cache', 'blast freezer · locked', 'extract b') are close to unreadable at couch distance.
findings.fix: Default to extracts, the mark, the player and hazards only. Show room and cache names on hover or zoom. Set all labels to 16px with a 1px --ui-void halo. Use --tx-1 for primary labels and --tx-2 for secondary ones. Collapse the repeated 'cache' text into the glyph, and nudge labels so there is at least an 8px gap between any two.

findings.what: The mark is a small 28px amber diamond and its chip is about 12px text. The chip touches the 'extract c' label, and the diamond sits next to the player arrow. The mark is the point of this screen, yet it is the same visual weight as the grey cache labels.
findings.fix: Make the pin 24px with a 2px ring and a --acc or P1 amber pulse. Put the chip at 16px on --ui-panel, 8px clear of 'extract c', and move 'extract c / closes in 3:00' 16px to the right.

findings.what: The earlier advice on rows was not applied. Every row is a flat grey name with a flat grey divider, and the price and the 0/2 count are stacked at 16px, so nothing is the hero. The dividers read as progress bars (3px, full width), which is misleading. The panel gives no sign of which contract matters.
findings.fix: Set names to 20px --tx-1. Make the dividers 1px --ui-line. Draw a real 4px progress track only on rows with progress, filled with --acc. Put '0/2' in --tx-2 on the same line as the price, or move it to the left under the name. Give the held or done row a 3px --ok bar on the left edge.

findings.what: Teal, red, amber, white and grey are all used as label colours. Red 'encampment' and 'hot ground' text is small and low in contrast on dark red. The blue water patch and the red hazard circle are muddy fills. The red circle runs over 'chill row' and 'scrap line'.
findings.fix: Keep colour for icons and rings, and give labels --tx-1 or --tx-2 only. Lower the hazard fill to 12% opacity with a 2px dashed --danger outline. Move the labels out of the circle.

findings.what: The subtitle 'sector map' is about 20px --tx-2, tight against the title with only about 20px between them. '6pm · clear' sits next to a 58px x button. The x border is stronger than on other windows.
findings.fix: Set the subtitle to 16px --tx-2 with a 16px gap after the title. Reduce the x to 40px with a --ui-line-hi border. Put 24px between '6pm · clear' and the x.

findings.what: The footer is 16px muted text and 'surveyed 3%' floats in the middle with no alignment to the map or the panel. The 'm' key chip is small and the gap before 'close' is cramped.
findings.fix: Right-align 'surveyed 3%' to the map's right edge, or move it into the map frame as a 16px corner stat. Make the chip 28px with 16px text and leave 24px between footer items.

findings.what: The contracts panel has about 8 rows with a lot of dead space inside each one, while the map is crammed. The panel top border and the map frame are not aligned, and the title row and the first row differ in height.
findings.fix: Move the map and panel top edges to the same y (160px). Tighten the row height to 64px. Give the freed space to the map, making it about 60% of the width.

v.verdict: The mark pill and the 'you' and crate tags now share one dark chip recipe, but the earlier hp bar, weapon strip and header fixes were not applied, so the HUD still looks cluttered and uneven.

findings.what: The hp bar is unchanged. It is still a fat green fill, flush against the left and bottom edges and clipped by the screen edge. 'hp 100' is in a condensed face at about 32px, drawn on the fill with weak contrast, and it is the loudest element at the bottom left.
findings.fix: Inset it 48px from the left and bottom. Make the track 12px tall on --ui-panel with an --ok fill. Put 'hp 100' at 20px in --tx-1 on the panel above the track, not on the fill.

findings.what: Ten numerals are still shown, with faint ghost weapon silhouettes at slots 5 to 0. The numerals sit at different heights from the tiles and are hard to read against the map. The empty slots add clutter and the tile sizes are inconsistent: slot 1 and the selected slot 2 are about 90px, the rest are loose silhouettes.
findings.fix: Show only owned slots plus at most 2 empty slots drawn as 1px --ui-line outlines. Make every tile 80x80 with a 4px radius. Set the numerals to 16px --tx-2 inside the tile corner. Keep lime only on the selected slot.

findings.what: The two collapsible headers use different widths and different heights, about 34px against 28px. Both are plain dark bars with a chevron, with no border or focus treatment. They read as two different components, and 'run info' is jammed against the minimap with no gap.
findings.fix: Make both 32px tall, with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius and 16px f-cond 600 text. Leave 8px under the minimap and give both the same 16px side padding.

findings.what: The four tags use four recipes. The sentry tag is an amber text chip, the seal and forge tags are bare coloured text with no chip, and the crate tag has a lime key cap on a dark chip. The seal and forge text is thin and loses contrast on the busy tiles. The shared recipe was applied only to the mark tags.
findings.fix: Use one recipe for every world tag: 16px f-cond 600, --tx-1 on --scrim, 4px radius, 8px horizontal and 4px vertical padding. Tint only a 2px left bar (--warn for sentry, --extract for the seal, --r-gold for the forge). Keep each tag within 16px of its target.

findings.what: The red cone is a hard-edged, high-alpha fill. It crowds the crate prompt and the barrels. The '!' marker, the sentry tag, the red ring and the barrels' own '!' icons pile up into one noisy knot.
findings.fix: Draw the cone at 15% alpha with a 1px --danger edge. Offset the sentry tag 24px above the sprite. Drop the duplicate '!' marker above it.

findings.what: The clock at 9:00 has no chip, so it sits directly on the beige wall at low contrast. The mark pill is 8px below it, with a small orange pointer that touches the pill's edge. The cluster is tight.
findings.fix: Put the clock on a --scrim chip at 32px. Leave 16px to the pill and set the pointer 6px below the pill's bottom edge.

findings.what: The card is better than the other HUD parts: its '30 / 60' hero number is clear. But the weapon name is right-aligned in a different place from the number and 'b / i backpack' is about 14px, which is too small and too dim. The card also sits 10px from the right edge and the bottom, while other elements use different margins.
findings.fix: Use a 48px margin from the right and bottom edges. Make 'b / i backpack' 16px --tx-2. Give the card the same 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius as the header bars.

findings.what: The hint is a small chip with a grey key cap. It floats on the map left of the weapon strip with no alignment to the strip or the hp bar, and its text is tiny.
findings.fix: Align its baseline to the weapon strip's top edge, set the text to 16px --tx-1 and make the key cap 24px tall. Place it 48px from the left, on the same row as the hp bar's label.

v.verdict: Removing the cache tags cleared the cluttered label pile-ups on the map, but the labels are still weak in tiers and contrast, and the contracts panel is unchanged: its bars are still thin grey rules, its text is still all one weight, and the 'open' row still breaks the count column.

findings.what: The progress bars were not changed from last time. They are still a thin grey rule, with no fill, and no 0/n row shows any progress. Reward and name have the same visual weight. The 'elite kill' row shows 'open' where every other row shows a count, which breaks the right-hand column.
findings.fix: Draw a 4px track in --ui-line with an --acc fill proportional to progress. Set names in --tx-1 at 20px and rewards in --tx-2 at 16px. Give every row the same count slot ('0/1'). Move 'holding' and 'open' into a status tag at the left of the bar.

findings.where: map labels, overall (extract c/b/a, zone names, POI labels)
findings.what: The three tiers I asked for are still not there. Zone names such as 'packing floor', 'chill row', 'the sump' and 'scrap line' are grey on dark grey and sit on top of hatching and wall art. 'foreman office · locked' and 'blast freezer · locked' are bold white, so they outrank the extract labels. The teal extract labels, at the same size as POI labels, are the only strong tier.
findings.fix: Extract labels 20px --extract. POI labels 16px --tx-1 with a 60% --ui-void chip behind them. Zone names 16px --tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better, with a 1px dark outline. Make 'locked' a --warn glyph instead of bold white text.

findings.where: map, strongbox label and icon (x 1015-1080, y 400-480)
findings.what: The cache pile-up is gone, but the 'strongbox' label sits above and left of its icon at 15px. It almost touches the 'blast freezer · locked' label (x 852-1000, y 417) and the room edge. The icon is a tiny circle-and-key glyph that is easy to miss.
findings.fix: Put the label 12px to the right of the icon, or below it, with a chip behind it. Move 'blast freezer · locked' at least 24px left. Make the icon 28px.

findings.what: 'extract b' and 'stays open' overlap the right-hand room's hatching and sit within about 10px of the room edge. The label is also placed to the left of its own marker at (1050, 551).
findings.fix: Centre the 'extract b' label under its marker and give it a chip. Keep it 16px clear of the room edge.

findings.where: map frame, empty lower-left and lower-right (x 160-1085, y 640-900)
findings.what: Large stretches of the map show only scattered noise pixels and tiny ring markers (e.g. (755,840), (604,896)). The rings carry no label and no legend explains them, so they read as clutter. The two 'encampment' labels in red compete with 'hot ground' and the danger zone.
findings.fix: Drop the unlabelled ring markers or add labels at 16px. Shrink the red 'encampment' labels to 16px, or give them a --danger diamond with the label in --tx-1.

findings.what: 'click to set a mark' and 'surveyed 2%' are 16px in the same grey with no separation. Only the 'm close' key chip is lime. There is no legend for the map symbols.
findings.fix: Put a 1px --ui-line divider between the two footer items. Add a small symbol legend (extract, encampment, strongbox) in 14px --tx-2.

v.verdict: The HUD is much cleaner than before, with one top-centre cluster, a single bottom weapon row and an uncluttered right side. But the raid controls panel is a large, always-open wall of text, and the left/bottom margins are inconsistent.

findings.what: The full controls list is open at 300x300px, and it sits mid-left rather than folded to one line at mid-bottom-left as the owner ordered. It is the largest panel on screen and competes with the gameplay area. Its text is 16px tx-2 on a near-black fill, and it has three section labels and 20 rows.
findings.fix: Fold it to one 32px-high chip at x48 y~930 reading 'f1 controls'. Open the full list only on F1, at 24px padding with a 4px radius. Drop the section labels to 14px tx-2 if they stay.

findings.what: The concealed and in-cover chips, the hp bar and the 'hp 100' text are packed into 120px. The hp bar is saturated green against the green map, and the 'hp 100' label is oversized and overlaps the bar edge. The hp bar sits at x24, off the 48px margin. The chips use three different heights and two border colours (amber and teal), which are not the --warn or --extract roles.
findings.fix: Put the hp bar at x48 y1020, 24px high and 380px wide, on a --ui-panel backing. Set the label at 20px f-cond 700 tx-1 inside the bar. Align the chips at x48 y968, 32px high, with 8px gaps and the same 4px radius.

findings.what: Only 3 of 10 slots have gear, and the empty ones are faint ghost silhouettes with floating digits that look like rendering leftovers. The slot tiles are 92x92, which is bigger than the system's 64px. The selected tile uses a hot amber border instead of lime --acc, which breaks the rule that lime means 'selected'.
findings.fix: Show only occupied slots, as 64x64 tiles with an 8px gap, centred on x960 and 24px from the bottom. Use a 2px --acc border on the selected tile. Set the key digit at 16px tx-2 inside the tile top-left. Dim the empty tiles to 30% and drop their silhouettes.

findings.what: The panel is right-aligned to a 10px margin, not 48px. 'scav pistol' is in white at about 22px and 'b / i backpack' is 14px, which is small. The '12 / 24' hero has good scale, but the slash and the 24 are in a different weight from the magazine count, and the panel is 240px wide.
findings.fix: Move the right edge to x1872, a 48px margin. Make the panel 220x120. Put the name at 16px tx-2, the magazine at 56px tx-1 and the '/ 24' at 24px tx-2. Set the backpack hint at 16px.

findings.where: Top-right 'run info' and 'current pillagers' panels, x8-368 y143-242 and x1603-1902 y17-53
findings.what: These are two different panel styles. The 'current pillagers' table is small (14-16px) with tight rows, its title is bold and it has a caret. The 'run info' dropdown is a different width and font weight, and its edge is 18px from the screen edge. The $ values are right-aligned but dense. The 'current pillagers' panel also starts at x8, not 48.
findings.fix: Give both panels the same --ui-panel fill, 4px radius and 16px padding, and use a 48px outer margin. Make the rows 24px high with 16px text, and make panel titles 16px tx-2. Align 'current pillagers' at x48 y~120.

findings.what: The clock is 28px and mixes with the sun icon. The extract chip is teal on a dark fill, which fits the extract role, but it is only about 24px high with 16px text, so it is small. The extract waypoint '152m' near the right wall duplicates it with a separate 'c 152m' chip. The result is that the extract info appears twice.
findings.fix: Keep the top chip only, and make the clock 32px f-cond 700 with a 56x56 icon slot. Drop 'c 152m' to a plain arrow, or hide it when the top chip shows. Space the chip 8px under the clock and make it 32px high.

findings.where: 'the long dock cache' tag, x1668-1798 y140-167
findings.what: The location label floats on the map with no anchor, in a panel style that doesn't match the others (a lighter border and a tight 8px padding). Its meaning is unclear.
findings.fix: Attach it to its marker with a 16px leader line, or restyle it as a --ui-panel chip with 16px text and 8px padding. Hide it when it isn't near the player.

v.verdict: The HUD is cleaner than before: run info is collapsed, the leaderboard is short and the timer is a single hero. The open controls card, the capitals on screen and the crowded bottom-left status cluster still hold it below a polished 4.

findings.what: The full card is open, about 300x300px. It covers the player's left flank, and the spec says it should start folded to one line in a career raid. Section labels are tiny, dim and unaligned, and the keycap column widths vary. 'full list' sits at the bottom as a second hint.
findings.fix: Fold it to one line at mid-bottom left, 'f1 controls', 16px --tx-2, and open it only on F1. When open, use 16px labels in --tx-1 and 1px --ui-line-hi keycaps. Make all keycap columns one fixed width (72px) and add 16px inner padding.

findings.where: leaderboard top-left, and the timer, the extraction chip and the 'c 152m' edge marker
findings.what: The leaderboard shows dollar values with a capital-$ style at about 14px, tight rows and a thin header, and its first row is 'you' with no emphasis. The 'value at risk' column is dim. Extraction distance appears twice, as the 'extract 152m' chip and the 'c 152m' edge marker, which breaks the one-place-per-line rule. The edge marker also truncates to 'c'.
findings.fix: Set leaderboard rows to 16px with 24px row height. Highlight 'you' in --acc and the other rows in --tx-1. Raise column text to --tx-2 at 16px. Drop the 'c 152m' marker or show only the arrow. Make the chip text 16px.

findings.where: bottom-left status cluster (concealed, in cover, hp 100)
findings.what: Two circular icons and two pills sit above an hp bar with no clear order. 'concealed' is amber and 'in cover' is a different style, so the two read as unrelated. The hp bar is a flat green slab, 400px wide, with 'hp 100' at an oversized scale and no frame. It is the only vital readout and it reads as an afterthought.
findings.fix: Make both pills one style: 16px f-cond 600, 4px radius, 8px padding, with the icon inside the pill. Put the hp bar in a 4px-radius track at 24px tall with the number right-aligned in 20px. Leave an 8px gap between pills and bar.

findings.what: The bar is a 300px dark strip with the title at 16px and a chevron. The whole thing floats at the screen edge with no inset, and it overlaps the building walls beneath it. The 'the long dock cache' tooltip floats below it, unattached to anything.
findings.fix: Inset the bar 24px from the screen edge, use --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Anchor the tooltip to its marker with a 4px pointer, or remove it.

findings.where: contract item banner above the weapon slots
findings.what: The banner has a yellow left bar, an icon and two phrases separated by a dot ('contract item nearby · gold glow marks the box'). The second phrase is an explaining sentence, and the banner runs into the slot area at the right.
findings.fix: Cut it to 'contract item nearby' at 20px. Move it 16px above the slot row and centre it over the slots.

findings.what: The numbers 5-0 for empty slots are floating labels with faint gun silhouettes, which makes the row cluttered. Slot 2 shows a white fist glyph with a blue 'f' badge. Slot 3 is a gap with no frame, so the row looks broken.
findings.fix: Draw all ten slots as 56px tiles with 1px --ui-line borders, at 40% opacity when empty. Keep the lime border only on the selected slot. Remove the ghost silhouettes.

findings.what: This is the best element, but the 'b / i backpack' hint is 14px and low contrast. The weapon name 'scav pistol' is right-aligned, but the hero '12 / 24' has no accent on the current count.
findings.fix: Set the hint to 16px --tx-2. Colour the '12' in --tx-1 at 56px and the '/ 24' in --tx-2 at 32px.

findings.what: The timer is only about 28px. The sun/day icon beside it is unlabelled, and the timer is below the 56px hero size the guide sets.
findings.fix: Raise the timer to 56px f-cond 800 and drop the icon, or place it 8px left of the timer at 24px.

v.verdict: This is a clean, consistent sector-map card with a good title, x close and footer hint, but the map labels are tiny and crowded, the contracts list is flat, and the earlier raid-HUD advice does not apply to this screen.

findings.where: Map labels across x160-1080 y190-880 (peddler, the long dock, foreman office, extract c, seal 0%, chill row)
findings.what: Labels are about 14px and sit on busy room outlines. Several collide with geometry or each other: 'strongbox' is clipped at the map edge, 'extract b' and 'chill row' touch, and 'extract a' overlaps the hot-ground rooms. Grey labels such as 'packing floor' and 'the sump' have weak contrast.
findings.fix: Set all map labels to 16px f-cond 600 tx-1. Give each a 2px --ui-void text halo, or a 4px-radius chip at 70% void. Move 'strongbox' 16px left of the map edge, and nudge 'extract b' and 'chill row' apart by at least 12px.

findings.what: All eight rows are identical. Reward and progress are stacked and right-aligned in 16px tx-2, so nothing marks the most valuable or nearest contract. The thin divider under each row doubles as a progress bar, and the empty state looks the same as a divider.
findings.fix: Put the reward on the row's right side at 20px f-cond 700 tx-1, and the 0/1 progress at 16px tx-2 on the same baseline. Replace the dividers with 1px --ui-line. Draw a separate 4px progress bar at x1144 only on rows with progress above 0, filled in --acc.

findings.what: There are three text groups of similar weight: 'cold storage' (32px), 'sector map', and 'elites and keys are live intel'. The last is an explaining sentence, which is clutter. 'dawn · clear' sits far right beside the close box and competes with it.
findings.fix: Delete 'elites and keys are live intel'. Set 'sector map' to 16px tx-2. Keep 'dawn · clear' at 16px tx-2 with 24px of space before the 48px close box.

findings.where: Map legend and in-map text, 'intel live' x178 y191
findings.what: 'Intel live' has a capital I. The map also has no legend for the red diamonds, teal rings or the hatched rooms, so you have to guess what the symbols mean.
findings.fix: Change it to 'intel live'. Add a one-line legend in the footer at 16px tx-2: teal ring = extract, red diamond = encampment, with a 12px glyph per item.

findings.what: 'click to set a mark' and 'surveyed 2%' are 16px in similar muted colour, and the close hint is small and far right. A pad player gets no focus indication, and 'click' is mouse-only wording.
findings.fix: Show the key hint for the device in use, such as 'a set mark', in a 20px lime-bordered key chip. Group 'surveyed 2%' at 16px tx-1 with its number. Keep 'm close' with a 24px chip.

findings.where: Map frame x153-1090 y160-920 against the contracts panel x1120-1765
findings.what: The map frame is a thick 4px grey border at a different radius from the 1px-bordered contracts panel. The right panel ends 55px short of the card's inner right edge, and its bottom does not line up with the map's.
findings.fix: Give both panels a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Set equal 32px gutters inside the card, and make both panels end at y920 and x1790.

findings.what: Titles are 20px tx-2 grey with the rest of the text, so the primary read is dim. 'haul over $1,200' contains a '$' on a goal value, which is correct. The text is low in contrast on the panel.
findings.fix: Set titles to 20px f-cond 600 tx-1 (#efe9dc) and push the muted tone to the secondary progress only.

v.verdict: The card frame is clean and consistent: a title on the left, an x on the right, a footer, and a calm contracts list. The map itself is the weak part, with small dim labels that collide with each other, and the contract rows are flat and unclear.

findings.where: map labels (packing floor, the long dock, the sump, scrap line, chill row, strongbox)
findings.what: The area names are about 14px, grey on a dark grey map, and they sit over the wall lines. They are the hardest text on screen to read from a couch, and they look weaker than the white labels (peddler, the forge). The map uses at least three label styles with no clear rule: white bold, grey, and teal.
findings.fix: Use one label rule. Area names are 16px f-cond 600 in --tx-2. Interactive points (peddler, forge, strongbox) are 16px in --tx-1. Extractions are 16px in --extract. Add a 2px --ui-void text shadow or halo so labels stay readable over walls.

findings.where: map label collisions (intel live, seal 0%, extract b / strongbox, extract a / hot ground, foreman office · locked)
findings.what: 'intel live' sits on the map frame line, so the border strikes through it. 'strongbox' is jammed against the extract b label and its tile edge. The extract a label overlaps the hot-ground circle and its wall lines. 'seal 0%' touches the forge label. The map looks crowded and unfinished.
findings.fix: Inset 'intel live' 8px below the frame, or move it into the header. Offset the extract b and strongbox labels by at least 16px, with the labels placed outside the tiles. Keep an 8px clear gap around every label, and nudge the labels that touch.

findings.what: Every row has the same weight. Reward ($960) and progress (0/1) are 16px and right-aligned, stacked tightly under each other. The progress bars are empty grey lines with no fill, so they carry nothing. Eight rows of the same height give the eye nowhere to go, and the first row, 'haul over $1,600', is not marked as the main one.
findings.fix: Keep names at 20px --tx-1. Put the reward at 20px --acc-free --tx-1 on the right, with progress at 16px --tx-2 directly beneath it. Make the bar 4px tall with a --ui-line track and a --acc fill that grows with progress. Add a 1px --ui-line divider between rows, with 16px padding top and bottom.

findings.where: header: 'elites and keys are live intel' and footer 'click to set a mark', 'surveyed 2%'
findings.what: The header sentence is an explaining line. It is tiny and tightly packed next to the sector map label, and the three header items read as one muddy line. The footer text is about 14–16px in dim grey, and a lowercase l can read as a capital I (intel/live) at this size.
findings.fix: Delete the header sentence or turn it into a 16px 'live intel' tag. Keep a 24px gap between the title and 'sector map', and make 'sector map' --tx-2 at 20px. Raise the footer hints to 16px --tx-2 and separate them by 32px.

findings.where: close controls (x top right, 'm close' bottom right)
findings.what: There are two ways to close, drawn in two different styles. The x is a boxed button. The 'm' key is a small lime chip that looks like a primary action, but it only means close. Lime is reserved for selected and the one main action.
findings.fix: Keep the x as the close control. In the footer, draw the 'm' keycap with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and --tx-1 text, not an --acc fill, and set both at 16px.

findings.what: The map frame is a thick 2px grey border with a darker inner area. The contracts panel is a thin-bordered --ui-panel with a different radius and a different heading height. They look like two separate UI systems, and their top and bottom edges differ by a few px.
findings.fix: Give both panels the same 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius and --ui-panel fill. Set the same 16px inner padding and the same top and bottom edges (y=160 to y=920).

findings.what: The count is small, dim and right-aligned against the 24px 'contracts' title. It is a useful summary but too faint to read, and it does not line up with the row amounts below.
findings.fix: Set it to 16px --tx-2 and align its right edge to the same 24px inset as the row values. Add a 1px --ui-line divider under the header row.

findings.what: The red hot-ground circle, the blue water area and the dashed red outline use different fills. The circle is a large muddy red wash, and the water is a flat blue block. Both are decorative and clash with the flat style of the rest of the map.
findings.fix: Draw the hot ground with a 1px dashed --danger outline and a 10% --danger fill. Make the water a 10% --r-rare fill. Keep both lower in value than the labels.

v.verdict: This is a readable raid HUD with a strong ammo readout, but the top-centre stack is crowded, the left controls panel is oversized, and a feed line collides with the players. Contrast is also uneven: the hotbar numbers sit on a pale road strip.

findings.where: feed line 'pillagers joined' at x895-1010 y903-920, behind the player 2 shield label and the avatars
findings.what: The feed text is about 30% opacity grey on a light road, and the 'shield' tag and avatars cut through it. It is unreadable and looks like a rendering bug.
findings.fix: Move the left feed to a fixed lane at x24, y300-420, away from players. Use 16px f-cond 600 tx-1 on a 70% --ui-void chip with 4px radius. Keep world labels like 'shield' 12px clear of any feed text.

findings.where: top-centre stack x858-1062 y18-200: timer, team score and mark banner
findings.what: Three boxes of different widths touch each other, with only 0 to 4px gaps. The timer (x890-1030) is narrower than the score box (x858-1062), so the stack has a ragged edge. The 'you 0 sp / p2 0 sp' text is about 12px and tiny. The mark banner sits right under the score and reads as part of it.
findings.fix: Make the timer and score one 220px-wide panel with a 1px --ui-line divider. Set the p1/p2 split at 16px tx-2. Put the 'mark 43m' alert banner 16px below the stack, as its own chip. Keep the timer as the hero at 56px 800 and shrink the team total to 32px.

findings.what: It is open at full size (311x348), which covers a large part of the map left of the action. The headers 'move', 'fight', 'gear' and 'raid' are about 14px and dim, and the 'move' key row repeats the 'move' header. The key caps are too similar to the plain labels, so the panel is noisy. Even for party walk-up, it competes with gameplay.
findings.fix: Open to one folded line ('f1 controls') at mid-bottom left. If it stays open for the demo, cut it to 6 core rows, set headers at 16px tx-2 with .04em tracking, and drop the panel to 80% opacity. Rename the first row's action to 'walk'.

findings.where: hotbar x655-1050 y970-1062 and slot numbers x555-1475 y972-988
findings.what: The slot numbers 1-9 and 0 are 14px dim grey on a pale, bright road strip, so contrast is under 2:1. Only two slots are filled and the other eight are invisible ghost icons, so the bar reads as scattered. The slot icons and the '360' ammo counts are small. The selected slot 5 has a gold border, which clashes with the lime 'selected' rule.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots as 64px --ui-panel squares with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and the number at 16px tx-1 in the top-left. Mark the selected slot with a 2px --acc border. Put the whole bar on a 70% void backing strip.

findings.what: 'hp 100' is about 32px, bigger than 'armour 60' at 16px, and the two bars are different heights. The text on the blue and green fills is low contrast white. The bars sit tight to the bottom edge, about 12px from it, so they miss the 5% margin.
findings.fix: Make both bars 20px high with a 4px gap. Put the number at 20px f-cond 700 in --acc-ink on the fill, or tx-1 on a void chip. Set the bottom margin to 48px and keep the labels on a shared left edge at x54.

findings.where: top-left 'keyboard' chip x6-105 y6-32 and 'player 2' card x16-170 y324-358
findings.what: The 'keyboard' chip is green with a mono-looking face and sits 6px from the edge, ignoring the margins. The player 2 card floats mid-left with no anchor and is only 14px text. It also sits near the controls panel.
findings.fix: Put the device chip at 16px f-cond 600 tx-2 inside the 48px margin (x48, y24), and drop its green fill. Anchor the player 2 card at x48 y72 at 20px, with a cyan 3px bar and a 16px label.

findings.where: world markers 'mark · 43m' and 'player 2 · 34m' x592-815 y578-640, with the 'mark 43m' banner at top
findings.what: The same mark is shown twice: as a world label and as the top banner. The world labels are 14px with a gap between the label and the diamond that differs on each, and the diamonds sit on black squares that look like placeholders. The text mixes ' · ' with a different format at the top ('mark 43m').
findings.fix: Show the mark only as the top-centre banner, per the rule of one place. Give the world diamonds a transparent background and a 2px 4px-radius ring in amber (p1) or cyan (p2). Use one format, 'name 43m', at 16px.

findings.where: goals dropdown x1652-1900 y18-52 and ammo panel x1708-1910 y922-1020
findings.what: The goals row has a chevron and 14px text, so it looks like a form select rather than a HUD item. It sits 20px from the edge, and the ammo panel is 10px from the right edge, so neither respects the 48px margin. The ammo number is a good hero, but 'support mg' is dim and small.
findings.fix: Set both panels' right edge at x1872 (48px margin). Make goals a plain 20px row without a chevron, and use --ui-line-hi for the border. Raise 'support mg' to 16px tx-1, and keep '60' at 56px 800 in --acc.

v.verdict: This is a live raid HUD, not the sector map I reviewed before, and it is crowded. Eleven separate pieces of UI sit in different styles, and the controls list and the score block dominate the view.

findings.where: controls list, left side (move / fight / gear)
findings.what: This is the always-open party list. It is a large 400x300 box that covers the left edge of the playfield with about 20 rows at roughly 16px. Its keycaps are a different style from every other chip on screen. It has no title, and 'move' and 'gear' are muted so far that they barely read as headers.
findings.fix: Fold it to one 16px line at mid-bottom left as the raid-controls order says, with f1 to open it. If the party demo must keep it open, cut it to the 8 most-used actions and use one keycap style: 1px --ui-line-hi border, --ui-raised fill, --tx-1 text, 4px radius. Make the column headers 16px --tx-1 at weight 700.

findings.where: top-centre: timer, team score, mark chip
findings.what: Three stacked boxes of different widths (timer 140, score 200, mark chip 80) sit in a column with ragged edges. The score box has tiny 'you 0 sp' and 'p1 0 sp' lines at about 13px, which is under the 14px floor. The hero '0 sp' is 24px, not 56px. The timer, which is the hero, looks the same as the score.
findings.fix: Make the timer 56px f-cond 800 with no box. Put the score on one 20px line directly under it: 'team 0 sp'. Move the per-player split into the tab or scoreboard, or set it at 16px --tx-2. Align every box to the same centre axis at 8px gaps and use a 4px radius throughout.

findings.where: world labels: 'chill row', 'mark 41m', 'player 1 · 50m', 'mark · 41m', 'the forge', 'in pillager's party'
findings.what: There are four label styles. 'chill row' is a wide-tracked grey outline that nearly vanishes on the tan wall. 'the forge' is amber at about 13px. 'mark 41m' appears twice, in the top chip and again on the marker next to the player. The 'in pillager's party' toast floats in the middle of the screen and has no clear purpose.
findings.fix: Use one rule: 16px f-cond 600 --tx-1 with a 2px --ui-void halo. Area names are --tx-2, and extraction labels are --extract. Show each mark once, either as the top chip or as the world marker. Move the party status to the left feed and remove the floating toast.

findings.what: The bars are a saturated blue and a green that sit off the palette, with no panel or border behind them. The 'hp 100' text is about 30px with a stroke, and the 'armour 60' text is drawn on the bar at a different size. The text is hard to read against the fill, and the bars collide with the 'the forge' label above them.
findings.fix: Put both bars on a --ui-panel plate with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Make the bars 12px tall with a --ui-line track. Make hp a --ok fill and armour a neutral --tx-2 fill. Put the number at 20px f-cond 700 --tx-1 to the right of each bar, not on top of it. Leave a 16px gap before the world label.

findings.what: The ammo block is well built, with a 56px hero number, but its 'auto rifle' label is 16px and the box edge is faint. The hotbar slots are 90px with the numbers 2 and 4 to 0 floating outside empty slots. The selected slot has an amber border, which is the player-1 colour, but the lime accent should mean selected.
findings.fix: Draw all slot outlines at the same 1px --ui-line. Mark the selected slot with a 2px --acc border. Move the slot numbers inside the top-left corner at 14px --tx-2. Give the ammo panel a 1px --ui-line-hi border so it matches the other panels.

findings.what: The goals bar is a 250px box with a chevron and a rounded-looking edge. The 'keyboard' tag uses a green mono-looking face and a different border from everything else. The two corners do not match each other or the rest of the HUD.
findings.fix: Make both 16px f-cond 600 --tx-1 on a --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Pin them to the same 24px margin. Make the goals chevron --tx-2.

findings.where: player 1 plate, left edge at y 325
findings.what: The plate is a small 150px box with a cyan-green bar. It is set apart from the hp bar by 600px and uses a bar colour that is neither P1 amber nor the --ok green. It duplicates the hp bar and the 'player 1' tag above the character.
findings.fix: Remove the plate in single-view play. If it is needed for the party, colour the name P1 amber and the bar --ok, and dock it with the hp stack at bottom-left.

findings.what: The tag is about 11px blue on a dark chip and is too small to read from a couch. The cyan ring around the P1 character reads as P2's colour, which breaks the rule that P1 is amber and P2 is cyan.
findings.fix: Make the tag 16px, in P1 amber on a --ui-void chip. Recolour the ring to amber for P1 and keep cyan for P2.

v.verdict: The raid HUD has the right pieces (hero ammo, hp bar, hotbar), but a large controls list opens on arrival, the corners are crowded, and text sizes are inconsistent. It also contradicts the owner's quiet-HUD and folded-controls orders, so it reads as a cluttered amateur overlay rather than a polished one.

findings.what: The full two-column key list is open on arrival. It covers about 300x300px of the play area, shows about 20 rows of 14-16px text, and sits right beside the player. The owner's order rs-1 says it should be folded to one short line at mid-bottom left, with F1 opening it. It is also the largest, brightest block on the screen, so the eye hits it before the player, the ammo or the objective.
findings.fix: Default to a single collapsed line, e.g. 'f1 controls', at mid-bottom left, about 16px tx-2, with no panel fill. Open the full list only on F1 and use it as a card with 16px labels and 24px padding. Do not show it in career raids on arrival.

findings.where: top-left: the 'current pillagers 3' panel, and the 'mark · 38m' tag and waypoint under it
findings.what: The panel is cramped. The rows are about 11-12px, below the 16px minimum for anything read. The line spacing is about 15px, the values hug the right edge, the 'value at risk' header is dim grey, and the chevron is tiny. The mark waypoint tag is another 12px label, and its 'mark 38m' text duplicates the 'mark 38m' in the top-centre banner. That is a line drawn twice, which the owner's order of 2026-10-27 calls a defect.
findings.fix: Set the rows at 16px f-cond 600 with 24px line height and 16px padding. Show the mark distance in one place only (the top-centre banner) and keep only the diamond icon at the waypoint, or drop the banner. Use tx-1 for names and tx-2 for the 'value at risk' header at 4.5:1 or better.

findings.what: The 'hp 100' text is bigger than the other HUD text at about 30px. It sits flush against the screen's left and bottom edges with no margin. The bar is flat, saturated green and about 20px tall with no frame, so it clashes with the dark panel language used for ammo. It also touches the status chips above it (concealed, in cover).
findings.fix: Inset it 5% from the edges (about 48px left, 32px bottom). Put the bar on a --ui-panel plate with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius, and use --ok for the fill. Set 'hp' at 16px label and the number at 32px title. Leave 16px between it and the chips.

findings.what: The slot numbers 4-0 float over the world with no frame, in dim grey (a contrast failure), and the ghost weapon silhouettes are barely visible, so the bar looks unfinished. The selected slot has an amber border, but lime --acc means selected and amber means P1, so the focus colour is ambiguous. The number labels are about 11px.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots as 72x72 --ui-panel tiles with a 1px --ui-line border at 4px radius, 8px gaps and 16px numbers in tx-2. Mark the selected slot with a 2px --acc border. Or show only the filled slots.

findings.where: bottom-left, the status chips ('concealed', 'in cover') and their icons
findings.what: The two chips use different treatments: amber text for concealed and teal for in cover. The two icon discs are unlabeled glyphs of different sizes and colours. The chips are about 22px tall with 14px text. Together they add more small colour accents to a corner that already has the hp bar. The colours also do not follow the palette: amber is warn only, and teal is extract only.
findings.fix: Use one chip style: 32px tall, --ui-panel fill, 16px f-cond text in tx-1, with a 3px left bar in a status colour. Drop the extra icon discs or make them the same size, 32px.

findings.where: bottom-centre, the 'contract item nearby · gold glow marks the box' banner
findings.what: This is an explaining sentence on screen, which is a defect by the owner's rules. It has an amber left bar, a document icon and a '·' separator, in a pill that nearly touches the hotbar's silhouettes. Its 14-15px text is hard to read against the water background.
findings.fix: Shorten it to 'contract item nearby' only, or show a gold marker on the box and no sentence. If it stays, use a 32px --ui-panel plate with 16px text and 16px clearance from the hotbar.

findings.where: top-right 'run info' dropdown and the 'c 152m' marker
findings.what: The 'run info' bar is a wide black field at 1 row, about 250px wide, with a chevron, and nothing in it tells the player what it does. It does not match the vertical 1 by 1 career HUD list that was ordered. The 'c 152m' chip and its cyan arrow sit about 12px from the edge, so they look misaligned with the other HUD margins.
findings.fix: Align the top-right stack to the same 48px margin as the other corners. Give 'run info' the same 16px type and --ui-panel plate as the pillagers list, and use one 16px chip style for 'c 152m' and the mark label.

findings.what: The timer is the only top-centre hero, but it is about 24px, well below the 56px hero size, and the icon beside it is unexplained. The orange 'mark 38m' banner under it is a second tag at about 14px, with a tiny arrow, so the two read as stacked clutter.
findings.fix: Set the timer at 32px f-cond 700 as the single hero, drop the icon or label it, and merge the mark distance into one 16px chip 16px below it. Give both the same --ui-panel plate.

v.verdict: The HUD is readable and the top-centre stack is cleaner, but the open controls panel, the feed line still sitting over the play area, the unframed hotbar and the mismatched vitals bars keep it from looking polished.

findings.what: The feed line is still drawn at the bottom centre, over the hotbar numbers 4-5 and the world. It also uses a different chip style from the other labels, and it collides with the hotbar row.
findings.fix: Move all feed lines to a fixed lane at x24, y300-420 (above the controls panel). Use a 16px f-cond 600 tx-1 chip on a 70% --ui-void fill with a 4px radius. Keep the lane free of world labels.

findings.what: The panel is fully open with 26 rows in two columns. It covers the left third of the playfield and shows the list that was meant to start folded. The group headers (move, gear, fight, raid) are almost the same size and colour as the rows, so there is no hierarchy. The 'move' row repeats the word 'move', and it is cluttered.
findings.fix: For career, fold it to one line 'f1 controls' at mid-bottom left, x24, 16px tx-2, and open it on F1. For the demo, keep 8 rows, set headers at 16px tx-2 with .04em tracking, and drop the panel to 80% opacity. Rename the first row's action to 'walk'.

findings.what: The 10 slots are not drawn as a bar. Slots 2 and 6 are filled tiles, and the rest are bare numbers floating over the map, so the row reads as scattered. The selected slot has a lime-amber border that looks like the gold rarity colour. Numbers at 12-14px are below the 16px floor.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots as 64px --ui-panel squares with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 8px apart, on a 70% void strip. Put the slot number at 16px tx-1 in the top-left. Mark the selected slot with a 2px --acc border and no glow.

findings.what: The armour and hp bars are different heights from each other. Their text is white on a light blue and a light green fill, which gives weak contrast, and the labels differ in weight. The hp bar sits at a 12px bottom margin, which is crowded against the screen edge.
findings.fix: Make both bars 20px high with a 4px gap. Use 20px f-cond 700 text in --acc-ink on the fill or tx-1 on a void chip. Align the labels on one left edge at x54, and set the bottom margin to 48px.

findings.what: The timer, team score and mark banner are three separate boxes of different widths (140, 200 and 80px) with no shared edge. The team score line is at 14px, below the 16px floor, and the 'you 0 sp / p2 0 sp' split is cramped. The 'chill row' zone name floats below with wide tracking and low contrast.
findings.fix: Put the timer and score in one 220px-wide panel with a 1px --ui-line divider. Keep the timer at 56px 800 as the hero. Set the split at 16px tx-2. Put the 'mark 43m' chip 16px below it, and render the zone name at 16px tx-1 with a void chip.

findings.where: top-right 'goals 0/3' x1652-1900 y18-52 and top-left 'keyboard' x8-105 y5-32
findings.what: 'goals 0/3' is a wide dropdown bar with a chevron and 14px text, and its dark box does not match the other panels. The 'keyboard' tag uses a green outline and monospace-like lettering that appears nowhere else, so these two read as debug UI.
findings.fix: Make goals a 220px --ui-panel chip with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 16px f-cond 600 text, with a 16px chevron. Restyle the 'keyboard' tag as a 16px tx-2 chip on --ui-panel, and use the same chip height (32px) for both.

findings.where: player 2 bar x16-170 y325-358 and world labels
findings.what: The 'player 2' bar uses a cyan label with two thin bars, and its style does not match the hp and armour bars. The marker labels 'mark · 43m' and 'player 2 · 34m' are small at about 13px. The 'shield' tag at x945-975 y597-608 is tiny.
findings.fix: Draw the player 2 bar with the same 20px bar style as the main vitals, scaled to 160px wide. Set all world labels to 16px f-cond 600 on a 70% void chip.

findings.what: The 30 / 180 readout is a good hero number, but the panel's right and bottom margins are 10px and 60px, which does not match the left vitals margin of 24px. The weapon name is small.
findings.fix: Align the panel's right edge to 24px from the screen edge and its bottom to the same baseline as the hp bar. Set the weapon name to 20px f-cond 600 tx-2, and keep 56px 800 for the 30.

v.verdict: The raid HUD is still a pile of mismatched boxes, floating labels and chips, and the earlier fixes were not applied. The open controls panel, a tiny timer, a duplicated mark label and unplated hp and armour bars compete with the world.

findings.where: top-centre timer, team score and mark chip
findings.what: The timer is a small boxed 9:59 and the score box below it sits at a different width. 'team score' is tiny, and the 'you 0 sp / p1 0 sp' split is cramped and ragged. The mark chip is stuck to the box's bottom edge. The three boxes do not share a centre axis or gaps, so this is the weakest cluster on screen.
findings.fix: Make the timer 56px f-cond 800 with no box. Put 'team 0 sp' on one 20px line under it. Drop the per-player split or set it at 16px --tx-2. Give every box a 4px radius, 8px gaps and one centre axis.

findings.what: The list is fully open with 24 rows, which is clutter. It covers about a fifth of the left screen and clips the wall. The raid-controls order says it should fold to one line, mid-bottom left, with f1 to open it. The column headers are tiny and dim, and the keycaps are inconsistent: some have a border and some do not.
findings.fix: Fold it to one 16px line, 'f1 controls', at mid-bottom left. If the party demo must keep it open, cut it to 8 actions. Use one keycap style: 1px --ui-line-hi border, --ui-raised fill, 4px radius. Set the headers at 16px --tx-1, weight 700.
