findings.what: The bars are flat colour slabs with no plate. The labels sit on top of the fills, and 'hp 100' is a different size from 'armour 60'. The saturated blue and green are the loudest colours on screen. They collide with the hotbar's left edge, and there is no gap between the two bars.
findings.fix: Put both bars on a --ui-panel plate with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Make the bars 12px tall on a --ui-line track. Use a --ok fill for hp and a --tx-2 fill for armour. Put the numbers at 20px f-cond 700 --tx-1 to the right of the bars. Leave an 8px gap between the bars and keep 16px clear of the hotbar.

findings.where: world labels: 'mark 39m', 'player 1 · 48m', 'mark · 39m', 'packing floor', 'the forge', 'the seal 0%', 'in pillager's party'
findings.what: The marks appear twice, once as the top chip and once as the world chip. Every label has a different treatment: a black box, a cyan box, bare yellow text, and widely letter-spaced grey text for the area name. The sizes are around 13px, below the 16px minimum. 'in pillager's party' is a floating toast near the bottom of the screen.
findings.fix: Use one rule: 16px f-cond 600 --tx-1 with a 2px --ui-void halo and no box. Area names are --tx-2 with no letter-spacing. Extraction labels are --extract. Show each mark once. Move the party status to the left feed.

findings.what: The slot numbers sit at different heights and offsets and are tiny and dim. Empty slots have no outline at all. The selected slot has an amber border instead of --acc lime, and the 'rb' tag and 360 count crowd the icon.
findings.fix: Give all 10 slots a 1px --ui-line outline on a --ui-panel fill, 64px square, 8px gaps. Mark the selected slot with a 2px --acc border. Put the numbers at 14px --tx-2 in the top-left corner inside the slot. Keep ammo counts at 16px in the bottom-right.

findings.what: The 60 / 360 number is a strong hero, but the panel is a plain box. Its border is weaker than the other panels. 'support mg' is small and right-aligned against the number, and the 360 is crammed against the 60.
findings.fix: Add a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius, and use the same padding as the other plates. Set 'support mg' at 16px --tx-2, left-aligned. Keep the 56px hero for 60 and set '/ 360' at 20px --tx-2.

findings.what: The goals bar is a wide black field with a tiny label and a chevron. It is a different width and style from the score box. The 'keyboard' tag has a green border and fill that match nothing else.
findings.fix: Make goals a compact --ui-panel plate with a 4px radius, 16px --tx-1 text and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Set the keyboard tag as a 16px --tx-2 text label with no coloured box.

findings.what: The plate has cramped 12px text and thin green and blue bars with no gap, and it sits in the wall shadow. It duplicates the hp and armour bars at bottom left.
findings.fix: Remove the plate if the bottom-left bars stay. Otherwise set the text at 16px, make the bars 6px with a 4px gap, and put it on a --ui-panel plate with 8px padding.

v.verdict: The full controls card is still open on arrival and still dominates the left side, and the top-left pillagers list, hp bar and chips remain small, cramped and inconsistent, so the earlier advice was mostly not followed.

findings.what: It is open in full on arrival, a 300x300 dark card that covers the playfield and is the biggest, busiest element on screen. The owner ordered it folded to one short line at mid-bottom left, opened with F1. Its key caps and labels mix sizes, and the last row, 'f1 full list', is tiny.
findings.fix: Fold it by default to one line 'f1 controls' at mid-bottom left, 16px tx-2, no fill. F1 opens a card with 16px labels, 24px padding, a --ui-panel fill and a 1px --ui-line-hi border at 4px radius. Align the key caps to one 32px cap width.

findings.what: The rows are about 12px type at about 15px leading, with the panel header crammed against the first row. The values in tx-2 are hard to read at couch distance, and the chevron is tiny. The panel is the wrong size next to the 20px 'run info' at top-right.
findings.fix: Set rows at 16px f-cond 600 with 24px line height and 16px padding, names in tx-1, the header in tx-2 at 16px, the panel 48px from the left and top edges, on --ui-panel with a 4px radius. Align the right edge of the panel with the run info dropdown's baseline.

findings.where: top-left, under the pillagers panel: 'mark · 38m' tag with a waypoint diamond
findings.what: It shows the same mark distance as the top-centre 'mark 38m' banner, so one line is drawn twice. This breaks the one-place rule, and the floating orange diamond reads as noise.
findings.fix: Keep the top-centre banner only. Remove the left tag, or keep only the diamond icon at the world waypoint with no text.

findings.what: The bar sits flush at the screen edge with no plate, no border and no inset. The 'hp 100' text overlaps the bar, and the green is a flat, loud fill that fights the amber chips above it. The 'hp' label and the number are both about 28px, so nothing leads.
findings.fix: Inset 48px left and 32px bottom. Put the bar on a --ui-panel plate with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius, fill --ok, 12px high. Set the 'hp' label at 16px tx-2 and the number at 32px tx-1 above or beside the bar, with 16px to the chips.

findings.what: Slot 1 is a 2px amber/gold ring and slots 2 and 3 are black tiles with no border. The empty slots are bare numbers with ghost guns, so the row has no rhythm. Amber here also collides with the P1 colour rule and lime is the 'selected' colour. The ammo counts sit right on the icons.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 as 72x72 --ui-panel tiles with a 1px --ui-line border, 4px radius, 8px gaps and 16px tx-2 numbers inside the top-left. Selected slot: 2px --acc border. Move ammo counts to a 16px label in the bottom-right corner of each tile.

findings.where: bottom-left: status chips 'concealed', 'in cover' and the two icon discs
findings.what: The chips use different styles: 'concealed' is amber text on black, 'in cover' is green text on dark teal, and the discs are 32px circles with a different outline weight. They are small (about 18px type) and cramped against the screen edge, and they sit 4px above the hp bar.
findings.fix: One chip style: 32px tall, --ui-panel fill, 16px f-cond in tx-1, a 3px left bar in a status colour (--warn, --ok), 4px radius. Put the icon inside the chip at 16px and drop the separate discs. Leave 16px between the chip row and the hp bar.

findings.where: bottom-centre, above the hotbar: 'contract item nearby · gold glow marks the box' toast
findings.what: It is an explaining sentence, which the brief calls clutter. It is a long amber-edged bar that sits almost against the controls card, 12px away, and adds a third amber treatment.
findings.fix: Shorten it to 'contract item nearby' at 20px. Centre it at the top of the left feed, not at mid-bottom, with 24px clear of other panels, on --ui-panel with a 3px --warn left bar.

findings.where: bottom-right: ammo card 'scav pistol 12 / 24' and 'b / i backpack'
findings.what: The 56px hero is right, but the card is 12px from the corner, with weapon name and hint in different small sizes. The 'b / i backpack' hint is about 12px, below the 14px floor.
findings.fix: Inset the card 48px from the right and 32px from the bottom, set the weapon name at 16px tx-2, the hero at 56px 800, and raise the hint to 14px tx-2 with 16px padding.

v.verdict: A functional but raw form dump: a card with a close X, then a stack of identical outlined boxes with no primary action, small low-contrast text, and a huge empty lower half.

findings.what: A 1190-character raw code in a blue browser-selection highlight, clipped at the top edge, is the largest and loudest thing on screen. The blue is off-palette and the clipped line looks broken. It shows an implementation detail the player never needs to read.
findings.fix: Hide the code. Show a single 'copy invite code' primary button (lime fill, 20px f-cond, 48px high) with a short 'copied' confirmation. If the code must be visible, use a 2-line field in --ui-raised with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, no selection highlight, and an ellipsis in the middle.

findings.what: There is no hierarchy and no primary action. 'copy by hand', 'let them in', 'new invite code', 'end the party' and 'mute' are all the same small outlined buttons, and 'end the party' (destructive) looks identical to the safe ones. Nothing is lime, and the title is a modest 32px.
findings.fix: Make 'let them in' the only lime-filled button (--acc, ink #11150a, 20px, 44px high). Make 'copy' and 'new invite code' secondary outlined buttons. Make 'end the party' a danger-red outline (--danger) and move it to the bottom right. Use a consistent 16px gap between buttons.

findings.what: There are explaining sentences ('up to four pillagers, one invite code.', 'turn on mic to use voice chat.', 'paste the reply code your friend sends back, it starts PTY1a.'). 'copy by hand' appears twice, as a heading and as a button. Text is about 14-15px in dim grey (below the 16px floor and below 4.5:1). The placeholder text is nearly invisible. The roster reads 'online host chec host you', which is broken. Also, 'PTY1a' has a capital letter, 'PTY1a' and the pasted code are exempt only as typed content, but the placeholder is not.
findings.fix: Delete the 'up to four' and 'turn on mic' sentences. Delete the stray 'copy by hand' heading. Shorten the paste hint to 'paste reply code' at 16px in --tx-2 or lighter. Fix the roster string to 'chec (host, you)'. Make every read text at least 16px.

findings.what: Rows are plain text with numbering ('1.', '2.'). There is no avatar, no P1 amber or P2 cyan identity swatch, and the divider lines are faint. 'mute' sits inside as a tiny button. The block is cramped, with only about 8px of padding.
findings.fix: Use 56px rows with a 4px player-colour bar at the left (amber P1, cyan P2), the name at 20px f-cond 600, and a 'host' tag at 16px --tx-2. Put 'mute' as a 16px ghost button at the right with 16px padding. Use 1px --ui-line row dividers.

findings.what: The content fills only the left 60% and the top 70% of the card. The right 40% and the bottom 30% are dead black. The controls hug the left edge, the mic row floats above the roster, and the section order is unclear (mic, roster, invite, reply, actions).
findings.fix: Use two columns inside the card. Left: roster and mic. Right: invite code and reply code steps. Put the actions in a 72px footer row. Space the sections 24-32px apart and give them labels ('invite', 'reply') at 16px.

findings.what: It is lime and letter-spaced, which breaks the rule that lime means selected or the main action. It is also the only coloured text, and the character count adds noise.
findings.fix: Set the label in --tx-2 at 16px with .04em tracking. Drop the character count.

findings.what: The toast overlaps the card's bottom border at y≈1024, so it is half in and half out of the frame. It is a boxed pill with no accent, and it does not match any other panel.
findings.fix: Anchor the toast 24px above the card bottom, inside the card or fully below it. Give it a 3px --ok left bar and a 4px radius.

findings.what: The X box is oversized (48px) and thin-lined, with a white stroke that is heavier than the title. No pad focus ring is visible on any button, only on the textarea.
findings.fix: Use a 40px X in --tx-2 with a 2px --acc focus outline. Show a 2px lime outline and an --ui-raised fill on the focused button.

v.verdict: The raid HUD carries a lot of working information, but nothing leads the eye: the controls panel is a washed-out ghost, the player list is a heavy slab, and several elements clip, overlap or break the style rules.

findings.what: The panel is faded to about 40% opacity on a busy map. The grey text is below the 4.5:1 floor, and the panel merges with the terrain. The rows 'item wheel', 'space' and 'ctrl / c' are cut off by the column edges. It also sits mid-left and high, not mid-bottom-left folded to one short line as the settled order says. The open list is a large block of text, which is clutter.
findings.fix: Fold it to one 16px line at bottom-left, centred around x≈200, with an 'f1 controls' hint. When open, use the opaque --ui-panel fill, --tx-2 text at full opacity, a 160px key column with a 24px gap, and no clipped labels.

findings.what: This is the heaviest block on screen. It has eight rows of 16px text with a $ column, in a dark slab with a square border. It competes with the timer and the player's own state. Names are packed at about 18px line pitch and the right-aligned $ values look dense. The one violet name (fbi_surveillance_van) has no stated meaning. The header 'value at risk' is small and low contrast.
findings.fix: Collapse to the top 3 plus 'you' by default, with the rest behind the chevron. Use a 24px row pitch and 8px padding, --tx-1 for the player's row and --tx-2 for the others. Drop the violet name unless it means a party member (P2 cyan, P1 amber).

findings.what: 'hp 100' at about 32px sits inside a saturated green bar with dark text. It reads as the loudest element but is not the hero. The bar touches the screen edge with about 20px margin, short of the 5% margin rule. The green is off-palette and looks like a default health bar. 'hp' is lower case but the numeral is as big as a title.
findings.fix: Set the margin to 48px. Reduce the bar to 14px height with a 56px hero number only for ammo. Use --ok #76b97c with a --ui-line track, with 'hp' at 16px and the 100 at 20px.

findings.what: The card is the strongest hero element (27 / 100), which is right. But it is clipped by the screen edge on the right, and it sits at a different inset from the hp bar. 'b / i backpack' at 14px is hard to read. The weapon slot row (1–0) floats mid-bottom with faint ghost icons and numbers at 14px that are near-invisible.
findings.fix: Inset the card 48px from the right and bottom, matching the hp bar. Make the key hint 16px --tx-2. Dim unused hotbar slots to a flat 1px --ui-line outline, not floating ghost icons. Align the hotbar baseline with the hp bar.

findings.what: The minimap is a black rectangle with a heavy chevron button and no border. It butts against the top and right edges with no margin. The 'run info' dropdown is a separate bar that is clipped at the right edge, and its text is tiny. Overall the corner does not match the left panel's style.
findings.fix: Inset the corner 48px. Give the minimap a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Use the same panel header style as 'current pillagers': 16px f-cond, 32px row, chevron in the same position.

findings.what: The timer is large white text over the map with no panel, so contrast varies with the terrain. The sunrise icon in the circle is a different style from the rest. The extract pill is a rounded teal-outline shape that does not match the 4px-radius panels used elsewhere. The little teal arrow below it is easy to miss.
findings.fix: Place the timer in a --ui-panel plate (56px hero, f-cond 800). Make the extract pill 4px radius with --extract text on --ui-panel at 20px. Put the direction arrow inline at 20px inside the pill.

findings.where: world labels around the player (online guest che, crawler a-39, sentry r-46, 'online guest che · 41m')
findings.what: Four name labels overlap each other and the player sprite. The crawler label is cut by the 'online guest che' tag, and two labels for the same player appear almost on top of each other. Label text is about 12–13px, below the 16px minimum. The map marker (white diamond) sits on top of a second label.
findings.fix: Show one label per entity at 16px with a 4px radius --ui-panel plate. Drop the duplicate 'online guest che' tag above the player, and keep the distance label only for off-screen or far players. Stack labels with an 8px gap.

findings.where: 'online guest che' bar, left under the list
findings.what: The nameplate bar for the local guest (blue name text, green bar) is a third style of panel, different from both the list above and the hp bar below. The blue name does not match P1 amber or P2 cyan. It also duplicates the world label.
findings.fix: Remove it or merge it into the list as the 'you' row. If kept, use the P2 cyan #47d8c6 name at 16px and the same panel fill as the list.

v.verdict: The raid HUD has a strong ammo hero and a clear hotbar, but the left side is overloaded: a roster, a nameplate, and a faded controls list stack up and overlap the action.

findings.what: The controls panel is a big translucent block with about 25 faint rows. The brief says it should be folded to one short line at mid-bottom left. It overlaps the player and the sentries, and it sits on the busiest part of the map. The grey text on the busy floor is low contrast and the columns are cramped. The 'move' text collides with the 'wasd' column.
findings.fix: Fold it to a single 16px line at bottom-left, about y=1000 above the hp bar, reading 'f1 controls'. Open it on F1 only, on a solid --ui-panel fill (#16191b at 90%), with text in --tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better.

findings.what: A permanent 8-row money table with names in 3 colours (white, purple, white) is always on screen. It competes with the player's own status and the minimap. The caret and the 'value at risk' header add clutter. The names are about 14px and the figures are tight, so the rows are cramped. It also covers part of the map and the 'crawler' ghost text.
findings.fix: Collapse it by default to one 20px row, such as 'pillagers 7'. Expand it on a hold key. If it stays, use 16px text, a 32px row pitch, a 1px --ui-line divider, and a solid --ui-panel fill. Keep names in --tx-1 and use one colour for the player's own row.

findings.what: The hp label is about 32px tall and hugs the bar's top-left. It is a mixed type size on a flat green bar. The bar is stretched into a long 400px slab, and its left edge hits the screen margin at 24px instead of 5%. It is less polished than the ammo block in the opposite corner, which uses a card, 56px hero numerals and a clear hierarchy.
findings.fix: Put hp in a card matching the ammo card (--ui-panel, 4px radius, 1px --ui-line-hi border). Use a 56px --fs-hero number with a 16px 'hp' label. Keep the bar at about 240px, 8px tall.

findings.what: The two feed lines have different treatments. The first has an amber bar, an icon and a '·' separator, and the second a grey bar. Their widths differ and they overlap the wall edge. The amber and white text weights are mixed, and the first line is two clauses long. Both also sit directly above the controls list, so the lower-left corner is crowded.
findings.fix: Use one row template: 3px bar, 16px text, 32px height, 8px gap, solid --ui-panel fill. Keep to one clause, for example 'contract item nearby'. Move the feed above the hp card at the left margin, clear of the controls line.

findings.what: The toast is a square-cornered black box with no accent bar, border or icon. It does not match the feed lines or the extract chip, and it floats at bottom-centre where the aim is, with no relation to the hotbar. It looks like a different panel language.
findings.fix: Use the feed row template at 4px radius with a 3px --ok bar. Or put it in the top-centre banner slot with the same chip style as 'extract 132m'.

findings.what: The empty slots 3-0 are bare numerals with ghost weapon silhouettes at about 8% opacity. They are below readable contrast and look like leftover debris on the map. The two filled slots are clean, but the row has no shared rail or panel.
findings.fix: Draw empty slots as 56px 4px-radius tiles with a 1px --ui-line border and a --tx-2 label at 16px. Align the gaps to 8px.

findings.what: The minimap is a hard black rectangle with no border, so it floats on the map. The 'run info' bar below it has a different background and chevron styling from the roster header. Its right edge is clipped to the screen edge at the map and has no 5% margin. The tiny icons are about 10px and unreadable.
findings.fix: Add a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Move it to 48px from the right and top edges. Make the 'run info' header the same height and fill as the roster header, with 16px text. Scale icons up to at least 14px.

findings.where: top-centre clock and extract chip (x903-1030, y10-75)
findings.what: The clock is white 9:00 at about 28px, with a small orange sun icon. The teal 'extract 132m' chip has a sharp square corner, small text and a tiny arrow. This is a good extract-only teal use, but the clock and the chip are different sizes and the chip is tight to its text. The 'packing floor' ghost label also fights with the roster.
findings.fix: Set the chip at 16px with 8px by 16px padding and a 4px radius. Make the clock 32px --fs-title. Fade 'packing floor' to a 2-second zone-entry toast.

v.verdict: This is a different screen from the earlier raid HUD review: it is the hub with a join-in-progress banner, and it is cluttered. Two competing top-centre banners, an orange warning label and mixed type sizes mean nothing leads the eye to one action.

findings.where: top-centre 'join the raid in progress' banner and 'enter raid!' button
findings.what: Two stacked CTAs fight each other: an amber filled banner and a lime 56px+ 'enter raid!' with an exclamation mark, overlapping the stash doorway. The banner's sub-line 'or go up at enter raid!' is an explaining sentence at about 10px. Amber is the warn colour, not the primary action, and sits beside the lime, which the guide forbids.
findings.fix: Merge them into one lime --acc plate. Primary line 'enter raid' at 32px f-cond 700, no '!'. Secondary 'raid in progress' at 16px --tx-2 beneath it, inside the same 1px --ui-line-hi panel. Delete the 'or go up at...' sentence and the amber fill.

findings.where: 'the last pour' station, 'experimental feature may glitch' label
findings.what: The label is amber text with asterisks on a dark chip at about 14px, overlapping the station and character. It is a disclaimer shown as clutter, and the *** decoration is template noise.
findings.fix: Remove the asterisks. Use a 16px --warn 'experimental' tag, 8px padding, inside the station label chip. Move the full warning into the station's own window.

findings.where: top-right money row: '$900  147 xp  stash $610 bag $0'
findings.what: Four items in three sizes and weights, running to x=1900 with about 20px of margin against a 48px guide. '147' is bigger than 'xp', and the 'stash/bag' group is about 14px and illegible from a couch. The right black bar behind it also makes the corner look unfinished.
findings.fix: Inset 48px. Use one 20px f-cond 600 row in --tx-1 with 16px --tx-2 labels, 24px gaps, and a 1px --ui-line divider. Drop 'xp' to a 16px label. Put the hero size only on the '$' figure if anything.

findings.what: All nine slots are shown. The unused guns are ghosted at about 15% opacity and read as floating icons, and the slot numbers are about 12px. The selected slot is gold-outlined while slot 3 has a purple fill and a lime bar, so selection is shown in three ways.
findings.fix: Show only the equipped slots. Dim the rest to a flat 1px --ui-line outline with no icon. Mark selection only with a 2px --acc border. Slot numbers 16px --tx-2. Inset the bar 48px from the bottom.

findings.where: station labels (wirt the gambler, the mainframe, shop craft and hire, settings, the stash, fashion)
findings.what: Each is a different-width dark chip with about 18px text and no icon or hierarchy. They are scattered at inconsistent offsets from their pads, and 'the stash' and 'fashion' collide with characters. The big translucent glow circles overlap and muddy the floor, and the mainframe has a stray second circle.
findings.fix: Use one chip style: 20px f-cond 600, 8px/16px padding, 4px radius, 1px --ui-line-hi border, anchored 16px above each pad. Reduce the pad circles to a 1px ring at 30% alpha. Delete the stray orange circle by the mainframe. Keep chips clear of NPC heads.

findings.what: The title is about 28px with a 14px 'items in stash · 1 run' subline. It is the strongest type on screen but sits 80px from the edge, off the 48px grid, and the subline is too small and low-contrast. It competes with the CTA.
findings.fix: Inset 48px. Title 32px --tx-1. Subline 16px --tx-2. Use a --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Tone the title down so 'enter raid' stays the first thing the eye hits.

findings.where: whole frame, left and right black bars
findings.what: The room does not fill the 16:9 frame, leaving 160px dead black columns and a pale wall rim. The HUD sits half on the room and half on the void, which looks like a letterbox error.
findings.fix: Extend the floor and walls to the full 1920 width, or tint the pillars to --ui-void with a 1px --ui-line edge. Anchor all HUD to the 48px screen margin, not to the room.

findings.what: A tiny cyan ring with a '2' at about 10px is the only sign of which character is the local guest. Cyan is correct for P2, but the badge is unreadable at 1080 from a couch.
findings.fix: Make the badge 20px with a --ui-void fill and a --extract-free P2 cyan ring. Add a 16px 'you' label above the character.

v.verdict: The feed lines and the join toast are gone, but the full controls list is still open at the left, the roster is still a table, and hp is still a bare bar, so the screen is still crowded and has no clear first read.

findings.what: The earlier advice was not followed. The list is fully open, with about 25 key chips in 3 columns. The raid-controls order says it starts folded to one short line, mid-bottom left, and F1 opens it. It is the largest panel on screen and pulls the eye away from the player. The 'f1 full list' footer admits it is a partial list.
findings.fix: Fold it to one 16px line 'f1 controls' at x=24, y=~1000, in --tx-2. Open it only on F1, as a 90% --ui-panel card with a 4px radius and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Chip text is 16px, with a 32px row pitch.

findings.what: A 9-row table is always on, with names and dollar values at about 14px and an 18px row pitch. That is below the 16px floor and it is dense. It sits flush against the screen edge at x=8, not on the 5% margin. The header carries two labels and a chevron.
findings.fix: Default it to a single 20px row, 'pillagers 7', with the chevron. When open, use 16px text, a 32px row pitch, 1px --ui-line dividers, and your own row in --acc. Move the left edge to x=48 and use a solid --ui-panel fill.

findings.what: The hp bar is a bare green bar with an oversized 'hp 100' label drawn over it. It has no card, so it matches neither the ammo card at bottom right nor the hotbar. It sits 12px from the bottom edge. The label crowds the bar and is hard to read over green.
findings.fix: Put it in a --ui-panel card with a 4px radius and a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 48px from the left and 32px from the bottom. Inside the card put a 16px 'hp' label, a 56px --fs-hero number in --tx-1, and an 8px bar about 240px wide in --ok.

findings.where: top-centre timer, chip and arrow (x900-1030, y10-90)
findings.what: The 8:52 timer has no panel and sits on the busy map. The menu icon is a loose circle beside it. The teal 'extract 135m' chip is good, but the arrow beneath it is tiny and floats. The cluster looks unfinished next to the heavier ammo card.
findings.fix: Put the timer in a --ui-panel plate at 32px --fs-title with 8px of padding. Align the menu icon to the plate's right edge. Make the extract chip 16px, and attach the arrow to the chip's bottom edge, 24px tall, in --extract.

findings.what: The map sits at the very screen edge, 18px from the top and 18px from the right, which is off the 5% margin. The chevron controls are cramped into the corners. 'run info' reads as a dropdown with no content or purpose. The map frame has no border and a different edge treatment from the other panels.
findings.fix: Inset it to 48px from the top and right, and add a 1px --ui-line-hi border with a 4px radius on the same --ui-panel as the other cards. Make the run info row 32px high with 16px text and 8px padding, and put the collapse chevron at 24px.

findings.what: The slot numbers 3 to 0 float as bare grey digits with no slot frames. They are dim (about 3:1 over the map). The two filled slots are heavier than the rest, and the 'f' chip in slot 2 is tiny.
findings.fix: Draw empty slots 56px square in --ui-panel at 60% with a 1px --ui-line border and put the digits inside at 16px in --tx-2. Raise the 'f' chip to 16px.

findings.what: The ammo card is the best-built panel. Its 12 / 24 numbers are the right hero scale. But its right edge sits 10px from the screen edge, and 'b / i backpack' at about 14px is dim.
findings.fix: Move the card's right edge to x=1872 (48px margin) and its bottom edge to y=1048. Set the hint text to 16px in --tx-2. Keep the 56px hero number.

findings.what: The roster and controls use near-black fills with a thin border and 4px radius. The ammo card and minimap use different fills and edge weights. Six panels use four different borders and paddings, so the HUD reads as separate pieces rather than a system.
findings.fix: Use one panel class everywhere: --ui-panel at 90%, a 1px --ui-line-hi border, a 4px radius, and 16px padding.

v.verdict: The capture is an almost empty dark void with only a small top-right money row, so the reticle and bullets under review are not visible and the shot is unusable as evidence.

findings.what: There is no world, player, reticle or bullets. The frame is flat #0b0c0d, so the reticle-through-bullets recipe cannot be judged. The capture was probably taken before the scene rendered, or the canvas failed.
findings.fix: Re-capture after the raid scene has rendered, at least 1s after the first frame. Assert that the player sprite and reticle pixels exist before saving the shot.

findings.what: It is a horizontal row of three mixed items ('$900', '0 xp', 'stash $0 bag $2,370') at three different sizes. The guide's career HUD is a vertical 1x1 list with every item the same size (cw-trcol).
findings.fix: Stack the items vertically at 16px f-cond 600 with an 8px gap, right-aligned at 5% margin (x=1824). Use one size for all items. Keep a 20px value size only if '$' is meant to be the hero.

findings.what: It is about 14px muted grey and runs together as one string, which is under the 16px floor for anything read. The bag value is the useful number and it has no emphasis.
findings.fix: Split it into two lines, 'stash $0' and 'bag $2,370'. Use 16px at tx-1 for the values and tx-2 for the labels. Add a 24px gap.

findings.what: The unit 'xp' is smaller and detached from its number, and the baselines differ. The gaps between the three groups are uneven (about 24px against 30px), so the row looks accidental.
findings.fix: Put the number and unit on one shared baseline with a 4px gap, and use the 8px grid (16 or 24px) between groups.

findings.what: The text sits about 20px from the right edge and 28px from the top, not at the 5% safe margin. It has no panel or shadow, so it will lose contrast over bright terrain.
findings.fix: Inset to 96px right and 54px top. Add a --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.6) plate with a 4px radius and 8px padding, or a 1px dark text shadow.

v.verdict: The screenshot is an almost empty dark frame with a small 'keyboard' chip and a tiny money line top-right, so there is no game, no reticle and no HUD to judge, and it looks like a broken or unrendered capture.

findings.what: The frame is a flat #0b0c0d void with no map, players, bullets or reticle. The filename promises a player 2 reticle test, but nothing in the image shows it. The scene did not render, or the capture was taken too early.
findings.fix: Re-capture after the raid scene has drawn at least 2 s of frames. The shot must show P2's reticle, its bullets and the arena. Fail the capture if the canvas is blank.

findings.what: The chip is the only thing on the left of the screen. It is a small green-outlined pill with ~16px bold text in a green that is not --acc lime, not P2 cyan and not --ok, and it sits only about 10px from the screen edge. It is a debug-looking label with no purpose or hierarchy.
findings.fix: If it stays, use an 8px grid: 48px margin (5% of the screen), --fs-label 16px f-cond 600, --tx-2 text, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius. Tint it P2 cyan only if it names P2's device. Otherwise remove it from the raid HUD.

findings.where: top-right money cluster (1630 to 1900, y 18 to 40)
findings.what: Three items sit at different sizes and weights with uneven gaps: '$900' is bold ~24px, '0' is ~22px, 'xp' is ~13px and 'stash $0 bag $2,370' is ~14px. The style guide wants a vertical 1 by 1 list with every item the same size (cw-trcol), and this is still a horizontal row. The '0' has no label until the 'xp' beside it. The 14px tx-2 text is below the 16px floor for anything read. The block hugs the edge with a margin of about 20px.
findings.fix: Build the cw-trcol column: right-aligned at 48px from the edge, one line per item, all 20px f-cond 600 with 8px row gaps. Show '$900', '0 xp' and 'stash $0', each with its --fs-label 16px label. Put 'bag $2,370' on its own line. Use --tx-1 for the values and --tx-2 for the labels.

findings.what: The brightest and heaviest thing on screen is '$900', so the eye lands on money rather than on the reticle, ammo, health or a timer. None of the usual raid HUD is visible: no health, ammo or extract status, and no party line. The player-2 state is not shown.
findings.fix: Check that the HUD layers really drew. The hero element (ammo, or the extract timer at 56px f-cond 800) should be the strongest thing. Money should drop to 20px tx-1.

findings.where: outer frame (1px border at the screen edge)
findings.what: A faint 1px lighter border runs round the whole frame. It looks like a stray canvas or stage outline, not a designed element, and it clips against the screenshot edge.
findings.fix: Remove the stage border, or hide it in captures. If a frame is wanted, give it a deliberate 1px --ui-line with no glow.

v.verdict: The raid scene now renders with a reticle, a clear ammo hero and a hotbar, but the HUD is crowded, the left panels are dense and the top-right is covered by a minimap panel with a stray capital.

findings.what: There is a capital 'I' in 'run Info', which breaks the all-lower-case rule. The bar is also a second collapsed header stacked under the minimap and says nothing useful.
findings.fix: Change the string to 'run info'. Make the bar the same 16px f-cond 600 as the other labels, with an 8px gap under the minimap, or fold it into the minimap header.

findings.where: left column: 'current pillagers' list, 'player 2' bar and the controls card
findings.what: Three dense panels stack down the left side, each with a different width and padding, and the 14px text is dim. The scoreboard lists 8 rows of tx-2 text next to full-width dollar values. 'dead' repeats on every row. This is clutter during play.
findings.fix: Show only the player's own row plus the top 3 by default, and mark the dead rows with a single glyph. Match the panel widths at 360px with 16px padding and 4px radius. Raise the row text to 16px.

findings.what: It is an always-open two-column cheat sheet of about 20 key rows, which covers a large part of the playfield. The spec says it should sit mid-bottom left and be folded to one short line until F1 opens it. The key caps are tiny and the text is 14-16px.
findings.fix: Collapse it to one line 'f1 controls' at 16px, 24px above the hotbar and left aligned at x=96. Open the full list only on F1.

findings.what: The 'hp 100' text sits at about 32px in dark text on a flat green bar. It crowds the bar edge and is a different size from every other label. It is also far larger than the ammo label next to it, which makes two competing heroes.
findings.fix: Set the hp bar to 320x24px with 'hp' at 16px f-cond 600 and the value at 20px on the bar's right side, inset 16px. Keep the 56px hero for ammo only.

findings.what: The minimap has a hard white band across it and a black empty area below, so it looks clipped or broken. It is much taller than it needs to be and the chevron button is tiny.
findings.fix: Crop the map to a 4:3 frame (about 300x225px), fill it fully, and use a 1px --ui-line-hi border with a 4px radius. Use an 8px inner margin.

findings.what: The 'player 2' bar at left has a dark box with a thin hp line that overlaps the world, and the 'a 117m' marker has an unlabelled 'a'. Both read as debug leftovers.
findings.fix: Replace 'a' with a clear glyph or the name, use 16px text in the same pill style as 'extract 117m', and align the P2 bar to the hp bar's left margin.

findings.what: The numerals sit loose on the ground strip with low contrast against the grey road, so they read as noise. The selected slot's amber border uses P1's colour, which clashes with the lime-as-selected rule.
findings.fix: Draw empty slots as 48px tiles with a 1px --ui-line fill and tx-2 numerals at 16px. Use --acc for the selected border.

findings.what: The timer at about 30px bold, a sun icon in a circle and the teal extract pill are three separately styled items that crowd one another. The pill nearly touches the timer.
findings.fix: Put the timer at 32px f-cond 700 with the icon removed or at 24px. Leave 8px between the timer and the pill, and use the same 4px radius.

v.verdict: The raid scene now renders and reads as a game, but the HUD is crowded, the controls panel is big and always open, and there is no reticle focus. The player's sprite is small and sits in a busy scene, with several competing hot spots and a lot of small text.

findings.what: The keys list is fully open and carries about 20 rows plus two group labels. It is nearly as big as the player list above it, so it competes with the action. The style guide says it should be folded to one short line at mid-bottom left, with F1 to open it.
findings.fix: Fold it to a single 16px line 'f1 controls' at x=48, y=1000. Open it only on F1, and cap the open height at 360px.

findings.where: hero ammo card and hp bar (bottom)
findings.what: The '30 / 60' ammo number is the only hero element, which is fine. The hp bar at bottom-left uses a different, flat, loud green fill and a larger 'hp 100' label, and it has no panel. It does not match the ammo card's dark panel, border or radius.
findings.fix: Put hp in a matching panel (fill #16191b, 1px #4a5257 border, 4px radius). Use a 20px 'hp' label at tx-2, a 32px value at tx-1, and a 12px bar in --ok.

findings.where: top-left player list and 'player 2' tag (16,143 to 367,333)
findings.what: There are 10 rows at about 14px, with muted grey text on dark and 'dead' repeated on every row. The mixed pink/purple highlight on 'fbi_surveillance_van' is off-palette. The header shows 'current pillagers 0' with an unclear count. The text is below the 16px floor, and there is a lot of noise.
findings.fix: Raise the rows to 16px. Show 'dead' once as a column header or drop it. Replace the purple with tx-1 or --acc for 'you'. Collapse the list to the top 3 rows plus 'n more'. Move the 'player 2' tag to an 8px gap below the panel.

findings.what: Slots 4 to 0 are drawn as bare faint numerals with no frame, so they look like stray debris. The slot sizes are inconsistent. The selected slot has a gold border, which clashes with the lime accent rule. The slots 1 and 3 icons are tiny.
findings.fix: Draw all 10 slots as 72px tiles with an 8px gap and a 1px --ui-line-hi border, or show only filled slots. Use a 3px --acc border for the selected slot. Raise the weapon icons to 48px.

findings.what: 'run Info' has a capital I, which breaks the all-lower-case rule. The minimap carries a heavy black void in its lower half and a white band across it. The collapse chevrons are tiny.
findings.fix: Change the text to 'run info'. Fit the minimap to the map bounds so the black area goes. Put a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius on both elements.

findings.what: The text 'contract item nearby · gold glow marks the box' is an explaining sentence. The gold bar and gold text collide with the reticle ring and the enemy name tag 'permanentlytilted', which clips under it.
findings.fix: Shorten it to 'contract item nearby'. Move it up to y=700 or to top-centre so it clears the enemy tag, and use 20px tx-1 on the panel.

findings.what: '9:00' is good, but the teal 'extract 117m' chip and the separate cyan arrow chip 'a 117m' at the left show the same distance twice. The 'a' label is meaningless.
findings.fix: Keep only the top-centre chip. Remove 'a 117m', or make the edge arrow carry just the arrow with no text. Use 16px type.

findings.what: My earlier advice was a vertical 1 by 1 list with the stash and bag values. None of it is visible, because the minimap now fills that corner. This capture does not show the career readout, so I cannot judge whether it was followed.
findings.fix: Place the stash and bag readouts in a vertical list under the 'run info' bar. Use 16px type and an 8px gap, right-aligned at x=1824.

v.verdict: The raid now draws, with a readable ammo block and hotbar, but the left side is a stack of competing panels, the controls list is open and hogging the left edge, capitals show on screen, and the fonts and margins are inconsistent.

findings.where: left column: controls panel (16,455 to 327,800) plus the value-at-risk panel (16,143 to 367,333)
findings.what: The controls list is fully open, about 310x345px, and covers the play area. The order says it should start folded to one short line, mid-bottom left, and open on F1. The 'full list' hint and the panel's size make the left edge heavy, and the two panels have different widths (311 and 351px). They also compete with the player hp bar, so there are three stacked boxes with no shared left edge or column grid.
findings.fix: Fold the controls to a single 16px line, 'f1 controls', at x=48 and y=1080-48-hotbar-aligned. Open it only on F1. Set the leaderboard and any other left panels to the same 320px width and the same 48px left margin, with 8px gaps between panels.

findings.where: text with capitals: 'current pillagers 0' reads '0 out · 7 dead' but the value-at-risk header, 'run Info' (1610,341), the '$' amounts and the 'fbi_surveillance_van' rows are mixed; 'run Info' and 'player I' show a capital I
findings.what: 'run Info' has a capital I. 'player 1' on the hp card and the in-world label appear to use a capital-I glyph. The owner ordered all lower case, so any capital is a defect.
findings.fix: Lower-case 'run info'. Render the digit 1 in 'player 1' with a clear numeral. Check the font fallback so that 'l', 'I' and '1' are distinguishable, and make sure no capital is drawn.

findings.where: top-right: minimap (1603,18 to 1901,318) and the 'run info' bar (1603,327 to 1901,362)
findings.what: The minimap is a large flat black box that is half empty below y=235 (a blank band under a white stripe). It reads as unfinished. The right margin is about 19px, not 48px. The 'run info' dropdown is a separate chrome bar with no fill logic shared with the other panels. The cw-trcol money list is missing, so the career HUD top-right is not built.
findings.fix: Use a 48px margin. Crop the minimap to the actual map area, or fill the empty region with the map. Give the run info bar the same 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius and --ui-panel fill as the other panels, and put the money list in a 1 by 1 column below it.

findings.what: The hero is split. The timer '8:59' (about 28px) is small, and the ammo '30' at about 56px is the only large element. The top centre has a timer, an 'extract 117m' chip and a sunrise icon stacked into a cluttered cluster. The teal chip uses --extract correctly, but the cyan 'a 117m' waypoint label duplicates the extract distance, which breaks the one-place-per-line rule.
findings.fix: Keep one hero: the ammo at 56px f-cond 800. Make the timer 32px --fs-title. Drop the duplicate 'a 117m' world label, or the top-centre chip. Keep the extract distance in exactly one place.

findings.what: Slot 1, 2 and 3 are lit while 4 to 0 are bare numerals floating on the road with no tile, so the row looks half drawn. The hp bar is a solid flat green block with oversized 'hp 100' text (about 34px) that is louder than the title scale. It sits at a 24px margin, not 48px, and the baselines don't line up with the hotbar or the ammo card (bottom edges 1058, 1068 and 1052).
findings.fix: Draw all ten slots as 4px-radius tiles, with the empty ones at 40 percent opacity. Cut 'hp 100' to 20px f-cond 600 inside a 12px-tall bar. Share one bottom edge at y=1032 (48px from the bottom) across the hp bar, hotbar and ammo card.

findings.what: This is still the chip I flagged before and it has not been fixed. It uses a green border and green tint at a 10px margin, off the 8px grid and off the P1 amber and P2 cyan rule. It sits above the 'current pillagers' panel, so it reads as debug output.
findings.fix: Remove it from the raid HUD, or move it to 48px,48px at 16px f-cond 600 in --tx-2 with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius, tinted for the player (P2 cyan).

findings.what: There are nine rows at about 14 to 15px with dense 18px line spacing. The dead values are muted grey on a dark panel, near the 4.5:1 floor, and the same panel carries the title, a 'value at risk' column header, a collapse chevron and a footer line. For a couch distance at 1080p this is too small, and it adds clutter.
findings.fix: Raise the rows to 16px f-cond 600 with 24px row height. Show the top 5 rows plus 'you'. Put 'dead' in the --danger colour and the amounts in --tx-1. Drop the footer, or fold it into the header.

findings.what: A pale 1px border still rings the whole frame, and my earlier advice to remove it or make it deliberate was not followed. It shows as a stray line at the top and right edges.
findings.fix: Remove the stage border, or hide it in captures. If a frame is wanted, use 1px --ui-line with no glow.

v.verdict: The raid now draws and reads as a real HUD with a clear ammo hero and extract timer, but the left side is crowded by two big panels, and there are capitals and inconsistent panel styling.

findings.where: left column: controls list (16,455 to 327,800) and current pillagers board (16,143 to 367,333)
findings.what: The controls list is fully open and as large as a settings card, with 8 to 9 sections and a key-chip grid. It crowds the left third of the arena beside the pillagers board. The owner's order (rs-1) says it sits mid-bottom left, folded to one short line, and opens on F1. The two panels are also different widths (311 vs 351) and neither has the same border or radius as the ammo card.
findings.fix: Fold the controls to one 16px line at x=48, y~1000 ('f1 controls'). Only open it on F1. Give the pillagers board and the ammo card the same 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius and --ui-panel fill at 80% alpha. Both get 48px margins.

findings.what: A capital 'I' appears in 'run Info', which breaks the all-lower-case rule. The caption is also 'player 1' on the HUD, a label that duplicates the nametag above the head. Elsewhere the in-world name tag reads 'player I', which is ambiguous in a condensed font.
findings.fix: Force 'run info' lower case. Remove the duplicate 'player 1' HUD tag, or fold it into the hp bar as '1 hp 100'.

findings.what: The chip sits at about 8px from the edge, outside the 48px margin and clipped into the frame. It is drawn in lime with a green border and mixes with the border of the stage. It does not name which player the device belongs to.
findings.fix: Move it to x=48, y=24. Use 16px f-cond 600 in --tx-2, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Tint it P1 amber if it stays, and drop it from the raid HUD otherwise.

findings.what: The hp bar is a flat bright green fill with oversized 'hp 100' text drawn directly on it, in a different style from the dark panel ammo card. It sits at 24px from the edge while the ammo card sits at 10px from the right, so the bottom corners do not mirror each other. The hp text also competes with the 56px ammo hero.
findings.fix: Put hp in a matching --ui-panel card (4px radius, 1px --ui-line-hi), 48px from the left and 48px from the bottom, mirroring the ammo card. Use a 12px --ok bar under a 32px '100' value with a 16px 'hp' label. Set the ammo card 48px from the right and bottom.

findings.what: Nine rows of 14px text in muted grey-blue sit on a translucent panel, with dead rows dimmed below 4.5:1. Names and '$x dead' values are tiny for a couch at 1080. The header 'value at risk' and the 'current pillagers 0' title are both small and weak.
findings.fix: Raise the rows to 16px minimum, --tx-2 on --ui-panel at 4.5:1 or better. Cap the list at 5 rows plus '+4 more'. Keep 'you $2,370' in 20px --tx-1.

findings.what: The minimap has a thick unbordered white strip, a bare black area in the lower half, and mixed-size glyphs. The collapsed 'run info' bar has a different border and font weight from every other panel.
findings.fix: Crop the minimap to the drawn area. Give the minimap and run info bar the same 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Align both to 48px from the right and 24px from the top.

findings.where: top-centre timer and extract chip (880 to 1040, 10 to 75)
findings.what: The 8:59 timer is about 30px, not the 56px hero, so the top of the screen is weak. The teal extract chip is fine, but the 'a 117m' pointer label at (455,141) is a third style of label.
findings.fix: Set the timer to 56px f-cond 800 --tx-1, with the extract chip below it at 16px. Draw the arrow label 'a 117m' in the same 16px chip style as 'extract 117m'.

findings.what: The slot numbers 4 to 0 float as bare grey digits with faint ghost icons under them, and the selected slot has an amber border, a fourth accent. The selected state should be lime, and the numbers are too dim to read.
findings.fix: Draw empty slots as 1px --ui-line outlined 4px-radius cells, with 16px --tx-2 numbers. Make the selected slot border 2px --acc.

v.verdict: This frame has no HUD at all, only a bare gameplay crop with a debug caption, so the earlier advice (run info bar, left lists, controls card, hp bar, minimap) can't be judged, and what remains is rough: a hard grey/green terrain split, a sprite name tag with weak contrast, and a tiny reticle.

findings.what: No hud is visible: no hp bar, ammo, hotbar, minimap, controls hint or feed. The earlier fixes (hp bar 320x24, 'f1 controls' line, 4:3 minimap, 'run info') can't be confirmed. If the capture is cropped or the hud is hidden, it's the wrong shot for judging the hud.
findings.fix: Re-shoot at full 1920x1080 with the hud on, no letterbox. Put hp 320x24 bottom-left at x=96, ammo as the 56px hero bottom-right, and a one-line 'f1 controls' at 16px above the hotbar.

findings.what: The tag is large (about 40px text) and red on a dark plate with a blue left stub, so it competes with the character. The red text reads as a danger state, but red is the p1 name colour, which clashes with the 'P1 is amber' rule. The hp bar under it is a thin red-on-grey strip, and the plate runs off the sprite's left edge.
findings.fix: Cut the name to 16px f-cond 600 in tx-1 on a --ui-panel plate at 80% opacity with a 4px radius. Use a 3px amber (p1) side bar instead of blue, and make the hp bar 4px tall, green to red by value. Centre it 8px above the head.

findings.what: The tag is a pale-blue 36px name on a dark box with a green bar, and it sits at the edge of the foliage. It has a different size, colour and plate shape from the p1 tag, and it's cyan text where p1's is red text. The two tags look like two different systems.
findings.fix: Use one nameplate component for both: 16px f-cond 600 tx-1 text, a 3px side bar in the player colour (p1 amber, p2 cyan), a 4px radius, and a 64x4 hp bar. Same offset above the head.

findings.what: A hard horizontal edge at y=708 where the green ground turns into a flat translucent grey slab looks like an overlay or a fog layer failing. A tan rectangle at (650-845, 903-975) floats with no meaning. The 1590x890 crop has a black letterbox, so the framing looks like a debug capture.
findings.fix: Blend the grey region with a 64px feathered edge or make it real terrain with a tile border. Give the tan block a texture or remove it. Capture the full 1920x1080 frame.

findings.what: The dashed ring is 205px with a pale grey stroke at low contrast over the grass, and the yellow tracer dash in the centre makes the aim point ambiguous. The ring is bigger than the sprite.
findings.fix: Shrink the ring to about 96px, use a 2px --tx-1 stroke with a 1px dark outline, a 4px lime centre dot, and draw the tracer behind the reticle.

findings.what: A debug label in about 22px white text sits on the black bars. It's lower case, which is fine, but it's not part of the game UI and isn't in the type scale.
findings.fix: Strip it from the capture or set it at 14px --tx-2 so it doesn't read as a HUD title.

findings.what: The red '!' floats in a spot unrelated to any source and has no label or anchor, so it's unclear whether it's a threat or a warning. It also collides visually with the name plate below it.
findings.fix: Anchor it 8px above the nameplate, 24px tall, in --danger with a 2px dark outline, or send it to the top-centre alert banner as the guide requires.

v.verdict: This is a zoomed crop of the play field with no HUD in frame, so none of the earlier hp, hotbar, controls or minimap advice can be judged. The only UI visible, a hint banner that collides with the player's name tag, reticle and alert mark, looks careless.

findings.where: hint banner 'arby · gold glow marks the box' (164,596 to 855,675)
findings.what: The banner is cut off at the left edge, so the line reads 'arby'. It sits on the reticle and on the 'wallnackwally' name tag. Its 44px text is far larger than the 20px body size, so it is the loudest thing on screen over the fight. The line is also an explaining sentence.
findings.fix: Anchor the banner inside the safe area (left edge at x >= 96, top-centre or the left feed). Use 20px f-cond 600 text on a #16191b panel with a 1px #4a5257 border and 4px radius, 16px padding. Keep it to a 2-word label such as 'gold crate' and clear it from the reticle.

findings.where: name tag 'wallnackwally' and its red hp bar (278,670 to 532,725)
findings.what: The banner's lower edge covers the top of the name text, and the cyan/blue slab at x=256 is an orphan. The tag clips and loses legibility exactly where the player's own character is.
findings.fix: Put the name tag 8px above the head (y=735 or higher) at 16px tx-1 with a 2px dark outline. Draw the hp bar at 6px height, 120px wide, centred on the tag. Move the banner so there is a 16px gap above the tag.

findings.what: The mark is a loose red glyph that straddles the banner's top edge and the 'o' of 'glow'. It is not tied to the banner or to any source.
findings.fix: Put it inside the banner as a 20px --warn glyph, left-aligned with 8px padding, or delete it. Do not let it overlap text.

findings.what: The tag is 36px blue text on a translucent navy box with no border. It is larger than the player's own 28px name tag, and it uses a cyan that is neither exactly --extract nor a UI token. The hp bar is a thin 12px green strip, and the 6px gap to the tag is not on the 8px grid.
findings.fix: Use 16px f-cond 600 for both players' tags. Fill #16191b at 80% with a 1px #4a5257 border and 4px radius. Keep P2 cyan only for the text or ring. Make the hp bar 6px high and put it 8px below the tag.

findings.what: The 200px pale dashed ring is low contrast against the olive ground and the grey road. It also overlaps the banner, and the banner hides its lower-left arc.
findings.fix: Draw the ring at 96px, 2px stroke, in --tx-1 with a 1px #0b0c0d outline. Keep it above the banner layer, or move the banner away from it.

v.verdict: This is a zoomed crop of the play area with no HUD visible, so the earlier panel, minimap and hotbar advice can't be checked. What is visible is a hint banner clipped by the left edge that sits on top of the reticle and the player's name tag.

findings.what: The banner is cut off at the left edge ('arby') and covers the aim reticle, the red '!' marker and the 'croucnspammer' name tag. It also carries two sentences of explanation, which is clutter.
findings.fix: Keep the banner fully inside the frame with a 48px margin. Anchor it top-centre at y=48 and keep it at least 120px clear of the reticle and the player. Cut it to one short line of 20px f-cond 600 (for example 'find the box'). Give it a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius and --ui-panel fill.

findings.where: player name tags ('player 1' at 1440,150 to 1590,210; 'croucnspammer' at 237,670 to 552,712)
findings.what: The name tags have inconsistent styles. 'player 1' is blue text with a dark box and the digit 1 looks like a capital I. 'croucnspammer' is red with a different box and a blue stripe on the left. The P1 and P2 colours do not follow the amber and cyan rule. The tag overlaps the banner and sits very close to the character.
findings.fix: Use one tag style at 16px f-cond 600 with +.04em tracking on a --ui-panel fill at 80% opacity. Colour P1 amber and P2 cyan, and use tx-1 for everything else. Put the tag 12px above the head. Use a numeral-1 glyph that cannot be mistaken for 'I'.

findings.what: The thin grey dashed ring has low contrast against the grass and the grey ground. It is overlapped by the banner and the name tag, so it is hard to find.
findings.fix: Draw the ring with a 2px --tx-1 stroke and a 1px dark outline, or in --acc at 90% opacity. Keep it on the top layer, above all text.

findings.where: capture frame (164,127 to 1755,1017) and the label at (32,32)
findings.what: The shot is a letterboxed crop with 40px of black margin on the left and top and no HUD. The debug caption 'tracer detail / player 2 / moving' is drawn at roughly 20px, in a different style from the game UI.
findings.fix: Capture the full 1920x1080 frame so the HUD can be reviewed. Keep the debug caption out of the shot.

findings.what: The bar is thin, 8px tall, and fused to the name tag. The red fill on a dark red track has weak contrast, and the P1 bar below 'player 1' is green, so the colours are inconsistent.
findings.fix: Make the bar 10px tall with a 1px --ui-line track and a --ok fill. Use --danger only below 30 percent. Leave a 4px gap under the tag.

findings.where: world props (box at 650,905 to 845,975; yellow glow at 1375,520 to 1560,690)
findings.what: The 'gold glow' box is a flat beige rectangle with no gold glow, so the hint doesn't match what is on screen. The yellow-green muzzle glow is large and washed out and reads as a rendering artefact.
findings.fix: Give the loot box a 3px --r-gold edge or rim light and a 4px radius. Cut the muzzle flash glow to 60% of its radius and 50% opacity.

v.verdict: The cluttered HUD from the last pass is gone, so this reads as a clean tracer-detail crop, but the name tags don't match each other, the P1 colour breaks the amber rule, and the frame has uneven margins.

findings.what: The two tags use different treatments. Player 1 is blue text with a soft halo and a tiny green bar, with no real panel behind it. The enemy tag has a dark panel, a blue side bar and a thick red bar. Both are blurry from upscaling. 'player 1' in blue also breaks the rule that P1 is amber and P2 is cyan.
findings.fix: Use one tag component for both: --ui-panel at 80% alpha, 4px radius, 16px f-cond 600 text, and a 3px left bar in the owner's colour (P1 amber, P2 cyan). Put a 6px hp bar under the name, 100% of the tag width. Draw it at native resolution so the text stays sharp.

findings.where: Frame margins: the crop sits at x164 to 1756 and y127 to 1017, with 164px of black left and right, 127px above and 63px below
findings.what: The picture is off-centre vertically and the margins don't match anything in the 8px grid. The caption floats in the dead black band with no relation to the frame.
findings.fix: Centre the frame, or run it full-bleed at 1920x1080. If it stays as a frame, use 48px margins on all sides, and put the caption either inside the top margin at x=48, y=24 or on a strip below the frame.

findings.what: It is white, roughly 22px, bold and condensed. It is not on a token size, it sits at x=32 off the 48px margin, and the slash separators make it read like a debug string. It is also the brightest text on the screen but is not the point of the picture.
findings.fix: Use 16px f-cond 600 in --tx-2 at x=48, y=24. Replace the ' / ' with a single gap and a 1px --ui-line divider, or split it into a 20px --tx-1 title and a 16px --tx-2 subtitle.

findings.what: The reticle is a thin pale-grey dashed ring on a pale-green ground, so contrast is poor. The ring is 205px wide and fades out. The muzzle flash and bullet streaks cross it.
findings.fix: Give the reticle a 2px --tx-1 stroke with a 1px dark outline (--ui-void at 60%). Or tint it to the shooter's colour. Lift the stroke to at least 3:1 against the grass.

findings.what: A hard horizontal edge splits the green grass from a flat grey slab. The grey wash makes the lower third look dead and draws the eye to the join.
findings.fix: Feather the transition over 40 to 60px, or apply the grey as a vignette at no more than 20% opacity. If it is a real terrain change, give it a border or a transition tile.

findings.what: The red '!' floats 15px above the tag. It is pure --danger on olive, so contrast is only moderate, and it has no backing shape.
findings.fix: Put it in a 24px --danger circle or triangle chip with --tx-1 glyph. Set it 8px above the tag and centred on the tag's left edge.

findings.what: The bar is about 114x13px with a thin dark outline and a green fill that is nearly the same as the surrounding bushes. It almost disappears.
findings.fix: Use a 6px bar with a 1px --ui-void border and a --ok fill on a --ui-panel track. Make its width match the tag.

v.verdict: The frame is still letterboxed with no HUD, and the nameplates are still unstyled blue-tinted boxes. The tracers pass through the reticle and the grey terrain split is still there, so most of the earlier advice was not applied.

findings.what: The capture is still letterboxed (about 80px bars at the sides, 48px at the top), shows no HUD (no hp, ammo or f1 controls line), and has a debug caption in the top-left corner. There is no hero number and nothing for the eye to land on.
findings.fix: Capture the full 1920x1080 frame with the HUD on. Put hp 320x24 bottom-left at x=96 and ammo as the 56px hero number bottom-right. Add a one-line 'f1 controls' at 16px mid-bottom-left. Remove the caption.

findings.what: The plate is a heavy dark box with a blue side tab and a large 40px red condensed word in a faux-bold stroke. The blue tab contradicts the colour rule (p1 amber, p2 cyan, hostile red), and the oversized text overpowers the character it labels. The hp bar is detached below the plate. The '!' alert icon floats separately above it.
findings.fix: Use one nameplate component: 16px f-cond 600 text, with tx-1 for friendly and --danger for hostile. Put it on a --ui-panel plate at 80% opacity with a 4px radius and a 3px side bar in the faction colour (red for hostile). Attach a 64x4 hp bar flush under the text with a 2px gap. Centre the plate 8px above the head, and put the '!' inside the plate or remove it.

findings.what: The name is about 40px bold, light blue with a dark stroke, on a dark box. The hp bar is a green bar with a white outline and does not match the hostile bar's style. P2 should be cyan, and this blue reads as neither cyan nor consistent with the hostile tag.
findings.fix: Reuse the same nameplate component as the hostile tag. Use a 3px --extract-teal or cyan p2 side bar, 16px text, and the same 64x4 hp bar style with no white outline. Keep the same offset above the head.

findings.where: terrain split (y688) and tan block (x616-833, y906-985)
findings.what: The terrain still changes abruptly at y688 from green to a flat grey wash. The tan rectangle is a flat untextured slab, and the pink dashes in the grey area look like stray debris.
findings.fix: Feather the grey region into the grass over 64px, or make it real terrain (a road tile with a 2px border). Texture the tan block as a crate or remove it. Cut the pink tracer fragments to about 40% opacity or use the p1 tracer colour.

findings.what: The ring is still about 225px, drawn as dashed light grey, and low contrast on the green. The yellow tracer dash crosses the centre, so it looks like a glitch instead of a dot. The dotted aim line from P2 ends at the ring with no relationship to it.
findings.fix: Shrink the ring to about 96px with a solid 2px --tx-1 stroke and a 1px dark outline. Use a 4px lime centre dot and draw tracers behind the reticle. Fade the dotted line over its last 64px before the ring.

findings.what: A large pale yellow disc sits under P2 with a gold ring and '!' marker. It reads as a hard-edged blob and competes with the character. The yellow also sits close to the lime accent and the tracer colour, so the meanings blur.
findings.fix: Reduce the glow to a 48px radius at 25% opacity with a feathered edge. Keep the gold ring as a 3px rarity stroke. Use lime only for selected or focus states.

findings.what: A small orange warning-triangle icon sits unlabelled beside the player's head with no frame or consistent size, and nothing says what it means.
findings.fix: Draw it at 16px --warn inside a 24px --ui-panel chip with a 4px radius. Place it in the nameplate row, not on the sprite.

v.verdict: The banner that covered the action is gone and the reticle is now clear, but the hostile tag is still a heavy dark box with a red bar and a loose '!' that sits too high above it. The player 2 tag is a different style, and the player 1 tag and hp bar are missing from the frame.

findings.what: A large dark box with a thick red side bar and a 40px red label, with a thin hp bar hanging off its bottom edge. It is the loudest element on screen, louder than the player. The tag floats about 40px above the head, so it does not read as attached to that enemy. The label word 'hostile' adds nothing.
findings.fix: Delete the box and the red side bar. Draw only a 6px by 96px hp bar, 8px above the head (y about 735), with a 1px #0b0c0d outline. Drop the 'hostile' word, or set it at 16px f-cond 600 in tx-1 with a 2px dark outline.

findings.what: The tag is about 44px, blue and pixel-outlined, and it has a different treatment from the hostile tag (flat dark box, pixel font look). The green hp bar floats under it, 100px or more above the head, so it is not attached to the character. A pixel-style face breaks the rule of Barlow only.
findings.fix: Use 16px f-cond 600 for the label. Fill #16191b at 80% with a 1px #4a5257 border and a 4px radius. Keep cyan only on the text. Move the tag to 8px above the head (y about 170). Make the hp bar 6px high, 96px wide, 8px under the tag.

findings.what: The '!' floats about 20px above the hostile box. It is a separate red glyph of the same weight as the box. It reads as stray noise and it is a second alert on top of the tag.
findings.fix: Delete it, or put it inside the tag as a 20px --warn glyph with 8px padding. Show it for 1 second only, when the enemy first notices the player.

findings.what: The ring is about 228px across with a thin dashed grey-white stroke. It is large for an aim reticle and is low contrast against the olive grass. The dashed ring has less weight than the tag boxes, so the eye goes to the tags first.
findings.fix: Make the ring 96px with a solid 2px stroke in --tx-1 and a 1px #0b0c0d outline, plus a 4px centre dot. Keep the gap in the tick marks.

findings.where: gold pickup glow and marker, (1418,530 to 1620,665)
findings.what: A big pale yellow disc sits behind P2's feet with a small gold ring and '!' icon. The disc looks like a rendering bug and washes out the character's legs. Lime and gold glow are too close to the accent.
findings.fix: Shrink the glow to 64px radius at 35% opacity. Use a 3px --r-gold ring only, and no filled disc.

findings.what: The 'tracer detail player 1 still' text is about 12px, below the 14px floor, and has low contrast on near-black. It sits outside the safe area at x 48.
findings.fix: If this is a shot caption, leave it out of the game frame. If it is on screen, remove it, or set it at 14px tx-2 with the left edge at x>=96.

findings.what: No player 1 tag or hp bar is visible, while P2 and the hostile both have one. The player is the least labelled unit on screen, so the hierarchy is inverted. The P1 amber ring is also not visible near the reticle.
findings.fix: Give P1 the same 16px tag and 6px hp bar as P2, in amber text, 8px above the head. Add a 2px amber ground ring at 40px radius under the feet.

v.verdict: The full 1920x1080 frame is now captured and the hint banner is gone. But the name tags are still inconsistent, the reticle is faint, and there is no HUD, so a player would still call this unpolished.

findings.what: The tag is about 40px tall, blue-tinted and outlined. It is far larger than the 'hostile' tag and breaks both the 16px label spec and the rule that P1 is amber. It is the loudest element on screen while the player's own character is off to one side. The '1' still looks like a lowercase 'l'. The green bar under it is detached and has no track.
findings.fix: Set the tag to 16px f-cond 600 with +.04em tracking on a --ui-panel fill at 80% opacity, 4px radius, no outline. Colour the text P1 amber, and use '1' with a flag or serif so it is not confused with 'l'. Put it 12px above the head. Make the bar 10px tall with a 1px --ui-line track.

findings.what: The tag is about 28px tall and red, with a blue left stripe. It is a different style from the 'player 1' tag, and the stripe is an unexplained colour. The text is cramped inside its box. The tag sits 80px above the enemy sprite and the red '!' floats above it, so neither reads as attached to the enemy. The 5px health bar is flush against the tag and is not aligned to the box edges.
findings.fix: Use the same 16px tag style as the player tags, in --danger text with no blue stripe. Anchor the tag 12px above the head, centred. Put the '!' inside the tag or 8px left of it at 20px. Give the bar a 4px gap below the tag and make its width equal to the tag width.

findings.what: The dashed ring is pale grey at about 50% opacity. It nearly disappears into the grass and the grey ground, and it is the most important aiming element. The tracer dash inside it is yellow, so it competes with the ring. The ring is 225px wide, far larger than the 30px gap it should give to the sprite.
findings.fix: Stroke the ring 2px in --tx-1 with a 1px #0b0c0d outer outline, at 100% opacity. Shrink the diameter to about 120px. Keep a 4px centre dot in --acc, and draw the whole reticle on the top layer.

findings.what: There is no HP, ammo or objective readout on a gameplay shot. The only information is world-space tags. The eye goes first to the big 'player 1' tag at top right, not to the player. The player 2 character at lower left has no tag of its own, so it is unclear which character the P2 camera is following.
findings.fix: Add a minimal HUD with 48px margins. Put the hp bar and ammo bottom-left, using the hero number at 56px f-cond 800 for ammo. Show a P2 tag in cyan above the controlled character. Keep every other element at 16 to 20px.

findings.what: The amber ring and the cyan ring are partly hidden under the sprites. The cyan ring has a stray '!' glyph at 1573,605. There is a yellow-green glow disc around 1420,520 to 1600,665 that looks like a rendering artifact and sits close to the lime accent colour, so it reads as 'selected'.
findings.fix: Draw the rings as 2px strokes beneath the feet at 100% opacity. Remove the '!' from the cyan ring, or replace it with a 16px label. Cap the muzzle-flash glow to a 40px radius and tint it warm white rather than lime.

findings.where: debug caption (48,15 to 224,32) and the frame border
findings.what: The caption 'tracer detail player 2 moving' is 14px, grey and cramped against the top-left corner. It is capture furniture rather than game UI. The black letterbox is 80px on the left and 48px on the top, so the frame is not centred.
findings.fix: Strip the caption from review shots, or move it outside the 1920x1080 image. Make the letterbox even at 0, so the capture is exactly 1920x1080 with no border.

findings.where: world props: tan rectangle (616,906 to 833,986) and grey ground band (80,690 to 1840,1030)
findings.what: The tan block is a flat unlit rectangle with no outline or shading. The ground splits abruptly at y=690 into a hard-edged grey slab. Both look like placeholder art next to the shaded trees, which draws the eye to the bottom of the frame and away from the action.
findings.fix: Add a 1px darker outline and a 4px drop shadow to the tan prop, or remove it. Blend the grey band edge with a 40px soft transition, or break it with the same grass tile used above.

v.verdict: The frame is now nearly full-bleed and the caption sits at x=48, but the two name tags still don't match, the hard grey ground seam is still there, and the caption text is tiny.

findings.what: The two tags are still different components. 'player 1' is pale blue with a blue outline and a green hp bar, and has no owner bar. 'hostile' is red on a dark plate with a blue left bar. The blue bar on the hostile tag reads as an owner colour, but P1 is amber and P2 is cyan. The 'player 1' text is also blue, not amber.
findings.fix: Use one tag component: --ui-panel at 80% alpha, 4px radius, 20px f-cond 600 --tx-1 text, and a 3px left bar in the owner colour (P1 amber, P2 cyan, hostile --danger). Put a 6px hp bar under every name, 100% of the tag width. Drop the blue text and outline.

findings.what: The hard horizontal edge between olive grass and flat grey is still there. It cuts through the 'hostile' tag and the shooter's feet, and the grey half reads as a missing texture, not terrain. It is the biggest thing the eye hits.
findings.fix: Feather the transition over 40 to 60px, or fill the lower area with grass tiles. If the grey is a real terrain change, give it a 2px edge tile and a darker shade, not a flat #7a7a80 slab.

findings.what: The caption is about 12px tall, below the 16px floor. The three parts are separated only by spaces, with no divider and no weight difference, and it drifts from the frame edge at x=80 so it lines up with nothing.
findings.fix: Use 16px f-cond 600 in --tx-2 at x=80, y=14, so it aligns with the frame's left edge. Make 'tracer detail' --tx-1 and separate the parts with a 1px --ui-line divider and 16px gaps.

findings.where: Frame margins (x0 to 80, x1840 to 1920, y0 to 48, y1032 to 1080)
findings.what: The frame is inset 80px left and right, 48px on top and 48px on the bottom. That is better than before, but it is a thin black mat with no border, so the shot floats.
findings.fix: Either run it full-bleed at 1920x1080 or keep the 48px margin and add a 1px --ui-line-hi border on the frame at 4px radius.

findings.what: The dashed ring and ticks are pale grey at roughly 40% opacity on olive, about 2:1 contrast. It is thin and gets lost beside the busy ground, and it is not tinted to the shooter.
findings.fix: Use a 3px --tx-1 stroke with a 1px --ui-void outline at 60%, and tint it with the shooter's colour (P2 cyan). That gives at least 3:1 against the grass.

findings.where: Yellow-green glow disc under the P2 character (1418,530 to 1600,665)
findings.what: A big pale lime circle sits under P2's feet and overlaps the cyan ring. Lime is the 'selected' accent, so it reads as a UI focus state, not a muzzle or ground effect, and it muddies the ring.
findings.fix: Cut its opacity to 15% or less, or remove it. Keep only the 3px cyan ring (#47d8c6 or the P2 cyan) as the P2 marker.

findings.what: A flat tan rectangle with hard edges sits alone in the grey area. It looks like a placeholder or a debug box, with no shadow and no texture.
findings.fix: Remove it, or replace it with a real prop (crate or mat) that has a 4px shadow and the same outline as the other props.

v.verdict: The lobby clutter and the banner are gone and the screen is now a real raid HUD, but five corners compete with no clear first read, there is a capital-letter slip, and the controls panel and the roster are oversized and cramped.

findings.where: top-right 'run info' bar under the minimap
findings.what: The label reads 'run Info' with a capital I, which breaks the all-lower-case order. The bar is a bare dark strip with a chevron, 8px from the minimap and 20px from the screen edge, so it looks pasted on.
findings.fix: Change the text to 'run info'. Make the minimap and the bar one 1px --ui-line-hi panel with a 4px radius. Put a 16px gap between the minimap and the bar, and inset the pair 48px from the top and right edges.

findings.where: left column: 'current pillagers 7' roster, 'host check' bar and controls list
findings.what: Three dark boxes stack down the left side. The roster (16px rows, $ values right-aligned) is the largest block on screen and pulls the eye before the player, the timer or the hp. The controls list is a 20-row, 8-10 line key grid, so it is clutter. The style guide asks for one short folded line mid-bottom-left in a career raid. The panels use different paddings and edge offsets (8px and 16px) and sit flush against the edges.
findings.fix: Fold the controls to one 16px --tx-2 line ('f1 controls'), centred bottom-left. Collapse the roster to a header row by default, expanded on a key. Give every left panel a --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 16px padding and a 48px edge inset.

findings.where: top-centre: '9:00' timer, 'extract 139m' chip and bolt icon
findings.what: The timer is the right hero element, but at about 28px it is half the 56px hero size. The teal chip below it is 16px and sits tight, and the bolt icon floats unexplained beside the clock. The teal chip over a light grey wall has weak edge contrast.
findings.fix: Set the timer to 56px f-cond 800 --tx-1. Put the extract chip 8px below it with a --ui-panel fill and a 1px --extract border, and remove or label the bolt icon. Put a 40% --scrim behind the group so it holds over bright walls.

findings.what: The hp bar is a 400px green slab with large text that has no padding, no border and no inset. It sits 20px from the edge, with its text clipped against the bar edge. The green is the loudest colour in the lower half and competes with the hotbar for first read.
findings.fix: Shrink it to a 240px by 16px bar with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a --ui-panel track. Put 'hp 100' at 20px f-cond 600 above the bar, with a 48px inset from the left and bottom edges. Use --ok for the fill.

findings.what: Slot 1 has an amber border, which is the P1 colour, but the guide says lime --acc means selected. The empty slots 3-0 show faint ghost weapon icons at 12px, which add noise, and the digits are tiny and unevenly spaced. Slot 2 shows a fist icon and an 'f' key tag that is barely readable. The bar's offset (bottom 25px) does not match the ammo card's (bottom 27px).
findings.fix: Use a 2px --acc border on the selected slot, and make P1 amber a name tint only. Remove the ghost icons on empty slots and draw them as 1px --ui-line outlines. Set the digits to 16px --tx-2. Align the bar and the ammo card on one 48px bottom inset.

findings.what: The card is well built, with a 56px hero number, a name and a hint, but the name is 24px, which is off the type scale. 'b / i backpack' at about 14px is too small for a couch read. It is also the second hero on screen, competing with the timer.
